# LEARNME: The Explicit Blackwell FP16 GEMM Kernel, From Design to Every Character

A lecture on `examples/70_blackwell_gemm/70_blackwell_fp16_gemm_explicit.cu`, the de-abstracted, zero-template re-implementation of CUTLASS example 70 for the fixed run `--m=8192 --n=8192 --k=8192` on an NVIDIA B200.

Retrive the Claude session with: `claude --resume aa5f968f-7641-4a17-be49-09c44708be24`

**Goal.** After working through these fourteen chapters you should be able to (1) read every line and character of the kernel and say why it is there, (2) rewrite the kernel from a blank file, top-level design first and PTX last, and (3) carry the method to other operators and write speed-of-light kernels of your own.

**How it is organised.** Chapters 1-4 are top-down: what the kernel is, the hardware it drives, the design decisions and their speed-of-light arithmetic, and the barrier protocol that ties the warps together. Chapters 5-11 are bottom-up: the source file section by section, every constant, every PTX wrapper, every role function, the prologue and the host launcher. Chapters 12-14 are mastery: what the compiler made of the code and what was measured, how to build such a kernel yourself and generalise it, and exercises with answers, a glossary and references.

**Sources.** Everything is grounded in the kernel source, the CUTLASS v4.7.1 headers it copies its PTX from, the knowledge base `Semantics-preserving-de-abstraction.md` in the same directory (the trace-verified protocol, the measured values and the acceptance results), the PTX ISA, and the NVIDIA and Colfax documentation cited in Chapter 14. Facts are labelled measured, derived from source, or analysis.

**Notation.** Rank `r = x + 2y` with `(x, y) = %cluster_ctaid`; the pair leader is the even rank and the peer is `r ^ 1`; CTA 0 is rank 0; tile coordinates `(tm, tn)` count 128 x 128 CTA tiles; `q` is the k-tile (0..127), `s` the smem stage (0..7), `kb` the k-block (0..3), `st` the TMEM accumulator stage (0..3), `e` the epilogue subtile (0..7), `i` the store box (0..3), `j` the register/column (0..15), `w = warp_idx - 4` the epilogue warp (0..3), `l` the lane (0..31); `smem_base` is the 32-bit `shared::cta` address of the dynamic shared memory; `T` is the TMEM base address.

# Chapter 1. Orientation: What This Kernel Is and How to Read It

**What you will learn**

- What `70_blackwell_fp16_gemm_explicit.cu` is: one `__global__` kernel plus one host launch function that re-implement, with no CUTLASS/CuTe abstraction, the GEMM that CUTLASS example 70 builds through `CollectiveBuilder`/`GemmUniversal`, for one fixed run (8192^3, fp16 in, fp32 out, alpha = 1, beta = 0, cluster (2,2,1)).
- How the kernel was derived (semantics-preserving de-abstraction: trace the compile-time resolution, trace the run-time protocol with probes, write the explicit kernel, verify value-equality and performance) and what was achieved (value-equal `D`, runtime ratio 0.99937, 26 registers).
- The file set (three source files, the harness, the CMake line, the trace tooling, the evidence directories) and the two call sites in the harness.
- The comment legend `[PROD]`/`[TRACE]`/`[CHECK]`/`[HOST]` and why the diagnostics are a source-level toggle rather than a second build target.
- The FILE MAP of the 12 sections, and which lecture chapter owns each section.
- The three-level picture (host `run()` -> kernel prologue -> five warp roles), one CTA, one cluster, and the data path TMA -> smem -> UMMA -> TMEM -> registers -> smem -> TMA -> global.
- Every line of the NUMBERS AT A GLANCE block, with one or two sentences of "why" and a pointer to the chapter that derives it.
- How to use this lecture, the prerequisites, the notation, and the 12 facts to keep in your head.

Conventions used in this chapter and in the whole lecture: `explicit.cu` is `examples/70_blackwell_gemm/70_blackwell_fp16_gemm_explicit.cu`, `explicit.hpp` and `util.hpp` are the two headers next to it, "the harness" is `70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.cu`, and "the note" is `examples/70_blackwell_gemm/Semantics-preserving-de-abstraction.md`. Every code quotation is copied verbatim from the source (line numbers checked with `grep -n`); CUTLASS line numbers quoted *inside* `explicit.cu` comments refer to commit `cb424739` and must be checked with `git show cb424739:<path>` because the working tree's CUTLASS headers carry the trace probe blocks of the note's Part C (see Section 1.4). Each chapter that cites CUTLASS headers says which numbering it uses: Chapters 6, 9, 10, 13 and 14 use the cb424739 numbers (the ones in explicit.cu's comments and in the note); Chapters 4, 5 and 7 use the working tree (HEAD of `dev/gemm-deabstraction`) and give the cb424739 number alongside where the two differ; Chapter 8 uses cb424739 for the kernel header and the working tree for `copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp`; Chapter 11 uses cb424739 for the kernel header and the working tree for the scheduler header; Chapters 2, 3 and 12 cite only regions that are identical in both trees. Only four headers differ, all by inserted trace-probe blocks (`git diff --stat cb424739 HEAD -- include/`): `cutlass/gemm/kernel/sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp` (working tree = cb424739 + 28 after cb424739's :616, + 34 after :731, + 40 after :872), `cutlass/gemm/kernel/sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp` (+ 6 after :445, + 9 after :464, + 31 after :469), `cute/arch/mma_sm100_umma.hpp` (+ 6 after :571) and `cute/atom/copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp` (+ 2, + 7 and + 32 after its hunks at :80, :414 and :1070); `git show cb424739:<path> | sed -n A,Bp` reproduces the comment numbering. Statements are labelled **measured** (note Parts D and G), **derived from source**, or **my analysis** where the distinction matters.

## 1.1 What the kernel is

### 1.1.1 The one-paragraph definition

`explicit.cu` opens with its own definition (explicit.cu:5-23):

```
/***************************************************************************************************
 * Explicit (de-abstracted) Blackwell FP16 GEMM of example 70.
 *
 * One __global__ kernel that re-implements, without any CUTLASS/CuTe abstraction, the GEMM that
 * examples/70_blackwell_gemm/70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.cu builds through CollectiveBuilder / GemmUniversal for the
 * fixed run  --m=8192 --n=8192 --k=8192  (alpha = 1, beta = 0, cluster (2,2,1)), plus the host function
 * explicit_gemm::run() that launches it exactly as GemmUniversalAdapter::run() launches the CUTLASS kernel.
 *
 * The knowledge base is examples/70_blackwell_gemm/Semantics-preserving-de-abstraction.md ("the note"):
 *   Section 6.2  shared-memory layout        Section 7   protocol (barriers, roles, CLC, TMA, UMMA, epilogue)
 *   Part B       PTX and coordinate formulas Part D      measured values (descriptors, masks, SASS inventory)
 *   Part E       this implementation's plan  (E.5 host function, E.6 kernel architecture, E.7 bring-up)
 * Every asm string below is copied from the CUTLASS source named next to it (commit cb424739); CuTe is used
 * only at compile time (cute::Swizzle cross-check of the epilogue smem formula); inline PTX covers tcgen05.*,
 * cp.async.bulk.tensor.*, mbarrier.*, fence.*, clusterlaunchcontrol.*, griddepcontrol.*, mapa, elect.sync,
 * bar.sync/arrive, barrier.cluster.* and prefetch.tensormap (Section 1 items 3-4).
 *
 * Address-space rule (E.6.1): every asm operand that names shared memory is the 32-bit shared::cta address
 * `smem_base + OFF_*`; every C++ dereference of shared memory uses the generic pointer `smem + OFF_*`.
```

Read the three claims in that banner as the three axes of the whole lecture:

1. **Same computation.** The kernel computes `D = alpha * A * B + beta * C` for the fixed problem exactly as the CUTLASS kernel does, value for value (the harness compares every one of the 8192 x 8192 outputs with `BlockCompareEqual`, harness:378). The reference kernel it replaces is instantiated at harness:102-156: `half_t` A (RowMajor = K-major), `half_t` B (ColumnMajor = K-major), `float` C/D (ColumnMajor = M-major), `MmaTileShape_MNK = Shape<_256,_128,_64>`, `ClusterShape_MNK = Shape<_2,_2,_1>`, `KernelScheduleAuto`, `EpilogueScheduleAuto`, `GemmUniversal`, `GemmUniversalAdapter` (note, Section 2).
2. **Same performance mechanisms.** Two-SM `tcgen05` MMA with a 2 x 2 x 1 cluster, TMA loads with A multicast, an 8-stage A/B shared-memory pipeline, a 4-stage TMEM accumulator pipeline, warp specialization, the persistent Cluster-Launch-Control (CLC) scheduler, and a TMA-store epilogue with 4 smem stages (note, Section 1 item 2). None of these may be approximated away; this is why the kernel is a legitimate "speed-of-light" study object rather than a toy.
3. **No hidden layers.** No `CollectiveMma`, `CollectiveEpilogue`, `GemmUniversal`, `PersistentTileSchedulerSm100`, `Pipeline*`, `TiledMma`, `TiledCopy`, `FusionCallbacks` (note, Section 1 item 3). Every PTX instruction the hardware executes is visible as an `asm volatile` string in Section 3 of the file (37 wrappers, W1-W37), and every "who calls which wrapper on which barrier with which count and parity" decision is visible in Sections 5-10. In `explicit.cu` CuTe appears only inside compile-time `static_assert`s: `cute::Swizzle<2,5,2>` to cross-check the hand-written epilogue swizzle formula (explicit.cu:198-201) and `cute::Swizzle<3,4,3>` to pin the A/B stage swizzle masks (explicit.cu:204). `explicit.hpp` additionally uses `cute::get<i>(p.problem_shape)` inside the host-only `make_params` template (explicit.hpp:39, 107-110), which is instantiated in the harness translation unit. No CuTe type reaches device code.

### 1.1.2 The fixed run

The kernel hard-codes one configuration (note, Section 0; util.hpp:29-39) and the host function rejects everything else before launching (explicit.cu:1266-1272). The configuration:

| Quantity | Value | Where it is fixed |
|---|---|---|
| M, N, K, L | 8192, 8192, 8192, 1 | `--m=8192 --n=8192 --k=8192`, also the `Options` defaults `m(8192), n(8192), k(8192),` (harness:209; the constructor opens at :207, :208 is `help(false),`) |
| A | fp16, M x K, K-major (`RowMajor`) | harness:102-104 (`ElementA = half_t`, `LayoutA = cutlass::layout::RowMajor`; B at :107-108, C/D at :112-113; :117-156 is the kernel functional config, tile and cluster shapes and the two `CollectiveBuilder`s); tensor map A: `FLOAT16`, dims (K, M, L) = (8192, 8192, 1), box (64, 64, 1), `SWIZZLE_128B` (explicit.hpp:50) |
| B | fp16, N x K, K-major (`ColumnMajor`) | tensor map B likewise (explicit.hpp:51) |
| C, D | fp32, M x N, M-major (`ColumnMajor`) | tensor maps C, D: `FLOAT32`, box (32, 16, 1), `SWIZZLE_128B_ATOM_32B` (explicit.hpp:52-53) |
| alpha, beta | 1.0f, 0.0f, **read at run time** from the parameter block | `alpha(1.f), beta(0.f),` harness:210; explicit.hpp:55; why run-time: Section 1.6 below, paragraph "epilogue" |
| cluster | (2, 2, 1) | util.hpp:31 |
| grid | (64, 64, 1) = (N/128, M/128, 1) after the AlongN transpose | util.hpp:32 |
| block | 256 threads = 8 warps | util.hpp:33 |
| dynamic smem | 230400 bytes | util.hpp:34 |
| machine | NVIDIA B200, CC 10.0, 148 SMs, SM clock 1965 MHz under load, CUDA 13.3 (nvcc 13.3.73), driver 610.57.04 | **measured**, note D.5 and G.2 |

Why hard-code? The note's Section 0 records the user's decision that the example is built and run in exactly one way, so the replacement may fold the shape, tile, stage and scheduler constants into `constexpr` values. The payoff is a kernel whose every number is visible and explainable (this lecture); the cost is generality (a different shape is rejected with `kErrorInvalidProblem`, explicit.cu:1268). Chapter 13 discusses how to re-generalize.

### 1.1.3 How it was derived: semantics-preserving de-abstraction

The kernel was not written from a blank page. It is the end product of a method whose record is the note (2059 lines, Parts A-I). The method matters as much as the result, because it is the method you will reuse when you write your own speed-of-light kernel for another operator (Chapter 13):

| Step | What was done | Note | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Fix the contract | Pin the build and run commands, the shape, alpha/beta, swizzle; define "same output" (exact compare) and "same performance" (interleaved five-run medians at steady clocks); forbid hidden layers | Part A, Sections 0-3, 12 | the equivalence contract |
| 2. Trace the compile-time resolution | Follow every `Auto` of the two `CollectiveBuilder`s to concrete types: the mainloop policy `MainloopSm100TmaUmmaWarpSpecialized<8,2,4,(2,2,1),Sm100>` (8 smem stages, 2 scheduler stages, 4 accumulator stages), the `Sm100TmaWarpSpecialized<4,2,16,true,false>` epilogue, `PersistentTileSchedulerSm100<(2,2,1),2>`, the six pipeline classes, the copy and MMA atoms | Sections 4-7, Part B | the protocol (barrier counts, parities, masks), the CuTe layouts, the coordinate formulas (B.4), the PTX inventory (B.5) |
| 3. Trace the run-time protocol with probes | Add `TRACE_RECORD` probes to four CUTLASS headers and host probes to the harness under a source-level toggle; run the fixed command once; decode 6864 records | Part C (plan), Part D (results) | **measured** facts the source cannot settle: shared-memory base `0x400 + (rank << 24)`, TMEM base 0, descriptor words, SASS lowering of every primitive (D.2), CLC dynamics (D.3), the performance baseline (D.4) |
| 4. Write the explicit kernel | Three files, one kernel, one host function mirroring `GemmUniversalAdapter::run()`, 37 PTX wrappers copied verbatim from the CUTLASS source | Part E (strategy), Part F (record) | `explicit.cu`, `explicit.hpp`, `util.hpp`, commit `829f0645` |
| 5. Verify | Toggle-on run: exact compare; the same 6864 non-tail records as the CUTLASS kernel's run; record-level identity (the multiset of `(rank, warp, lane, v0..v9)` tuples, even including `(bx, by)`) for every non-CLC record kind (K1 smem offsets, K2 TMEM base, K3 MMA operands, K4a/K4b TMA load and store operands, kinds 10 and 11) and protocol-level identity (same slots, parities, counts and barrier addresses) for the CLC kinds K5a/K5b/K5c, which differ in 26 of 1024, 290 of 1024 and 1160 of 4096 tuples because they carry the tile ids the hardware scheduler handed out, which vary from run to run; `check_trace.py` 4112 PASS, 0 FAIL; toggle-off: five interleaved runs against the pristine binary, PTX/SASS inventory (`check_sass.py` 93 PASS, 0 FAIL after the G.6 parser fix; the committed `sass_checklist.txt` shows 89 PASS and one tooling FAIL, Section 1.2), two toggle-off builds give identical SASS | Part G, Part H, Part I | the acceptance table (I.2) |

What was achieved (**measured**, note Part G; the numbers you should remember):

- **Value-equal D** in every run: one toggle-on run with `D` sentinel-filled to `0xFF` bytes beforehand (so an unwritten element would read as NaN), plus five toggle-off runs, all `Disposition: Passed` with the exact compare (G.1). Two qualifications the note itself makes (G.1, Section 8), so that you weigh this evidence correctly: the harness seeds A, B and C identically on every run (`initialize_block(block_A, seed + 2023)` etc. with the global `seed` zero-initialized, harness:183, 331-333), so strictly it is the same input six times; and `BlockFillRandomUniform` with scope [-8, 8] and integer rounding (harness:307-312) makes every input an integer, so the fp32 accumulation is exact in *any* summation order for K <= 262144 and alpha = 1, beta = 0 gives D = acc exactly. "Value-equal D" therefore proves the computation, not the instruction sequence; the instruction-level equivalence is established structurally, by the PTX/SASS inventories and the probe records (G.3, G.1).
- **Runtime** median 0.889354 ms for the explicit kernel against 0.889917 ms for the same-day pristine CUTLASS binary, interleaved, five runs each: ratio **0.99937** (G.2). `GFLOPS = 2 x 8192^3 / Avg runtime`, so 0.889354 ms is about 1.236 x 10^6 GFLOPS = 1.236 PFLOP/s. One thing to know before Chapter 3 compares this with a speed-of-light bound: `Avg runtime` is not kernel-only. `GpuTimer` brackets ten `gemm.initialize()` + `explicit_gemm::run()` pairs; the GPU is idle at `timer.start()` (the reference compare drains the stream), so iteration 0's host work (six tensor-map encodes, the attribute calls, the launch) is exposed, while iterations 1-9 hide theirs behind the previous kernel (note E.5.4, Section 12 item 1; the same holds for the baseline, which is why the comparison is apple-to-apple). Kernel-only figures derived from 0.889 ms are therefore upper bounds (D.4). Chapter 3 puts this against the tensor-core peak and derives the "speed of light" for this shape.
- **Resources** `REG 26, STACK 0, LOCAL 0, SHARED 1024` (the system-reserved kilobyte), `CONSTANT[0] 1536` = 0x380 + the 640-byte parameter block (G.3). The CUTLASS kernel uses 68 registers; the difference is the omitted beta != 0 path and fewer live values, not a different hot loop (G.3, "Why 26 and not 68"; Chapter 12).
- **Occupancy at run time**: 33 clusters resident, 132 SMs busy and 16 idle (**measured**, D.3, confirmed for the explicit kernel in G.1). Tiles per cluster in the traced run: 13 clusters processed 32 tiles, 19 processed 31, and the probed cluster (0,0) processed 19 because its K3/K4a/K4b probes made it 1.7x slower per tile (13 x 32 + 19 x 31 + 19 = 416 + 589 + 19 = 1024; D.3, D.1 D9). The untraced timed runs are not instrumented: for them "31 or 32 tiles per cluster" is the balanced expectation (1024 = 33 x 31 + 1), not a measurement. Chapter 3 and Chapter 7 explain why 33 and not 148/4 = 37.

### 1.2.1 The two call sites in the harness

The harness is the oracle: it fills the inputs, runs the reference GEMM, compares exactly, and times. The de-abstraction replaced exactly one thing in it, `gemm.run()`, at two places (`grep -n "explicit_gemm::run" 70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.cu`):

```
416:  CUTLASS_CHECK(explicit_gemm::run(gemm));
439:      CUTLASS_CHECK(explicit_gemm::run(gemm));
```

Line 416 is the correctness/warm-up launch (harness:415-416, "Correctness / Warmup iteration"); line 439 is the body of the ten-iteration timed loop, immediately after `CUTLASS_CHECK(gemm.initialize(arguments, workspace.get()));` at harness:438. The template `explicit_gemm::run(Gemm const&)` (explicit.hpp:129-132) calls `make_params(gemm)` and then the non-template `run(ExplicitGemmParams const&)` defined at explicit.cu:1265.

Why does `gemm.initialize()` still run in the timed loop when the CUTLASS kernel is never launched? Because `initialize()` is what encodes the tensor maps with the driver, and the explicit kernel reads those very bytes out of `gemm.params()`. Six encodes but four maps: `initialize()` performs six `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled` calls in the order A, B, A-fallback, B-fallback, C, D, because CUTLASS's mainloop `Params` carry `tma_load_a`, `tma_load_b`, `tma_load_a_fallback` and `tma_load_b_fallback` (note 5.3). For a static (2,2,1) cluster the two fallback maps are byte-identical to the primaries (**measured**, D.1 D3) and exist only for CUTLASS's fallback-cluster launch path, so `ExplicitGemmParams` holds four `CUtensorMap` fields and `make_params` copies exactly four, `tma_a`, `tma_b`, `tma_c`, `tma_d` (explicit.hpp:50-53, 103-106). If you go looking for two "missing" maps in `make_params`, that is where they went. Keeping it makes the timed interval apple-to-apple with the baseline: the same six encodes per iteration plus one attribute call on the (now never-launched) CUTLASS kernel; the explicit path adds its own two `cudaFuncSetAttribute` calls and one `cudaLaunchKernelExC` (note, Section 12 item 1 and E.5.4). Re-encoding the maps inside the host function ("Option B") is a recorded optional follow-up (note I.3 item 1), and Chapter 11 shows what it would take.

The other unguarded harness edits are the two include lines: harness:1 `#include "70_blackwell_fp16_gemm_explicit_util.hpp"` (the toggle line, Section 1.3) and harness:88 `#include "70_blackwell_fp16_gemm_explicit.hpp"` after `#include "helper.h"`. The five toggle-guarded blocks (two guarded includes at harness:2-4 and 89-91, three guarded calls at harness:389-392 `trace_begin`, 411-413 `trace_host_probes<Gemm>`, 421-424 `trace_end`) compile to nothing in the performance binary.

Also unchanged, and executed before `gemm.initialize()`: the workspace query and allocation (harness:401-404) and `CUTLASS_CHECK(gemm.can_implement(arguments))` (harness:407). The explicit path bypasses `can_implement`, which is why `run()` carries its own guard block (explicit.cu:1267-1272: mode, shape, raster order and swizzle divisor, tile counts, scalar pointers, `beta == 0`), and why `-0.0f` passes the beta guard exactly as CUTLASS's `is_zero()` would: `params.beta != 0.0f` is false for `-0.0f` (explicit.cu:1272 and its trailing comment).

## 1.3 The comment legend: `[PROD]`, `[TRACE]`, `[CHECK]`, `[HOST]`

Every section banner and many trailing comments in the three source files carry tags. The legend is in the file header (explicit.cu:26-36):

```
 * HOW TO READ THIS FILE (legend used in every section banner and in trailing comments)
 *
 *   [PROD]  production path: compiled into the performance binary (line 1 of the util header commented out).
 *   [TRACE] diagnostics only: every such block sits inside #if defined(CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE), is compiled only
 *           when the trace toggle is on (note, Part H.2.1) and emits no instruction otherwise; the SASS of two toggle-off
 *           builds is identical (E.8 D6, G.3). Nothing in a [TRACE] block changes what the kernel computes.
 *   [CHECK] compile-time verification: static_assert and constexpr cross-checks (incl. the CuTe swizzle check); no code.
 *   [HOST]  host-side code: the launch mirror and the trace entry points.
 *   Hardware families named in the banners and wrapper tags: tcgen05 (TMEM alloc/dealloc, MMA, commit, ld), TMA
 *   (cp.async.bulk.tensor loads/stores, prefetch.tensormap), mbarrier (init/arrive/expect_tx/try_wait), CLC
 *   (clusterlaunchcontrol), GDC (griddepcontrol), LAYOUT (CuTe layout, coordinate and byte-offset arithmetic written out).
```

How to use the tags when reading:

- When you want **the kernel the GPU runs**, read `[PROD]` and skip every `#if defined(CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE)` block. There are 29 such preprocessor lines in `explicit.cu` (`grep -c '^#if defined(CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE)'`; a plain `grep -c` says 30 because the legend text at line 29 also matches), always paired with an `#endif` (and sometimes an `#else`) close by; with the toggle off, Section 2 reduces to its `#else` branch (explicit.cu:235-240: `EXPLICIT_WAIT` is the plain blocking wait `mbar_wait`, and the CLC record kinds are 0) and Section 12 vanishes. Two things the preprocessor does *not* remove, and why they cost nothing: `clc_consume<TraceKind>` stays a template, instantiated with `K_CLC_SCHED_KIND = K_CLC_MMA_KIND = 0u` (explicit.cu:238-239), and `EXPLICIT_WAIT(addr, parity, site, tile, q)` expands to `mbar_wait((addr), (parity))` (explicit.cu:237), the site/tile/q arguments vanishing. A template parameter is a compile-time constant, so `clc_consume<0u>` compiles to exactly what a non-template function would; the evidence that no hidden cost survives is G.3 D6 (two toggle-off builds, byte-identical SASS) and the SASS inventory, which contains no record-buffer store.
- When you want **to know a number is right**, read `[CHECK]`: the `static_assert`s of Section 1 (explicit.cu:158-204) pin the smem offsets to the CUTLASS `SharedStorage` layout, the descriptor words to their bit maps, the barrier counts to their formulas, and the epilogue swizzle to `cute::Swizzle<2,5,2>`; the `static_assert`s of `explicit.hpp` pin the parameter-block offsets the device reads.
- When you want **to see how the kernel is launched**, read `[HOST]`: Section 11 (`run()`, explicit.cu:1265-1329) and the header bridge.
- The hardware-family words (`tcgen05`, `TMA`, `mbarrier`, `CLC`, `GDC`, `LAYOUT`) tell you which Chapter 6 wrapper group and which Chapter 2 hardware unit a section belongs to. `LAYOUT` marks the places where CuTe layout algebra was replaced by written-out integer arithmetic: the coordinate formulas in `clc_consume` (Section 5), the TMA coordinates in the producer (Section 6), the descriptor increments in the MMA role (Section 8), and the swizzled store offsets in the epilogue (Section 9).

### 1.3.1 Why a source-level trace toggle exists

Three constraints forced the design (note, Section 0, consequences; C.1 rule 2; E.2.3):

1. **One build command, one run command, no second target.** The user fixed the `cmake` and run lines; the probes had to be reachable without adding a CMake target, a compile definition or a command-line flag. The only place left is the source itself: line 1 of `util.hpp` (util.hpp:1 begins `// #define CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE 1`). Uncomment it, rebuild with the same command, run the same command, and you get the diagnostics binary; re-comment and rebuild for the performance binary. `deabstraction_trace_run.sh` flips it with `sed`.
2. **Two translation units must agree.** `explicit.cu` and the harness both include `util.hpp` *first* (explicit.cu:1, harness:1), so one edit switches both; `deabstraction_trace.hpp` makes its device globals `static __device__` so each TU owns a private copy without `-rdc`.
3. **The performance binary must be provably untouched by the diagnostics.** Every probe sits inside `#if defined(CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE)`, so the preprocessor removes it. The `restore` step of the script rebuilds toggle-off and diffs the explicit kernel's SASS against the earlier toggle-off build: byte-identical (**measured**, note G.3 D6: `sass_explicit_after.txt` identical to `sass_explicit.txt`). The toggle-on explicit binary ran at `Avg runtime` 1.13341 ms (G.2): 1.13341 / 0.889354 = 1.274, about 27% slower than the performance binary, and 1.13341 / 1.00684 = 1.126, about 12.6% slower than the CUTLASS kernel's own toggle-on binary of 2026-09-09 (1.00684 ms). The note's Part H shorthand "about 12% slower (G.2)" is the second ratio. That 12.6% delta is the cost of the E.7.2 diagnostics the CUTLASS trace build did not have: every blocking wait reads `%globaltimer` at entry and after each failed `try_wait`, and the role warps write heartbeats to host-mapped pinned memory at tile start and tail. Neither trace binary may be timed (note, Part H, "Two rules").

A consequence for you as a reader: **the CUTLASS headers of this tree are not pristine**. Four of them carry the Part C probe blocks under the same macro (`git diff --stat cb424739 -- include/`: 121 insertions and 12 deletions in total across `cute/arch/mma_sm100_umma.hpp` (+6), `cute/atom/copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp`, `cutlass/gemm/kernel/sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp` (+40) and `cutlass/gemm/kernel/sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp` (+31)). The line numbers that `explicit.cu` quotes for CUTLASS (for example `kernel :617, 681, 726, 807, 869` for the role dispatch, explicit.cu:1190) are therefore valid at commit `cb424739`, and you check them with `git show cb424739:include/cutlass/gemm/kernel/sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp | sed -n 617p`, which prints `if (is_participant.main_load) {` (verified; 681 `else if (is_participant.sched) {`, 726 `else if (is_participant.mma) {`, 807 `else if (is_participant.epi_load) {`, 869 `else if (is_participant.epilogue) {`). In the working tree those lines are displaced by the inserted probe blocks.

## 1.4 The FILE MAP: 12 sections

The banner lists the sections (explicit.cu:38-50):

```
 * FILE MAP (section numbers appear in the banners below)
 *    1. configuration constants, Section 6.2 shared-memory map, descriptor and protocol constants   [PROD] [CHECK] LAYOUT
 *    2. trace-only types: hang records, heartbeats, K_TAIL, EXPLICIT_WAIT                            [TRACE]
 *    3. PTX wrappers W1-W37, one asm string each, copied from CUTLASS                                [PROD] tcgen05 TMA mbarrier CLC GDC
 *    4. pipeline-state and descriptor helpers; trace-only bounded wait and heartbeat                 [PROD] [TRACE]
 *    5. clc_consume: the CLC response consumer shared by warps 0, 1, 2, 4-7                           [PROD] CLC LAYOUT
 *    6. producer_role (warp 2): TMA loads of A and B into the 8-stage smem ring                       [PROD] TMA mbarrier
 *    7. scheduler_role (warp 1 of rank 0): CLC queries and the throttle                               [PROD] CLC mbarrier
 *    8. mma_role (warp 0): TMEM allocation, 4 UMMAs per k-tile, commits, deallocation                 [PROD] tcgen05
 *    9. epilogue_role (warps 4-7): tcgen05.ld, alpha/beta, swizzled smem stores, TMA stores of D      [PROD] tcgen05 TMA LAYOUT
 *   10. the __global__ kernel: prologue (barrier inits, cluster rendezvous, initial tile), dispatch    [PROD]
 *   11. run(): the host launch mirror of GemmUniversalAdapter::run()                                  [HOST] [PROD]
 *   12. trace_begin / trace_end / mismatch dump                                                       [HOST] [TRACE]
```

The sections appear in the file in this order because C++ needs definitions before uses: constants before wrappers that embed them, wrappers before helpers, helpers before roles, roles before the kernel that dispatches them, the kernel before the host function that takes its address. The same order is a sensible *bottom-up* reading order, and it is the order of Chapters 5-11.

## 1.5 The three-level picture

### 1.5.1 Host `run()` -> kernel prologue -> five warp roles

```
LEVEL 0  HOST            explicit_gemm::run(gemm)                               explicit.hpp:129-132 -> explicit.cu:1265
                         make_params(gemm): copy tma_a, tma_b, tma_c, tma_d, m, n, k, l, alpha, beta (+ guard fields)
                         out of gemm.params(), which the unchanged gemm.initialize() filled
                         guards (shape, mode, raster, tiles, pointers, beta == 0)
                         cudaFuncSetAttribute(MaxDynamicSharedMemorySize, 230400)
                         cudaFuncSetAttribute(NonPortableClusterSizeAllowed, 1)
                         cudaLaunchKernelExC: grid (64,64,1), block (256,1,1), cluster (2,2,1), smem 230400, stream 0
                         cudaGetLastError
                                                   |
                                                   v
LEVEL 1  PROLOGUE        explicit_blackwell_fp16_gemm_kernel(params)            explicit.cu:1095-1188, all 256 threads of each of the 4096 CTAs
                         smem_base = shared::cta address of the dynamic smem   (0x400 + (rank << 24), measured)
                         warp_idx, lane, lane_pred (elect.sync), rank, is_cta0, is_leader (rank even), peer (rank ^ 1)
                         alpha, beta, k_tiles = (k + 63) >> 6 = 128; prefetch.tensormap A, B (warp 1 of EVERY CTA) and C, D (warp 3 of every CTA)
                         33 mbarrier.init: four fenced groups (warp 0: 8 full + 8 empty mainloop; warp 4: 2 + 2 CLC; warp 5: 4 + 4 accumulator;
                         warp 3: 2 + 2 throttle; one fence.mbarrier_init.release.cluster after each) + the tmem_dealloc init by warp 0 after the
                         fourth fence, with no fence of its own (explicit.cu:1165-1167); 16 + 4 + 8 + 4 + 1 = 33
                         barrier.cluster.arrive.relaxed -> (x, y) = %cluster_ctaid, initial (tm, tn) from blockIdx -> barrier.cluster.wait
                                                   |
                                                   v
LEVEL 2  ROLES           if (warp_idx == 2)            producer_role   explicit.cu:762   TMA A (multicast) + B per k-tile into the 8-stage ring
         (explicit.cu:   else if (warp_idx == 1 && is_cta0) scheduler_role explicit.cu:820   CLC queries + throttle (rank 0 only)
          1190-1202)     else if (warp_idx == 0)       mma_role        explicit.cu:881   TMEM alloc; leader: 4 UMMAs per k-tile + commits; dealloc
                         else if (warp_idx >= 4)       epilogue_role   explicit.cu:995   tcgen05.ld -> alpha/beta -> swizzled smem -> TMA store
                         (warp 3, and warp 1 of ranks 1-3: fall through and exit)
```

The dispatch itself (explicit.cu:1190-1203):

```
  // 7.3 step 7: role dispatch in the baseline's branch order (kernel :617, 681, 726, 807, 869); warp 3 and warp 1 of ranks 1-3 fall through and exit
  if (warp_idx == 2) {
    producer_role(params, smem_base, x, y, is_cta0, lane_pred != 0u && is_leader, k_tiles, tm, tn);
  }
  else if (warp_idx == 1 && is_cta0) {
    scheduler_role(smem_base, x, y, lane, tm, tn);
  }
  else if (warp_idx == 0) {
    mma_role(smem, smem_base, x, y, rank, is_leader, peer, lane_pred, k_tiles, tm, tn);
  }
  else if (warp_idx >= 4) {
    epilogue_role(params, smem, smem_base, x, y, rank, is_leader, warp_idx, lane, alpha, beta, tm, tn);
  }
}
```

Two facts about this block that you would not guess from the C++. First, ptxas did not compile the if/else chain into a compare-and-branch chain as it did for the CUTLASS kernel: it built a three-entry jump table. `CONSTANT[2]:12` in the resource line is that table (three 4-byte entries), and the prologue reads it with `UISETP.LT.U32 UP0, UR20, 0x2; USEL UR4, UR20, 0x2, UP0; USHF.L.U32 UR4, UR4, 0x2; LDCU UR10, c[0x2][UR4]; BRXU UR10` (**measured**, G.3; `sass_explicit.txt` at `0x0a60-0x0ae0`): targets for warp 0, warp 1 and warp >= 2, the last split again on `warp_idx == 2`. It executes once per thread in the prologue and is in the same cost class as the CUTLASS kernel's branch chain. (`CONSTANT[0] 1536` is the parameter bank: 0x380 + the 640-byte `ExplicitGemmParams`; Chapter 12.) Second, of the 33 `mbarrier.init` above, only the `tmem_dealloc` init has no `fence.mbarrier_init.release.cluster` of its own (explicit.cu:1165-1167, comment "no fence of its own"); this copies the CUTLASS kernel, which initializes that barrier after all its pipeline constructors and relies on the cluster rendezvous that follows (`pipeline_init_arrive_relaxed`, kernel :578-580 at `cb424739`, with the comment "We need this to guarantee that the Pipeline init is visible to all producers and consumer threadblocks in the cluster"). That is why the comment at explicit.cu:1178, "no remote barrier operation before this point", is load-bearing: the first remote operation on any barrier happens only after every CTA has passed `barrier.cluster.wait`, and the first use of `tmem_dealloc` is the very last protocol step of the kernel, long after many cluster-scope release/acquire pairs (my analysis; Chapter 11).

Three design facts to absorb now (each is derived in a later chapter):

- **Warp specialization.** Each warp runs one role for the whole kernel, communicating through `mbarrier`s in shared memory and through TMEM. No warp ever does two kinds of work; the producer never computes, the MMA warp never loads, the epilogue warps never touch A or B. This is what lets the tensor core, the TMA unit and the store path run concurrently (Chapter 3, Chapter 4).
- **Persistence.** Every role is a `do { ... } while (valid);` loop over tiles (explicit.cu:776-796, 831-856, 909-949, 1024-1075). A CTA does not exit after one 128 x 128 tile; it asks the CLC scheduler for another cluster tile and continues until the response says "not cancelled" (Chapter 7).
- **Roles are per warp, decisions are per lane.** Inside a role, `elect_one_sync()` picks one lane to issue a TMA load (explicit.cu:740), an MMA, a commit or a CLC query, while barrier waits are executed by all 32 lanes (the `mbarrier.try_wait` is per thread). Two deliberate exceptions: the TMA stores are issued by all 32 lanes of warp 4 with uniform operands and no election (`issue_tma_store = (w == 0u)`, explicit.cu:1018; one `UTMASTG` per box in the SASS, note Section 13 item 8), and the CLC full-barrier arming is done by lanes 0..3 by predicate, one lane per destination CTA, not by election (explicit.cu:842). Chapter 6 (W2) and Chapters 8-10 show every election.

### 1.5.2 One CTA: 8 warps and their roles

```
 one CTA = one SM: 256 threads = 8 warps; 230400 B dynamic smem (so exactly 1 CTA per SM); allocates all 512 columns of its OWN SM's
 Tensor Memory through one tcgen05.alloc.cta_group::2 issued jointly with its pair peer (one paired allocation, two separate 256 KiB memories)
 +--------+----------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
 | warp 0 | MMA                  | tcgen05.alloc (both CTAs); pair LEADER only: per k-tile wait full[s], 4 x tcgen05.mma, commit   |
 |        | mma_role             | empty[s] (mask 0xF); per tile commit acc_full[st] (mask 0x3 << 2y); tails; dealloc handshake     |
 | warp 1 | Sched                | EVERY rank: prefetch tma_a/tma_b (one lane) in the prologue; rank 0 then: throttle wait/release, |
 |        | scheduler_role       | arm clc_full of CTAs 0..3 (lanes 0..3), clusterlaunchcontrol.try_cancel (one lane), consume;    |
 |        |                      | ranks 1-3 then fall through the dispatch and exit                                                |
 | warp 2 | MainloopLoad         | per k-tile wait empty[s]; leader lane arrive.expect_tx 49152 on full[s]; one lane issues TMA A   |
 |        | producer_role        | (multicast 0x5 << x) and TMA B; rank 0 also feeds the throttle; 8 tail waits                     |
 | warp 3 | EpilogueLoad         | prefetch tma_c/tma_d (one lane), init the 4 throttle barriers (one lane), then EXIT: the C       |
 |        | (no role function)   | producer is needed only for beta != 0                                                            |
 | warp 4 | Epilogue w = 0       | TMEM lanes [0, 32): rows 0..31 of the CTA's 128 x 128 tile; ALSO issues all TMA stores of D       |
 | warp 5 | Epilogue w = 1       | TMEM lanes [32, 64): rows 32..63                                                                  |
 | warp 6 | Epilogue w = 2       | TMEM lanes [64, 96): rows 64..95                                                                  |
 | warp 7 | Epilogue w = 3       | TMEM lanes [96, 128): rows 96..127                                                                |
 +--------+----------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
 named barriers: bar 6 (160 threads = warp 0 + warps 4-7): TMEM address handshake; bar 1 (128 threads = warps 4-7): epilogue subtile sync
```

The warp numbering is the CUTLASS kernel's `WarpCategory` enum (`MMA = 0, Sched = 1, MainloopLoad = 2, EpilogueLoad = 3, Epilogue = 4`; `sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:234-240` at `cb424739`), kept so that the explicit kernel's barrier initialization order and dispatch order match the baseline's (note 7.1). Why warp 4 issues the stores: `issue_tma_store = (w == 0u)` (explicit.cu:1018) mirrors the CUTLASS epilogue's choice of its first warp; all 32 lanes execute the store instruction with uniform operands, so no election is needed (note, Section 13 item 8; Chapter 10).

Two terms used in the table and everywhere below, defined here at first use. The **leader lane** is the `elect.sync`-elected lane of the *pair leader's* warp 2: `is_leader_lane = lane_pred != 0u && is_leader` is computed at the dispatch (explicit.cu:1192) and consumed at explicit.cu:736, the only place that executes `mbarrier.arrive.expect_tx` on a mainloop barrier. On a peer CTA no thread ever executes `arrive.expect_tx`, so the peer's eight `full[s]` barriers are initialized but never armed and never waited on; only the leader's `full[s]` carry traffic, and "count 1 + 49152 tx" always refers to the leader's barrier. **Transaction bytes** (`tx`, `expect_tx`): an `mbarrier` phase keeps two pending counts, arrivals (in threads) and transaction bytes; the phase completes only when both reach zero (PTX `mbarrier` semantics; quoted from the PTX ISA by the Colfax Blackwell cluster tutorial, "When both counts reach 0, the phase is completed"). `arrive.expect_tx(N)` performs one arrival and adds N to the expected byte count; the TMA unit (and the CLC response) subtract bytes as data lands. So the leader lane's single `arrive.expect_tx(49152)` plus 49152 bytes of landed boxes complete one `full[s]` phase. Chapter 2 explains the mechanism, Chapter 4 derives every count.

### 1.5.3 One cluster: 4 CTAs, ranks, pairs, multicast partners

```
 cluster (2,2,1): (x, y) = %cluster_ctaid, rank r = x + 2y (x = r & 1, y = r >> 1)
 cluster tile = 256 (M) x 256 (N) of D; CTA (x, y) owns the 128 x 128 CTA tile (tm, tn) with tm % 2 == x

                     x = 0 (M half 0)                       x = 1 (M half 1)
              +----------------------------------+----------------------------------+
   y = 0      | rank 0  PAIR LEADER              | rank 1  peer of rank 0           |   MMA pair {0, 1}: the leader's warp 0 issues
   (N half 0) | tile (tm, tn)                    | tile (tm + 1, tn)                |   tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2 over M 256 = both
              | rows [128 tm, +128)              | rows [128 tm + 128, +128)        |   CTAs' A stages, N 128 = both CTAs' B halves
              | cols [128 tn, +128)              | cols [128 tn, +128)              |   (columns [128 tn, +128))
              +----------------------------------+----------------------------------+
   y = 1      | rank 2  PAIR LEADER              | rank 3  peer of rank 2           |   MMA pair {2, 3}: same, for
   (N half 1) | tile (tm, tn + 1)                | tile (tm + 1, tn + 1)            |   columns [128 (tn + 1), +128)
              +----------------------------------+----------------------------------+

 A multicast partners (same x, hence same tm, hence the same 128 rows of A):   {0, 2} with mask 0x5 and {1, 3} with mask 0xA (= 0x5 << x)
   each CTA loads ITS OWN 64-row half of the 128 x 64 A stage (rows 128 tm + 64 y .. +64) and the TMA writes it at
   OFF_SMEM_A + 16384 s + 8192 y in BOTH partners, so after both halves land every CTA holds the whole 128 x 64 A stage.
 B is not multicast: each CTA loads its own 64 columns (128 tn + 64 x .. +64) into OFF_SMEM_B + 8192 s; the pair's 2SM MMA
   reads the leader's B half (columns 128 tn .. +64) and the peer's B half (128 tn + 64 .. +64) = the full N 128 of the MMA.
 Barriers that cross CTA boundaries: the leader's full[s] (credited by the peer's TMA bytes through the peer-bit mask), every
   CTA's empty[s] (both leaders' tcgen05.commit, mask 0xF), the leader's acc_empty[st] (256 epilogue threads of both CTAs),
   CTA 0's clc_empty[idx] (800 threads of all four CTAs), the pair's acc_full[st] (leader's commit, mask 0x3 << 2y), the
   tmem_dealloc handshake (leader <-> peer).
```

Three geometry facts that every later chapter relies on (derived from source; note 7.1, 7.4, B.4; verified by the K4a/K5c probe records, D.1 D8-D9):

1. **x selects the M half, y selects the N half, and the pair shares y.** A `tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2` computes a 256 (M) x 128 (N) tile: M 256 is the two CTAs of the pair stacked along M (rank 2y rows then rank 2y+1 rows), N 128 is their common 128 columns. So the two CTAs of a pair must differ in M and agree in N: that is `x` (M) varying, `y` (N) fixed. The leader's TMEM holds rows [0, 128) of the MMA tile and the peer's TMEM holds rows [128, 256); each CTA's epilogue stores its own 128 x 128 (the `LayoutC_TV` line of the Section 1 LAYOUT comment, explicit.cu:130-131).
2. **A is shared along y, B along x.** CTAs with the same `x` have the same `tm`, so they need the same A rows: A is multicast to ranks `x` and `x + 2` (mask `0x5 << x`). CTAs of a pair have the same `tn`, so the MMA needs both CTAs' B columns: the 2SM MMA reads the peer's B half directly through the descriptor, no multicast needed. This halves the A bytes a cluster pulls from L2 per k-tile: without multicast each of the 4 CTAs would fetch its whole 16384-byte A stage, 4 x 16384 = 65536 bytes of A per k-tile per cluster; with multicast each CTA fetches one 8192-byte box, 4 x 8192 = 32768 bytes; B is 4 x 8192 = 32768 bytes either way; so 65536 instead of 98304 bytes per k-tile per cluster (derived from source; Chapter 3 does the full bandwidth accounting).
3. **The launch coordinate is AlongN-transposed.** `grid = (64, 64, 1)` with `gridDim.x = N / 128` and `gridDim.y = M / 128` (definition `kGridX = kFixedN / kCtaTileN, kGridY = kFixedM / kCtaTileM` at util.hpp:32; the comment "x indexes N, y indexes M after the AlongN transpose" is util.hpp:28), yet inside the cluster `x` selects M. CUTLASS itself computes the grid as `ctas_m = round_up(ceil_div(8192, 256) * 2, 2) = 64` (the MMA tile M, then times the 2 CTAs of a pair, then rounded to the cluster) and `ctas_n = round_up(ceil_div(8192, 128), 2) = 64`, then applies the AlongN transpose `grid = ((ctas_n/2)*2, (ctas_m/2)*2, 1)` (note 7.4, Section 13 item 5); util.hpp's shortcut `N/128 x M/128` is correct only because 8192 divides both tile sizes. The reconciliation is the initial-tile formula (explicit.cu:1175-1176): `tm = 2 (blockIdx.y >> 1) + (blockIdx.x & 1)`, `tn = 2 (blockIdx.x >> 1) + (blockIdx.y & 1)`: the cluster index `(CX, CY) = (blockIdx.x >> 1, blockIdx.y >> 1)` walks N along grid x and M along grid y, while the intra-cluster bits are swapped. The same shape appears in the CLC mapping (explicit.cu:692-693): `tm = 2 (y0 >> 1) + (x0 & 1) + x`, `tn = 2 (x0 >> 1) + (y0 & 1) + y`, where `(x0, y0)` is the first-CTA id of the cancelled cluster (both even, so this reduces to `tm = y0 + x`, `tn = x0 + y`). Chapter 7 derives both from `swizzle_and_rasterize` and `possibly_transpose_work_tile`.

### 1.5.4 The data path

```
   global A (fp16, M x K, K-major)        global B (fp16, N x K, K-major)                    global D (fp32, M x N, M-major)
            |                                      |                                                     ^
            | TMA 2SM load, multicast 0x5 << x     | TMA 2SM load (no multicast)                         | TMA store (warp 4): 4 boxes of
            | box (64 k, 64 rows) = 8192 B         | box (64 k, 64 rows) = 8192 B                        | (32 m, 16 n) = 2048 B per subtile,
            | completes on the LEADER's full[s]    | completes on the LEADER's full[s]                   | commit_group, wait_group.read 1
            v                                      v                                                     |
   +------------------------------------------------------------------+     +----------------------------------------------------+
   | smem A ring  OFF_SMEM_A = 33792: 8 stages x 16384 B (128 x 64)   |     | smem C/D  OFF_SMEM_CD = 512: 4 stages x 8192 B      |
   | smem B ring  OFF_SMEM_B = 164864: 8 stages x  8192 B ( 64 x 64)  |     | (128 x 16 fp32), Swizzle<2,5,2>, stage = e % 4      |
   | both Swizzle<3,4,3> (SWIZZLE_128B), written by the TMA unit       |     | written by 16 st.shared.b32 per lane per subtile    |
   +------------------------------------------------------------------+     +----------------------------------------------------+
            |                                                                                            ^
            | tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2.kind::f16 (pair leader, one elected lane): descriptors name       | d = fmaf(beta, 0.0f, alpha * acc)
            | the A stage (both CTAs, 256 rows) and the B stage (both halves, 128 columns), K 16;        | (FMUL + FFMA per value, run-time
            | 4 per k-tile (kb = 0..3, +32 B each); first of a tile with scale_c = 0, then accumulate    |  alpha and beta), 16 values per lane
            v                                                                                            |
   +----------------------------------------------------+   tcgen05.ld.sync.aligned.32x32b.x16.b32   +------------------------------+
   | TMEM: 128 lanes (rows) x 512 columns, base T = 0   | -----------------------------------------> | registers: 16 x fp32 per lane |
   | accumulator stage st = columns [128 st, +128)      |   warp w reads lanes 32 w .. 32 w + 31,      | lane l of warp w holds row    |
   | = one 128 x 128 fp32 tile; 4 stages = 512 columns  |   columns 128 st + 16 e .. +15 (subtile e)   | 32 w + l, columns 16 e .. +15 |
   +----------------------------------------------------+                                              +------------------------------+
```

Why the path has this shape, in one sentence per hop (each is a chapter):

- **TMA -> smem** (Chapter 8): a single thread issues a bulk tensor copy described by a driver-encoded `CUtensorMap`; the hardware writes the 128-byte-swizzled tile and credits transaction bytes to an `mbarrier`, so 31 lanes and 7 other warps do nothing for the load.
- **smem -> UMMA -> TMEM** (Chapter 9): `tcgen05.mma` reads A and B from shared memory through 64-bit descriptors (start address, leading/stride byte offsets, swizzle mode) and accumulates into Tensor Memory, a per-SM 128 x 512 x 32-bit array that is not the register file, so the accumulator costs zero registers and the MMA warp's 32 lanes stay nearly idle while the tensor core works.
- **TMEM -> registers -> smem -> TMA -> global** (Chapter 10): the only way out of TMEM is `tcgen05.ld` into registers (one warp sees 32 lanes = 32 rows); the epilogue scales, writes a 128 x 16 column slab into a swizzled smem stage, and one warp hands the slab to the TMA store unit, which writes the M-major D tile; the `wait_group.read 1` lets one store still be reading smem while the next slab is being produced.

---

## 1.6 NUMBERS AT A GLANCE, line by line

The block (explicit.cu:52-70):

```
 * NUMBERS AT A GLANCE (fixed run; Section 0, D.7, and TRACE_H1/TRACE_ENCODE of trace_out_v2/host.txt)
 *   problem      M = N = K = 8192, fp16 A (M x K, K-major) and B (N x K, K-major), fp32 D (M x N, M-major), alpha = 1, beta = 0, L = 1
 *   cluster      (2,2,1): rank = x + 2y with x = %cluster_ctaid.x, y = %cluster_ctaid.y; the MMA pair is {2y, 2y+1} (same y);
 *                the even rank is the pair leader that issues the MMAs for both CTAs; CTAs x and x+2 share the A rows (multicast)
 *   grid         (64,64,1) CTAs; 32 x 32 = 1024 cluster tiles of 256 x 256 handed out dynamically by CLC to 33 resident clusters
 *   tile         CTA tile 128 (M) x 128 (N) x 64 (K) per k-tile; 128 k-tiles per tile; one tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2 covers
 *                M 256 (both CTAs' A) x N 128 (both CTAs' B halves) x K 16, so 4 MMAs per k-tile
 *   smem         230400 B dynamic, base 0x400 + (rank << 24) (measured, D.1); barriers 0..391, C/D 512 + 4 x 8192,
 *                A 33792 + 8 x 16384 (Swizzle<3,4,3>), B 164864 + 8 x 8192 (Swizzle<3,4,3>)
 *   TMA boxes    A and B: (64 k, 64 rows, 1) = 8192 B, SWIZZLE_128B; D: (32 m, 16 n, 1) = 2048 B, SWIZZLE_128B_ATOM_32B
 *   per stage    each CTA receives the whole 128 x 64 A stage (its own 64-row half + the other cluster row's half by multicast)
 *                and its own 64 x 64 B half; the pair leader's full[s] barrier expects 2 x (16384 + 8192) = 49152 bytes
 *   TMEM         512 columns allocated, base 0 (measured); accumulator stage st = columns [128 st, 128 st + 128) of 128 lanes (rows)
 *   descriptors  A 0x4000404000010880 + 1024 s + 2 kb, B 0x4000404000012880 + 512 s + 2 kb (low word in 16-byte units); idesc 0x10200010
 *   barriers     mainloop full 1 (+49152 tx) / empty 2; CLC full 1 (+16 tx) / empty 800; acc full 1 / empty 256; throttle 32 / 32; tmem_dealloc 32
 *   masks        A multicast 0x5 << x (ranks x, x+2); mainloop release 0xF (all four); accumulator commit 0x3 << 2y (the pair);
 *                the peer bit (bit 24) cleared on a shared::cluster address names the pair leader's barrier
 *   epilogue     8 subtiles of 128 x 16 per tile; tcgen05.ld.32x32b.x16 gives lane l the 16 columns 16e..16e+15 of TMEM row 32w + l;
 *                Swizzle<2,5,2> on the 8192-byte C/D stage; four (32, 16) TMA store boxes per subtile
```

**problem.** The GEMM is `D[m][n] = alpha * sum_k A[m][k] * B[n][k] + beta * C[m][n]` with K the contiguous dimension of both A and B ("K-major"), the "TN" case in CUTLASS's BLAS-style naming (T = row-major, N = column-major, so K-major A with K-major B is "TN"; media/docs/cpp/blackwell_functionality.md:70; line 15 lists TN, NT, TT and NN as all supported for `kind::f16`, and `include/cute/arch/mma_sm100_desc.hpp` gives canonical K-major (:701-705) and MN-major (:771-775) descriptor layouts for every swizzle mode, so nothing in the hardware is "designed for TN"). K-major is simply the layout the baseline uses; its payoff is that one 64-element k-tile row of A or B is exactly one 128-byte `SWIZZLE_128B` row (Chapter 3). D is M-major (column-major) so a TMA store box of 32 consecutive m values is 128 contiguous bytes. `L = 1` means no batch; the kernel passes the constant 0 as the third tensor coordinate everywhere (G.3, "Generality"). alpha and beta are run-time parameters by design (see **epilogue** below). Chapter 3 (shape), Chapter 5 (tensor maps).

**cluster.** `rank = x + 2y` is the column-major cluster layout the hardware uses for `%cluster_ctarank` (note 7.1). The pair is `{2y, 2y + 1}` because the 2SM MMA needs the two CTAs to stack along M and share N (Section 1.5.3 fact 1); the even rank leads by *convention*, not by hardware rule: the hardware defines the pair as the two CTAs whose `%cluster_ctarank` differ only in bit 0, i.e. {2i, 2i+1}, and lets one thread of *either* CTA issue the pair's `tcgen05.mma` as long as the other CTA stays active; CUTLASS always picks the even CTA (`is_mma_leader_cta = (rank % 2 == 0)`, note 7.1) and the explicit kernel keeps that choice because two other mechanisms do single out the even CTA: the peer-bit barrier addressing ("masks" below) and the `cta_group::2` TMA completion rule ("per stage" below). (Pair definition and "either CTA may issue" from secondary sources: the mlc.ai "Blackwell Tensor Core: tcgen05.mma" chapter, "That thread may belong to either CTA, but the peer CTA must remain active", and the Colfax Blackwell cluster tutorial, "in CUTLASS, we will always choose the even CTA as the leader"; the PTX ISA "CTA Pair" section could not be fetched here and is not quoted.) CTAs `x` and `x + 2` share `tm`, hence the A rows, hence the multicast. Chapter 2 (SM pairs and clusters on SM100), Chapter 4 (the pair's barriers).

**grid.** 4096 CTAs = 8192/128 x 8192/128; in cluster units 32 x 32 = 1024 cluster tiles of 256 x 256. "Handed out dynamically by CLC" means the grid is a *work list*, not a residency plan: only 33 clusters (**measured**, D.3) fit at once, and each resident cluster takes its launch tile first and then repeatedly cancels not-yet-launched clusters and takes their tiles: in the traced run 32 tiles for 13 clusters, 31 for 19 and 19 for the probe-slowed cluster (0,0) (**measured**, D.3); the untraced distribution is not measured. Why 33 and not 148/4 = 37 (inferred, note D.3): a TPC (texture processing cluster) is a pair of SMs (2j, 2j+1) in NVIDIA's SM hierarchy and a GPC (graphics processing cluster) is a group of TPCs; every MMA pair was observed on an SM pair (2j, 2j+1), i.e. one TPC, and both pairs of a cluster inside one SM-id group; so a 2 x 2 cluster needs two whole TPCs in one GPC, and the 8 leftover TPCs cannot be paired. The arithmetic: 148 SMs = 74 TPCs; 132 busy SMs = 66 TPCs = 33 clusters x 2 TPCs; 16 idle SMs = 8 TPCs. Chapter 3 (the occupancy consequence), Chapter 7 (CLC protocol), Chapter 11 (the launch).

**tile.** The CTA tile is 128 x 128 because the MMA tile is 256 x 128 split across the pair along M. K is consumed 64 at a time (one "k-tile" = one smem stage) because the harness fixes `MmaTileShape_MNK = Shape<_256,_128,_64>` (harness:123) and the builder uses that K verbatim (explicit.cu:132 quotes the resolved `TileShape (256, 128, 64)`); what makes the choice natural (my analysis) is that 64 fp16 = 128 bytes = exactly one `SWIZZLE_128B` row, so an A row of a stage is one swizzle-atom row; 8192 / 64 = 128 k-tiles per tile. Each `tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2.kind::f16` has K = 16 (the fp16 instruction K), so a 64-wide k-tile is 4 MMAs with descriptor start addresses 32 bytes apart (16 fp16). Chapter 3 (why 256 x 128 x 64 is the speed-of-light choice), Chapter 9 (the 4 MMAs).

**smem.** 230400 bytes is the CUTLASS `SharedStorageSize`: 512 bytes of control (barriers, CLC responses, TMEM pointer, padding to 512), 4 x 8192 + 512 pad = 33280 of epilogue stages, 8 x 16384 of A stages at 33792, 8 x 8192 of B stages at 164864 (note 6.2; `static_assert`s at explicit.cu:158-160). Why 8 stages: the builder takes the largest count that fits the 232448-byte opt-in limit after two carveouts, `floor((232448 - 192 - 33792) / 24592) = floor(198464 / 24592) = 8` (note 6.1; `sm100_compute_stage_count_or_override`, `include/cutlass/gemm/collective/builders/sm100_umma_builder.inl:84`, fed by `KernelSmemCarveout` at :288-294). The three constants, so that you can reproduce the division: 24592 = 16384 (one A stage) + 8192 (one B stage) + 16 (one 8-byte `full` and one 8-byte `empty` barrier per stage, `sizeof(PipelineTmaUmmaAsync<1>::SharedStorage)`); 192 = the builder's *estimate* of the kernel-level control storage (accumulator pipeline 64 + CLC pipeline 32 + load-order barrier 16 + tmem_dealloc barrier 8 + throttle pipeline 32 + 2 x 16 CLC responses + 2 x 4 TMEM pointers; the real struct has one 4-byte `tmem_base_ptr`); 33792 = the epilogue `SharedStorage` (33280 of tensor stages + 64 of load-pipeline barriers = 33344, rounded up to its 512-byte alignment). The bound: 8 x 24592 = 196736 <= 198464 < 9 x 24592 = 221328. The base `0x400 + (rank << 24)` is **measured** (D.1 D5): the low kilobyte is the system-reserved shared memory that `cuobjdump` reports as `SHARED:1024` for every kernel, and the cluster rank is inserted as address byte 3, bits [24, 32) (the `mapa` lowering is a `PRMT ..., 0x654` byte-3 insert, D.2), of which only bits 24-25 can be nonzero for a 4-CTA cluster (measured bases `0x00000400`, `0x01000400`, `0x02000400`, `0x03000400`; note 6.2 therefore writes "rank in bits [24,26)"; how wide the field is for larger clusters is not established by the note, whose D5 prediction was [24,28)). Bit 24 being rank bit 0 is what makes the peer-bit trick ("masks" below) possible. What the base requires of the kernel: `__launch_bounds__(256, 1)`, `extern __shared__ char smem[]` without an alignment attribute, and zero static `__shared__` anywhere in the translation unit (explicit.cu:1085-1086, 1095-1097; note 6.2, D.7): any static shared variable, for example one added by trace code, would move the dynamic base and break the 1024-byte alignment the `Swizzle<3,4,3>` A/B stages and the 512-byte alignment the `Swizzle<2,5,2>` C/D stages need (`static_assert`s at explicit.cu:162-163). "barriers 0..391" in the banner is the *used* part of the control block: 43 x 8 = 344 bytes of barrier slots (0..343), 8 bytes of padding (344..351; `PipelineStorage` is an `aligned_struct<16>`), two 16-byte CLC responses (352..383), the 4-byte `tmem_base_ptr` at 384 rounded up to the next 8-byte slot (392); bytes 392..511 are padding so that `OFF_SMEM_CD = 512` meets its 512-byte alignment. The control block proper is 0..511 (fact 10 below). Of the 43 slots, 10 are never initialized: `epi_load full[4]` at 128, `epi_load empty[4]` at 160 and `load_order[2]` at 192 belong to the beta != 0 path (explicit.cu:141-143; note E.10 item 6: the CUTLASS kernel initializes all 43, the explicit kernel 33). Two more barrier subtleties to carry forward: the `clc_empty` barriers of ranks 1-3 are initialized but never used (every consumer arrives on CTA 0's), and the `clc_full` barriers of CTAs 1-3 are completed entirely by remote actions, rank 0's `arrive.expect_tx` plus the multicast response bytes (note 7.4). Chapter 5 (map and alignments), Chapter 3 (budget), Chapter 4 (barriers).

**TMA boxes.** A and B boxes are (64 k, 64 rows, 1) fp16 = 64 x 64 x 2 = 8192 bytes: the k extent is one 128-byte swizzle row, and the row extent 64 is one CTA's half of the 128-row A stage (and the whole of the 64-column B stage), so every load instruction moves exactly one 8192-byte box and the leader's transaction count is a multiple of 8192. The D box is (32 m, 16 n, 1) fp32 = 32 x 16 x 4 = 2048 bytes: 32 fp32 along m are 128 contiguous bytes of the M-major D (one `SWIZZLE_128B_ATOM_32B` row), 16 n is the epilogue subtile width, so a 128 x 16 subtile is four boxes. Chapter 5 (encodes), Chapter 8 (loads), Chapter 10 (stores).

**per stage.** Each CTA's A stage is filled by two 8192-byte multicast boxes (its own half at `+8192 y` and its partner's half at the other offset); its B stage by one 8192-byte box. The leader's `full[s]` counts the bytes of *both* CTAs of the pair because every 2SM load (`cp.async.bulk.tensor...cta_group::2`) completes on the leader's barrier through the peer-bit-masked address: 2 CTAs x (2 x 8192 A + 8192 B) = 6 boxes x 8192 = 49152 = `kMainloopTxBytes` (explicit.cu:180). How a multicast A box issued by, say, rank 3 (mask 0xA, destinations ranks 1 and 3) can credit rank 0's and rank 2's barriers: for `.multicast::cluster` the data and the `complete_tx` signal are delivered at the same CTA-relative smem offset in every destination CTA, and for `.cta_group::2` the mbarrier operand selects the even or the odd CTA of each destination's pair, so the masked operand `(smem_base + OFF_MAIN_FULL + 8 s) & 0xFEFFFFFF` means "the even CTA's `full[s]`" in each destination pair: the box landing in rank 1 credits rank 0's barrier and the box landing in rank 3 credits rank 2's (the PTX ISA `cp.async.bulk.tensor` rule, "the mbarrier signal is multicast either to all the odd-numbered CTAs or even-numbered CTAs for each possible CTA-Pair within a cluster" and "the source data is multicast to the same offset as dstMem in the shared memory of each destination CTA", reached here only through a search-engine excerpt of the ISA page, not the page itself: (unverified) as a quotation, consistent with note B.6 and the K4a records of D.1 D8). Chapter 8 derives which barrier each of the six boxes completes on. The MMA warp of the leader therefore waits on one barrier for the whole 256 x 64 A and 128 x 64 B operand set of its 4 MMAs. Chapter 4 (why one barrier per pair), Chapter 8 (who issues what).

**TMEM.** `tcgen05.alloc.cta_group::2` with 512 columns allocates the same 512-column range in *each* SM's own Tensor Memory: one paired allocation, two separate memories (`Sm100TmemCapacityColumns = 512`, `include/cute/arch/tmem_allocator_sm100.hpp:120`; "Both CTAs _must_ provide the exact same dst_ptr", :128; TMEM is 128 lanes x 512 columns x 32 bits = 256 KiB per SM, Colfax TMEM tutorial, consistent with note 6.3). Nothing crosses the SM boundary: the leader's TMEM holds its 128 accumulator rows and the peer's TMEM holds the other 128, which is why each CTA runs its own epilogue over its own 128 rows (note 6.3, B.6; Section 1.5.3 fact 1). The base was 0 in every CTA (**measured**, D.1 D6) but is read from the allocation result, never assumed (explicit.cu:888). The accumulator pipeline has 4 stages of 128 columns: a 128 x 128 fp32 CTA tile is 128 lanes x 128 columns, and 4 x 128 = 512 uses every column. Why 4: it is the `AccumulatorPipelineStageCount` of the mainloop dispatch policy, the third parameter of `MainloopSm100TmaUmmaWarpSpecialized<8,2,4,(2,2,1),Sm100>` (`include/cutlass/gemm/dispatch_policy.hpp:1021-1035`, `int AccumulatorPipelineStageCount_,` at :1025; note D.1 D1), and it lets the MMA warp run several tiles ahead of the epilogue (Chapter 3 derives the choice, Chapter 4 quantifies the slack). A TMEM address is `(lane << 16) | column` (Chapter 2, Chapter 10).

**descriptors.** The 64-bit UMMA shared-memory descriptor is `{hi = 0x40004040, lo}`: `hi` encodes SBO = 64 x 16 B = 1024 B (one 8-row swizzle atom), version 1, layout type 2 = `SWIZZLE_128B`; `lo` encodes LBO = 1 (16 B, the value CUTLASS writes for this layout; Chapter 9 explains LBO and SBO) in bits [16, 30) and `(start_address >> 4) & 0x3FFF` in bits [0, 14). For the measured base: `(0x400 + 33792) >> 4 = 0x880` and `(0x400 + 164864) >> 4 = 0x2880`, giving `lo_a = 0x10880` and `lo_b = 0x12880` (explicit.cu:171-177). Per stage the start address grows by 16384 B (A) = 1024 units of 16 B, or 8192 B (B) = 512 units; per k-block by 32 B = 2 units. `idesc = 0x10200010` is the instruction descriptor: bit 4 c_format F32 (0x10), bits [17, 23) N/8 = 16 (0x200000), bits [24, 29) M/16 = 16 (0x10000000), and 0x10 + 0x200000 + 0x10000000 = 0x10200010 (explicit.cu:173-176). Every other field is zero for a reason you can check in the bit map (`InstrDescriptor`, `include/cute/arch/mma_sm100_desc.hpp:416-443`): a_format and b_format are F16, whose encoding is 0 (bits [7, 10) and [10, 13)); a_major and b_major are K-major, encoding 0 (bits 15 and 16); no negate (bits 13, 14), dense (bit 2), no saturate (bit 3), no sparse id (bits [0, 2)), no shift (bits [30, 32)). Chapter 9 (bit by bit), Chapter 5 (the constants).

**barriers.** Mainloop `full[s]`: count 1 (the leader lane's `arrive.expect_tx`) plus 49152 transaction bytes; `empty[s]`: count 2 because both pair leaders `tcgen05.commit` with mask 0xF, so each CTA's `empty[s]` receives exactly two arrivals per stage use (one from each pair of the cluster; `cluster_m / atom_m + cluster_n / atom_n - 1 = 2/2 + 2/1 - 1 = 2`, explicit.cu:182). CLC `full[idx]`: count 1 (rank 0's lane arms it remotely) plus 16 bytes (the response); `empty[idx]`: 800 = 32 (rank-0 warp 1) + 4 CTAs x (32 warp 0 + 32 warp 2 + 128 epilogue threads), every consuming thread arriving remotely on CTA 0's barrier (explicit.cu:181, 183). Accumulator `full[st]`: 1 (the leader's commit); `empty[st]`: 256 = 2 CTAs x 128 epilogue threads arriving on the leader's barrier (explicit.cu:184). Throttle 32/32: rank 0's producer warp arrives with all 32 lanes, the scheduler warp releases with all 32 lanes (explicit.cu:185). `tmem_dealloc` 32: the whole peer warp 0 arrives (explicit.cu:185). Chapter 4 derives each count from "who arrives".

**masks.** The A multicast mask has bit i set for destination rank i: `0x5 = 0b0101` reaches ranks 0 and 2, `0xA = 0b1010` reaches ranks 1 and 3; `0x5 << x` picks the pair of CTAs with this CTA's `x` (explicit.cu:772). The mainloop release mask 0xF makes one `tcgen05.commit` arrive on all four CTAs' `empty[s]`, needed because all four CTAs' A halves (multicast) and both CTAs' B halves were consumed by the pair's MMA. The accumulator commit mask `0x3 << 2y` (0x3 for pair {0, 1}, 0xC for pair {2, 3}) arrives on both CTAs' `acc_full[st]` because both epilogues read their halves of the same MMA result (explicit.cu:902). The peer bit: a `shared::cluster` address carries the rank in address byte 3, of which only bits 24-25 are nonzero for this 4-CTA cluster ("smem" above); clearing bit 24 (`& 0xFEFFFFFF`, explicit.cu:187; `cute::Sm100MmaPeerBitMask`, `include/cute/arch/copy_sm100_tma.hpp:45`) turns "my barrier" into "my pair leader's barrier" without a `mapa`. nvcc folds known-zero alignment bits into the constant, and what it emits depends on the site: in the explicit kernel's SASS the literal `0xfefffff8` appears exactly once, at the epilogue's accumulator release (`mbar_arrive_cluster_masked`), while for the producer's hoisted 1024-byte-aligned barrier base the mask was folded as `& 0xfefffff0` (equivalent for s <= 7), so the CUTLASS kernel's per-k-tile `ULOP3 ..., 0xfefffff8` has no counterpart (**measured**, G.3); the CUTLASS kernel's own PTX/SASS show `0xFEFFFFF8` everywhere (note 7.2, D.2, D.6 item 2). Chapter 4, Chapter 6 (W11, W21).

**epilogue.** 128 columns / 16 = 8 subtiles per tile, chosen so that one `tcgen05.ld.32x32b.x16` (32 lanes x 16 columns x 32 bits) per warp per subtile yields exactly one 128 x 16 slab across the four warps, and so that the slab is 8192 bytes = one epilogue smem stage. Lane l of warp w gets row 32w + l (its TMEM lane) and columns 16e..16e + 15 of stage st. `Swizzle<2,5,2>` on byte offsets (bits [5, 7) ^= bits [7, 9)) is what the `SWIZZLE_128B_ATOM_32B` TMA store expects in smem; the epilogue computes it by hand (explicit.cu:1013, cross-checked against `cute::Swizzle<2,5,2>` at compile time at explicit.cu:198-201). Four (32, 16) store boxes cover the 128 rows. The arithmetic form `t = alpha * acc; d = fmaf(beta, 0.0f, t)` with run-time alpha and beta is kept deliberately: with compile-time `1.0f`/`0.0f` the compiler would fold `1.0f * acc` to `acc` (an exact IEEE identity) and `fmaf(0.0f, 0.0f, t)` to a single `+0.0f + t` (one FADD), removing the per-element FMUL + FFMA pair that the CUTLASS kernel executes and that the equivalence contract requires (note Section 0, D.7). Be precise about what the fold would change: only the instruction stream, not the values. `fmaf(+0.0f, 0.0f, t)` computed at run time is `(+0.0 * 0.0) + t = +0.0 + t`, exactly what the folded form computes, so both turn a `-0.0` product into `+0.0` and agree bit for bit; that is also why the compiler cannot fold `+0.0f + t` further to `t` (`+0.0 + (-0.0) = +0.0`). The one numerical consequence of the epilogue's form is therefore this: with beta = 0 the FFMA computes `0 * 0 + t`, so a `-0.0` product becomes `+0.0` (note Section 8); only dropping the add altogether (`alpha * acc` alone) would change the sign of zero relative to the CUTLASS result (note D.7: "never `alpha * acc` alone (sign of zero), never a separate add"). Chapter 10.

---

## 1.7 How to use this lecture

### 1.7.1 Three passes

- **Top-down (Chapters 2-4).** Chapter 2 is the machine: what an SM100 SM pair, TMEM, `tcgen05`, TMA multicast, `mbarrier` transaction counting and CLC are, as a GEMM writer needs them. Chapter 3 is the design: from 8192^3 to the 256 x 128 x 16 MMA, the 8/4/2 stage counts, the 230400-byte budget, and the speed-of-light bound the measured 0.889 ms is compared against. Chapter 4 is the protocol: every barrier, its count, its parity sequence, and the per-tile timeline of the five roles. After these three chapters you should be able to draw Section 1.5.3 and Section 1.5.4 from memory and say why each arrow exists.
- **Bottom-up (Chapters 5-11).** The 12 sections of the file in order: constants and tensor maps (5), the 37 wrappers character by character (6), the pipeline helpers, `clc_consume` and the scheduler warp (7), the producer (8), the MMA warp (9), the epilogue (10), the kernel prologue and the host mirror (11). Every line of `explicit.cu` is quoted and explained somewhere in these chapters.
- **Mastery (Chapters 12-14).** What ptxas made of it and what was measured (12), how to write it yourself in a construction order that keeps the kernel debuggable at every step, the pitfalls, and a speed-of-light recipe for other operators (13), exercises, glossary and references (14).

### 1.7.2 Prerequisites

You need to be fluent in CUDA C++ (grids, blocks, warps, shared memory, `__shfl_sync`, inline `asm volatile` with constraints `"r"`, `"l"`, `"h"`, `"n"`), and to know what a GEMM tile loop is. You do **not** need prior Blackwell knowledge: TMEM, `tcgen05`, 2SM MMA, TMA multicast and CLC are introduced in Chapter 2 and used concretely afterwards. Hopper-era concepts (TMA, `mbarrier`, warp specialization, clusters, `elect.sync`) make Chapters 2 and 4 faster but are also covered.

Authoritative references you will want open. The CUTLASS sources, the local CUTLASS documentation and the note were opened and verified line by line while writing this chapter; the PTX ISA is a single very large page that could not be fetched in full here (only its table of contents came back), so every ISA-level statement in this chapter is labelled as consistent with the CUTLASS source, note B.6 and the secondary write-ups listed below rather than quoted from the ISA text. Where this chapter paraphrases ISA wording it says so and marks it (unverified); Chapter 2 and Chapter 6 are the places to replace those paraphrases with the ISA's own sentences once the sections named below are opened.

- The PTX ISA (version 9.4 at the time of writing): <https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/index.html>. The sections to open for the (unverified) items of this chapter: "CTA Pair" (9.7.18.5.1: the pair definition and which CTA may issue `cta_group::2` instructions), `tcgen05.alloc` (both CTAs of the pair execute it with the same column count), `cp.async.bulk.tensor` (the `.cta_group::2` mbarrier operand rule and the `.multicast::cluster` ctaMask), `mbarrier.try_wait` (phaseParity refers to the current or the immediately preceding phase) and `clusterlaunchcontrol.try_cancel` (16-byte response, `.multicast::cluster::all`). The chapters to bookmark: "TensorCore 5th Generation Family Instructions" (`tcgen05.alloc/dealloc/relinquish_alloc_permit`, `tcgen05.mma`, `tcgen05.commit`, `tcgen05.ld`, `tcgen05.wait::ld`, and the "Tensor Memory" description), "Data Movement and Conversion Instructions: Tensor copy" (`cp.async.bulk.tensor`, `prefetch.tensormap`), "Parallel Synchronization and Communication Instructions: mbarrier", "clusterlaunchcontrol.try_cancel" and "clusterlaunchcontrol.query_cancel", "griddepcontrol", "elect.sync", and "mapa".

### 1.7.3 Notation (used in every chapter, exactly as written here)

| Symbol | Meaning | Range / definition |
|---|---|---|
| `(x, y)` | `%cluster_ctaid.x`, `%cluster_ctaid.y` | x, y in {0, 1} |
| `r` | cluster rank `%cluster_ctarank` | `r = x + 2y`, 0..3 |
| pair leader / peer | even rank / `r ^ 1` | pair `{2y, 2y + 1}` |
| CTA 0 | rank 0 | the only CTA with a scheduler warp; owner of the used `clc_empty` barriers |
| `(tm, tn)` | tile coordinates in 128 x 128 CTA-tile units | 0..63 each; `tm % 2 == x` for every tile a CTA receives |
| `q` | k-tile index inside a tile | 0..127 |
| `s` | smem stage of the A/B ring | 0..7 |
| `kb` | k-block inside a k-tile (one MMA) | 0..3 |
| `st` | accumulator (TMEM) stage | 0..3 |
| `e` | epilogue subtile | 0..7 |
| `i` | TMA store box inside a subtile | 0..3 |
| `j` | value / column index inside a subtile | 0..15 |
| `w` | epilogue warp `warp_idx - 4` | 0..3 |
| `l` | lane | 0..31 |
| `smem_base` | 32-bit `shared::cta` address of the dynamic smem | `0x400 + (r << 24)` measured, computed at run time |
| `OFF_*` | byte offsets from `smem_base` | exactly as named in explicit.cu:139-155 |
| `T` | TMEM base address returned by `tcgen05.alloc` | measured 0, never assumed |
| `T` (tile count) | in the tail-parity discussions of Chapters 4, 7, 12, 13 and 14, `T` also denotes the number of tiles a cluster processed, because the note's own tail formulas `((T + i) % S, 1 ^ (((T + i) / S) & 1))` are quoted there; Chapter 8 writes `n_tiles` for the same quantity; the context always makes the meaning clear | 32, 31 or 19 in the traced run |
| `full[s]`, `empty[s]` | mainloop barriers at `OFF_MAIN_FULL + 8s`, `OFF_MAIN_EMPTY + 8s` | |
| `acc_full[st]`, `acc_empty[st]` | accumulator barriers | `OFF_ACC_FULL + 8st`, `OFF_ACC_EMPTY + 8st` |
| `clc_full[idx]`, `clc_empty[idx]` | CLC barriers | `OFF_CLC_FULL + 8idx`, `OFF_CLC_EMPTY + 8idx` |
| `{index, phase}` | a pipeline state | producers start `{0, 1}`, consumers `{0, 0}` |
| leader lane | the `elect.sync`-elected lane of the pair leader's warp 2 | `lane_pred != 0u && is_leader` (explicit.cu:1192); the only thread that arms `full[s]` |
| tx, `expect_tx` | transaction bytes pending on an mbarrier phase | the phase completes when arrivals *and* bytes both reach zero; TMA and the CLC response subtract bytes (Section 1.5.2) |

Two address-space words you must keep apart (explicit.cu:21-22): an **asm operand** that names shared memory is always the 32-bit `shared::cta` integer `smem_base + OFF_*` (what `mbarrier.*`, `cp.async.bulk.tensor`, `tcgen05.*`, `mapa` and `ld.shared` take); a **C++ dereference** of shared memory is always through the generic pointer `smem + OFF_*` (used in exactly three places: reading `tmem_base_ptr` at explicit.cu:888 and 998, and the epilogue's 16 stores at explicit.cu:1047).
