## 4.6 The dataflow graph

Legend: `r0..r3` are ranks (`r = x + 2y`); `W0`, `W1`, `W2`, `W4-7` are warps; `->` is an arrival or a byte completion; `[barrier]@rK` is a barrier in CTA K's shared memory. The four CTAs run the same code; the arrows differ only through `x`, `y`, `is_leader`, `is_cta0`.

```
 MAINLOOP SMEM RING (per stage s; repeated 128 times per tile)
 ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   r0.W2  A box (mcast 0x5: r0,r2)  ---------+--------------------------------+
   r2.W2  A box (mcast 0x5: r0,r2)  ---------+---> complete_tx 8192 x2 into   |---> complete_tx 8192 x2 into
   r0.W2  B box (r0 only)           -------------> [full[s]]@r0 (masked addr) |     [full[s]]@r2 (masked addr)
                                                    + r0.W2 leader lane: arrive.expect_tx 49152 (count 1)
   r1.W2  A box (mcast 0xA: r1,r3)  ---------+---> copy landing in r1: complete_tx 8192 into [full[s]]@r0   (r1 is r0's peer: bit 24 cleared)
                                             +---> copy landing in r3: complete_tx 8192 into [full[s]]@r2   (r3 is r2's peer)
   r3.W2  A box (mcast 0xA: r1,r3)  ---------+---> copy landing in r1: complete_tx 8192 into [full[s]]@r0
                                             +---> copy landing in r3: complete_tx 8192 into [full[s]]@r2
   r1.W2  B box (r1 only)           -------------> complete_tx 8192 into [full[s]]@r0
   r2.W2  B box, r3.W2 B box        -------------> complete_tx 8192 each into [full[s]]@r2
                                                    + r2.W2 leader lane: arrive.expect_tx 49152

   r0.W0  waits [full[s]]@r0 -> 4 x tcgen05.mma (reads r0+r1 smem) -> tcgen05.commit mask 0xF ---> [empty[s]]@r0,r1,r2,r3 (1 arrival each)
   r2.W0  waits [full[s]]@r2 -> 4 x tcgen05.mma (reads r2+r3 smem) -> tcgen05.commit mask 0xF ---> [empty[s]]@r0,r1,r2,r3 (1 arrival each)
   rK.W2  waits [empty[s]]@rK (count 2 = one commit from each leader) before reusing stage s

 ACCUMULATOR RING (per tile t, stage st = t % 4)
 ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   r0.W0  waits [acc_empty[st]]@r0 (count 256) ... after k-tile 127: tcgen05.commit mask 0x3 ---> [acc_full[st]]@r0, @r1
   r2.W0  waits [acc_empty[st]]@r2 (count 256) ... after k-tile 127: tcgen05.commit mask 0xC ---> [acc_full[st]]@r2, @r3
   r0.W4-7 wait [acc_full[st]]@r0 -> 8 x tcgen05.ld -> wait::ld -> 128 x arrive (masked) ---> [acc_empty[st]]@r0
   r1.W4-7 wait [acc_full[st]]@r1 -> 8 x tcgen05.ld -> wait::ld -> 128 x arrive (masked) ---> [acc_empty[st]]@r0   (bit 24 cleared)
   r2.W4-7 / r3.W4-7: the same into [acc_empty[st]]@r2

 CLC RING (per tile t, slot i = t % 2)                       THROTTLE RING (rank 0 only)
 ------------------------------------------------------------  --------------------------------------------
   r0.W2 (start of tile t): wait [thr_empty[i]]@r0 -> 32 x arrive (local) ---> [thr_full[i]]@r0
   r0.W1: wait [thr_full[i]]@r0 -> 32 x arrive (mapa 0) ---> [thr_empty[i]]@r0
   r0.W1: wait [clc_empty[i]]@r0 (count 800)
   r0.W1 lanes 0..3: arrive.expect_tx 16 (mapa lane) ---> [clc_full[i]]@r0, @r1, @r2, @r3 (count 1 each)
   r0.W1 elected lane: try_cancel ... multicast::cluster::all ---> response bytes into slot i of r0..r3, complete_tx 16 on each [clc_full[i]]@rK
   rK.W0, rK.W2, rK.W4-7 (all K) and r0.W1: wait own [clc_full[i]]@rK -> decode -> fence.proxy.async -> arrive (mapa 0) ---> [clc_empty[i]]@r0
                                                                                          32 + 4 x (32 + 32 + 128) = 800 arrivals

 EXIT HANDSHAKE (once)
 ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
   r1.W0: 32 x arrive (mapa peer) ---> [tmem_dealloc]@r0 ; r0.W0 waits parity 0 ; r0.W0: 32 x arrive (mapa peer) ---> [tmem_dealloc]@r1 ; r1.W0 waits parity 0
   r3.W0 / r2.W0: the same
```

Byte ledger per stage (every box is 8192 B; "via peer bit" means the copy landed in the odd CTA and the masked operand named the even CTA's barrier):

```
 [full[s]]@r0 = A(r0, landed in r0) + A(r2, landed in r0) + A(r1, landed in r1, via peer bit) + A(r3, landed in r1, via peer bit) + B(r0) + B(r1, via peer bit) = 6 x 8192 = 49152
 [full[s]]@r2 = A(r0, landed in r2) + A(r2, landed in r2) + A(r1, landed in r3, via peer bit) + A(r3, landed in r3, via peer bit) + B(r2) + B(r3, via peer bit) = 6 x 8192 = 49152
 [full[s]]@r1 = [full[s]]@r3 = 0 (initialised, never arrived on, never waited)
```

Three address mechanisms appear, and it pays to keep them apart:

| Mechanism | Instruction operand | Who computes the target | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Peer bit (`& 0xFEFFFFFF`) | a `shared::cluster` address that is the local `shared::cta` address with bit 24 cleared | the issuing thread, arithmetically | TMA load barrier operand (`full_masked_base`, :770); accumulator release (W11, :370-379) |
| Multicast mask (16-bit) | `tcgen05.commit ... multicast::cluster [addr], mask`; `cp.async.bulk.tensor ... multicast::cluster ..., mask` | the hardware delivers to the same offset in every masked CTA | mainloop release `0xF`; accumulator commit `0x3 << 2y`; A load `0x5 << x` |
| `mapa` | `mapa.shared::cluster.u32 rem, addr, cta_id` | the hardware maps a local address to CTA `cta_id`'s copy | CLC release and throttle release (`cta_id = 0`); CLC arming (`cta_id = lane`); dealloc handshake (`cta_id = peer`) |

Why three and not one? The peer bit is free (one `LOP3`) but can only name the even CTA of a pair; `mapa` names any CTA but costs an instruction per target and produces one arrival; a multicast mask reaches several CTAs with one instruction but only at the same offset. The kernel uses the cheapest mechanism that fits each case. nvcc folds the peer mask: the literal `0xFEFFFFF8` (explicit.cu:187 comment) survives in the explicit kernel's SASS only at the epilogue's accumulator release (`0x44c0`), while in the producer the mask was folded onto the hoisted 1024-byte-aligned `smem_base` as `& 0xFEFFFFF0` (`0x0c00`) with `8 s` added afterwards by `ULEA` (note G.3; the baseline applies `0xfefffff8` per k-tile, note D.2). All three masks equal `0xFEFFFFFF` on every barrier address of this kernel because the low bits they clear are known to be zero: the barriers are 8-byte aligned, `smem_base = 0x400 + (r << 24)` has bits 0..9 zero, and `8 s <= 56` fits in the four low bits the producer's fold leaves.

## 4.7 The per-tile timeline

### 4.7.1 The Gantt chart

Durations are to scale only roughly. "Measured" numbers are from the note (D.3, G.2); derived figures are marked. One tile of the fixed run takes about 0.889 ms / 32 tiles = 27.8 us per cluster (derived from the measured `Avg runtime` 0.889354 ms and the measured 32/31 tiles per cluster), i.e. about 217 ns per k-tile; the CLC query-to-consume latency is 1408 ns median and the scheduler's throttle wait 28.8-37.7 us per tile (both measured in the CUTLASS kernel's trace build, note D.3, where an unprobed tile took 31.90 us); the explicit kernel's own trace build measured 1024 ns median and 35.46 us per tile, the latter inflated by its extra wait diagnostics, and note G.2 marks both as irrelevant to the toggle-off binary. Where this chapter says "~1.4 us" for the CLC round trip it uses the CUTLASS trace figure.

```
 time ->        tile t (128 k-tiles, ~27.8 us)                                                 | tile t+1
 ============================================================================================|==========================
 W2 (loads)     [thr]|L0 L1 .. L7|L8 ..... Lq issued when empty[q%8] flips (<= 8 ahead) ..... L127|[CLC t]|[thr]|L0 L1 .. L7|L8 ...
                 ^rank 0 only           ^ L8 waits for the commit of k-tile 0                     ^ consume AFTER issuing tile t's loads
                                                                                             tile t+1's first 8 loads start ~8 k-tiles
                                                                                             before W0 finishes tile t
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 W0 (MMA issue) [CLC t]|[acc_empty t%4]|F0 MMMM C|F1 MMMM C| ... |F127 MMMM C|[acc_full commit]|[CLC t+1]|[acc_empty]|F0 MMMM C| ...
                 ^ consume BEFORE computing tile t          ^ Fq = wait full[q%8]; MMMM = 4 x tcgen05.mma; C = commit mask 0xF
 tensor core          ......|MMA q=0 |MMA q=1 | ... (executes behind the issue; the commit of q fires when q's 4 MMAs are done)
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 W1 (sched,     [thr_full t ... wait until rank 0's W2 starts tile t]|[rel]|[clc_empty t%2]|[arm x4]|[QUERY t]|[CLC t consume]|[thr_full t+1 .....
  rank 0 only)                                                                              ^ ~1.4 us later the response lands in all 4 CTAs
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 W4-7 (epilogue)[CLC t]|[acc_full t%4 ...... waits the whole mainloop of tile t ......................]|e0 e1 e2 e3 e4 e5 e6 e7|[CLC t+1]|[acc_full ...
                 ^ consume BEFORE storing tile t                                                       ^ epilogue of tile t runs during the
                                                                                                         mainloop of tile t+1 (TMEM stage ring)
                                                                                           e7: tcgen05.ld, wait::ld, arrive acc_empty, then math+stores
 TMA store unit                                                                                        |g0|g1|g2|g3|g4|g5|g6|g7|   (bulk groups, read 1 behind)
```

How to read it:

1. **Loads run ahead.** Warp 2 issues k-tile q as soon as `empty[q % 8]` flips, i.e. as soon as both leaders have committed k-tile q - 8. In steady state the loads are up to 8 stages (about 1.7 us, derived) ahead of the MMA issue. At the tile boundary nothing special happens in the smem ring: k-tile 0 of tile t + 1 takes the stage after k-tile 127 of tile t, and its loads are issued while warp 0 is still on k-tiles 120..127 of tile t.
2. **The MMA warp never waits for the epilogue in steady state.** Its only dependency on the epilogue is `acc_empty[t % 4]`, released by the epilogue of tile t - 4. With 4 TMEM stages the epilogue may lag up to three tiles before the MMA warp stalls; measured skew is far smaller (see 4 below).
3. **The epilogue of tile t overlaps the mainloop of tile t + 1.** The epilogue waits `acc_full[t % 4]` for essentially the whole mainloop of tile t, then runs its eight subtiles while the MMA warp is already issuing tile t + 1 into TMEM stage `(t + 1) % 4`. This is what the TMEM ring buys: the tensor core is not idle during the epilogue. (The epilogue's duration was not measured in the note; my estimate is a few microseconds, well under a mainloop.)
4. **CLC positions.** The scheduler issues query t as soon as rank 0's loader has started tile t (throttle), which is about 8 k-tiles before the MMA warp finishes tile t - 1, and consumes response t about 1.4 us later. Warp 0 and warps 4-7 consume response t at the *start* of tile t; warp 2 consumes it *after* issuing tile t's 256 loads. Measured in the CUTLASS kernel's trace (note Section 7.6, cluster (0,0); note D.3): warp 0's first consume preceded its first `tcgen05.mma` by 1248 ns (the first TMA box had to land), and rank 0's warp 0 consumed each response 96 ns (median) after the scheduler did, which I read as "the MMA warp is usually already at its CLC wait when the response lands". That is a bubble in the *issue* stream, not necessarily in the tensor core, which executes the queued MMAs of the previous k-tiles asynchronously (my analysis).

### 4.7.2 Where each role consumes, and why the fetched tile becomes current only at the end

| Role | Consume position in the loop body | Line | Why there (derived from source + my analysis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| warp 0 (MMA) | first statement of the body, before `acc_empty` wait and the k-loop | 913 | The body computes the *current* tile with the current `(tm, tn)`; consuming first makes the exit decision available at the end and releases the CLC slot (32 of 800) as early as possible. |
| warps 4-7 (epilogue) | first statement, before the `acc_full` peek | 1028 | Same; in addition the epilogue's 128 arrivals are the largest share of the 800, and if they came *after* the store of tile t the CLC slot would be released about one mainloop later, stalling the scheduler's query t + 2 behind the epilogue (only two slots). |
| warp 2 (producer) | after both `load_ktiles` calls and a `__syncwarp()` | 793 | The producer is the role that needs the next coordinates soonest (its loads for tile t + 1 start before the MMA finishes tile t) and it is the throttle producer: query t is issued only after it has *started* tile t, so consuming before the loads would make every tile wait for the CLC round trip (~1.4 us) before its first TMA. The `__syncwarp()` (CUTLASS kernel :691 in the working tree, :663 in cb424739: "Sync warp to prevent non-participating threads entering next wave early") reconverges the warp after the elected-lane TMA issues. |
| rank 0 warp 1 (scheduler) | right after issuing query t | 853 | It has nothing else to do, and it must learn validity to stop: issuing a query after observing a failed one is undefined behaviour (CUDA Programming Guide, CLC page: "Submitting another cancellation request after observing a previously failed request is undefined behavior"). |

In every role the fetched coordinates are parked in `tm_next, tn_next` and adopted only at the end of the body (explicit.cu:794, 854, 947, 1073: `tm = tm_next; tn = tn_next;`), and the loop condition is the validity of the *fetched* response (`while (valid)`). Consequences, all measured in note D.3/G.1: a cluster that processes T tiles (T is the cluster's tile count here and in Section 4.8, the symbol of the note's tail formulas and Chapter 8's `n_tiles`; not the TMEM base T of Chapters 9-10) issues exactly T queries (T - 1 answered "cancelled", the last "not cancelled"); every participating warp consumes exactly T responses; the initial tile (from `blockIdx`, explicit.cu:1177-1178) is computed *after* response 0 has been consumed; and the last valid tile is computed and stored *after* the not-cancelled response has been consumed. The not-cancelled response's `x0, y0, z0` are never read (`if (valid)` guards the mapping, explicit.cu:691-694) because the predicated `get_first_ctaid` leaves them unwritten (note D.3).

## 4.8 The exit protocol

There is no cluster-wide synchronisation at kernel exit (note, Section 7.10). A CTA's shared memory disappears when its last warp exits; any remote arrival still in flight into that memory is undefined behaviour (the distributed-shared-memory rules of the CUDA Programming Guide require the target CTA to still be running when its shared memory is accessed, paraphrased; note B.6 states the kernel-level rule as "a CTA must not exit while peers may still arrive on its barriers"). The kernel therefore makes every role that *owns a barrier other CTAs arrive on* wait for the last such arrivals before it leaves. Which barriers receive remote arrivals that no ordinary wait already covers?

| Barrier | Remote arrivals from | Already covered by a normal wait? | Tail |
|---|---|---|---|
| `empty[s]`@every CTA | both leaders' `tcgen05.commit` (mask `0xF`) | No: after its last load the producer never waits `empty` again | **Tail 1**, warp 2, 8 waits |
| `clc_empty[i]`@CTA 0 | 800 arrivals per response from all four CTAs | No: after its last query the scheduler never waits `clc_empty` again | **Tail 2**, rank 0 warp 1, 2 waits |
| `acc_empty[st]`@leader | the peer's 128 epilogue threads (+ own 128) | No: after its last tile the leader's warp 0 never waits `acc_empty` again | **Tail 3**, leader warp 0, 4 waits |
| `tmem_dealloc`@both | the other MMA warp's 32 arrivals | (it *is* the handshake) | **Tail 4** |
| `full[s]`@leader, `acc_full[st]`@both, `clc_full[i]`@all | bytes / commits / arming | Yes: consumed by local waits before the role can finish | none needed |
| `thr_*`@CTA 0 | none (CTA-local) | n/a | none needed |

Warp 1 of ranks 1-3 and warp 3 of every CTA exit right after the rendezvous (explicit.cu:1190-1202: they match no branch); nothing targets them. Rank 1's and rank 3's `acc_empty`, every CTA's `clc_empty` except CTA 0's, and the peers' `full[]` are initialised but never arrived on, so they need no tail.

### 4.8.1 Tail 1: the producer's 8 empty waits (explicit.cu:797-806, verbatim)

```
  // load_tail = producer_tail (sm90_pipeline.hpp:445-454): 8 blocking waits continuing the producer state (Section 7.10 tail 1)
  #pragma unroll
  for (int i = 0; i < kStages; ++i) {
    EXPLICIT_WAIT(empty_base + 8u * st.prod_idx, st.prod_phase, TAIL_MAINLOOP, tile, uint32_t(i));
#if defined(CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE)   // [TRACE]
    heartbeat(tile, HB_TAIL);
    trace_tail(TAIL_MAINLOOP, st.prod_idx, st.prod_phase, tile);
#endif
    advance<kStages>(st.prod_idx, st.prod_phase);
  }
```

This is `PipelineTmaAsync::producer_tail` (sm90_pipeline.hpp:448-454: `for (count < Stages) { empty_barrier_ptr_[state.index()].wait(state.phase()); ++state; }`), reached through `load_tail` (sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp:632-641, the call at :640). The sm90 line numbers are the right ones for an sm100 pipeline because `PipelineTmaUmmaAsync::producer_tail` (sm100_pipeline.hpp:702-704) is a one-line forward to `impl_.producer_tail`, where `Impl = PipelineTmaAsync<Stages>` (:542) comes from sm90_pipeline.hpp; likewise `PipelineUmmaAsync::producer_tail` (:219-221) forwards to `PipelineAsync<Stages>` (:124), which is tail 3 below. It *continues the producer state*: after T tiles the producer has made N = 128 T steps, so tail step i waits on `empty[(128 T + i) % 8] = empty[i]` with parity `1 ^ (((128 T + i) / 8) & 1) = 1 ^ ((16 T) & 1) = 1` for every T. In words: "has the last use of stage i been released?" Phase count of `empty[i]` after T tiles is 16 T; the producer's next-use parity is 1; waiting parity 1 returns when phase 16 T - 1 (odd) is complete, i.e. when both leaders' commits for k-tile 127 - (7 - i) have landed. Measured (note G.1): every mainloop tail step waited parity 1 in all 33 clusters (`k_tail_mainloop_parity` PASS).

### 4.8.2 Tail 2: the CLC producer's 2 waits (explicit.cu:857-867, verbatim)

```
  // CLC producer_tail (sm100_pipeline.hpp:1041-1050): test_wait, then the blocking wait only if not done (Section 7.10 tail 2)
  #pragma unroll
  for (int i = 0; i < kClcStages; ++i) {
    uint32_t const done = mbar_test_wait(smem_base + OFF_CLC_EMPTY + 8u * clp_idx, clp_phase, 1u);
    if (!done) { EXPLICIT_WAIT(smem_base + OFF_CLC_EMPTY + 8u * clp_idx, clp_phase, TAIL_CLC, tile, uint32_t(i)); }
#if defined(CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE)   // [TRACE]
    heartbeat(tile, HB_TAIL);
    trace_tail(TAIL_CLC, clp_idx, clp_phase, tile);
#endif
    advance<kClcStages>(clp_idx, clp_phase);
  }
```

`PipelineCLCFetchAsync::producer_tail` (sm100_pipeline.hpp:1041-1050) probes with `test_wait` first and blocks only if needed; the explicit kernel keeps that shape so that the SASS keeps its two `SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64` without `.TRYWAIT` (note D.2 row `mbarrier.test_wait.parity`). With T queries issued, step i waits `clc_empty[(T + i) % 2]` with parity `1 ^ (((T + i) >> 1) & 1)`: the 800 releases of response T - 2 (slot `T % 2`) and then of response T - 1.

### 4.8.3 Tail 3 and tail 4: the leader's 4 accumulator waits and the dealloc handshake (explicit.cu:952-971, verbatim with the trace lines)

```
  if (is_leader) {                                                                              // accumulator producer_tail (:789; sm90_pipeline.hpp:1129-1134) (Section 7.10 tail 3)
    #pragma unroll
    for (int i = 0; i < kAccStages; ++i) {
      EXPLICIT_WAIT(acc_empty_base + 8u * accp_idx, accp_phase, TAIL_ACC, tile, uint32_t(i));
#if defined(CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE)   // [TRACE]
      heartbeat(tile, HB_TAIL);
      trace_tail(TAIL_ACC, accp_idx, accp_phase, tile);
#endif
      advance<kAccStages>(accp_idx, accp_phase);
    }
  }
  // TMEM deallocation handshake (:794-796): the peer arrives on the leader's barrier, both wait phase 0, the leader arrives on the peer's (Section 7.10 tail 4)
  if (!is_leader) { mbar_arrive_remote(smem_base + OFF_TMEM_DEALLOC, peer); }
  EXPLICIT_WAIT(smem_base + OFF_TMEM_DEALLOC, 0u, WAIT_TMEM_DEALLOC, tile, 0u);
#if defined(CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE)   // [TRACE]
  heartbeat(tile, HB_TAIL);
  trace_tail(WAIT_TMEM_DEALLOC, 0u, 0u, tile);
#endif
  if (is_leader) { mbar_arrive_remote(smem_base + OFF_TMEM_DEALLOC, peer); }
  tmem_dealloc_2sm(T, kTmemColumns);                                                            // (:804), both CTAs
```

Tail 3 is `PipelineAsync::producer_tail` (sm90_pipeline.hpp:1129-1134, `producer_acquire(state); ++state;` S times) called by the leader only (kernel :821-824: "Leader MMA waits for leader + peer epilogues to release accumulator stage"). With T tiles, step i waits `acc_empty[(T + i) % 4]` with parity `1 ^ (((T + i) >> 2) & 1)`: the 256 releases of the last use of each TMEM stage, from both CTAs' epilogues.

Tail 4 is the CUTLASS sequence at kernel :826-830 ("Leader does wait + arrive, follower does arrive + wait"; `arrive(mma_peer_cta_rank, not is_mma_leader_cta); wait(dealloc_barrier_phase); arrive(mma_peer_cta_rank, is_mma_leader_cta)`). The peer's 32 lanes arrive on the leader's `tmem_dealloc` (count 32, one phase); both wait parity 0 on their own barrier; the leader's 32 lanes then arrive on the peer's. Why? `tcgen05.dealloc.cta_group::2` must follow *all* TMEM reads of both CTAs (note B.6), and the only warp that knows both epilogues are done is the leader's warp 0, after tail 3. The handshake therefore (a) stops the peer's warp 0 from deallocating before the leader has finished tail 3, and (b) stops the leader from deallocating before the peer's warp 0 has reached the handshake, so that the pair-wide deallocation and the remote arrive into the peer both find a live CTA (derived from source; the ordering rationale is my analysis). The peer-side reason deserves to be explicit: the peer's warp 0 never waits `acc_empty` (only the leader does, explicit.cu:915-918), so it has no knowledge of whether *its own* epilogue warps have finished their `tcgen05.ld` of the last tile; the handshake borrows the leader's tail-3 knowledge (the 256 arrivals include the peer's 128). Without it the peer could execute `tcgen05.dealloc.cta_group::2` while its own TMEM reads were in flight, corruption or a fault, on top of the exited-CTA hazard. Measured (note G.1): 1518 `K_TAIL` records = 46 per cluster = rank 0: 8 + 2 + 4 + 1, rank 1: 8 + 1, rank 2: 8 + 4 + 1, rank 3: 8 + 1.

### 4.8.4 The parities, worked for T = 32, 31 and 19

These are the three tile counts observed in the traced run (note D.3: 32 tiles for 13 clusters, 31 for 19, 19 for the probe-slowed cluster (0,0)).

| Tail | T = 32 | T = 31 | T = 19 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1, mainloop: `empty[(128T+i)%8]`, i = 0..7 | index 0..7, parity 1 for all | index 0..7, parity 1 | index 0..7, parity 1 |
| 2, CLC: `clc_empty[(T+i)%2]`, i = 0, 1 | (0, parity 1), (1, parity 1) | (1, parity 0), (0, parity 1) | (1, parity 0), (0, parity 1) |
| 3, accumulator: `acc_empty[(T+i)%4]`, i = 0..3 | (0,1), (1,1), (2,1), (3,1) | (3,0), (0,1), (1,1), (2,1) | (3,1), (0,0), (1,0), (2,0) |
| 4, dealloc: own barrier | parity 0 | parity 0 | parity 0 |

Check one: T = 19, tail 3, i = 1: `n = 20`, index `20 % 4 = 0`, `20 / 4 = 5`, parity `1 ^ (5 & 1) = 0`. TMEM stage 0 was used by tiles 0, 4, 8, 12, 16: five uses, five releases, so `acc_empty[0]` has completed phases 0..4 once all 256 arrivals of tile 16 are in; the current phase is then 5 (odd); waiting parity 0 asks for phase 4, the preceding one: it returns exactly when tile 16's releases are complete. The lesson of the table (note Section 7.2): *all S tail waits use the same parity only when `N % S == 0`*; a kernel that hard-codes one parity for the whole tail hangs or exits early whenever the tile count is not a multiple of the stage count. The dealloc wait is always parity 0 because that barrier completes exactly one phase in the kernel's life.

### 4.8.5 The last TMA store group

The epilogue has no tail for beta = 0: `store_tail` (sm100_epilogue_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:1271 ff.) is gated on `is_producer_load_needed()`, which is false, so no `cp.async.bulk.wait_group.read 0` executes (explicit.cu:1076 comment; note D.2: the `DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x0` exists at `0xb760` but the epilogue warps take the `EXIT` before it). The invariant at exit is therefore the one left by the last subtile's `wait_group.read 1`: **at most one bulk group (the final subtile's four stores) may still be reading its smem stage when the epilogue warps exit.** Measured (note D.1 D15): every run of the fixed command passed with this condition. The note's rule for any rewrite: preserve or tighten it (a `wait_group.read 0` or `wait_group 0` before exit is allowed), never loosen it.

---

## 4.9 Hazards, what prevents them, and what happens without them

"Hang" means a wait whose phase never completes; "corruption" means a wrong D with the kernel completing normally. The failure column is my analysis of each missing element; the elements themselves are derived from source.

| # | Hazard | Protocol element | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | smem **WAR**: TMA writes stage s while the tensor core still reads use n - 8 | `empty[s]` count 2; both leaders' `tcgen05.commit` mask `0xF` after the fourth MMA; producer waits `empty[s]` with parity `1 ^ ((n/8)&1)` | Corruption (the UMMA reads a mix of two k-tiles). Using `mbarrier.arrive` instead of `tcgen05.commit`: corruption, since the arrive fires at issue, not at completion. Count 1 instead of 2: corruption in the CTA whose multicast half is overwritten before the *other* leader has read it. |
| 2 | smem **RAW**: UMMA reads stage s before all six boxes have landed | `full[s]` count 1 + 49152 tx; the leader's `arrive.expect_tx`; every box names the leader's barrier (peer bit) | tx too small (e.g. 24576, forgetting the x2): the phase completes after half the bytes, corruption. tx too large: hang. Boxes credited to the wrong barrier (peer bit not cleared): the leader's phase never completes, hang. |
| 3 | TMEM **RAW**: epilogue loads stage st before the 512 MMAs have finished | `acc_full[st]` count 1 completed by the leader's `tcgen05.commit` mask `0x3 << 2y` | Corruption (partial sums). Mask `0x3` for both pairs: pair {2,3}'s epilogue never sees its commit, hang; pair {0,1} gets two arrivals per phase on a count-1 barrier, undefined. |
| 4 | TMEM **WAR**: MMA of tile t + 4 overwrites stage st while `tcgen05.ld` of tile t is in flight | `acc_empty[st]` count 256; `tcgen05.wait::ld` before each thread's arrive; leader waits before the first MMA of the tile | Without `wait::ld`: corruption (the arrive precedes the asynchronous load's completion). Count 128: the leader proceeds when only one CTA's epilogue has released, corruption in the other CTA's rows. |
| 5 | **Generic-proxy writes vs TMA store**: the TMA unit reads the C/D stage before the 128 threads' `st.shared` are visible to the async proxy | `fence.proxy.async.shared::cta` by every thread, then `bar.sync 1, 128`, then the stores | Stale smem in D: corruption. Fence without the `bar.sync`: warp 4 may issue before the other three warps have fenced, corruption. |
| 6 | **C/D stage WAR**: threads write stage `(e+1)%4` while a TMA store still reads it | `cp.async.bulk.commit_group` + `wait_group.read 1` by warp 4, then `bar.sync 1, 128` | Corruption in D (the store reads a half-overwritten stage). The second `bar.sync` is what propagates warp 4's wait to the other warps. |
| 7 | **CLC response visibility and WAR**: a consumer reads slot i before the 16 bytes landed, or the next `try_cancel` overwrites slot i before a consumer has read it | `clc_full[i]` 1 + 16 tx (arrive.expect_tx by rank 0 lanes 0..3, bytes by the CLC unit); `fence.proxy.async` after the decode; `clc_empty[i]` count 800 before reissue | Reading early: a stale or torn response, a tile computed twice or never. Count smaller than 800: the producer reissues while a slow warp still reads, same effect. The `fence.proxy.async` closes the generic-read/async-write window. |
| 8 | **Barrier init visibility**: a remote arrive or `complete_tx` hits a barrier word that is not yet initialised in that CTA | `fence.mbarrier_init.release.cluster` after each init group; `barrier.cluster.arrive.relaxed` + `barrier.cluster.wait` before any remote operation | The arrival is lost or lands on garbage: hang (a phase that never completes) or, if the init lands after the arrival, a count that is one too high: hang. |
| 9 | **TMEM base visibility**: the epilogue reads `tmem_base_ptr` before `tcgen05.alloc` wrote it | `__syncwarp()` then `bar.arrive 6, 160` in warp 0; `bar.sync 6, 160` in warps 4-7 | Wrong TMEM addresses: corruption or an illegal-address fault. |
| 10 | **Not-cancelled response decoded as a tile** | `if (valid)` around the `(tm, tn)` mapping; the loop exits on `!valid` | The stale `x0, y0` of the previous response are reused: a tile computed twice (and the CTA keeps running past the end of the grid). Issuing another query after a failed one is undefined behaviour. |
| 11 | **Over-reservation of tiles** | throttle ring (query t only after rank 0's loader began tile t) | Not a correctness hazard: the kernel stays correct but a cluster may hold up to two unstarted tiles, lengthening the tail of the grid. |
| 12 | **CTA exit with remote arrivals pending** | Tails 1-4 (4.8) | Undefined behaviour: an arrive into the shared memory of an exited CTA; in practice a hang of the arriving side or a corrupted barrier of whatever CTA next occupies that SM (my analysis). |
| 13 | **`scale_c` not reset per tile** (not a barrier, but part of the per-tile contract) | `scale_c = 0` before the first MMA of every tile (explicit.cu:917), 1 afterwards | The new tile accumulates onto the previous tile's TMEM contents: corruption. |

**Deadlock-freedom (my analysis, derived from the source structure).** Every ring is bounded and used in order, and the cross-ring dependencies form a directed acyclic graph per tile: `query t` needs {rank 0's loader started tile t; all 800 consumers released response t - 2}; `response t` -> {warp 0 and warps 4-7 start tile t; warp 2 starts tile t + 1}; `full[s]` for k-tile q of tile t needs {the four producers issued q, which needs `empty[s]` = both leaders' commits for q - 8}; `acc_full[t % 4]` needs the 128 commits of tile t; `acc_empty[t % 4]` for tile t needs the epilogue of tile t - 4; `clc_empty` for query t needs the epilogue to have *consumed* response t - 2, which it does as the first statement of tile t - 2's body (explicit.cu:1028, before the `acc_full` peek at :1030), so the requirement is only that the epilogue has finished *storing* tile t - 3, which needs `acc_full[(t - 3) % 4]`, i.e. the mainloop of tile t - 3, long complete. Every dependency points to strictly earlier work, so no cycle exists. Two couplings are worth knowing because they bound how far roles can drift apart: the 4-stage TMEM ring lets the epilogue lag the MMA by at most 3 tiles, and the 2-slot CLC ring lets it lag by at most about 2 (query t waits for the epilogue's release of response t - 2, and the MMA waits for response t); so in this kernel the CLC ring, not the TMEM ring, is the tighter bound on MMA-epilogue skew. Finally, the four CTAs stay consistent because the response is multicast: all four decode the same tile sequence, so the pair's MMA (which reads both CTAs' smem) and the A multicast (which writes both cluster rows) always refer to the same `(tm, tn)` in every CTA.

## 4.10 The protocol card

One line per barrier: *producer (how) -> barrier -> consumer (how)*; counts; parity rule. P = producer parity `1 ^ ((n/S)&1)`, C = consumer parity `(n/S)&1`, n = use index.

```
 MAIN full[s]   8 x @leader(0,8s)   leader lane W12 arrive.expect_tx 49152 + 6 TMA boxes (peer-bit addr)   -> W0 leader waits C, n = 128t+q
 MAIN empty[s]  8 x @all(64,8s)     W0 of both leaders: tcgen05.commit mask 0xF (count 2)                  -> W2 waits P, n = 128t+q  (tail: 8 waits, parity 1)
 ACC  full[st]  4 x @both(240,8st)  W0 leader: tcgen05.commit mask 0x3<<2y (count 1)                       -> W4-7 wait C, n = t (peek once, wait at e = 0)
 ACC  empty[st] 4 x @leader(272,8st) 128 threads x 2 CTAs: wait::ld then W11 arrive (peer-bit) (count 256)  -> W0 leader waits P, n = t (tail: 4 waits)
 CLC  full[i]   2 x @all(208,8i)    r0.W1 lanes 0..3 W13 arrive.expect_tx 16 via mapa + response bytes      -> every consuming warp waits C, n = t
 CLC  empty[i]  2 x @CTA0(224,8i)   800 threads W10 arrive via mapa 0 after decode + fence.proxy.async       -> r0.W1 waits P, n = t (tail: test_wait+wait x2)
 THR  full[i]   2 x @CTA0(304,8i)   r0.W2 32 lanes W9 local arrive (count 32)                                -> r0.W1 waits C, n = t
 THR  empty[i]  2 x @CTA0(320,8i)   r0.W1 32 lanes W10 arrive via mapa 0 (count 32)                          -> r0.W2 waits P, n = t
 DEALLOC        1 x @both(336)      peer W0 32 lanes arrive(mapa peer) -> leader waits 0 -> leader arrives(mapa peer) -> peer waits 0
 bar 1 (128)    epilogue warps: after fence.proxy.async (before TMA store) and after wait_group.read 1 (before next stage write), per subtile
 bar 6 (160)    W0 bar.arrive after tcgen05.alloc + __syncwarp; W4-7 bar.sync before reading tmem_base_ptr
 bulk groups    W4: 4 stores, commit_group, wait_group.read 1 per subtile; no wait 0 at exit (<= 1 group pending)
 start states   producers {0,1}; consumers {0,0}; advance: ++idx == S -> idx = 0, phase ^= 1
 init           W0: main 8+8, dealloc 1; W4: CLC 2+2; W5: acc 4+4; W3: throttle 2+2; fence.mbarrier_init after each group;
                barrier.cluster.arrive.relaxed -> setup -> barrier.cluster.wait; no remote op before the wait
```

## Checkpoint

1. A freshly initialised mbarrier has count 2. Thread A waits with parity 0, thread B with parity 1. Which returns immediately, and what has to happen for the other to return?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
B returns immediately: the barrier is in phase 0, and "the phase with parity 1" among the current and the preceding phase is the preceding one, deemed complete. A blocks until phase 0 completes, which needs two arrivals (and, if any `expect_tx` was issued in this phase, the tx-count back to zero). This is why producers start at `{0, 1}` and consumers at `{0, 0}` (4.2.3).
</details>

2. Why is the mainloop full barrier's expected transaction count 49152 and not 24576, and why does it live only in the pair leader?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
Six 8192-byte boxes land in the pair per stage: two A halves and one B half in each of the two CTAs. Every box names the leader's barrier (its own `shared::cta` address with bit 24 cleared, or, for multicast, the destination pair's leader), so the leader's barrier must expect all six: 2 x (16384 + 8192) = 49152. The peer's barrier gets nothing because the only reader of the pair's stage is the leader's `tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2`, which reads both CTAs' smem (4.4.1).
</details>

3. Derive the mainloop empty barrier count and the commit mask for a hypothetical cluster (2,1,1) with the same 2SM MMA (one pair, no multicast across rows).

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
`cluster_m / atom_m + cluster_n / atom_n - 1 = 2/2 + 1/1 - 1 = 1`: only the pair leader reads what a CTA wrote. `calculate_multicast_mask<kRowCol>` yields the CTAs in the same MMA column or row, i.e. both CTAs: mask `0x3`. Each CTA then receives exactly one commit per k-tile, matching count 1 (4.4.2).
</details>

4. After T = 31 tiles, which `acc_empty` barrier does the leader's first tail wait address, with which parity, and what event completes it?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
`n = T + 0 = 31`: index `31 % 4 = 3`, parity `1 ^ ((31 / 4) & 1) = 1 ^ (7 & 1) = 0`. Stage 3 was used by tiles 3, 7, ..., 27: seven uses; after the seventh release the barrier is in phase 7 (odd), and waiting parity 0 asks for the preceding phase 6, which completes when the 256 epilogue arrivals of tile 27 are in (4.8.4).
</details>

5. The producer peeks 130 times per tile but only 128 peeks are used. Where are the two wasted ones, and why does the MMA warp have none?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
Each `load_ktiles` call peeks once before its loop and once per iteration after `advance`; the peek after the last iteration of each of the two calls (8 and 120 k-tiles) looks at a stage the call does not use, and the next call re-peeks. The MMA loop guards its in-loop peek with `k <= 0 ? 1 : try_wait` and so skips the peek after the last k-tile, giving 1 + 127 = 128 peeks, all consumed (4.5.2).
</details>

6. Why do warps 0 and 4-7 consume the CLC response *before* working on the current tile while warp 2 consumes *after* issuing its loads? What would happen if warp 2 also consumed first?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
The body always works on the current tile and adopts the fetched one at the end; consuming first lets warps 0 and 4-7 release the CLC slot early (the epilogue's 128 arrivals are the largest share of the 800) and have the exit decision ready. Warp 2 of rank 0 is the throttle producer: query t is issued only after it has started tile t, so if it waited for response t before its first load, every tile would begin with a ~1.0-1.4 us CLC round trip (trace builds, 4.7.1) before any TMA is issued (4.7.2).
</details>

7. Name the element that prevents each of these and the failure without it: (a) the epilogue arriving on `acc_empty` right after issuing its last `tcgen05.ld`; (b) warp 4 issuing the TMA store right after its own `fence.proxy.async`; (c) the leader's warp 0 exiting right after its last `acc_full` commit.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
(a) `tcgen05.wait::ld` must precede the arrive, because `tcgen05.ld` is asynchronous; without it the MMA of tile t + 4 can overwrite TMEM still being read: corruption. (b) `bar.sync 1, 128` after the fences, so that all 128 threads' writes are fenced; without it the store may read other warps' unfenced data: corruption. (c) Tail 3 (four `acc_empty` waits) and the dealloc handshake; without them the peer's 128 arrivals and the dealloc arrive may target an exited CTA: undefined behaviour, in practice a hang (4.9, 4.8).
</details>

8. The kernel is rebuilt for K = 6656 (104 k-tiles per tile) with the same 8-stage ring. At which stage and with which consumer parity does the MMA warp wait for k-tile 0 of tile 1, and does `ProducerState` need any change?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
n = 104 t + q = 104: stage 104 mod 8 = 0, use floor(104 / 8) = 13, consumer parity 13 mod 2 = 1 (producer parity 0). Tile 1 starts at stage 0 but with the phase bit flipped relative to tile 0, because 13 wraps is odd. `ProducerState` needs no change: `advance<8>` flips the bit once per wrap, so the carried state is already right; only the "every tile looks like tile 0" shortcut, true iff K mod 16 == 0, is lost (4.3.3).
</details>

# Chapter 5. The Foundation: Files, the Parameter Block, Tensor Maps, and Section 1 Constants

**What you will learn**

- How the three source files (`util.hpp`, `explicit.hpp`, `explicit.cu`) and the unchanged harness are split into two translation units, why the trace toggle must be line 1 of the header both TUs include first, and why the build uses no `-rdc` and keeps both GEMM kernels in one binary.
- Every byte of `ExplicitGemmParams` (640 bytes with CUDA 13.3), which of them the device actually reads (12 bytes of scalars, `k`, `alpha`, `beta`, plus the four 128-byte maps), and why four 128-byte `CUtensorMap` objects travel by value inside a `const __grid_constant__` parameter.
- What `gemm.initialize()` still does on every timed iteration (six `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled` calls), the exact encoder inputs of the A/B and C/D tensor maps, and the two box-truncation rules that make the A box (64, 64, 1) and the D box (32, 16, 1).
- Every constant of Section 1 of `explicit.cu` with its derivation: the tile and pipeline depths, the byte map of the 230400-byte shared-memory window, the 64-bit UMMA shared-memory descriptor and the 32-bit instruction descriptor bit by bit (with the worked example `0x4000404000011484`), the protocol counts, masks and hints, and the `cute::Swizzle<2,5,2>` cross-check done by hand.
- What the trace-only Section 2 adds and why it is invisible in the production binary.

Notation reminder: rank `r = x + 2y`; `smem_base = 0x400 + (r << 24)` (measured); `OFF_*` names exactly as in `explicit.cu`; `T` is the TMEM base (measured 0). "Measured" means the note's Parts D/G; "derived" means read from `explicit.cu` or the CUTLASS tree; everything else is marked as my analysis. CUTLASS line numbers in this chapter are those of the **working tree** (HEAD of `dev/gemm-deabstraction`). That tree is commit cb424739 plus inert trace-probe blocks in four headers, so four files have shifted numbers; `explicit.cu`'s own comments cite cb424739 numbers. Section 5.1.3 lists the four files and the mapping.

## 5.1 The file set and the build

### 5.1.1 Four files, two translation units

```
                 70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.cu  (harness TU)          70_blackwell_fp16_gemm_explicit.cu  (kernel TU)
                 line 1: #include "..._explicit_util.hpp"          line 1: #include "..._explicit_util.hpp"
                 line 88: #include "..._explicit.hpp"              line 83: #include "..._explicit.hpp"
                 CUTLASS headers (CollectiveBuilder, Gemm, ...)    cutlass/cutlass.h, cute/swizzle.hpp (+ cute/container/tuple.hpp via explicit.hpp)
                        |                                                 |
                        |  instantiates make_params<Gemm>,                |  defines __global__ kernel,
                        |  run<Gemm>(gemm) (templates)                    |  defines run(ExplicitGemmParams const&)
                        v                                                 v
            +--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
            |  70_blackwell_fp16_gemm_explicit.hpp  : struct ExplicitGemmParams (the ABI) |
            |  70_blackwell_fp16_gemm_explicit_util.hpp : toggle (line 1), constants       |
            +--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                        \                                                 /
                         \  nvcc, whole-program per TU (no -rdc)        /
                          v                                            v
                     70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.o  +  70_blackwell_fp16_gemm_explicit.o  -->  one executable
                     (CUTLASS kernel's cubin,       (explicit kernel's cubin)
                      never launched)
```

The include order is load-bearing. `explicit.cu:1` and the harness's line 1 are both `#include "70_blackwell_fp16_gemm_explicit_util.hpp"`:

```
$ sed -n 1p explicit.cu
#include "70_blackwell_fp16_gemm_explicit_util.hpp"   // line 1 of that header is the trace toggle (E.2.3); must be the first include
$ grep -n "explicit" 70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.cu
1:#include "70_blackwell_fp16_gemm_explicit_util.hpp"   // line 1 of this header is the de-abstraction trace toggle (Part E.2.3 of Semantics-preserving-de-abstraction.md)
88:#include "70_blackwell_fp16_gemm_explicit.hpp"
391:  explicit_gemm::trace_begin(block_D.get(), block_D.size() * sizeof(typename Gemm::EpilogueOutputOp::ElementOutput));
416:  CUTLASS_CHECK(explicit_gemm::run(gemm));
422:  // E.7.3: H3 on the explicit kernel, dump of K0 + warm-up records, disable before the timed launches; B4 mismatch dump if the compare failed
423:  explicit_gemm::trace_end("launch0.csv", result.passed, block_D.get(), block_ref_D.get(), options.m, options.n);
439:      CUTLASS_CHECK(explicit_gemm::run(gemm));
```

The kernel TU's include set (`explicit.cu:72-80`) is `<cuda.h>`, `<cuda_runtime.h>`, `<cstdint>`, `<cstdio>`, `cutlass/cutlass.h`, `cute/swizzle.hpp` and `explicit.hpp`; through `explicit.hpp` (`:33`, `:39`) it also gets `<cuda.h>` for `CUtensorMap` and `cute/container/tuple.hpp` for `cute::get`. The transitive closure of `cute/swizzle.hpp` is 39 headers (note, Section E.2.1), none of them a CUTLASS kernel or collective header: the kernel TU never sees `cutlass/gemm/*`, which is why the enumerators `AlongN` and `kGemm` appear as literals in `util.hpp` (5.2.2).

Why the toggle must be seen first and identically by both TUs: the macro `CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE` changes the *set of symbols and code paths the two TUs must agree on* (`explicit.hpp:82-89` declares `trace_begin`/`trace_end` only under the toggle, and the harness's guarded blocks at lines 391 and 423 call them). It does not change the layout of `ExplicitGemmParams`: the struct (`explicit.hpp:49-63`) contains no `#if`, and its `static_assert`s pin the offsets regardless of the toggle. If one TU saw the macro and the other did not, the harness would call functions the kernel TU never defined, or the kernel TU would compile diagnostics that the harness never arms. Putting the `#define` on line 1 of a header that is the first include of both `.cu` files makes one edit flip both TUs, and lets a script flip it with `sed '1s|...|...|'` (note, Section E.2.3). It also guarantees the macro is defined before any CUTLASS header that contains a probe block (note, Section E.2.3: `cutlass/cutlass.h` pulls in only `helper_macros.hpp` and standard headers).

### 5.1.2 CMake: one line, two objects, no `-rdc`

```
$ sed -n 36,46p examples/70_blackwell_gemm/CMakeLists.txt
if(CUTLASS_NVCC_ARCHS MATCHES "100a|100f|101a|101f|103a|103f")
cutlass_example_add_executable(
  70_blackwell_fp16_gemm
  70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.cu
  70_blackwell_fp16_gemm_explicit.cu
  TEST_COMMAND_OPTIONS
  TEST_SWIZZLE_1
  TEST_SWIZZLE_2
  TEST_SWIZZLE_5
  TEST_SWIZZLE_5_UNEVEN
)
```

Line 40 is the only build change. It must sit before `TEST_COMMAND_OPTIONS`, because `cutlass_example_add_executable` parses its arguments with `cmake_parse_arguments` and forwards everything unparsed as sources: `cutlass_add_executable(${NAME} ${__UNPARSED_ARGUMENTS} BATCH_SOURCES OFF)` (`examples/CMakeLists.txt:46`). `BATCH_SOURCES OFF` means no unity build: each `.cu` becomes its own object with its own fatbin (`sm_100a` cubin + `compute_100a` PTX, measured nvcc line in note Section 0).

There is no `-rdc`/`-dc` on the nvcc line (note, Section 0 quotes the measured command). The only place CUTLASS turns on `CMAKE_CUDA_SEPARABLE_COMPILATION` is under `CUTLASS_ENABLE_SYNCLOG`, which is off:

```
$ sed -n 477,480p CMakeLists.txt
set(CUTLASS_ENABLE_SYNCLOG OFF CACHE BOOL "Enable synchronization event logging for race condition debugging. WARNING: This redefines __syncthreads() and __syncwarp() in all downstream code!")

if (CUTLASS_ENABLE_SYNCLOG)
  set(CMAKE_CUDA_SEPARABLE_COMPILATION ON)
```

Three consequences you must design around when you write such a split yourself:

| Consequence | Why | Where it shows in the code |
|---|---|---|
| The shared header may contain no non-`inline`, non-template definition | Without relocatable device code each TU is a whole program; a plain function defined in a header included twice is two definitions of one symbol at link time | `util.hpp:51` `inline cutlass::Status status_from_cuda`; `explicit.hpp:99-132` are templates; `explicit.hpp:80` is a declaration only |
| Device code can live in exactly one TU | `__global__`/`__device__` definitions in a shared header would produce two independent copies, one per fatbin; a non-`static` one would also produce duplicate host-side shadow symbols at link time (inferred from nvcc whole-program semantics; the note marks it "confirm at the first toggle-on build", Section E.3.2, and the implementation simply avoided the case) | all device code is in `explicit.cu`; `explicit.hpp:12-13` states the rule |
| Both GEMM kernels remain in the binary | `gemm.initialize()` passes `device_kernel<GemmKernel>` to `cudaFuncSetAttribute` (`gemm_universal_adapter.h:344-347`), an odr-use that instantiates the CUTLASS kernel into the harness TU's fatbin; it is compiled, loaded, given its attribute on every iteration, and never launched | harness lines 410 and 438 (`gemm.initialize`) |

The cost of the third row is build time and binary size only; the per-iteration `cudaFuncSetAttribute` on the never-launched kernel is the baseline's own call, so the timed interval stays comparable (Chapter 12 does the accounting).

### 5.1.3 The working tree versus commit cb424739: four headers carry inert probes

`git diff --stat cb424739 -- include/` lists exactly four files. Every inserted hunk is a `#if defined(CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE)` probe block (`TRACE_RECORD`/`TRACE_IN_FIRST_CLUSTER` calls that the note's Part C used to instrument the CUTLASS kernel), so the headers are inert in the performance build: the CUTLASS kernel's SASS is byte-identical before and after a toggle-on build (note G.3, D6). They do shift line numbers, which matters when you read `explicit.cu`'s comments (cb424739 numbers) against the tree (working-tree numbers):

| File | Inserted hunks (`@@` headers) | Effect on numbers cited in this chapter |

| `cute/atom/copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp` | +2 after `:77`, +5 more after `:411`, +25 more after `:1068` | working tree `:116`, `:376` (the two `tma_desc_` members) = cb424739 `:114`, `:374`; `:767` = `:760`; `:783-787` = `:776-780`; `:813-838` = `:806-831`; `:984-991` = `:977-984`; `:1003-1009` = `:996-1002`; `:1046-1048` = `:1039-1041`; `:1054-1066` = `:1047-1059`; `:1071-1075` = `:1064-1068` |
| `cutlass/gemm/kernel/sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp` | +28 after `:614`, +6 after `:729`, +6 after `:870` | everything up to `:614` is unchanged (`:136-147`, `:182-212`, `:225-232`, `:511-514`); `k_tile_prologue = min(Stages, k_tile_count)` is `:657` in the tree and `:629` at cb424739, which is the number `explicit.cu:115` and `:788` quote |

## 5.2 `util.hpp`, line by line

The whole file:

```cpp
// #define CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE 1  // De-abstraction trace toggle (Part C / E.2.3 of Semantics-preserving-de-abstraction.md): uncomment, rebuild with the unchanged cmake command, run the fixed command once; re-comment for the performance binary. Both .cu files include this header first, so the toggle is seen identically by both translation units.
/***************************************************************************************************
 * Host-side helpers for the explicit (de-abstracted) Blackwell FP16 GEMM of example 70
 * (Part E.2.3 of examples/70_blackwell_gemm/Semantics-preserving-de-abstraction.md).
 *
 * Rules (E.2.3): line 1 is the trace toggle; this header includes only <cuda_runtime.h>, <cstdio>, <cstdint> and
 * cutlass/cutlass.h (for cutlass::Status); it holds no device code, no CuTe/CUTLASS kernel types, and it
 * must not redefine CUDA_CHECK / CUTLASS_CHECK (examples/common/helper.h defines them for the harness).
 * Every helper is `inline` or a macro because both translation units include this header.
 *
 * Legend (as in the .cu): [PROD] production, [HOST] host-side, [CHECK] compile-time verification, [TRACE] toggle-on only.
 * The toggle on line 1 selects between the two binaries the note distinguishes: commented out = the performance binary
 * (Part H.1); uncommented = the diagnostics binary that records TRACE_* lines and launch0.csv (Part H.2.1). Both .cu files
 * include this header first, so one edit switches both translation units; deabstraction_trace_run.sh flips it with sed.
 **************************************************************************************************/
#pragma once

#include <cuda_runtime.h>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdint>

#include "cutlass/cutlass.h"

namespace explicit_gemm {

// ---- [PROD] [CHECK]  Section 0 constants that need no CUDA type (checked here so a typo is a build error in both TUs).
//      The fixed run in numbers: 8192^3 problem, 128 x 128 CTA tiles, 64-wide k-tiles (128 per tile), 2 x 2 clusters, grid 64 x 64
//      (x indexes N, y indexes M after the AlongN transpose), 256 threads, 230400 B of dynamic shared memory, 32 x 32 cluster tiles.
constexpr int      kFixedM = 8192, kFixedN = 8192, kFixedK = 8192, kFixedL = 1;   // Section 0 shape
constexpr int      kCtaTileM = 128, kCtaTileN = 128, kTileK = 64;                  // Section 4 CTA tile / k-tile
constexpr int      kClusterX = 2, kClusterY = 2, kClusterZ = 1;                    // Section 2 cluster (2,2,1)
constexpr unsigned kGridX = kFixedN / kCtaTileN, kGridY = kFixedM / kCtaTileM, kGridZ = 1;   // (64,64,1) after the AlongN transpose (Section 7.4, B.1.2 step 2)
constexpr unsigned kBlockThreads = 256;                                             // Section 4
constexpr unsigned kSmemBytes = 230400;                                             // Section 6.2 SharedStorageSize
constexpr unsigned kProblemTilesM = kFixedM / 256, kProblemTilesN = kFixedN / 256, kProblemTilesL = 1;   // 32 x 32 cluster tiles (B.1.1 step 11)
constexpr int      kRasterOrderAlongN = 1;   // enum class RasterOrder { AlongM = 0, AlongN = 1 } (tile_scheduler_detail.hpp:38-41; measured AlongN 1, D.5 H4)
constexpr int      kModeGemm = 0;            // GemmUniversalMode::kGemm (gemm_enumerated_types.h:57-64)
constexpr uint64_t kSmemDescConst = 0x4000404000010000ull;   // D.7 UMMA smem descriptor constant part
constexpr uint32_t kInstrDescConst = 0x10200010u;            // D.7 instruction descriptor

static_assert(kGridX == 64 && kGridY == 64 && kGridZ == 1, "Section 0 launch grid");
static_assert(kGridX % kClusterX == 0 && kGridY % kClusterY == 0 && kGridZ % kClusterZ == 0, "grid divisible by the cluster (check_cluster_dims)");
static_assert(kClusterX * kClusterY * kClusterZ <= 32, "cluster size <= MaxClusterSize (cluster_launch.hpp:82)");
static_assert(kFixedK % kTileK == 0 && kFixedK / kTileK == 128, "128 k-tiles per tile (Section 7.4)");
static_assert(kProblemTilesM == 32 && kProblemTilesN == 32, "32 x 32 cluster tiles (Section 7.4)");
static_assert(kSmemBytes <= 232448, "opt-in dynamic shared memory of the B200 (Section 0)");

// ---- [HOST] [PROD]  Status mapping used by the host function (E.5.2): mirrors ClusterLauncher's Return_Status (cluster_launch.hpp),
//      cudaSuccess -> kSuccess, any CUDA error -> kInvalid.  run() in the .cu then collapses kInvalid (and a non-success
//      cudaGetLastError) to kErrorInternal, as GemmUniversalAdapter::run() does (gemm_universal_adapter.h:564-574; F.2 item 11).
inline cutlass::Status status_from_cuda(cudaError_t e) {
  return e == cudaSuccess ? cutlass::Status::kSuccess : cutlass::Status::kInvalid;
}

// ---- [TRACE]  Trace-only host printing (compiles to nothing with the toggle off).  Currently unused: the toggle-on prints of the .cu
//      sit inside #if defined(CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE) blocks and call std::printf directly (F.2 item 12). ----
#if defined(CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE)
#define EXPLICIT_GEMM_TRACE_PRINTF(...) std::printf(__VA_ARGS__)
#else
#define EXPLICIT_GEMM_TRACE_PRINTF(...) do { } while (0)
#endif

} // namespace explicit_gemm
```

### 5.2.1 Line 1: the toggle

A comment-prefixed `#define`. Commented out = the performance binary; uncommented = the diagnostics binary, which is about 12% slower than the CUTLASS kernel's own toggle-on build (1.133 vs 1.007 ms `Avg runtime`, note G.2), i.e. about 27% slower than the 0.889 ms performance binary, and must never be timed (note Part H). It is line 1 and not, say, line 17 after `#pragma once`, because the flipping script edits exactly line 1 (`sed '1s|...|...|'`), and because nothing may precede it that could depend on the macro. Note that `#pragma once` is on line 16: the toggle is *above* the include guard, which is harmless (a second inclusion re-evaluates a comment).

### 5.2.2 The constants (`util.hpp:29-39`) and where each number comes from

| Constant | Value | Derivation | Who uses it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kFixedM/N/K/L` | 8192, 8192, 8192, 1 | The fixed command line `--m=8192 --n=8192 --k=8192`; `Options` defaults are the same (harness lines 207-211) | `run()` guards (`explicit.cu`, Section 11) |
| `kCtaTileM/N` | 128, 128 | `CtaShape_MNK = (128,128,64)` = the 256x128 MMA tile divided by the 2-CTA atom along M (note, Section 4; Chapter 3 derives why 256x128) | `kThreads`/`kMma*` asserts; grid |
| `kTileK` | 64 | `BLK_K = 64` fp16 = 128 bytes per smem row, the SW128 swizzle span (`Layout_K_SW128_Atom<half_t>`: 8 rows x 1024 bits, `mma_traits_sm90_gmma.hpp:84`) | `kKBlocks = 64 / 16 = 4` |
| `kClusterX/Y/Z` | 2, 2, 1 | `ClusterShape_MNK = Shape<_2,_2,_1>` in the harness (line 125) | launch attribute |
| `kGridX, kGridY` | 64, 64 | `N / 128`, `M / 128`: grid **x indexes N** and **y indexes M** because the CLC scheduler's `AlongN` heuristic transposes the grid (`possibly_transpose_grid`, `sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp:216`; Chapter 7) | `run()` |
| `kBlockThreads` | 256 | 8 warps = 5 roles: Sched 32 + MMA 32 + MainloopLoad 32 + EpilogueLoad 32 + Epilogue 128 (`sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:136-147` via note Section 4) | `kThreads`, `__launch_bounds__` |
| `kSmemBytes` | 230400 | `sizeof(SharedStorage)` of the CUTLASS kernel (measured `sizeof_SharedStorage 230400`, note D.1 D2); Section 5.7 rebuilds it byte by byte | `cudaFuncSetAttribute`, launch |
| `kProblemTilesM/N/L` | 32, 32, 1 | 8192 / 256: the scheduler counts **cluster tiles** of 256 x 256 (2 x 2 CTA tiles), not CTA tiles | `run()` guard against `p.scheduler.problem_tiles_*` |
| `kRasterOrderAlongN` | 1 | `enum class RasterOrder { AlongM, AlongN }` (`tile_scheduler_detail.hpp:38-41`), so `AlongN == 1`; the kernel TU may not include `cutlass/gemm/*` (note, E.2.1), hence the literal | `run()` guard |
| `kModeGemm` | 0 | `enum class GemmUniversalMode { kGemm, ... }` (`gemm_enumerated_types.h:57-64`) | `run()` guard |
| `kSmemDescConst` | `0x4000404000010000` | the rank-independent part of both UMMA descriptors (Section 5.8) | `explicit.cu:174` cross-check |
| `kInstrDescConst` | `0x10200010` | the instruction descriptor (Section 5.8) | `explicit.cu:173` |

Why these live here and not in `explicit.cu`: they need no CUDA type, and putting them in the header that both TUs include turns a typo into a build error in *both* TUs (the harness-side `make_params` and the kernel-side guards would otherwise disagree silently).

### 5.2.3 The `static_assert`s (`util.hpp:41-46`)

| Assert | What it protects | What breaks without it |
|---|---|---|
| grid `== (64,64,1)` | the hard-coded grid of `run()` equals the baseline's `get_grid_shape` for this shape | a wrong grid would launch too few or too many clusters; CLC would still hand out all 1024 tiles only if the grid is exactly 64 x 64 |
| grid divisible by cluster | the runtime rejects a cluster launch whose grid is not a multiple of the cluster in every dimension; this is `ClusterLauncher::check_cluster_dims` (`cluster_launch.hpp:103-112`) at compile time | `cudaLaunchKernelExC` would fail at run time |
| cluster size `<= 32` | `MaxClusterSize = 32` (`cluster_launch.hpp:82`) | same |
| `K % 64 == 0`, `K / 64 == 128` | the documented loop shape: `kPrologueKTiles = kStages = 8` and the `8 + 120` split of the producer's two `load_ktiles` calls (`explicit.cu:788-791`), and the k-tile counters of the MMA warp, all assume 128 full 64-wide k-tiles. The device nevertheless computes `k_tiles = (params.k + 63) >> 6` at run time (`explicit.cu:1112`), and the host guard rejects any `k != 8192` (`:1268`), so the assert protects the documented shape, not the kernel's correctness for other multiples of 64 | with `K % 64 != 0` the last k-tile would be a partial box: TMA zero-fills the out-of-bounds elements (numerically correct) but `k_tiles` and the loop split would differ from the documented ones; with `K / 64 != 128` the 8 + 120 figures in every comment would be wrong |
| 32 x 32 cluster tiles | the `tiles_*` guard values | mismatch with the scheduler's `problem_tiles_*` |
| `kSmemBytes <= 232448` | 232448 B = 227 KiB is the maximum opt-in dynamic shared memory on the B200 (measured, note Section 0) | the `MaxDynamicSharedMemorySize` attribute call would fail |

### 5.2.4 `status_from_cuda` (`util.hpp:51-53`)

`cudaSuccess -> kSuccess`, anything else `-> kInvalid`. This is exactly `Return_Status` in `cluster_launch.hpp:73-78` (the `NDEBUG` form, which `Release` selects), used by `ClusterLauncher::init` (`cluster_launch.hpp:144`). `run()` then collapses `kInvalid` to `kErrorInternal` the way `GemmUniversalAdapter::run()` does (`gemm_universal_adapter.h:564-574`), so the harness's `CUTLASS_CHECK` (`examples/common/helper.h:43-52`) prints the same status strings for the same failures. The macro `EXPLICIT_GEMM_TRACE_PRINTF` (`util.hpp:57-61`) is defined but unused; it is kept so that the header's contract matches the plan (note, Section F.2 item 12).

## 5.3 `explicit.hpp`, line by line

The whole file:

```cpp
/***************************************************************************************************
 * Declarations of the explicit (de-abstracted) Blackwell FP16 GEMM of example 70
 * (Part E.2.2 of examples/70_blackwell_gemm/Semantics-preserving-de-abstraction.md).
 *
 * This header is included by both 70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.cu (the harness) and
 * 70_blackwell_fp16_gemm_explicit.cu (the kernel).  It holds
 *   - ExplicitGemmParams: the plain-old-data parameter block of the explicit kernel (the ABI between the
 *     two translation units), passed __grid_constant__;
 *   - the declaration of explicit_gemm::run(ExplicitGemmParams const&), defined in the .cu;
 *   - the template bridge make_params(gemm) / run(gemm) that copies the driver-encoded tensor maps, the
 *     problem shape, alpha and beta out of gemm.params() after the unchanged gemm.initialize().
 * Rules (E.2.2): no __device__/__global__ code, no CUTLASS/CuTe include other than cutlass/cutlass.h and
 * cute/container/tuple.hpp, no non-inline non-template definition (no -rdc: both TUs include this file).
 *
 * Legend (as in the .cu): [PROD] production, [HOST] host-side, [CHECK] compile-time verification, [TRACE] toggle-on only.
 * Everything in this header is [HOST] [PROD] except the two [TRACE] declarations under CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE.
 *
 * Byte map of ExplicitGemmParams (CUDA 13.3: alignof(CUtensorMap) = 128, sizeof = 640; CUDA 12.x: 64 and 576; the [CHECK] asserts below
 * pin every offset the device reads, so both are valid):
 *     0  tma_a   128 B   CUtensorMap of A      (device: prefetch + TMA loads, warp 2)
 *   128  tma_b   128 B   CUtensorMap of B      (device: prefetch + TMA loads, warp 2)
 *   256  tma_c   128 B   CUtensorMap of C      (device: prefetch only; beta = 0 means C is never read)
 *   384  tma_d   128 B   CUtensorMap of D      (device: TMA stores, warp 4)
 *   512  m, n    516 n   520  k   524  l       (device reads only k: ld.param.b32 [+520]; k_tiles = (k + 63) >> 6 = 128)
 *   528  alpha   532  beta                     (device: ld.param.v2.b32 [+528]; the epilogue's FMUL / FFMA operands)
 *   536  mode  540  raster_order  544  swizzle_divisor  548  tiles_m  552  tiles_n  556  tiles_l   (host guards only)
 *   560  alpha_ptr  568  beta_ptr              (host guards only: must be null)
 *   576  end of the fields; padded to 640 (or 576) by the CUtensorMap alignment. In SASS the block starts at c[0x0][0x380],
 *        so k is c[0x0][0x588], alpha/beta c[0x0][0x590]/[0x594] and CONSTANT[0] = 0x380 + 640 = 1536 (G.3).
 **************************************************************************************************/
#pragma once

#include <cuda.h>                        // CUtensorMap
#include <cstddef>                       // offsetof
#include <cstdint>
#include <utility>                       // std::declval

#include "cutlass/cutlass.h"             // cutlass::Status
#include "cute/container/tuple.hpp"      // cute::get<i>(p.problem_shape)

#include "70_blackwell_fp16_gemm_explicit_util.hpp"

namespace explicit_gemm {

// [PROD]  The kernel parameter block.  Passed by value as `const __grid_constant__`, so the device reads
// tma_a/tma_b/tma_d (and prefetches tma_c) from parameter space (constant bank 0), k, alpha and beta once at
// entry (E.6.3 step 2).  The remaining fields are host-only validation data for the guards of E.5.1 and are
// never read on the device.  Field order: maps first (64/128-byte aligned), then the scalars.
struct ExplicitGemmParams {
  CUtensorMap tma_a;        // A, encoded by gemm.initialize(): FLOAT16, (K, M, L), box (64, 64, 1), SWIZZLE_128B (Section 5.3)
  CUtensorMap tma_b;        // B, likewise (K, N, L)
  CUtensorMap tma_c;        // C, FLOAT32, (M, N, L), box (32, 16, 1), SWIZZLE_128B_ATOM_32B; prefetched only (beta = 0)
  CUtensorMap tma_d;        // D, likewise; the store descriptor
  int   m, n, k, l;         // problem shape from p.problem_shape; the device reads only k (k_tiles = (k + 63) >> 6)
  float alpha, beta;        // run-time scalars (Section 0): p.epilogue.thread.op_2.op_0.scalars[0], p.epilogue.thread.op_0.scalars[0]
  // ---- host-only validation fields (E.5.1); never read on the device ----
  int   mode;               // int(p.mode), must be kModeGemm (0)
  int   raster_order;       // int(p.scheduler.raster_order_), must be kRasterOrderAlongN (1)
  int   swizzle_divisor;    // p.scheduler.divmod_swizzle_size_.divisor, must be 0 (swizzle disabled)
  unsigned tiles_m, tiles_n, tiles_l;   // p.scheduler.problem_tiles_m_/n_/l_, must be 32, 32, 1
  float const* alpha_ptr;   // p.epilogue.thread.op_2.op_0.scalar_ptrs[0], must be nullptr (no pointer path in the explicit kernel)
  float const* beta_ptr;    // p.epilogue.thread.op_0.scalar_ptrs[0], must be nullptr
};

// [CHECK] the ABI between the two translation units: offsets the device reads, and the two admissible sizes
static_assert(alignof(CUtensorMap) >= 64, "CUtensorMap must be at least 64-byte aligned (E.9 item 15: 64 in CUDA 12.x headers, 128 in CUDA 13 headers)");
static_assert(sizeof(CUtensorMap) == 128, "CUtensorMap is 128 bytes (copy_sm90_desc.hpp:292)");
static_assert(offsetof(ExplicitGemmParams, tma_a) == 0 && offsetof(ExplicitGemmParams, tma_b) == 1 * sizeof(CUtensorMap) &&
              offsetof(ExplicitGemmParams, tma_c) == 2 * sizeof(CUtensorMap) && offsetof(ExplicitGemmParams, tma_d) == 3 * sizeof(CUtensorMap),
              "the four maps are contiguous at the front of the parameter block");
static_assert(offsetof(ExplicitGemmParams, m) == 4 * sizeof(CUtensorMap) && offsetof(ExplicitGemmParams, k) == 4 * sizeof(CUtensorMap) + 8 &&
              offsetof(ExplicitGemmParams, alpha) == 4 * sizeof(CUtensorMap) + 16 && offsetof(ExplicitGemmParams, beta) == 4 * sizeof(CUtensorMap) + 20,
              "scalar field offsets");
static_assert(sizeof(ExplicitGemmParams) == 576 || sizeof(ExplicitGemmParams) == 640,
              "expected 4 x 128 + 12 x 4 + 2 x 8 = 576 bytes (640 if alignof(CUtensorMap) is 128); E.2.2 [confirm at first build]");
static_assert(sizeof(ExplicitGemmParams) <= 4096, "kernel parameter block limit");

// [HOST] [PROD]  The host function (E.5): mirrors GemmUniversalAdapter::run() for the explicit kernel.  Defined in
// 70_blackwell_fp16_gemm_explicit.cu.  Declared before the template so that the unqualified call below finds it.
cutlass::Status run(ExplicitGemmParams const& params);

#if defined(CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE)
// [HOST] [TRACE]  Toggle-on host entry points (E.7.3), defined in 70_blackwell_fp16_gemm_explicit.cu and called only by the harness's
// guarded blocks: trace_begin resets/arms the kernel TU's record buffer, runs the K0 probe kernel and sentinel-fills D
// (E.7.2 B3); trace_end runs H3 on the explicit kernel, dumps the records, disables recording before the timed launches
// and prints the B4 mismatch dump if the compare failed.  Declarations only (no definition in this shared header, E.2.2).
void trace_begin(void* d_ptr, size_t d_bytes);
void trace_end(char const* csv_path, bool passed, float const* d_ptr, float const* ref_d_ptr, int m, int n);
#endif

// [HOST] [PROD]  Bridge: read the CUTLASS Params object that gemm.initialize() built (public accessor
// GemmUniversalAdapter::params(), gemm_universal_adapter.h:226-228) into the explicit parameter block.
// Instantiated only in the harness TU, where Gemm and every CUTLASS header are visible.  Member paths: E.1.1.
// This is the only place where CUTLASS types are touched on the explicit path: the six tensor maps were encoded by
// gemm.initialize() (cuTensorMapEncodeTiled, Section 5.3) and are copied here as 128-byte opaque blobs; the four
// integers of the problem shape and the two scalars are copied out of the epilogue's fusion tree. Expected values for the
// fixed run: m = n = k = 8192, l = 1, alpha = 1.0f, beta = 0.0f, mode 0 (kGemm), raster_order 1 (AlongN), swizzle_divisor 0,
// tiles (32, 32, 1), both pointers null (E.5.1 rejects anything else).
template <class Gemm, class = decltype(std::declval<Gemm const&>().params())>
ExplicitGemmParams make_params(Gemm const& gemm) {
  auto const& p = gemm.params();
  ExplicitGemmParams e{};
  e.tma_a = p.mainloop.tma_load_a.tma_desc_;            // Copy_Traits<SM100_TMA_2SM_LOAD_MULTICAST,...>::tma_desc_ (public)
  e.tma_b = p.mainloop.tma_load_b.tma_desc_;            // Copy_Traits<SM100_TMA_2SM_LOAD,...>::tma_desc_
  e.tma_c = p.epilogue.tma_load_c.tma_desc_;            // Copy_Traits<SM90_TMA_LOAD,...>::tma_desc_
  e.tma_d = p.epilogue.tma_store_d.tma_desc_;           // Copy_Traits<SM90_TMA_STORE,...>::tma_desc_
  e.m = cute::get<0>(p.problem_shape);
  e.n = cute::get<1>(p.problem_shape);
  e.k = cute::get<2>(p.problem_shape);
  e.l = cute::get<3>(p.problem_shape);
  // Sm90LinearCombination tree: op_0 = beta broadcast, op_1 = C fetch, op_2 = (alpha * acc) tree whose op_0 is the
  // alpha broadcast, op_3 = multiply_add (sm90_callbacks_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:182-213,
  // sm90_visitor_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:711-714, 1192-1197; Sm90ScalarBroadcast::Params = Arguments
  // {scalars[1], scalar_ptrs[1], dScalar[1]}, sm90_visitor_load_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:1017-1023).
  e.beta      = p.epilogue.thread.op_0.scalars[0];
  e.beta_ptr  = p.epilogue.thread.op_0.scalar_ptrs[0];
  e.alpha     = p.epilogue.thread.op_2.op_0.scalars[0];
  e.alpha_ptr = p.epilogue.thread.op_2.op_0.scalar_ptrs[0];
  e.mode            = static_cast<int>(p.mode);
  e.raster_order    = static_cast<int>(p.scheduler.raster_order_);
  e.swizzle_divisor = static_cast<int>(p.scheduler.divmod_swizzle_size_.divisor);
  e.tiles_m = p.scheduler.problem_tiles_m_;
  e.tiles_n = p.scheduler.problem_tiles_n_;
  e.tiles_l = p.scheduler.problem_tiles_l_;
  return e;
}

// [HOST] [PROD]  What the harness calls in place of gemm.run() (E.4): the same params_ snapshot that run() would have used.
template <class Gemm, class = decltype(std::declval<Gemm const&>().params())>
cutlass::Status run(Gemm const& gemm) {
  return run(make_params(gemm));
}

} // namespace explicit_gemm
```

### 5.3.1 The parameter block as bytes

With the CUDA 13.3 headers `alignof(CUtensorMap) = 128` (measured: `sizeof(ExplicitGemmParams) = 640` and `CONSTANT[0] = 0x380 + 640 = 1536`, note G.3). The layout is then:

```
offset  size  field            device use                                   host use
------  ----  ---------------  -------------------------------------------  -----------------------------
   0    128   tma_a            prefetch.tensormap; cp.async.bulk.tensor A    copied from p.mainloop.tma_load_a
 128    128   tma_b            prefetch.tensormap; cp.async.bulk.tensor B    copied from p.mainloop.tma_load_b
 256    128   tma_c            prefetch.tensormap only (beta = 0)            copied from p.epilogue.tma_load_c
 384    128   tma_d            cp.async.bulk.tensor stores of D              copied from p.epilogue.tma_store_d
 512      4   m                -                                             guard  == 8192
 516      4   n                -                                             guard  == 8192
 520      4   k                ld.param.b32 [+520]  -> k_tiles = (k+63)>>6   guard  == 8192
 524      4   l                -                                             guard  == 1
 528      4   alpha            ld.param.v2.b32 [+528] (FMUL operand)         -
 532      4   beta             (same v2 load; FFMA operand)                   guard  == 0.0f
 536      4   mode             -                                             guard  == 0 (kGemm)
 540      4   raster_order     -                                             guard  == 1 (AlongN)
 544      4   swizzle_divisor  -                                             guard  == 0
 548      4   tiles_m          -                                             guard  == 32
 552      4   tiles_n          -                                             guard  == 32
 556      4   tiles_l          -                                             guard  == 1
 560      8   alpha_ptr        -                                             guard  == nullptr
 568      8   beta_ptr         -                                             guard  == nullptr
 576     64   tail padding     sizeof rounds up to a multiple of alignof(CUtensorMap) = 128  -> 640
```

How the numbers fall out: four 128-byte maps are 512 bytes; twelve 4-byte fields are 48 bytes (512..560); `alpha_ptr` needs 8-byte alignment and 560 is a multiple of 8, so there is no gap; two pointers end at 576; `sizeof` must be a multiple of the struct's alignment (that of its most-aligned member, `CUtensorMap`), so 576 rounds to 640 under 128-byte alignment and stays 576 under 64-byte alignment. The `static_assert` at `explicit.hpp:74-75` admits both, and the offset asserts at `:68-73` pin the offsets of everything the device reads, the four 128-byte maps at 0/128/256/384 and the 12 bytes of scalars (`k` at 520, `alpha` and `beta` at 528/532), independent of the alignment, which is what makes the header portable across CUDA 12.x and 13.x. The `<= 4096` assert (`:76`) is a guard against growing the block past the classic kernel-parameter limit (newer toolkits allow larger blocks; the figure is a conservative bound, not a hardware fact).

Measured use on the device (note G.3, PTX inventory of the explicit kernel): exactly two `ld.param` instructions, `ld.param.b32 [+520]` for `k` and `ld.param.v2.b32 [+528]` for `alpha, beta`, plus four `cvta.param` for the map addresses; `m`, `n`, `l` and everything from offset 536 on are never read on the device. In SASS the parameter block starts at `c[0x0][0x380]`, so `alpha, beta` are `LDCU.64 UR26, c[0x0][0x590]` (= 0x380 + 528) and the D map's generic address is formed from the parameter base at `c[0x0][0x348]` plus `0x180` (= 384), measured in note G.3.

Three consequences of that inventory for the field list:

- **The shape never reaches a device instruction.** The single `ld.param.b32 [+520]` feeds `int const k_tiles = (params.k + 63) >> 6;` (`explicit.cu:1112`) = 128; `m`, `n`, `l` exist only so that the host guard can enforce 8192/8192/1 before launching (`explicit.cu:1268`, note E.5.1). Tile coordinates come from CLC responses and `blockIdx`, never from `m`/`n` (Chapter 7).
- **Why each host-only field has the type it has.** `tiles_m/n/l` are `unsigned` because they copy `uint32_t problem_tiles_m_/n_/l_` of `PersistentTileSchedulerSm100Params` (`tile_scheduler_params.h:1845-1847`); `mode` and `raster_order` are `int` casts of `enum class GemmUniversalMode` (`gemm_enumerated_types.h:57-64`) and `enum class RasterOrder` (`tile_scheduler_detail.hpp:38-41`) because the header may not name those CUTLASS types (5.1.1); `swizzle_divisor` is the `int32_t divisor` of a `FastDivmod` (`fast_math.h:327`); `alpha_ptr`/`beta_ptr` are `float const*` because `ElementScalar = float` and `Sm90ScalarBroadcast::Arguments` holds `Element const* scalar_ptrs[1]` (`sm90_visitor_load_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:1017-1023`).
- **What the two pointers mean in the baseline.** When `alpha_ptr`/`beta_ptr` are non-null, `Sm90ScalarBroadcast` loads the scalar from global memory instead of using `scalars[0]` (the baseline PTX tests the pointer and has five `ld.global.b32` sites for that path; note D.6 item 13). The explicit kernel implements only the immediate form, so `run()` returns `kErrorNotSupported` for a non-null pointer (`explicit.cu:1271`); the fields exist to make that refusal explicit rather than silent.

### 5.3.2 Why four `CUtensorMap`s by value, and why `const __grid_constant__`

A TMA instruction (`cp.async.bulk.tensor`) does not take a global pointer to the tensor and a shape; it takes the *address of a 128-byte tensor map* that the driver encoded on the host. The PTX ISA restricts where that object may live: "The tensor-map is a 128-byte opaque object either in .const space or .param (kernel function parameter) space or .global space" (PTX ISA, tensor-map section; see References). The cheapest of the three on the device is `.param`: the block is copied into constant bank 0 by the launch, it is read through the constant cache, and `prefetch.tensormap` warms the cache line ("brings the cache line containing the specified address in the .const or .param memory state space for subsequent use by the cp.async.bulk.tensor instruction", same source). This is exactly what CUTLASS does: `Params` is passed `__grid_constant__` and the device prefetches and issues TMA with the generic address of the parameter-space descriptor (note, Section 5.3, last bullet; `device_kernel.h:118`).

`__grid_constant__` is what makes `&params.tma_a` legal and cheap. The CUDA C++ Programming Guide (5.4 "C/C++ Language Extensions", "`__grid_constant__` Parameters"; see References) states: "Annotating a `__global__` function parameter with `__grid_constant__` prevents the compiler from creating a per-thread copy of the parameter" and "Kernel parameters annotated with `__grid_constant__` must have `const`-qualified non-reference types." Without the annotation, taking the address of a by-value parameter makes the compiler materialise a copy in thread-local memory, because a plain by-value parameter is a modifiable object whose address must be distinct from the read-only parameter bank; this is C++ semantics, not a PTX limitation (PTX has had `cvta.param` since ISA 7.7, so a kernel parameter does have a generic address). With the annotation the parameter is read-only for the whole grid and the compiler emits `cvta.param` to form a generic address that points *into* the parameter bank. The explicit kernel's PTX shows exactly four `cvta.param` (note G.3), one per map, and the SASS forms the `UTMACCTL.PF` and `UTMALDG`/`UTMASTG` map operands from the parameter base `c[0x0][0x348]` plus the map's offset in *this* block, 0x0/0x80/0x100/0x180 (G.3 records the B map as `UIADD3 ..., 0x80` and the D map as `+0x180`; the `+0x80/0x180/0x580/0x680` operands listed in note D.2 belong to the baseline's 2048-byte `Params`). `const` is required by the qualifier.

Why *copies* of the four maps and not the CUTLASS `Params` itself: the baseline's `Params` is 2048 bytes (`.param .align 128 .b8 [2048]`, measured note D.2) because each TMA member is a `Copy_Atom` that embeds the descriptor plus CuTe basis metadata, and it carries six maps (A, B, A-fallback, B-fallback, C, D).
