The explicit kernel needs four opaque blobs and three scalars, so `ExplicitGemmParams` keeps only those; copying the 128-byte blobs out of `gemm.params()` after the unchanged `gemm.initialize()` guarantees the bytes are identical to what the CUTLASS kernel would have used (note, Section 5.3; the fallback maps are byte-identical to the primaries and never touched on the device, note D.1 D3). Field order "maps first" keeps every map at a multiple of its own alignment without padding holes between them (`explicit.hpp:48`).

Why `tma_c` is carried and prefetched although C is never read: the explicit kernel keeps the baseline's four `prefetch.tensormap` sites, A and B by warp 1 and C and D by warp 3, in every CTA regardless of beta (`explicit.cu:1113-1120`; the baseline's are the four `UTMACCTL.PF` of note D.2), so the PTX inventory keeps `prefetch.tensormap` 4 (note G.3) and the instruction stream stays comparable. The prefetch is harmless (one constant-cache line fill in the prologue) and keeps the C map live for a future beta != 0 path. A from-scratch beta = 0 kernel could drop the C map and its prefetch entirely and shrink the block to 512 bytes. Chapter 11 covers the prologue that issues them.

Why `alpha` and `beta` are run-time fields even though the run fixes them to 1 and 0: with compile-time `1.0f`/`0.0f` the compiler would fold `1.0f * acc` to `acc` (an exact IEEE identity) and `fmaf(0.0f, 0.0f, t)` to `+0.0f + t`, removing the per-element `FMUL` + `FFMA` pair that the baseline emits and that fixes the sign of zero (note, Section 0 and D.7 "Arithmetic"). Reading them from the parameter block keeps the baseline's arithmetic form bit for bit (Chapter 10).

### 5.3.3 `make_params`: what `gemm.params()` is and where the members live

`gemm` is a `GemmUniversalAdapter<GemmKernel>`; `gemm.params()` returns `params_`, the `GemmKernel::Params` that `gemm.initialize()` built with `GemmKernel::to_underlying_arguments` (`gemm_universal_adapter.h:226-228` for the accessor, `:328` for the assignment). Its members are (`sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:225-232`):

```cpp
  struct Params {
    GemmUniversalMode mode{};
    ProblemShape problem_shape{};
    MainloopParams mainloop{};
    EpilogueParams epilogue{};
    TileSchedulerParams scheduler{};
    KernelHardwareInfo hw_info{}; 
  };
```

Every member path in `make_params` resolves as follows (all verified in the tree):

| `make_params` expression | Type / definition | Why it is the right member |
|---|---|---|
| `p.mainloop.tma_load_a` | `Params::TMA_A tma_load_a` (`sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp:326`), a `Copy_Atom<Copy_Traits<SM100_TMA_2SM_LOAD_MULTICAST,...>>` | `Copy_Atom<Copy_Traits<Args...>, T>` derives from `Copy_Traits` (`cute/atom/copy_atom.hpp:52`), whose public member is `TmaDescriptor tma_desc_` (`copy_traits_sm100_tma.hpp:165` for the multicast op, `:68` for the plain 2SM op); `TmaDescriptor = CUtensorMap` (`copy_sm90_desc.hpp:292`) |
| `p.mainloop.tma_load_b` | `Params::TMA_B tma_load_b` (`:327`) | same, non-multicast op |
| `p.epilogue.tma_load_c`, `p.epilogue.tma_store_d` | `struct Params { FusionCallbacks::Params thread{}; TMA_C tma_load_c; TMA_D tma_store_d; }` (`sm100_epilogue_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:286-292`) | `TMA_C`/`TMA_D` are `TiledCopy`s, and `TiledCopy : Copy_Atom` (`copy_atom.hpp:188`), so `.tma_desc_` is reachable (`copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp:116` for `SM90_TMA_LOAD`, `:376` for `SM90_TMA_STORE`) |
| `cute::get<i>(p.problem_shape)` | `ProblemShape = Shape<int,int,int,int>` (harness line 151) | the fourth mode is `L = 1` |
| `p.epilogue.thread.op_0.scalars[0]` | beta | see the tree below |
| `p.epilogue.thread.op_2.op_0.scalars[0]` | alpha | see the tree below |
| `p.mode` | `GemmUniversalMode` | `kGemm = 0` |
| `p.scheduler.raster_order_`, `.divmod_swizzle_size_.divisor`, `.problem_tiles_m_/n_/l_` | `PersistentTileSchedulerSm100Params` (`tile_scheduler_params.h:1845-1852`) | the fields the CLC scheduler would read on the device; the explicit kernel hard-codes their values and the host guard checks them |

The fusion tree is the one place where the member path is not obvious. The epilogue's `FusionCallbacks::Params` is the `Params` of `Sm90LinearCombination` (`sm90_callbacks_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:182-190`):

```
Sm90EVT< multiply_add,                       // node op  -> op_3   : d = beta * c + (alpha * acc)
         Sm90ScalarBroadcast (beta),         // child 0  -> op_0   : scalars[0] = beta, scalar_ptrs[0] = beta_ptr
         Sm90SrcFetch (C),                   // child 1  -> op_1
         Sm90EVT< multiplies,                // child 2  -> op_2   : the (alpha * acc) subtree
                  Sm90ScalarBroadcast (alpha),//   child 0 -> op_2.op_0 : scalars[0] = alpha
                  Sm90AccFetch > >            //   child 1 -> op_2.op_1
```

`Sm90EVT = Sm90TreeVisitor<NodeOp, ChildOps...>` derives from `Sm90VisitorImpl<ChildOps..., NodeOp>` (`sm90_visitor_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:711-714`): children *before* the node op, so `Params` is `{op_0, op_1, op_2, op_3}` (`:1192-1197`) with `op_0` = beta and `op_3` = the multiply-add. `Sm90ScalarBroadcast::Params = Arguments = {scalars[1], scalar_ptrs[1], dScalar[1]}` (`sm90_visitor_load_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:1017-1023`). Hence beta is `op_0.scalars[0]` and alpha is `op_2.op_0.scalars[0]`: the counter-intuitive order (beta first) is a direct consequence of the tree shape. The two `scalar_ptrs` are copied only so that the host guard can reject the pointer form, which the explicit kernel does not implement (the baseline compiles that path and never takes it; note D.6 item 13).

Why a template with a SFINAE default argument (`class = decltype(std::declval<Gemm const&>().params())`): the header must not name the CUTLASS `Gemm` type (that would drag the whole CUTLASS tree into the kernel TU and break the "device code in one TU, CuTe only for the swizzle check" rule). A template is instantiated only where it is called, i.e. in the harness TU, where `Gemm` is complete. The default argument makes the overload disappear for any `Gemm` without `params()`, so `run(ExplicitGemmParams const&)` and `run(Gemm const&)` never collide. `run(ExplicitGemmParams const&)` is declared *before* the template (`explicit.hpp:80`) so that the unqualified `run(make_params(gemm))` inside the template finds it by ordinary lookup at definition time.

### 5.3.4 `run(gemm)`: the harness-facing wrapper

`run(Gemm const&)` is a two-liner because the semantics must be "the same `params_` snapshot `gemm.run()` would have used": `gemm.run()` reads `params_` (`gemm_universal_adapter.h`, the non-static `run` forwards `params_`), and `make_params` reads the same `params_` through `params()`. Nothing is synchronised, nothing is re-encoded; the cost is a 640-byte struct copy per call (Chapter 11 covers the body of `run(ExplicitGemmParams const&)`).

## 5.4 The harness side: two call sites, one timed loop, six encodes

### 5.4.1 The two call sites

The harness's `run<Gemm>(options)` (lines 384-455) is unchanged except for the two lines that launched the CUTLASS kernel:

```
$ sed -n 410,416p 70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.cu
  CUTLASS_CHECK(gemm.initialize(arguments, workspace.get()));
#if defined(CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE)
  trace_host_probes<Gemm>(gemm);   // C.4.1: H1 types/sizes/offsets, H2 tensor maps, H5 build macros
#endif

  // Correctness / Warmup iteration
  CUTLASS_CHECK(explicit_gemm::run(gemm));
$ sed -n 435,441p 70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.cu
    GpuTimer timer;
    timer.start();
    for (int iter = 0; iter < options.iterations; ++iter) {
      CUTLASS_CHECK(gemm.initialize(arguments, workspace.get()));
      CUTLASS_CHECK(explicit_gemm::run(gemm));
    }
    timer.stop();
```

Line 416 is the warm-up/correctness launch whose output `verify()` compares against the reference GEMM (line 420); line 439 is the timed launch, ten iterations by default. Both must change together: if only line 439 were changed, `verify()` would validate the *CUTLASS* kernel's `D`, and the explicit kernel's module load and first launch would fall inside the timed interval (note, Section E.4). The whole sequence of `run<Gemm>`:

```
initialize(options)                       harness :318-334   fill A, B, C (integers in [-8, 8], seeds 2023/2022/2021), allocate D, ref_D
Gemm gemm;                                :395
arguments = args_from_options(options)    :398               {kGemm, {m,n,k,1}, {A,dA,B,dB}, {{alpha,beta},C,dC,D,dD}}
Gemm::get_workspace_size(arguments)       :401               0
gemm.can_implement(arguments)             :407               K % 8 == 0, M % 4 == 0 (note, Section 3)
gemm.initialize(arguments, workspace)     :410               6 x cuTensorMapEncodeTiled + cudaFuncSetAttribute (5.4.2)
explicit_gemm::run(gemm)                  :416               warm-up: make_params + launch (Chapter 11)
verify(options)                           :420               reference GEMM + exact compare, cudaDeviceSynchronize
timer.start(); 10 x { initialize; explicit_gemm::run } ; timer.stop()   :436-441
```

### 5.4.2 What `gemm.initialize()` still does, every iteration

`GemmUniversalAdapter::initialize` (`gemm_universal_adapter.h:312-355`) does three things: `GemmKernel::initialize_workspace`, `params_ = GemmKernel::to_underlying_arguments(args, workspace)`, and, because `SharedStorageSize = 230400 >= 48 KiB`, `cudaFuncSetAttribute(device_kernel<GemmKernel>, cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize, 230400)` (`:342-347`) on the CUTLASS kernel, which is never launched. `initialize_workspace` is a no-op success here because the workspace is 0 bytes: `GemmKernel::get_workspace_size` (`sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:339-351`) sums the epilogue's and the scheduler's requests, the fusion tree sums its four leaves (`sm90_visitor_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:1236-1247`), each of which returns 0 (`Sm90ScalarBroadcast`, `sm90_visitor_load_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:281-282`, and likewise the fetch and compute nodes), and the CLC scheduler's `Params::get_workspace_size` returns 0 unconditionally (`tile_scheduler_params.h:1988-2002`; only stream-K schedulers need reduction workspace). The harness prints and allocates that 0 (`harness :401`), and `GemmKernel::initialize_workspace` (`:355-375`) forwards to the same two components, which touch no device memory (note B.1.1 item 13: "no device memory touched"). That is why one timed iteration's `initialize()` is pure host work. `to_underlying_arguments` builds (note, Section 5.2):

| Order | Encoded map | Built by | Used by the explicit kernel? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `tma_load_a` | `make_tma_atom_A_sm100` (`sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp:377-383`) | yes (`tma_a`) |
| 2 | `tma_load_b` | `make_tma_atom_B_sm100` (`:385-391`) | yes (`tma_b`) |
| 3 | `tma_load_a_fallback` | same, with the fallback cluster layout (`:393-399`) | no; byte-identical to 1 (measured, note D.1 D3) |
| 4 | `tma_load_b_fallback` | (`:401-407`) | no; byte-identical to 2 |
| 5 | `tma_load_c` | `get_tma_load_c` (`sm100_epilogue_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:309`), built even for beta = 0 | prefetched only (`tma_c`) |
| 6 | `tma_store_d` | `get_tma_store_d` (`:312`) | yes (`tma_d`) |

Each `make_tma_copy_desc` call is one `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled` through the driver-entry-point wrapper plus a `cudaDriverGetVersion` for the version fixup (`copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp:1054-1071`). So one `initialize()` is 6 x {`cudaGetDriverEntryPointByVersion`, `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled`, `cudaDriverGetVersion`} + 1 attribute call = 19 runtime/driver calls, and one timed iteration of the explicit path is those 19 plus the 4 of `explicit_gemm::run` (two attribute calls, the launch, `cudaGetLastError`) = 23, against the baseline's 22 (note, Section E.5.4). None of them synchronises (read from the code; note G.2 C4). That they therefore hide behind the ~0.889 ms kernel from iteration 1 on, leaving only iteration 0's host work exposed in both binaries alike, is **inferred**, not measured (note E.5.4 and B.1.2 step 7 record that it was not measured; `nsys profile --trace=cuda` on the fixed command would verify it). Chapter 12 returns to this.

The driver-version fixup at `copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp:1071-1075` (clear bit 21 of the descriptor's second word when `driver_version <= 13010` and the tensor is smaller than 131072 bytes) cannot trigger here, and both conditions fail independently. `cudaDriverGetVersion` encodes "1000 x major + 10 x minor" (CUDA Runtime API, `cudaDriverGetVersion`: "CUDA 9.2 would be represented by 9020"), so the measured `driver=13030` (note D.1 D3) is CUDA 13.3 and the threshold `13010` means "drivers up to CUDA 13.1"; and the tensors are 8192 x 8192 x 2 B = 134217728 B (A, B) and 8192 x 8192 x 4 B = 268435456 B (C, D), three orders of magnitude above the 131072-byte (128 KiB) threshold.

### 5.4.3 The tensor-map encoder inputs

`cuTensorMapEncodeTiled(&desc, dataType, rank, globalAddress, globalDim, globalStrides + 1, boxDim, elementStrides, interleave, swizzle, l2Promotion, oobFill)` (`copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp:1054-1066`). The inputs for the fixed run (note, Section 5.3; measured as six `TRACE_ENCODE` lines, note D.1 D3):

| Map | dataType | TMA mode order (innermost first) | globalDim | globalStrides (bytes, modes 1..2) | boxDim | elementStrides | swizzle |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A, A-fallback | `FLOAT16` | (K, M, L) | (8192, 8192, 1) | (16384, 0) | (64, 64, 1) | (1, 1, 1) | `CU_TENSOR_MAP_SWIZZLE_128B` |
| B, B-fallback | `FLOAT16` | (K, N, L) | (8192, 8192, 1) | (16384, 0) | (64, 64, 1) | (1, 1, 1) | `CU_TENSOR_MAP_SWIZZLE_128B` |
| C | `FLOAT32` | (M, N, L) | (8192, 8192, 1) | (32768, 0) | (32, 16, 1) | (1, 1, 1) | `CU_TENSOR_MAP_SWIZZLE_128B_ATOM_32B` |
| D | `FLOAT32` | (M, N, L) | (8192, 8192, 1) | (32768, 0) | (32, 16, 1) | (1, 1, 1) | `CU_TENSOR_MAP_SWIZZLE_128B_ATOM_32B` |

Common to all six: `CU_TENSOR_MAP_INTERLEAVE_NONE`, `CU_TENSOR_MAP_L2_PROMOTION_L2_128B`, `CU_TENSOR_MAP_FLOAT_OOB_FILL_NONE` (`copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp:1046-1048`). Why each column is what it is:

- **dataType.** The TMA element type, `FLOAT16` for the fp16 operands and `FLOAT32` for the fp32 output; the swizzle span and the box limits are expressed in bytes, so the element size enters everywhere below.
- **Rank 3, and why L is kept.** CUTLASS drops a gmem mode from the tensor map only when its shape is statically `Int<1>` or its stride statically `Int<0>` (`construct_tma_gbasis`, `copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp:813-838`). The harness's strides come from `make_cute_packed_stride(StrideA{}, {m, k, 1})` (harness line 320): `L = 1` and the batch stride 0 are *run-time* `int`/`int64_t` values, so the batch mode survives with extent 1 and stride 0. Consequence on the device: every TMA coordinate is 3-D, and the kernel passes the literal `0` as the third coordinate (`explicit.cu:747-748`, `:754-755`, `:1066`). The driver accepts a literal 0 byte stride (the source asserts only `stride % 16 == 0` and `< 2^40`, `:984-991`; all six encodes returned `CUDA_SUCCESS`, note D.1 D13).
- **Mode order and strides.** Modes are ordered by increasing stride and mode 0's stride is implicit (1 element). A is M x K row-major, so K is innermost: modes (K, M, L) with byte strides (2K = 16384, 0). B is N x K "column-major" in the harness's `LayoutB`, i.e. K-major as well: (K, N, L), (16384, 0). C and D are M x N column-major, i.e. M-major: (M, N, L), (4M = 32768, 0). The 16-byte-multiple rule on strides (driver API) holds trivially.
- **globalDim** is the full tensor, (8192, 8192, 1): TMA clips at these bounds and zero-fills out-of-bounds elements (`OOB_FILL_NONE` means "fill with zeros", not "no fill"; the alternative `NAN_REQUEST_ZERO_FMA` fills NaN). No box is ever out of bounds in this run, so the fill mode is never exercised.
- **boxDim** is the smem image one TMA instruction moves; Section 5.4.4 derives the two shapes.
- **elementStrides** (1, 1, 1): dense boxes, no striding inside the box.
- **Swizzle.** `Swizzle<3,4,3>` (the SW128 K-major atom) maps to `SWIZZLE_128B` = "16-byte chunks within a 128-byte span"; `Swizzle<2,5,2>` (the SW128_32B M-major fp32 atom) maps to `SWIZZLE_128B_ATOM_32B` = "32-byte chunks within a 128-byte span" (`to_CUtensorMapSwizzle`, `copy_sm90_desc.hpp:240-262`; the `ATOM_32B` enumerator exists only for CUDA > 12.6). The TMA unit applies the XOR on write (loads) and undoes it on read (stores), so the kernel never computes `Swizzle<3,4,3>` and computes `Swizzle<2,5,2>` only because it writes the C/D stage itself (Section 5.10).
- **L2 promotion 128 B.** The driver API describes `CUtensorMapL2promotion` as the parameter that "specifies L2 fetch size which indicates the byte granularity at which L2 requests are filled from DRAM" (CUDA Driver API, Tensor Map Object Management; see References); `CU_TENSOR_MAP_L2_PROMOTION_L2_128B` selects 128 bytes, so each 128-byte box row is fetched as whole L2 lines. CUTLASS hard-codes this for every tiled map (`copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp:1047`).
- **Interleave NONE.** The box is a plain dense sub-tensor, not the 32-byte interleaved format.

The encoder's constraints, which you must satisfy when you encode maps for a different operator (CUDA Driver API, `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled`, quoted in the References), and how the six maps meet them:

| Constraint (driver API) | A, B maps | C, D maps |
|---|---|---|
| `tensorMap` "must be aligned to 64 bytes"; the object is 128 bytes | `CUtensorMap` members at offsets 0/128 of a 128-aligned block | 256/384 |
| `globalAddress` "must be 16 byte aligned" | `cudaMalloc` pointers (the CUDA Programming Guide guarantees at least 256-byte alignment) | same |
| `globalDim` entries "must be non-zero and less than or equal to 2^32" | (8192, 8192, 1) | (8192, 8192, 1) |
| `globalStrides` "must be a multiple of 16 and less than 2^40" | 16384, 0 | 32768, 0 |
| `boxDim` entries "must be non-zero and less than or equal to 256" | (64, 64, 1) | (32, 16, 1) |
| inner box dimension in bytes `<= 32` / `<= 64` / `<= 128` for the 32B / 64B / 128B swizzles ("`CU_TENSOR_MAP_SWIZZLE_128B*` require the bounding box inner dimension to be <= 128") | 64 x 2 B = 128 | 32 x 4 B = 128 |
| `elementStrides` entries "must be non-zero and less than or equal to 8" | (1, 1, 1) | (1, 1, 1) |

The inner-dimension rule is the one that shapes both boxes (5.4.4 and 5.4.5): it is why a k-tile is 64 fp16 and why the D box is 32 fp32 wide.

### 5.4.4 The two box-truncation rules

Both boxes are *smaller* than the logical per-CTA tile, for two different reasons.

**A: (64 K, 64 M, 1), from the multicast split.** The per-CTA A stage is logically (64 K, 128 M) = 16384 bytes. But `make_tma_atom_A_sm100` passes `num_multicast = size<2>(cluster_vmnk) = 2` because the op is `SM100_TMA_2SM_LOAD_MULTICAST` (`copy_traits_sm100_tma.hpp:754-758`: "Use only the N-CTAs in the Multicast"), and `make_tma_copy_desc` divides the box by the multicast count starting from the *last* mode (`copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp:1003-1009`):

```
for (i = tma_dim-1, multicast = 2; multicast > 1; --i):      i = 2 (L): box 1   -> ceil_div(1, 2) = 1, multicast = ceil_div(2, 1) = 2 (nothing absorbed)
    new_mult = ceil_div(multicast, box[i])                     i = 1 (M): box 128 -> ceil_div(128, 2) = 64, multicast = ceil_div(2, 128) = 1 (stop)
    box[i]   = ceil_div(box[i], multicast)                     result: (64, 64, 1) = 8192 bytes
    multicast = new_mult
```

The two CTAs that share a `tm` (ranks `x` and `x + 2`, same `x`, different `y`) each load a different 64-row half (rows `128 tm + 64 y .. +64`) and multicast it to both, so each CTA still receives the full 128 x 64 stage while issuing only half the bytes (Chapter 8). The destination offset of the half is `+ 8192 y` inside the 16384-byte stage (`explicit.cu:768`). This split is only legal because 64 rows is a multiple of the 8-row swizzle atom: the SW128 pattern XORs the 16-byte chunk index with `row % 8`, and `(64 y + r) % 8 == r % 8`, so the half written at `+8192 y` carries exactly the swizzle phase the UMMA descriptor expects for rows `64 y + r` of the stage. The transaction count follows: each CTA's stage receives its own A half (8192 B), the A half multicast by the CTA with the same `x` and the other `y` (rank `r ^ 2`, not the pair peer `r ^ 1`; 8192 B) and its own B box (8192 B); the pair leader's barrier is credited for both CTAs of the pair, 2 x 24576 = 49152 B (`kMainloopTxBytes`, Section 5.9).

**C/D: (32 M, 16 N, 1), from the 128-byte swizzle span.** The epilogue subtile is (128 M, 16 N) fp32 = 8192 bytes, but the box is 2048 bytes. `construct_tma_gbasis` inverts the *non-swizzled* smem stage layout, `((32,4),(4,4)):((1,512),(32,128))` in elements (32 M contiguous, 4 N at stride 32 elements = 128 B, then the next 32-row block at stride 512 elements = 2048 B, then the next 4 columns at stride 128 elements = 512 B), and truncates at the first smem mode whose gmem basis stride is not 1 (`copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp:767` and `:783-787`): after 32 contiguous M elements and 16 N columns, the next M block jumps by 512 elements, which is not a continuation of the M mode, so the box stops at (32, 16). This agrees with the driver's rule that for the 128-byte swizzles the inner box dimension in bytes is at most 128: 32 fp32 = 128 B (driver API doc, `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled`). One `copy(tma_store_d, ...)` of a subtile therefore expands into **four** TMA stores `i = 0..3` with coordinates `(128 tm + 32 i, 128 tn + 16 e, 0)` from smem `stage_base + 2048 i` (`explicit.cu:1053-1066`), 32 stores per CTA tile (note, Section 13 item 14 records that an earlier plan had this wrong).

### 5.4.5 What one TMA box is

A box is a dense sub-tensor in global memory and a *contiguous* image in shared memory whose rows are the innermost dimension (128 bytes here) and whose 16-byte (or 32-byte) chunks are permuted by the swizzle:

```
A box, map A, coordinates (64 q, 128 tm + 64 y, 0): 64 rows of 64 fp16 = 64 x 128 B = 8192 B

global (row-major A, K contiguous)                 smem image (SWIZZLE_128B): line r at +128 r,
row 128tm+64y+r, k = 64q .. 64q+63                 16-byte chunk c of the row stored at chunk position c ^ (r % 8)
       k = 64q         ...        64q+63           position:  0  1  2  3  4  5  6  7
 r=0  [c0 c1 c2 c3 c4 c5 c6 c7]                     r=0      [c0 c1 c2 c3 c4 c5 c6 c7]
 r=1  [c0 c1 c2 c3 c4 c5 c6 c7]                     r=1      [c1 c0 c3 c2 c5 c4 c7 c6]
 r=2  [c0 c1 c2 c3 c4 c5 c6 c7]                     r=2      [c2 c3 c0 c1 c6 c7 c4 c5]
 ...                                                ...
 r=7  [c0 c1 c2 c3 c4 c5 c6 c7]                     r=7      [c7 c6 c5 c4 c3 c2 c1 c0]
 r=8  (same as r=0)                                 r=8      [c0 c1 c2 c3 c4 c5 c6 c7]   (period 8 lines = 1024 B = one swizzle atom)
 ...
 r=63

D box, map D, coordinates (128 tm + 32 i, 128 tn + 16 e, 0): 16 columns of 32 fp32 = 16 x 128 B = 2048 B

global (column-major D, M contiguous)              smem image (SWIZZLE_128B_ATOM_32B): line n at +128 n,
column 128tn+16e+n, m = 128tm+32i .. +31           32-byte chunk q of the line stored at chunk position q ^ (n % 4)
       m -> 32 values                              position:  0  1  2  3
 n=0  [q0 q1 q2 q3]                                 n=0      [q0 q1 q2 q3]
 n=1  [q0 q1 q2 q3]                                 n=1      [q1 q0 q3 q2]
 n=2  [q0 q1 q2 q3]                                 n=2      [q2 q3 q0 q1]
 n=3  [q0 q1 q2 q3]                                 n=3      [q3 q2 q1 q0]
 n=4  (same as n=0)                                 n=4      [q0 q1 q2 q3]   (period 4 lines = 512 B = one swizzle atom)
 ...
 n=15
```

Three things to internalise, because they drive the Section 1 constants: (1) a box row is at most the swizzle span, so the k-tile is 64 fp16 and the D box's M extent is 32 fp32; (2) the swizzle period is 1024 B (SW128) or 512 B (SW128_32B), which is why the A/B stage bases must be 1024-byte aligned and the C/D stage bases 512-byte aligned (`explicit.cu:162-163`): the hardware computes the XOR from the *absolute* shared address bits, so a misaligned base would shift the pattern; (3) the swizzle is a pure permutation of chunks inside a line, so byte totals and transaction counts are unaffected.

## 5.5 `explicit.cu` Section 1, group 1: configuration constants

```
$ sed -n 104,120p explicit.cu
constexpr uint32_t kThreads       = kBlockThreads;   // 8 warps: 0 MMA, 1 Sched (rank 0), 2 MainloopLoad, 3 EpilogueLoad (exits), 4-7 Epilogue
constexpr int      kMmaM          = 256, kMmaN = 128, kMmaK = 16;   // one tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2 per k-block
constexpr int      kKBlocks       = kTileK / kMmaK;                 // 4 MMAs per k-tile
constexpr int      kStages        = 8;               // A/B smem pipeline (Section 4)
constexpr int      kAccStages     = 4;               // TMEM accumulator pipeline, 128 columns each
constexpr int      kClcStages     = 2;               // CLC response slots
constexpr int      kThrottleStages= 2;
constexpr int      kEpiStages     = 4;               // 8192-byte C/D smem stages (reused, ReuseSmemC)
constexpr int      kEpiSubtiles   = 8;               // 128x16 subtiles per 128x128 tile
constexpr int      kEpiTileN      = 16;
constexpr uint32_t kTmemColumns   = 512;             // tcgen05.alloc / dealloc column count
constexpr int      kPrologueKTiles= kStages;         // first load() call covers min(8, k_tiles) k-tiles (kernel :629)
constexpr uint32_t kStageBytesA   = 128 * 64 * 2;    // 16384
constexpr uint32_t kStageBytesAHalf = kStageBytesA / 2;   // 8192: one CTA's 64-row half of the 128x64 A stage (B.4); equal to kStageBytesB by coincidence of the tile shape
constexpr uint32_t kStageBytesB   = 64 * 64 * 2;     // 8192
constexpr uint32_t kEpiStageBytes = 128 * 16 * 4;    // 8192
constexpr uint32_t kStoreBoxBytes = 32 * 16 * 4;     // 2048: the D map's box is (32 M, 16 N, 1) (Section 5.3)
```

| Constant | Value | Why this value (derived unless marked) |
|---|---|---|
| `kThreads` | 256 | 8 warps, one role each: 0 MMA, 1 scheduler (rank 0 only), 2 mainloop producer, 3 epilogue-load (exits for beta = 0), 4-7 epilogue. Warp-specialised kernels give each asynchronous engine (TMA, tensor core, TMEM readers) its own warp so that no warp ever waits on two engines (Chapter 4) |
| `kMmaM, kMmaN, kMmaK` | 256, 128, 16 | The atom `SM100_MMA_F16BF16_2x1SM_SS` with `Shape_MNK (256,128,16)` (measured, note D.1 D1; `mma_sm100_umma.hpp:552`). M = 256 is the largest `cta_group::2` M (the `m_dim` field admits 64, 128, 256, `mma_sm100_desc.hpp:435`), and the pair's two 128-row CTA tiles stack into it; N = 128 is the CTA tile N, assembled from the two CTAs' 64-column B halves; K = 16 fp16 is the atom's fixed K for `kind::f16` (one 32-byte slice of a 128-byte smem row) |
| `kKBlocks` | 4 | 64 / 16: four MMAs per k-tile, each advancing the descriptor start address by 32 B (Section 5.8) |
| `kStages` | 8 | The builder's carveout formula (note, Section 6.1): `floor((232448 - 192 - 33792) / 24592) = floor(198464 / 24592) = 8`, where 232448 is the opt-in smem, 192 the kernel-level barrier carveout, 33792 the epilogue storage and 24592 = 16384 (A) + 8192 (B) + 16 (one `PipelineTmaUmmaAsync<1>` storage) per stage (`sm100_umma_builder.inl:84-99`). Depth 8 is what fits, not a tuned number; Chapter 3 shows it covers the TMA latency with margin |
| `kAccStages` | 4 | the 2SM branch of the builder: `AccumulatorPipelineStageCount_ = TotalTmem / (CtaTileM x CtaTileN) = (128 x 512) / (128 x 128) = 65536 / 16384 = 4`, then `AccumulatorPipelineStageCount = min(4u, 4) = 4` (`sm100_umma_builder.inl:260-267`). Numerically the same as 512 / 128 only because the CTA tile has 128 rows = `TotalTmemRows`; the 1SM M = 64 case takes a different branch, `(512 / CtaTileN) x 2`. The whole 512-column TMEM is sliced into four 128 x 128 fp32 accumulators so the MMA warp can run up to 3 tiles ahead of the epilogue |
| `kClcStages` | 2 | `SchedulerPipelineStageCount = 2` (`sm100_umma_builder.inl:282`): two 16-byte CLC response slots; one query in flight while the previous response is consumed (Chapter 7) |
| `kThrottleStages` | 2 | the throttle pipeline reuses the scheduler's stage count (`sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp:82`) |
| `kEpiStages` | 4 | `StagesC = ReuseSmem ? max(min(EpiTiles, 4), StagesD + 1) : min(EpiTiles, 4)` with `EpiTiles = 8`, `StagesD = min(8, 2) = 2`, `ReuseSmem = (sizeof_bits(C) = 32) > 8` (`sm100_builder.inl:1109-1115`): `max(4, 3) = 4` reused C/D stages of 8192 B |
| `kEpiSubtiles` | 8 | 128 / 16 subtiles per 128 x 128 tile |
| `kEpiTileN` | 16 | `EpilogueTileAuto` -> (128, 16) (`sm100_builder.inl:999-1046`). `M = min(CtaM, 32 x WarpM) = min(128, 32 x 4) = 128`, with `TmemWarpShape_MN = (4, 1)` for a 2SM atom whose MMA M is 256 (`:1074-1079`). `N_perf` takes the *residual-load* branch because `DisableSource = is_void_v<ElementC> = false` (`:984`; `ElementC = float` even though beta = 0 at run time), and in that branch `MaxBits = 32`, `CtaM > 64`, `CtaN <= 128` give 16 (`:1024-1025`). `N_min_C = N_min_D = 8 x WarpN = 8` because C and D are M-major (`:1039-1042`). `N_tmp = min(128, max(16, 8, 8)) = 16`, and `128 % 16 == 0`, so `N = 16` (`:1045-1046`). 16 fp32 columns = one `tcgen05.ld.32x32b.x16` per lane. With `ElementC = void` the same formulas give `N_perf = 4096 / 128 = 32` (`:1018-1019`): an EpilogueTile (128, 32), 4 subtiles of 16384 B, and a re-derived C/D stage count (my reading of the same code) |
| `kTmemColumns` | 512 | the whole TMEM: on sm_100a/sm_100f it has "a two-dimensional structure of 512 columns and 128 rows per CTA, with each cell being 32-bits in size" (PTX ISA 9.7.18.1), 256 KiB per SM; the pair allocates all of it with one `cta_group::2` alloc. The count is constrained by the ISA: "The unit of allocation is 32 columns and the number of columns being allocated must be a power of 2" (9.7.18.1.2) and, for `tcgen05.alloc`, "If .exclusive is not specified, the operand nCols must be a power of 2, in the range [32, 512]"; 512 is the maximum |
| `kPrologueKTiles` | 8 | the baseline's `load()` is called twice per tile, first for `min(Stages, k_tiles)` k-tiles and then for the rest (kernel `:657` in the tree, `:629` at cb424739, the number `explicit.cu:115` quotes), originally to interleave the C load between them; with beta = 0 nothing sits between the two calls, but keeping the split keeps the two rolled loops (8 + 120) the baseline's SASS has (note D.7) |
| `kStageBytesA` | 16384 | 128 rows x 64 fp16 x 2 B |
| `kStageBytesAHalf` | 8192 | one CTA's 64-row half (the A box), see 5.4.4. The source comment warns that it is "equal to kStageBytesB by coincidence of the tile shape" (`explicit.cu:117`): 64 x 64 x 2 B (half of the 128-row A stage) equals 64 x 64 x 2 B (the 64-column B half) only because `CtaM / 2 = CtaN / 2 = 64`. With a different tile aspect, say `CtaN = 256` (a 256 x 256 x 16 MMA, the largest `cta_group::2` N), the per-CTA B half would be 128 x 64 x 2 B = 16384 B while the A half stayed 8192 B, so the two constants would differ, which is why the kernel keeps separate names instead of reusing one |
| `kStageBytesB` | 8192 | 64 rows x 64 fp16 x 2 B: the per-CTA B half is 64 N-rows because the pair's MMA N = 128 is split across the two CTAs |
| `kEpiStageBytes` | 8192 | 128 x 16 fp32 x 4 B: one subtile |
| `kStoreBoxBytes` | 2048 | 32 x 16 fp32 x 4 B: one D box, four per subtile |

## 5.6 The LAYOUT comment block, decoded mode by mode

```
$ sed -n 122,135p explicit.cu
// LAYOUT  What the CUTLASS kernel's CuTe types say about the same buffers (TRACE_H1 lines of trace_out_v2/host.txt), for reference;
// this kernel never computes these layouts: the TMA unit writes them (SWIZZLE_128B) and the UMMA unit reads them through the descriptor.
//   SmemLayoutA  = Sw<3,4,3> o ((_128,_16),_1,_4,(_1,_8)) : ((_64,_1),_0,_16,(_0,_8192))   [fp16 elements]
//                  row m of a k-block holds 16 k values at m * 64 + k; the 4 k-blocks of a k-tile are 16 elements (32 B) apart;
//                  stage s is 8192 elements (16384 B) apart; Swizzle<3,4,3>: byte-address bits [4,7) ^= bits [7,10), i.e. the
//                  16-byte chunk inside a 128-byte row is XOR-ed with (row % 8). A row is 64 fp16 = 128 B (K-major, SW128 atom 8 x 64).
//   SmemLayoutB  = Sw<3,4,3> o ((_64,_16),_1,_4,(_1,_8)) : ((_64,_1),_0,_16,(_0,_4096))    [64 N rows per CTA, 8192 B per stage]
//   SmemLayoutAtomC/D = Sw<2,5,2> o (_32,_4) : (_1,_32)                                  [fp32; 32 M x 4 N atom = 512 B, see epilogue_role]
//   TiledMMA     = MMA_Atom SM100_MMA_F16BF16_2x1SM_SS 256x128x16, ThrLayoutVMNK (2,1,1,1); LayoutC_TV (_2,(_128,_128)):(_128,(_1,_256)):
//                  CTA v of the pair owns accumulator rows [128 v, 128 v + 128) of the 256 x 128 MMA tile, i.e. its own 128 x 128 CTA tile.
//   EpilogueTile = (128, 16); TileShape (256, 128, 64) per pair; CtaShape_MNK (128, 128, 64); ClusterShape (2, 2, 1).
//   Tensor maps (TRACE_ENCODE): A, B FLOAT16 dim 3 shape (8192, 8192, 1) stride bytes (16384, 0) box (64, 64, 1) SWIZZLE_128B L2 promotion 128 B;
//                C, D FLOAT32 shape (8192, 8192, 1) stride bytes (32768, 0) box (32, 16, 1) SWIZZLE_128B_ATOM_32B. Coordinates are
//                (innermost, outer, batch): (k, row, 0) for A/B and (m, n, 0) for C/D, in elements.
```

A CuTe layout `Shape : Stride` maps a coordinate to an element index by the dot product of coordinate and stride; `Sw<B,M,S> o L` applies the swizzle to the *offset* that `L` produces (in the units `L` is written in; here the composed layouts are printed in element units but the swizzle is defined on byte-level bit positions, which is why the comment restates it in bytes). Reading each one:

**`SmemLayoutA = Sw<3,4,3> o ((_128,_16),_1,_4,(_1,_8)) : ((_64,_1),_0,_16,(_0,_8192))`** has four modes:

| Mode | Shape | Stride (fp16 elements) | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `(128, 16)` | `(64, 1)` | one MMA atom's A slice: row `m` (0..127), `k` (0..15) within the 16-wide k-block -> `64 m + k`; a row is 64 elements = 128 B (the whole k-tile row), the k-block occupies 16 of them |
| 1 | `1` | `0` | the number of atom tiles along M (1: the atom's per-CTA M of 128 is the CTA tile) |
| 2 | `4` | `16` | the k-block index `kb` (0..3): `+16` elements = `+32` B per k-block |
| 3 | `(1, 8)` | `(0, 8192)` | the stage index `s` (0..7), printed nested; `8192` elements = 16384 B per stage (coalesces to `8:8192`, note D.6 item 18) |

So, in bytes from `OFF_SMEM_A`, before swizzling: `o(m, k, kb, s) = 128 m + 2 k + 32 kb + 16384 s`. `Swizzle<3,4,3>` then XORs bits [4,7) with bits [7,10): `phys = o ^ ((o & 0x380) >> 3)`. Since `128 m` is the only term reaching bits [7,10) within a stage, bits [7,10) are `m % 8`, and the physical byte is

```
phys(m, k, kb, s) = 16384 s + 128 m + 16 * ( ((32 kb + 2 k) >> 4) ^ (m & 7) ) + (2 k & 15)
```

Worked example: `m = 5, k = 3, kb = 2, s = 0`: `o = 640 + 6 + 64 = 710 = 0x2C6`; chunk bits `(0x2C6 >> 4) & 7 = 4`, row bits `(0x2C6 >> 7) & 7 = 5`, new chunk `4 ^ 5 = 1`; `phys = 640 + 16 + 6 = 662 = 0x296`. The kernel never evaluates this: TMA writes the box with exactly this permutation (5.4.5) and the UMMA unit reads it through a descriptor whose `layout_type = SWIZZLE_128B` tells it to apply the same XOR (Section 5.8). The comment exists so that you can check the two sides agree.

**`SmemLayoutB = Sw<3,4,3> o ((_64,_16),_1,_4,(_1,_8)) : ((_64,_1),_0,_16,(_0,_4096))`** is the same with 64 N-rows per CTA, so `o(n, k, kb, s) = 128 n + 2 k + 32 kb + 8192 s` and a stage is 4096 elements = 8192 B.

**`SmemLayoutAtomC/D = Sw<2,5,2> o (_32,_4) : (_1,_32)`** in fp32 elements: element `(m, n)` of the 32 x 4 atom at `m + 32 n`, i.e. byte `4 m + 128 n`; a column of 32 fp32 is one 128-byte line, four lines make the 512-byte atom. `Swizzle<2,5,2>` XORs bits [5,7) (the 32-byte chunk inside the line, `(m >> 3) & 3`) with bits [7,9) (the line index, `n & 3`):

```
phys_atom(m, n) = 4 (m & 7) + 32 * ( ((m >> 3) & 3) ^ (n & 3) ) + 128 n
```

The full 8192-byte stage tiles this atom 4 x along M (stride 2048 B) and 4 x along N (stride 512 B), the non-swizzled `((32,4),(4,4)):((1,512),(32,128))` of 5.4.4, so for `m` in 0..127, `n` in 0..15: `byte(m, n) = 2048 (m >> 5) + 512 (n >> 2) + phys_atom(m & 31, n & 3)`. Substituting `m = 32 w + l` (epilogue warp `w`, lane `l`) and `n = j` gives `2048 w + 4 (l & 7) + 128 (j & 3) + 32 (((l >> 3) & 3) ^ (j & 3)) + 512 (j >> 2)`, which is exactly how the epilogue assembles its store address (Chapter 10): the per-lane table `st_off[c] = OFF_SMEM_CD + 2048u * w + 4u * (l & 7u) + 128u * c + 32u * (((l >> 3) & 3u) ^ c);` for `c = j & 3` (`explicit.cu:1013`), plus `512u * uint32_t(j >> 2)` and the stage term `kEpiStageBytes * uint32_t(e & 3)` added at the store itself (`explicit.cu:1047`).

**`TiledMMA = MMA_Atom SM100_MMA_F16BF16_2x1SM_SS 256x128x16, ThrLayoutVMNK (2,1,1,1)`**: the atom is one 256 x 128 x 16 MMA executed cooperatively by two "threads" (V = the two CTAs of the pair); the tiling repeats it once along M, N and K, so one atom *is* the MMA tile. **`LayoutC_TV (_2,(_128,_128)) : (_128,(_1,_256))`** maps `(v, (m, n))` to `128 v + m + 256 n` in the 256 x 128 accumulator indexed column-major with M stride 1 and N stride 256: CTA `v` owns rows `[128 v, 128 v + 128)`, every column. That is why the pair leader's single `tcgen05.mma` fills both CTAs' TMEM and why each CTA's epilogue only ever reads its own 128 rows (Chapters 9 and 10).

**`EpilogueTile = (128, 16)`**: the subtile moved per TMA store round; **`TileShape (256, 128, 64)`** is the pair's MMA tile per k-tile, **`CtaShape_MNK (128, 128, 64)`** the per-CTA share, **`ClusterShape (2, 2, 1)`** the launch cluster. The last two comment lines restate the tensor maps of 5.4.3 and fix the coordinate convention the kernel uses in every TMA call: `(k, row, 0)` for A/B, `(m, n, 0)` for C/D, in elements, innermost first.

## 5.7 `explicit.cu` Section 1, group 2: the shared-memory map

```
$ sed -n 137,166p explicit.cu
// LAYOUT  Section 6.2 byte offsets from the dynamic shared-memory base (== the CUTLASS SharedStorage layout, TRACE_HOST off_* lines).
// Shared::cta address of anything = smem_base + OFF_* with smem_base = 0x400 + (rank << 24); e.g. rank 2's acc_full[1] is 0x02000400 + 240 + 8.
constexpr uint32_t OFF_MAIN_FULL      =      0;   // 8 x 8 B ClusterTransactionBarrier, count 1
constexpr uint32_t OFF_MAIN_EMPTY     =     64;   // 8 x 8 B ClusterBarrier, count 2
constexpr uint32_t OFF_EPI_LOAD_FULL  =    128;   // 4 x 8 B (beta != 0 only; reserved, not initialised: E.10 item 6)
constexpr uint32_t OFF_EPI_LOAD_EMPTY =    160;   // 4 x 8 B (idem)
constexpr uint32_t OFF_LOAD_ORDER     =    192;   // 2 x 8 B (idem)
constexpr uint32_t OFF_CLC_FULL       =    208;   // 2 x 8 B, count 1 (+16 tx bytes)
constexpr uint32_t OFF_CLC_EMPTY      =    224;   // 2 x 8 B, count 800 (only CTA 0's are used)
constexpr uint32_t OFF_ACC_FULL       =    240;   // 4 x 8 B, count 1
constexpr uint32_t OFF_ACC_EMPTY      =    272;   // 4 x 8 B, count 256
constexpr uint32_t OFF_THROTTLE_FULL  =    304;   // 2 x 8 B, count 32
constexpr uint32_t OFF_THROTTLE_EMPTY =    320;   // 2 x 8 B, count 32
constexpr uint32_t OFF_TMEM_DEALLOC   =    336;   // 1 x 8 B, count 32
constexpr uint32_t OFF_CLC_RESPONSE   =    352;   // 2 x 16 B, alignas(16)
constexpr uint32_t OFF_TMEM_BASE_PTR  =    384;   // 4 B, written by tcgen05.alloc
constexpr uint32_t OFF_SMEM_CD        =    512;   // 4 x 8192 B, Swizzle<2,5,2>, 512-byte aligned
constexpr uint32_t OFF_SMEM_A         =  33792;   // 8 x 16384 B, Swizzle<3,4,3>, 1024-byte aligned
constexpr uint32_t OFF_SMEM_B         = 164864;   // 8 x  8192 B, idem
constexpr uint32_t kSmemBaseLow24     =  0x400;   // measured base (D.1 D5): 0x400 + (rank << 24); computed at run time, never assumed

static_assert(OFF_SMEM_A == OFF_SMEM_CD + kEpiStages * kEpiStageBytes + 512, "Section 6.2 (FusionStorage pad to 512)");
static_assert(OFF_SMEM_B == OFF_SMEM_A + kStages * kStageBytesA, "Section 6.2");
static_assert(kSmemBytes == OFF_SMEM_B + kStages * kStageBytesB, "Section 6.2: SharedStorageSize 230400");
static_assert(kStageBytesAHalf == 64u * 64u * 2u, "one CTA's 64x64 fp16 half of the 128x64 A stage (B.4): TMA box (64, 64, 1)");
static_assert(OFF_SMEM_A % 1024 == 0 && OFF_SMEM_B % 1024 == 0, "SW128 stage bases need 1 KiB alignment (Section 7.5)");
static_assert(OFF_SMEM_CD % 512 == 0, "SW128_32B epilogue stages need 512 B alignment (Section 7.7)");
static_assert(OFF_CLC_RESPONSE % 16 == 0 && OFF_TMEM_BASE_PTR % 4 == 0, "b128 response slots");
static_assert(kSmemBaseLow24 + kSmemBytes < (1u << 18), "14-bit UMMA start-address field spans 256 KiB (B.3.2 step 4)");
static_assert(kThreads == 256 && kMmaM == 256 && kMmaN == 128 && kKBlocks == 4, "Section 4");
```

### 5.7.1 The byte map

The offsets are the CUTLASS `SharedStorage` of `sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:182-212` flattened: a `PipelineStorage` (`aligned_struct<16>`) of all barrier arrays in declaration order, the CLC response slots, the TMEM base word, then `TensorStorage` (epilogue storage first, mainloop storage second). Every barrier is one 8-byte `mbarrier` object (`ClusterBarrier`/`ClusterTransactionBarrier`, `barrier.h`). The map, with every barrier (counts are Section 5.9's; init warps are the prologue's, Chapter 11):

```
offset   size   region / object                            count or alignment           initialised by
------   -----  -----------------------------------------  ---------------------------  --------------------
     0     64   OFF_MAIN_FULL    full[s], s = 0..7, 8 B    1 (+ 49152 tx bytes)         warp 0 (elected lane)
    64     64   OFF_MAIN_EMPTY   empty[s], s = 0..7        2                            warp 0
   128     32   OFF_EPI_LOAD_FULL  [0..3]                  (C-load pipeline, beta != 0)  not initialised
   160     32   OFF_EPI_LOAD_EMPTY [0..3]                  (idem)                       not initialised
   192     16   OFF_LOAD_ORDER   [0..1]                    (idem)                       not initialised
   208     16   OFF_CLC_FULL     full[0..1]                1 (+ 16 tx bytes)            warp 4
   224     16   OFF_CLC_EMPTY    empty[0..1]               800                          warp 4  (only CTA 0's are arrived on)
   240     32   OFF_ACC_FULL     full[st], st = 0..3       1                            warp 5
   272     32   OFF_ACC_EMPTY    empty[st], st = 0..3      256                          warp 5  (only the leader's are arrived on)
   304     16   OFF_THROTTLE_FULL  [0..1]                  32                           warp 3  (rank 0 uses them)
   320     16   OFF_THROTTLE_EMPTY [0..1]                  32                           warp 3
   336      8   OFF_TMEM_DEALLOC                           32                           warp 0 (lane_pred lane)
   344      8   padding                                    PipelineStorage is aligned_struct<16> -> sizeof 352
   352     32   OFF_CLC_RESPONSE  response[0..1], 16 B     alignas(16); read by ld.shared.b128
   384      4   OFF_TMEM_BASE_PTR                          written by tcgen05.alloc, read by warps 0 and 4-7
   388    124   padding                                    tensors.epilogue is alignas(512)
   512  32768   OFF_SMEM_CD   C/D stage (e % 4), 4 x 8192  Swizzle<2,5,2>; 512 % 512 == 0
 33280    512   FusionStorage (an empty tuple, 1 B) + pad  the epilogue SharedStorage is padded to its own 512-B alignment
 33792 131072   OFF_SMEM_A    A stage s, 8 x 16384         Swizzle<3,4,3>; 33792 = 33 x 1024
164864  65536   OFF_SMEM_B    B stage s, 8 x 8192          Swizzle<3,4,3>; 164864 = 161 x 1024
230400          end = kSmemBytes                           2048 B below the 232448-B opt-in maximum
```

Two remarks on the totals. First, the stage count: the builder's formula (5.5, `kStages`) had `198464 - 8 x 24592 = 1728` B left, far short of the 24592 B a ninth stage costs in that formula (24576 B of tensors + 16 B of barriers); the *physical* slack is `232448 - 230400 = 2048` B, 320 B more, because the builder's estimate `192 + 33792 + 8 x 24592 = 230720` overstates the real `SharedStorage` by 320 B: it budgets the epilogue as its full `SharedStorage` of 33792 B (the 33280-byte `TensorStorage` plus a 64-byte load pipeline, rounded to 512; note, Section 6.1) where the kernel embeds only the 33280-byte `TensorStorage` (+512 too many), while its 192-byte kernel carveout plus the 8 x 16 B of mainloop barriers inside the stages under-budget the real 512-byte pre-tensor area by 192 B. Either way a ninth stage is out of reach.

Second, where the two pads come from. `tensors.epilogue` starts at 512 and not at 388 because the epilogue's `CollectiveStorageReuseC` declares its `smem_C`/`smem_D` union members `alignas(MaxSmemAlignment)`, with `SmemAlignmentD = cutlass::detail::alignment_for_swizzle(SmemLayoutD{}) = 1 << (B + M + |S|) = 1 << (2 + 5 + 2) = 512` for `Swizzle<2,5,2>` (`sm100_epilogue_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:170-172`, `:189-192`; `cutlass/detail/layout.hpp:420-426`). The kernel's `TensorStorage : cute::aligned_struct<128, _1>` (`sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:204`) therefore inherits alignment 512 from its first member, and the compiler rounds 388 up to 512. The 512 bytes at 33280 are the `sizeof` rounding of the epilogue `TensorStorage { CollectiveStorage collective; FusionStorage thread; }` (`:207-214`): 32768 B of stages plus the 1-byte empty `FusionStorage` of the linear-combination tree = 32769, rounded to the struct's own 512-byte alignment = 33280, so the mainloop storage starts at 512 + 33280 = 33792. The mainloop `TensorStorage` only declares `aligned_struct<128>` (`sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp:224`): the 1024-byte alignment that `Swizzle<3,4,3>` needs (`alignment_for_swizzle = 1 << (3 + 4 + 3) = 1024`) is *declared nowhere* and holds only because 33792 = 33 x 1024 happens to be a multiple (note, Section 6.2). That is precisely why the explicit kernel's `static_assert` at `:162` exists: it turns a coincidence into a checked invariant. Measured confirmation: `alignof 512`, `PipelineStorage 352`, `EpilogueSharedStorage 33792`, `off_epilogue_thread 33280`, `off_smem_A 33792` (note D.1 D2).

Three facts about the base make this map usable (all measured, note D.1 D5, and all restated at `explicit.cu:138` and `:156`):

1. The dynamic shared memory of rank `r` starts at the 32-bit `shared::cta` address `0x400 + (r << 24)`. The low kilobyte is the system-reserved shared memory (`SHARED:1024` in the resource line of every kernel in the binary, note G.3). What lives there is visible in the SASS (note D.2, `tcgen05.alloc` row, and D.6 item 7): ptxas lowers the `cta_group::2` TMEM allocation into an atomic in the leader's elected lane followed by a handshake with the peer that stores the result locally (`STS [UR29+0x180], R9<<5`), forwards it with `st.async`, and completes a barrier in the peer's reserved kilobyte at `(rank << 24) + 0x48`, with bookkeeping words at `+0x50/+0x54/+0x58`. The kernel declares no static `__shared__` (`sharedSizeBytes 0`, note D.1 D4), so `extern __shared__ char smem[]` is the first user byte, at `0x400`. This is why `kSmemBaseLow24 = 0x400`, and why adding any static `__shared__` variable would move the dynamic base (static storage precedes the dynamic array; my analysis) and invalidate the compile-time cross-checks that use `kSmemBaseLow24`, though not the kernel itself, which computes the base at run time (fact 3). The rank sits in address byte 3 (bits [24,32)); only bits 24-25 are set for a 4-CTA cluster.
2. Therefore `smem_base + OFF_*` is the shared address of anything, and clearing bit 24 of such an address names the same object in the *pair leader* (the even rank): `0xFEFFFFFF` (Section 5.9).
3. The kernel *computes* `smem_base = __cvta_generic_to_shared(smem)` at run time (`explicit.cu:1098`) and never assumes `0x400`; `kSmemBaseLow24` exists only for the compile-time cross-checks at `:165` and `:177`.

The address-space rule that follows (stated at `explicit.cu:22-23`): every `asm` operand naming shared memory is the 32-bit `smem_base + OFF_*`; every C++ dereference uses the generic pointer `smem + OFF_*`. The two classic mistakes have different symptoms. Forgetting `smem_base` and passing a bare `OFF_*` as a `shared::cta` operand is off by exactly `0x400` = 1 KiB in rank 0 (it lands in the reserved kilobyte) and by `0x1000400` / `0x2000400` / `0x3000400` (16 / 32 / 48 MiB + 1 KiB) in ranks 1-3 (it names rank 0's window instead of this CTA's). Passing the 64-bit generic pointer where a 32-bit shared operand is expected is not an offset error at all: the generic address is truncated to 32 bits and becomes an arbitrary shared address or a fault.

### 5.7.2 What each `static_assert` protects

| Line | Assert | Protects | What breaks without it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 158 | `OFF_SMEM_A == 512 + 4 * 8192 + 512` | the 512-byte pad after the C/D stages (the empty `FusionStorage` padded to the epilogue storage's 512-byte alignment) | an A stage base off by 512 breaks the 1024-byte swizzle alignment and every A address |
| 159 | `OFF_SMEM_B == OFF_SMEM_A + 8 * 16384` | A and B stages are contiguous | B addresses and the B descriptor base |
| 160 | `kSmemBytes == OFF_SMEM_B + 8 * 8192` | the requested dynamic size equals the laid-out size | too small: the last B stages overrun; too large: wasted smem, fewer resident CTAs only if it crossed a boundary (here still 1 CTA/SM) |
| 161 | `kStageBytesAHalf == 64 * 64 * 2` | the multicast half equals one A box | the `+ 8192 y` destination and the 49152 transaction count |
| 162 | `OFF_SMEM_A % 1024 == 0`, `OFF_SMEM_B % 1024 == 0` | SW128 swizzle period | TMA writes and UMMA reads XOR with absolute address bits [7,10); a base not 1024-aligned shifts the pattern between writer and reader -> garbage operands |
| 163 | `OFF_SMEM_CD % 512 == 0` | SW128_32B period | same for the epilogue: the kernel's `st.shared` XOR and TMA's un-swizzle would disagree |
| 164 | `OFF_CLC_RESPONSE % 16 == 0`, `OFF_TMEM_BASE_PTR % 4 == 0` | `ld.shared.b128` of the response needs a 16-byte aligned address; the b32 store of `tcgen05.alloc` needs 4 | misaligned-address fault |
| 165 | `0x400 + 230400 < 2^18` | the UMMA start-address field holds `(addr & 0x3FFFF) >> 4`: the encode mask spans `2^18` B = 256 KiB of `shared::cta` space (5.8.1) | nothing launchable on a B200 can violate it: the largest window is `0x400 + 232448 = 233472 < 262144`, and a kernel with `230400 + 30720 = 261120` B of shared memory could not be launched at all. The assert documents the 256 KiB span and would fire only if `kSmemBaseLow24` or the offset table were changed to assume a base high enough to wrap; an address at or above 256 KiB would wrap silently inside the descriptor and the MMA would read the wrong stage |
| 166 | `kThreads == 256`, `kMmaM == 256`, `kMmaN == 128`, `kKBlocks == 4` | the Section 4 configuration the rest of the file hard-codes | every loop bound and every descriptor increment |

## 5.8 `explicit.cu` Section 1, group 3: the UMMA descriptors

```
$ sed -n 168,177p explicit.cu
// tcgen05 LAYOUT  UMMA shared-memory descriptors (Section 7.6, D.7): 64-bit = {hi word constant, lo word = LBO (1 = 16 B) | (start_address >> 4)
// in a 14-bit field}. Per stage s and k-block kb the low word is lo_a = 0x10880 + 1024 s + 2 kb, lo_b = 0x12880 + 512 s + 2 kb (units of 16 B:
// 1024 = 16384 B, 512 = 8192 B, 2 = 32 B = 16 fp16 k values). Example, rank 0, s = 3, kb = 2: desc_a = 0x4000404000011484, desc_b = 0x4000404000012E84.
constexpr uint32_t kSmemDescHi  = 0x40004040u;   // SBO = 64 (1024 B) at [32,46), version = 1 at [46,48), layout_type = 2 (SWIZZLE_128B) at [61,64)
constexpr uint32_t kSmemDescLo0 = 0x00010000u;   // LBO = 1 (16 B) at [16,30); start address (addr >> 4) & 0x3FFF is OR'ed in at run time
constexpr uint32_t kInstrDesc   = kInstrDescConst;   // 0x10200010: c_format F32 (bit 4), n_dim 128 >> 3 = 16 at [17,23), m_dim 256 >> 4 = 16 at [24,29)
static_assert(((uint64_t(kSmemDescHi) << 32) | kSmemDescLo0) == kSmemDescConst, "D.7 descriptor constant 0x4000404000010000");
static_assert((64u | (1u << 14) | (2u << 29)) == kSmemDescHi, "SmemDescriptor high word (mma_sm100_desc.hpp:101-127)");
static_assert(((1u << 4) | (16u << 17) | (16u << 24)) == kInstrDesc, "InstrDescriptor bit map (mma_sm100_desc.hpp:416-443)");
static_assert(((kSmemBaseLow24 + OFF_SMEM_A) >> 4) == 0x880 && ((kSmemBaseLow24 + OFF_SMEM_B) >> 4) == 0x2880, "D.7: desc_a low word 0x10880, desc_b 0x12880 for the measured base");
```

`tcgen05.mma` does not take pointers to A and B. It takes two 64-bit *shared-memory descriptors* that encode where an operand starts in shared memory and how its 8-row swizzle atoms are laid out, plus a 32-bit *instruction descriptor* that encodes types, shapes and major-ness. The MMA unit walks the operand from the descriptor alone; the kernel's only job is to form the right bits. The table below reproduces the `SmemDescriptor` union of `mma_sm100_desc.hpp:101-127` (CUTLASS's bitfield names and ranges). The authoritative definition is PTX ISA Table 49, "Shared memory descriptor layout" (9.7.18.4.1; see References), which draws some field boundaries differently; the two agree on every bit the kernel sets, and the differences and the ISA's extra rules follow the table.

### 5.8.1 The 64-bit shared-memory descriptor

| Bits | Field (`mma_sm100_desc.hpp`) | Value here | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| [0,14) | `start_address_` = (shared address >> 4) | A: `(smem_base + 33792 + 16384 s + 32 kb) >> 4`, masked to 14 bits; B: `(smem_base + 164864 + 8192 s + 32 kb) >> 4` | 16-byte units (the 4 LSBs are "not included", so operands must be 16-byte aligned); the 14 encoded bits, i.e. the ISA's `(x & 0x3FFFF) >> 4`, span 256 KiB, hence the assert at `:165`; the mask `& 0x3FFF` drops the rank bits [24,26) of `smem_base`, which makes the descriptor rank-independent: the leader's MMA reads the *same CTA-relative offset* in both CTAs of the pair (note B.6) |
| [14,16) | unused | 0 | |
| [16,30) | `leading_byte_offset_` (LBO) >> 4 | 1 (= 16 B) | `make_umma_desc` sets `leading_byte_offset_ = stride_10 = 1` for a swizzled K-major canonical layout (`mma_sm100_desc.hpp:831-832`, with `expected_stride_10 = 1` asserted a few lines above); for K-major SW128 the K extent of one MMA (16 fp16 = 32 B) lies inside one 128-byte row, so the field carries the canonical placeholder rather than a real stride (my analysis of the canonical-layout comment at `:801-809`) |
| [30,32) | unused | 0 | |
| [32,46) | `stride_byte_offset_` (SBO) >> 4 | 64 (= 1024 B) | the byte distance between consecutive 8-row swizzle atoms along M/N: 8 rows x 128 B = 1024 B (`Layout_K_SW128_Atom`: `Shape<_8,_1024>` bits, `mma_traits_sm90_gmma.hpp:84`); the MMA's 128 (A) or 64 (B) rows are 16 or 8 such atoms |
| [46,48) | `version_` | 1 | "Set the version for blackwell" (`mma_sm100_desc.hpp:746`); Hopper's wgmma descriptor had 0 here |
| [48,49) | unused | 0 | |
| [49,52) | `base_offset_` | 0 | the swizzle phase of the start address; 0 is valid because every stage base is 1024-byte aligned (`:757-758`, `constexpr uint8_t base_offset = 0`), and advancing the start address by 32/64/96 B for `kb` does not touch address bits [7,10) |
| [52,53) | `lbo_mode_` | 0 | "legacy mode by default" (`:747`) |
| [53,61) | unused | 0 | |
| [61,64) | `layout_type_` | 2 = `SWIZZLE_128B` | `enum class LayoutType { SWIZZLE_NONE = 0, SWIZZLE_128B_BASE32B = 1, SWIZZLE_128B = 2, SWIZZLE_64B = 4, SWIZZLE_32B = 6 }` (`:82-88`); it tells the MMA unit to apply the same 16-byte-chunk XOR that TMA applied on write |

**What PTX ISA Table 49 says, where it differs from the union, and the rules you need for other layouts.** The ISA defines bits 0-14 (15 bits) as `matrix-descriptor-encode(start address)` with bit 15 reserved 0; bits 16-30 (15 bits) as the encoded leading-dimension byte offset (relative) *or* byte address (absolute), bit 31 reserved; bits 32-45 the encoded SBO; bits 46-48 (3 bits) a fixed constant `0b001`; bits 49-51 the matrix base offset; bit 52 the leading-dimension stride mode (0 relative offset, 1 absolute address); bit 53 the `lut::b` K-segment selector; bits 54-60 fixed 0; bits 61-63 the swizzle mode (0 none, 1 = 128-byte with 32-byte atom, 2 = 128-byte, 4 = 64-byte, 6 = 32-byte; 3, 5, 7 invalid); and `matrix-descriptor-encode(x) = (x & 0x3FFFF) >> 4`. CUTLASS's 14-bit `start_address_` plus 2 unused bits and its 14-bit LBO plus 2 unused bits are the same bits with a narrower name; its `version_ = 1` at [46,48) is bit 46 of the ISA's fixed `0b001`. So the 256 KiB span of the start address is a property of the encode mask `0x3FFFF`, not of a "14-bit field" as such (the assert at `:165` is written against the span). The ISA adds three rules the kernel satisfies by construction but that you must check when you encode a different layout: (1) "The following must be 16-byte aligned: Matrix start address, Leading dimension byte offset, Stride dimension byte offset", hence the `>> 4`; (2) the base offset "is 0 when the repeating pattern of the specified swizzling mode starts" on a 1024-byte boundary for 128-byte swizzle, 512-byte for 64-byte swizzle, 256-byte for 32-byte swizzle (Table 50), and "Otherwise, the base offset must be a non-zero value, computed using the following formula: base offset = (pattern start addr >> 0x7) & 0x7", which is why the 1024-byte alignment of every A/B stage base (5.7.2, line 162) lets CUTLASS hard-code `base_offset = 0`; (3) "The byte address mode for the leading dimension stride is supported on sm_103a", so on the B200 the LBO is always a relative offset (`lbo_mode_ = 0`).

Assembling the constant high word: SBO `64 = 0x40` at hi bits [0,14); version `1 << 14 = 0x4000`; layout type `2` in the 3-bit field [61,64) is `0b010`, i.e. global bit 62 = hi bit 30 = `0x40000000`. Sum: `0x40004040`, which is the second `static_assert` (`64u | (1u << 14) | (2u << 29)`: `2 << 29 = 1 << 30`). The constant low word is LBO `1 << 16 = 0x10000`. Together `0x4000404000010000 = kSmemDescConst` (first assert).

The run-time part is the start address. For the measured base `0x400`: `(0x400 + 33792) >> 4 = 0x8800 >> 4 = 0x880` and `(0x400 + 164864) >> 4 = 0x28800 >> 4 = 0x2880` (fourth assert), so the stage-0, k-block-0 low words are `0x10880` and `0x12880`, and

```
lo_a(s, kb) = 0x10880 + 1024 s + 2 kb        (16384 B per stage = 1024 units; 32 B per k-block = 2 units)
lo_b(s, kb) = 0x12880 +  512 s + 2 kb        ( 8192 B per stage =  512 units)
```

**Worked example, recomputed (rank 0, `s = 3`, `kb = 2`).** A: shared address `0x400 + 33792 + 3 x 16384 + 2 x 32 = 0x400 + 0x8400 + 0xC000 + 0x40 = 0x14840`; `>> 4 = 0x1484`; `& 0x3FFF = 0x1484` (fits); `lo = 0x10000 | 0x1484 = 0x11484`; `desc_a = 0x40004040_00011484`. Check with the increment form: `0x10880 + 3 x 1024 + 4 = 0x10880 + 0xC00 + 0x4 = 0x11484`. B: `0x400 + 164864 + 3 x 8192 + 64 = 0x400 + 0x28400 + 0x6000 + 0x40 = 0x2E840`; `>> 4 = 0x2E84`; `lo = 0x12E84`; `desc_b = 0x40004040_00012E84`; increment form `0x12880 + 3 x 512 + 4 = 0x12880 + 0x600 + 0x4 = 0x12E84`. Both match the comment and the measured K3 records (`desc_a = 0x4000404000010880` at `s = 0, kb = 0`, `+2` per k-block, `+0x400` A / `+0x200` B per stage; note D.1 D7).

How the kernel builds them (`explicit.cu:896-897`, `:928-929`, `:933-934`): once per role entry, `desc_lo_a = kSmemDescLo0 | (((smem_base + OFF_SMEM_A) >> 4) & 0x3FFFu)`; per k-tile, `uint32_t const lo_a = desc_lo_a + 1024u * rs;` (`rs` the read stage); per k-block, `desc64(kSmemDescHi, lo_a + 2u * uint32_t(kb))`. The addition is on the 32-bit low word, not the 64-bit value, exactly as CUTLASS's `DescriptorIterator::operator+` does for nvcc <= 13.3 (`mma_sm100_desc.hpp:843-874`, the add at `:870`: "Use 32-bit calculation rather than 64-bit calculation as we only update part of desc"); in SASS this is a `ULEA` per stage and a `UIADD3 +2/+4/+6` per k-block with a `UMOV 0x40004040` for the high word (measured, note D.2 and G.3). Why the start address advances by 32 B per k-block inside a swizzled row: the descriptor's address is the *unswizzled* position of element (row 0, k = 16 kb); the hardware derives every other element's physical chunk by XORing with the row index, so stepping the base through the four 32-byte slices of the 128-byte row is the canonical way to iterate K (it is what `UMMA::smem_desc` iterators do).

### 5.8.2 The 32-bit instruction descriptor

`InstrDescriptor` (`mma_sm100_desc.hpp:416-443`), value `0x10200010` (decimal 270532624, the `mov.b32` operand in the PTX, note Section 7.2):

| Bits | Field | Value | Meaning here |
|---|---|---|---|
| [0,2) | `sparse_id2_` | 0 | no sparsity metadata |
| [2,3) | `sparse_flag_` | 0 | dense |
| [3,4) | `saturate_` | 0 | no saturation (S8 only anyway) |
| [4,6) | `c_format_` | 1 = F32 | fp32 accumulator in TMEM (`0x10` = bit 4) |
| [6,7) | unused | 0 | |
| [7,10) | `a_format_` | 0 = F16 | `F32F16Format: 0 = F16, 1 = BF16, 2 = TF32` |
| [10,13) | `b_format_` | 0 = F16 | |
| [13,14) | `a_negate_` | 0 | |
| [14,15) | `b_negate_` | 0 | |
| [15,16) | `a_major_` | 0 = K-major | A is M x K row-major (K contiguous) |
| [16,17) | `b_major_` | 0 = K-major | B is N x K with K contiguous (the harness's `ColumnMajor` B) |
| [17,23) | `n_dim_` = N >> 3 | 16 -> N = 128 | `0x200000` = 16 << 17; "3 LSBs not included", valid 1 (N = 8) .. 32 (N = 256) |
| [23,24) | unused | 0 | |
| [24,29) | `m_dim_` = M >> 4 | 16 -> M = 256 | `0x10000000` = 16 << 24; "4 LSBs not included. Valid values are: 4 (M=64), 8 (M=128), 16 (M=256)" |
| [29,30) | K dimension (an anonymous `: 1` in the union, `:436`) | 0 | PTX ISA Table 51 names bit 29 "K Dimension": for `.kind::f16` its value is "(Dense K=16 / Sparse K=32) = 0", and it is likewise 0 for the tf32, f8f6f4 and i8 kinds; the only column with value 1 is the dense K = 64 kind. CUTLASS leaves the bit unnamed because it is always 0 for the kinds it emits. K is therefore encoded, as the fixed value 0, not a free parameter |
| [30,32) | `max_shift_` | 0 | weight-stationary shift, unused |

`0x10000000 + 0x200000 + 0x10 = 0x10200010`, the third assert (`(1u << 4) | (16u << 17) | (16u << 24)`). K is not a free parameter: bit 29 carries it as the fixed value 0, which for `kind::f16` means K = 16 elements per instruction (the atom's `Shape_MNK (256,128,16)`), which is why four instructions cover a 64-wide k-tile. The descriptor is identical for all 512 MMAs of a tile and for every tile; the only per-instruction variation is the `scale_c` predicate (0 for the first MMA of a tile, 1 afterwards; Chapter 9).

## 5.9 `explicit.cu` Section 1, group 4: protocol constants

```
$ sed -n 179,192p explicit.cu
// mbarrier  Protocol constants (Section 7.2): arrive counts and transaction bytes of every barrier, and the multicast masks
constexpr uint32_t kMainloopTxBytes  = 2 * (kStageBytesA + kStageBytesB);   // 49152: six 8192-byte boxes per stage credit the leader
constexpr uint32_t kClcTxBytes       = 16;
constexpr uint32_t kMainFullCount    = 1, kMainEmptyCount = 2;      // 2/2 + 2/1 - 1
constexpr uint32_t kClcFullCount     = 1, kClcEmptyCount  = 800;    // 32 + 4 * (32 + 128 + 32); beta = 0
constexpr uint32_t kAccFullCount     = 1, kAccEmptyCount  = 256;    // 2 x 128 epilogue threads
constexpr uint32_t kThrottleCount    = 32, kTmemDeallocCount = 32;
constexpr uint16_t kMainloopReleaseMask = 0xF;                       // calculate_multicast_mask<kRowCol> (sm100_pipeline.hpp:57-91)
constexpr uint32_t kPeerBitMask      = 0xFEFFFFFFu;                  // cute::Sm100MmaPeerBitMask (copy_sm100_tma.hpp:45); nvcc folds it to 0xFEFFFFF8
constexpr uint64_t kCacheHintEvictNormal = 0x1000000000000000ull;    // TMA::CacheHintSm100::EVICT_NORMAL = Sm100MemDescDefault
constexpr uint32_t kWaitTicks        = 0x989680u;                    // ClusterBarrier::wait suspend-time hint (barrier.h:415)
constexpr uint32_t kBarEpilogue      = 1, kBarTmemAlloc = 6;         // ReservedNamedBarriers (barrier.h:169-178)
constexpr uint32_t kEpilogueThreads  = 128, kTmemAllocBarThreads = 160;
static_assert(kMainloopTxBytes == 49152 && kClcEmptyCount == 32 + 4 * (32 + 128 + 32), "Section 7.2 counts");
```

Chapter 4 explains the protocol these numbers implement; here is why each number is what it is (all derived from the sources named, matching note Section 7.2):

| Constant | Value | Derivation |
|---|---|---|
| `kMainloopTxBytes` | 49152 | Transaction bytes expected on the pair leader's `full[s]`: the TMA boxes that land in *both* CTAs of the pair all credit the leader's barrier (the peer's loads name the leader's barrier through the peer-bit mask). Per CTA and stage: own A half 8192 + multicast A half 8192 + own B 8192 = 24576; two CTAs: 49152 = 6 boxes x 8192 |
| `kClcTxBytes` | 16 | one CLC response is a 16-byte `b128` (`CLCResponse { uint32_t data[4]; }`, `sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp:74`) |
| `kMainFullCount` | 1 | one `mbarrier.arrive.expect_tx` by the leader's elected lane per stage; everything else is transaction bytes |
| `kMainEmptyCount` | 2 | `PipelineTmaUmmaAsync`'s `multicast_consumer_arrival_count = size<0>(cluster_shape) / size<0>(atom_thr_shape) + size<1>(cluster_shape) / size<1>(atom_thr_shape) - 1` (`sm100_pipeline.hpp:565-566`; the per-warpgroup variant at `:358-359`) with `cluster_shape = (2,2,1)` and `atom_thr_shape = (2,1,1)`: `2/2 + 2/1 - 1 = 2` (note, Section 7.2). It counts MMA *leaders*, not CTAs: each leader's `tcgen05.commit` multicasts one arrive to every CTA in its mask (`0xF`, all four), and the stage `s` of CTA `r` may be refilled only after two consumers are done with what sits in it or came from it (my analysis of the geometry): `r`'s own pair leader, which reads `r`'s smem (its 128 A rows and its 64-column B half) with the 2SM MMA, and the other pair's leader, which reads the A half that `r` multicast into the CTA with the same `x` (rank `r ^ 2`); `r`'s producer overwrites both copies when it refills `s`, so both leaders' commits must have landed |
| `kClcFullCount` | 1 | one remote `arrive.expect_tx(16)` per CTA by lanes 0..3 of rank 0's scheduler warp, completed by the multicast response |
| `kClcEmptyCount` | 800 | every thread that consumes a response arrives remotely on **CTA 0's** `empty[idx]`: rank 0's scheduler warp (32) + per CTA the producer warp (32), the four epilogue warps (128) and the MMA warp (32): `32 + 4 x 192 = 800`; it would be 928 with the beta != 0 epilogue-load warp (kernel `:511-514`, note Section 13 item 17) |
| `kAccFullCount` | 1 | the leader's `tcgen05.commit` (pair-multicast) per accumulator stage |
| `kAccEmptyCount` | 256 | every epilogue thread of *both* CTAs (2 x 128) arrives on the **leader's** `acc_empty[st]` through the peer-bit mask |
| `kThrottleCount` | 32 / 32 | rank 0's producer warp arrives with all 32 lanes on `throttle_full`; rank 0's scheduler warp arrives with all 32 lanes on `throttle_empty` |
| `kTmemDeallocCount` | 32 | the exit handshake: the peer's whole warp 0 arrives once on the leader's barrier, then the leader's on the peer's. It is 32 and not 1 because the arrive is warp-wide with no election: CUTLASS initialises the barrier with `NumMMAThreads` = 32 (`sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:565`, `:138`) and every lane of the MMA warp executes `tmem_deallocation_result_barrier.arrive(mma_peer_cta_rank, ...)` (`:828`), one remote `mbarrier.arrive.shared::cluster` per lane; Chapter 11 walks the handshake |
| `kMainloopReleaseMask` | `0xF` | `calculate_multicast_mask<kRowCol>` (`sm100_pipeline.hpp:57-91`): every CTA in the same MMA row *or* column; with a 2 x 2 cluster and a 2 x 1 atom that is all four ranks, so each leader's commit releases the stage in every CTA. 16-bit because `tcgen05.commit ... multicast::cluster` takes a `.b16` CTA mask (`"h"` operand) |
| `kPeerBitMask` | `0xFEFFFFFF` | `cute::Sm100MmaPeerBitMask` (`copy_sm100_tma.hpp:45`): clears bit 24, the rank's bit 0, of a `shared::cta` address, turning "my barrier" into "the pair leader's barrier" (ranks `2y+1 -> 2y`; a no-op on even ranks). nvcc folds the known-zero low bits of the barrier address into the constant where it can. In the explicit kernel the literal `0xFEFFFFF8` (`and.b32 ..., -16777224`, the three alignment bits of an 8-byte-aligned barrier address folded in) survives only at the epilogue's accumulator release (SASS `0x44c0`); in the producer warp the mask was folded onto the hoisted 1024-byte-aligned barrier base as `& 0xFEFFFFF0` (PTX `-16777232`, SASS `ULOP3 ... 0xfefffff0` at `0x0c00`), equivalent for `s <= 7` (measured, note G.3). The `-16777224` of note D.6 item 2 describes the CUTLASS baseline, which carries the `and` per k-tile. All three forms are semantically identical for every barrier address |
| `kCacheHintEvictNormal` | `0x1000000000000000` | `TMA::CacheHintSm100::EVICT_NORMAL` (`copy_sm90_desc.hpp:193-197`) = `cute::Sm100MemDescDefault` (`copy_sm100_tma.hpp:46`), the 64-bit L2 cache-policy operand of every `cp.async.bulk.tensor ... .L2::cache_hint` load; "normal" priority, the value CUTLASS passes by default for the mainloop loads. In SASS it is the register pair `{0x0, 0x10000000}` (note D.2) |
| `kWaitTicks` | `0x989680` = 10,000,000 | the suspend-time hint operand of `mbarrier.try_wait.parity` (`timeHint` in the PTX ISA; CUTLASS's local variable is `ticks`): a time limit in **nanoseconds** after which a suspended thread resumes even if the phase is incomplete, so the loop around it re-tests. PTX ISA, `mbarrier.test_wait`/`mbarrier.try_wait`: "Suspended thread resumes execution when the specified phase completes OR before the phase completes following a system-dependent time limit. The optional 32-bit unsigned integer operand timeHint specifies the time limit, in nanoseconds, that may be used for the time limit instead of the system-dependent limit" (see References). 10 ms is CUTLASS's "arbitrarily large" value (`barrier.h:414-415`); it is a hint, so a shorter system limit may wake the thread earlier. In SASS it becomes `NANOSLEEP.SYNCS 0x989680` in the retry loop (note D.2) |
| `kBarEpilogue` | 1 | `ReservedNamedBarriers::EpilogueBarrier = 1` (`barrier.h:169-170`): the 16 named-barrier syncs per tile among the 128 epilogue threads. ID 0 is avoided because `__syncthreads()` uses it |
| `kBarTmemAlloc` | 6 | `ReservedNamedBarriers::TmemAllocBarrier = 6` (`barrier.h:175`): warp 0 `bar.arrive`s and warps 4-7 `bar.sync` after the TMEM base is written |
| `kEpilogueThreads` | 128 | the four epilogue warps; `bar.sync 1, 128` counts threads and the count must be a warp multiple |
| `kTmemAllocBarThreads` | 160 | warp 0 (32, arriving) + warps 4-7 (128, syncing) on barrier 6 |

The `static_assert` at `:192` re-derives the two counts that are easiest to get wrong (the transaction bytes and the 800).

## 5.10 `explicit.cu` Section 1, group 5: the CuTe swizzle cross-check

```
$ sed -n 194,204p explicit.cu
// [CHECK] LAYOUT  CuTe cross-check (compile time only, the only use of CuTe in this TU): the epilogue smem byte formula uses
// Swizzle<2,5,2> on byte offsets, bits [5,7) ^= bits [7,9) (Layout_MN_SW128_32B_Atom<float>, Section 4; B.3.3 step 17).
// Example: byte offset 0x1E4 (row 121 of a 32 x 4 fp32 atom column block) -> 0x1E4 ^ ((0x1E4 & 0x180) >> 2) = 0x1E4 ^ 0x60 = 0x184.
__host__ __device__ constexpr uint32_t epi_swz(uint32_t o) { return o ^ ((o & 0x180u) >> 2); }
using EpiSwizzle = cute::Swizzle<2, 5, 2>;
static_assert(EpiSwizzle::num_bits == 2 && EpiSwizzle::num_base == 5 && EpiSwizzle::num_shft == 2, "Swizzle<2,5,2>");
static_assert(EpiSwizzle::yyy_msk::value == 0x180 && EpiSwizzle::zzz_msk::value == 0x60, "Swizzle<2,5,2> masks: bits [7,9) fold into bits [5,7)");
static_assert(epi_swz(0x080u) == EpiSwizzle{}(0x080u) && epi_swz(0x1E4u) == EpiSwizzle{}(0x1E4u) && epi_swz(0x7FFCu) == EpiSwizzle{}(0x7FFCu),
              "epi_swz matches cute::Swizzle<2,5,2> (E.6.1) [confirm at first build: apply() is constexpr]");
// Swizzle<3,4,3> (A/B stages) is applied by the TMA unit on write and by the UMMA unit on read (SWIZZLE_128B); the kernel never computes it.
static_assert(cute::Swizzle<3, 4, 3>::yyy_msk::value == 0x380 && cute::Swizzle<3, 4, 3>::num_shft == 3, "Swizzle<3,4,3>: 16-byte chunk ^= row mod 8");
```

### 5.10.1 `cute::Swizzle<B, M, S>` in one picture

`cute/swizzle.hpp:42-96` defines the functor on an integer offset:

```
      0bxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxYYYxxxxxxxZZZxxxx          (the header's own picture, swizzle.hpp:43-47)
                                    ^--^  M = num_base : the M least-significant bits are left alone
                       ^-^       ^-^      B = num_bits : the width of the two masks
                         ^---------^      S = num_shft : the distance from the YYY mask down to the ZZZ mask

      bit_msk = (1 << B) - 1
      yyy_msk = bit_msk << (M + max(0, S))          the source bits
      zzz_msk = bit_msk << (M - min(0, S))          the target bits (for S > 0 this is bit_msk << M)
      apply(o) = o ^ ((o & yyy_msk) >> S)           ZZZ ^= YYY   (swizzle.hpp:78: offset ^ shiftr(offset & yyy_msk, msk_sft))
```

So a swizzle XORs a B-bit field at bit position `M + S` into the B-bit field at bit position `M`, and leaves everything else alone. Why it is written this way for GPU shared memory: the low `M` bits address bytes inside one access unit (a 16- or 32-byte chunk), the `ZZZ` bits select the chunk within a line, and the `YYY` bits are the line (row) index; XORing the chunk with the row rotates which bank a given logical chunk lands in from row to row, so that a column of chunks does not pile onto one bank group. CUTLASS gives each swizzle a name by its `(B, M, S)`:

| Swizzle | `bit_msk` | `yyy_msk` (source bits) | `zzz_msk` (target bits) | Plain English | TMA enumerator |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Swizzle<3,4,3>` | 7 | `7 << 7 = 0x380`, bits [7,10) | `7 << 4 = 0x70`, bits [4,7) | the 16-byte chunk index (3 bits, 8 chunks of a 128-byte line) ^= line index mod 8 | `SWIZZLE_128B` |
| `Swizzle<2,5,2>` | 3 | `3 << 7 = 0x180`, bits [7,9) | `3 << 5 = 0x60`, bits [5,7) | the 32-byte chunk index (2 bits, 4 chunks of a 128-byte line) ^= line index mod 4 | `SWIZZLE_128B_ATOM_32B` |

Both have the line index at bit 7 because both have 128-byte lines; they differ in the chunk size (16 B vs 32 B), hence `M = 4` vs `M = 5` and `B = 3` vs `B = 2`. `S = B` in both, which is what makes the two fields adjacent.

Why the hardware keys the XOR on *absolute* shared-address bits and not on a buffer-relative row index: the TMA unit and the UMMA unit see only addresses, a destination or start address plus a swizzle mode, never a CuTe layout or a buffer base. Both compute the physical chunk from bits [7,10) (SW128) or [7,9) (SW128_32B) of the address they are handed. Three facts stated separately in this chapter are consequences of this one rule: the A/B stage bases must be 1024-byte aligned and the C/D bases 512-byte aligned (`explicit.cu:162-163`, 5.7.2) so that the address bits the hardware XORs with are the row index the layout means; the UMMA descriptor's `base_offset` can be 0 (5.8.1) only because of that alignment, and would otherwise have to carry `(pattern start >> 7) & 7`; and the epilogue's `st.shared` must apply the same XOR to the same address bits (`epi_swz`, `:197`) so that TMA's un-swizzle on the way out recovers the logical column. Sections 5.4.5 (2), 5.7.2 and 5.8.1 are three views of this single rule.

### 5.10.2 The asserts, by hand

- `:199` pins the three template parameters.
- `:200` computes the masks: for `<2,5,2>`, `bit_msk = 3`, `yyy_msk = 3 << (5 + 2) = 3 << 7 = 0x180`, `zzz_msk = 3 << (5 - 0) = 0x60`. Correct.
- `:197` is the hand-written formula `epi_swz(o) = o ^ ((o & 0x180) >> 2)`, i.e. `apply` with these masks and `S = 2`. `:201` checks it against the real `cute::Swizzle` at three points (this works because `Swizzle::apply` is `constexpr`, `swizzle.hpp:73-79`):
  - `0x080`: `0x080 & 0x180 = 0x080`; `>> 2 = 0x20`; `0x080 ^ 0x20 = 0x0A0`. (Line 1, chunk 0 -> chunk 1.)
  - `0x1E4` (the comment's example): `0x1E4 = 0b1_1110_0100`; `& 0x180 = 0x180` (bits 7 and 8 set: line 3 of the 4-line period); `>> 2 = 0x60`; `0x1E4 ^ 0x60 = 0b1_1000_0100 = 0x184`. In atom terms `0x1E4 = 484 = 4 x 121`: element 121 of a 32 x 4 fp32 atom block, i.e. line `n = 3` (bytes 384..511), byte 100 within the line, chunk `100 >> 5 = 3`, offset 4 inside the chunk; swizzled chunk `3 ^ 3 = 0`, so the physical byte is `384 + 0 + 4 = 388 = 0x184`.
  - `0x7FFC`: `& 0x180 = 0x180`; `^ 0x60` -> `0x7F9C`. (The last word of the whole 32768-byte four-stage C/D region, `OFF_SMEM_CD`-relative: `4 x 8192 - 4 = 32764 = 0x7FFC`; the last word of a single 8192-byte stage would be `0x1FFC`.)
- `:204` checks `Swizzle<3,4,3>`: `yyy_msk = 7 << (4 + 3) = 0x380` and `S = 3`, which is the "16-byte chunk ^= row mod 8" statement of Sections 5.4.5 and 5.6.

Why the kernel needs `Swizzle<2,5,2>` in software but not `Swizzle<3,4,3>`: the A/B stages are written by TMA and read by the MMA unit, two hardware agents that both know `SWIZZLE_128B`, so no thread ever touches those bytes. The C/D stage is written by *threads* (`st.shared.b32` in the epilogue) and read by TMA with `SWIZZLE_128B_ATOM_32B`; TMA will un-permute the 32-byte chunks on the way out, so the threads must store each value at the permuted position, or column `j` of the output would receive the data of column `j ^ (chunk bits)`. This is the only piece of CuTe the TU uses, and only at compile time (`explicit.cu:17-18`): the device code evaluates the integer formula, never a `cute::Layout`.

## 5.11 Section 2 in brief: the trace-only types

```
$ sed -n 206,240p explicit.cu
///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
// 2. [TRACE]  Trace-only diagnostics (E.7.2 B1/B2, E.7.3): hang records in a host-mapped pinned buffer, heartbeats, K_TAIL.
//    With the toggle off this section reduces to the two #else lines: EXPLICIT_WAIT is the plain blocking wait and the CLC
//    record kinds are 0 (clc_consume then emits nothing).
///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
#if defined(CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE)   // [TRACE]
enum WaitSite : uint32_t {
  WAIT_NONE = 0, WAIT_MAINLOOP_FULL, WAIT_MAINLOOP_EMPTY, WAIT_ACC_FULL, WAIT_ACC_EMPTY, WAIT_CLC_FULL, WAIT_CLC_EMPTY,
  WAIT_THROTTLE_FULL, WAIT_THROTTLE_EMPTY, WAIT_TMEM_DEALLOC, TAIL_MAINLOOP, TAIL_ACC, TAIL_CLC, WAIT_SITE_COUNT
};
struct HangRec {                       // 64 bytes; slot ((by * 64 + bx) * 8 + warp)
  uint32_t site, bx, by, rank;         // site != 0 once a wait exceeded kHangNs
  uint32_t warp, lane, addr, parity;   // barrier shared::cta address and parity of the stuck wait
  uint32_t tile, ktile;                // tile counter and k-tile of the stuck wait
  uint32_t hb_tile, hb_phase;          // heartbeat (lane 0 of each role warp): tile counter and phase marker
  uint64_t t;                          // %globaltimer at the hang record
  uint32_t hb_valid, pad_[1];
};
static_assert(sizeof(HangRec) == 64, "HangRec");
constexpr uint32_t kHangSlots = 64 * 64 * 8;
constexpr uint64_t kHangNs = 4000000000ull;        // 4 s
constexpr uint64_t kHangSpinNs = 1000000000ull;    // 1 s of extra spinning so that every stuck warp records
enum HbPhase : uint32_t { HB_TILE_START = 1, HB_TAIL = 2, HB_ALLOC = 3, HB_EXIT = 4 };
static __device__ HangRec* g_explicit_hang_buf = nullptr;
// K_TAIL (kind 13) is declared in deabstraction_trace.hpp's TraceKind enum (additive kind; kinds 12-15 were free, K_COUNT = 16)
// [TRACE] every blocking wait of the roles goes through this macro: with the toggle on it is the bounded, hang-recording wait (4 s)
#define EXPLICIT_WAIT(addr, parity, site, tile, q) mbar_wait_traced((addr), (parity), (site), (tile), (q))
constexpr uint32_t K_CLC_SCHED_KIND = K_CLC_SCHED;   // clc_consume<> record kinds (K5b, K5c)
constexpr uint32_t K_CLC_MMA_KIND   = K_CLC_MMA;
#else
```
