```
// [PROD] with the toggle off: the baseline's mbarrier.try_wait.parity loop with the 0x989680 suspend hint (W6); site/tile/q vanish
#define EXPLICIT_WAIT(addr, parity, site, tile, q) mbar_wait((addr), (parity))
constexpr uint32_t K_CLC_SCHED_KIND = 0u;             // no records with the toggle off
constexpr uint32_t K_CLC_MMA_KIND   = 0u;
#endif
```

What this is for. A warp-specialised cluster kernel that deadlocks gives you nothing: the GPU hangs and the host waits forever. The toggle-on build therefore replaces every blocking wait with `mbar_wait_traced` (`explicit.cu:629-657`), which runs the same `try_wait.parity ... 0x989680` loop but in C++ with `%globaltimer`, and after `kHangNs = 4 s` writes a `HangRec` (which barrier address, which parity, which warp/lane/rank, which tile and k-tile) into a host-mapped pinned buffer, spins one more second so that *every* stuck warp records, then `__trap()`s. The host (`explicit_trace_wait_and_check`, Section 11 of the file) polls the launch for 20 s and prints the records. One `HangRec` is 64 bytes so that a slot is one cache-line-sized write; there are `64 x 64 x 8` slots, one per (CTA, warp) of the 64 x 64 grid, addressed as `((by * 64 + bx) * 8 + warp)`. Heartbeats (`heartbeat(tile, phase)`, lane 0 of each role warp) stamp the slot with the last tile and phase (`HB_TILE_START`, `HB_TAIL`, `HB_ALLOC`, `HB_EXIT`) so that a hang report also says how far each warp got. `K_TAIL` and the two `K_CLC_*` kinds are record types for the CLC consume and the tail waits (Chapter 7).

What matters for the production kernel: with the toggle off, `EXPLICIT_WAIT(addr, parity, site, tile, q)` *is* `mbar_wait(addr, parity)`, the W6 wrapper that copies `ClusterBarrier::wait` (`barrier.h:410-430`); `site`, `tile`, `q` vanish in the preprocessor and `K_CLC_SCHED_KIND = K_CLC_MMA_KIND = 0` make `clc_consume<0>` emit nothing. The SASS of two toggle-off builds is byte-identical (measured, note G.3 D6), and the `__device__` variable `g_explicit_hang_buf` is absent from the production cubin: it is declared only under `#if defined(CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE)` (`explicit.cu:211`, `:229`; derived from the source, the note never names the variable), and G.3's resource line reports `GLOBAL:10`, ten one-byte libcu++ tag objects that no instruction of the kernel references, which is consistent with it. So nothing in Section 2 costs an instruction or a byte of global memory in the binary you time.

## 5.12 What to carry forward

- The ABI is `ExplicitGemmParams`: four opaque 128-byte maps at 0/128/256/384, `k` at 520, `alpha, beta` at 528/532, 640 bytes in all; everything after 536 is host-only.
- Every shared-memory operand in the rest of the file is `smem_base + OFF_*` (shared) or `smem + OFF_*` (generic), with the map of 5.7.1; the base is `0x400 + (r << 24)` and bit 24 is the pair bit.
- Every descriptor is `0x40004040_000(1|2)xxxx` with the low word `0x10880 + 1024 s + 2 kb` (A) or `0x12880 + 512 s + 2 kb` (B), and every MMA uses `idesc = 0x10200010`.
- Every barrier count and mask of Chapter 4 is a constant of 5.9; every box shape of Chapters 8 and 10 is a constant of 5.5 and 5.4.4.

Chapter 6 turns to the 37 PTX wrappers that consume these constants.

## Checkpoint

1. The CUDA 12.x headers give `alignof(CUtensorMap) = 64`. What is `sizeof(ExplicitGemmParams)` then, which `static_assert`s in `explicit.hpp` change their verdict, and does the device code need to change?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
576 bytes: the fields end at 576 and 576 is already a multiple of 64, so there is no tail padding. No assert changes verdict: `alignof >= 64` still holds, the map offsets are multiples of `sizeof(CUtensorMap) = 128` regardless of alignment, the scalar offsets are pinned relative to `4 * 128`, and the size assert admits both 576 and 640. The device reads `k`, `alpha`, `beta` at fixed offsets 520/528/532 and the four maps at 0/128/256/384, all unchanged, so no device code changes. Only `CONSTANT[0]` in the SASS resource line would read `0x380 + 576`.
</details>

2. Why is the A tensor map's box (64, 64, 1) and not (64, 128, 1), given that each CTA's A stage is 128 x 64? Give the exact mechanism and the alignment fact that makes the resulting half-stage writes legal.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
`make_tma_atom_A_sm100` passes `num_multicast = 2` for `SM100_TMA_2SM_LOAD_MULTICAST` (`copy_traits_sm100_tma.hpp:755-758`), and `make_tma_copy_desc` divides the box by the multicast count starting from the last mode (`copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp:1003-1009`): the L box of 1 absorbs nothing, the M box 128 becomes 64. Each of the two CTAs sharing `tm` loads a different 64-row half and multicasts it to both at `+ 8192 y` inside the stage. It is legal because 64 rows is a multiple of the 8-row SW128 swizzle atom (1024 B): `(64 y + r) % 8 == r % 8`, so the half written at an 8192-byte offset carries the swizzle phase the UMMA descriptor expects.
</details>

3. Recompute `desc_b` for rank 1, `s = 5`, `kb = 1`, and explain why the result is the same as for rank 0.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
Rank 1's base is `0x01000400`. Shared address `0x01000400 + 164864 + 5 x 8192 + 32 = 0x01000400 + 0x28400 + 0xA000 + 0x20 = 0x01032820`; `>> 4 = 0x103282`; `& 0x3FFF = 0x3282` (the rank bit at address bit 24 becomes bit 20 after the shift and is dropped by the 14-bit mask). `lo = 0x10000 | 0x3282 = 0x13282`; `desc_b = 0x4000404000013282`. Increment form: `0x12880 + 5 x 512 + 2 = 0x12880 + 0xA00 + 0x2 = 0x13282`. Rank 0 gives the identical value because the masked field only sees the low 18 bits of the address, which are the same in every CTA; the MMA unit interprets the start address CTA-relative in both CTAs of the pair.
</details>

4. The mainloop `empty[s]` barrier has count 2 while the `full[s]` barrier has count 1 plus 49152 transaction bytes. Derive both from the cluster geometry.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
`full[s]`: one `mbarrier.arrive.expect_tx` by the pair leader's elected lane (count 1); the bytes are the six 8192-byte boxes that land in the two CTAs of the pair (per CTA: its own A half, the multicast A half from the CTA with the same `x`, its own B box), `2 x 3 x 8192 = 49152`, all credited to the leader's barrier because the peer's loads name the leader's barrier through the peer-bit mask. `empty[s]`: `PipelineTmaUmmaAsync`'s `size<0>(cluster) / size<0>(atom_thr) + size<1>(cluster) / size<1>(atom_thr) - 1 = 2/2 + 2/1 - 1 = 2` (`sm100_pipeline.hpp:565-566`), the number of MMA leaders whose `tcgen05.commit` (mask `0xF`, all four CTAs) must have released the stage: the CTA's own pair leader, which reads the CTA's smem (A rows and B half) with the 2SM MMA, and the other pair's leader, which reads the A half this CTA multicast into the CTA with the same `x` (rank `r ^ 2`); the producer overwrites both copies on refill, so both commits must have landed.
</details>

5. Apply `Swizzle<2,5,2>` by hand to byte offset `0x2A8` and state which atom line and chunk it is before and after.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
`0x2A8 = 680`. Line index = bits [7,9) = `(0x2A8 >> 7) & 3 = 5 & 3 = 1` (within the 512-byte atom period: `680 - 512 = 168`, line 1 of the second atom). Chunk = bits [5,7) = `(0x2A8 >> 5) & 3 = 21 & 3 = 1`. `yyy = 0x2A8 & 0x180 = 0x080`; `>> 2 = 0x20`; `0x2A8 ^ 0x20 = 0x288`. After: chunk `1 ^ 1 = 0`, same line, same offset 8 inside the chunk. So logical chunk 1 of line 1 is stored at chunk 0.
</details>

6. Why does the build need no `-rdc`, and what rule does that impose on `explicit.hpp` and `util.hpp`? Name one definition in each header and say why it is allowed.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
Separable compilation is only enabled under `CUTLASS_ENABLE_SYNCLOG` (`CMakeLists.txt:479-480`), which is off, and the measured nvcc line has no `-rdc`; each `.cu` is a whole program, so a symbol defined in a header included by both TUs would be defined twice at link time. Hence the headers may contain only declarations, templates, `inline` functions and macros, and no device code. `util.hpp:51` `inline cutlass::Status status_from_cuda(...)` is allowed because it is `inline`; `explicit.hpp:99-126` `make_params` is allowed because it is a template instantiated only in the harness TU. `explicit.hpp:80` `run(ExplicitGemmParams const&)` is a declaration; its definition is in `explicit.cu` only. (The further consequence for *device* code in a shared header, two copies per fatbin plus duplicate host-side shadow symbols for a non-`static` definition, is inferred in the note, Section E.3.2, not demonstrated; the implementation avoided the case.)
</details>

7. A colleague proposes passing a `CUtensorMap const*` (pointer to a global-memory copy) in the parameter block instead of the maps by value. What changes on the device, and what did the by-value choice buy?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
TMA accepts a tensor map in `.param`, `.const` or `.global` space, so it would work, but the descriptor would live in global memory: every `prefetch.tensormap`/`cp.async.bulk.tensor` would take a global address, the kernel would need the generic-proxy/tensormap fence discipline if the map were ever modified, and the first touch would be a global-memory miss instead of a constant-bank read. By value in a `const __grid_constant__` parameter, the four maps are copied into constant bank 0 at launch, `&params.tma_a` is a `cvta.param` address with no local copy, `prefetch.tensormap` warms the constant cache, and the bytes are exactly those `gemm.initialize()` encoded (the explicit path copies them out of `gemm.params()`). It also keeps the launch a single 640-byte parameter copy with no extra allocation.
</details>

# Chapter 6. The Vocabulary: PTX Wrappers W1-W37, Character by Character

**What you will learn**

- How Section 3 of explicit.cu (explicit.cu:243-601) turns 37 PTX instructions into C++ one-liners, and why each wrapper does exactly one thing while every protocol decision (who, which barrier, which parity, which count) is kept out of it.
- The anatomy of an inline-asm statement as this kernel uses it: operand numbering, `%%` escaping, `{ }` scoping, the constraint letters `"r"`, `"l"`, `"h"`, `"n"`, `"=r"`, `"+r"`, what `asm volatile` buys, and when the `"memory"` clobber is needed and when it is safely absent.
- Every dot-qualifier of every instruction: `.cta_group::2`, `.shared::cluster`, `.mbarrier::complete_tx::bytes`, `.multicast::cluster`, `.L2::cache_hint`, `.bulk_group`, `.sync.aligned`, `.mbarrier::arrive::one`, `.multicast::cluster::all`, `.parity`, `.release.cluster`, `.relaxed.aligned`, `.read`, and why each one is there.
- The hardware mechanics behind the wrappers: mbarrier phases and parity, the peer-bit address trick, TMA multicast crediting, `tcgen05.commit` as the only legal way to release a stage read by the tensor core, the TMEM lane-quadrant rule, CLC responses, and grid dependency control.
- For each wrapper: its CUTLASS origin (verified file:line), who calls it in explicit.cu (verified line numbers and actual arguments), how many times it executes per tile per CTA, and what SASS it became.

Chapter 4 explained the protocol these wrappers implement; Chapter 5 defined the constants they consume (`OFF_*`, `kPeerBitMask`, the counts and masks); Chapters 7-11 show the call sites in their roles. This chapter is the dictionary between those two levels: the exact text of each instruction and the reason for every character in it. CUTLASS line numbers in this chapter use the cb424739 numbering of explicit.cu's comments and the note; of the four headers whose working-tree lines are shifted by inserted trace probes (Chapter 1), two are cited here: `mma_sm100_umma.hpp` (working tree = cb424739 + 6 from :572; the `SM100_MMA_F16BF16_2x1SM_SS` struct is :549-587 in cb424739, :549-593 at HEAD) and `sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp` (+ 28 from :617, so `kernel :620`, `:688` and `:781` are `:648`, `:716` and `:821` in the working tree).

## 6.0 Why a vocabulary layer, and how to read an inline-asm statement

### 6.0.1 The design rule of Section 3

The banner at explicit.cu:243-254 states the contract:

```
// 3. [PROD]  E.6.2 PTX wrappers (W1-W37); each asm string is copied verbatim from the CUTLASS source named in its comment,
//    so the emitted PTX is identical to the CUTLASS kernel's (verified row by row in G.3). Grouped by hardware family:
//      warp/cluster identity  W1 (shfl), W2 (elect.sync), W3/W4 (%cluster_ctarank, %cluster_ctaid)
//      mbarrier               W5 init, W6 blocking wait, W7 peek, W8 test_wait, W9 local arrive, W10 remote arrive (mapa),
//                             W11 pair-leader arrive (peer bit), W12 local arrive.expect_tx, W13 remote arrive.expect_tx
//      fences                 W14 fence.mbarrier_init, W15 fence.proxy.async (generic-proxy writes -> async proxy)
//      cluster / named bars   W16/W17 barrier.cluster arrive/wait, W18/W19 bar.sync / bar.arrive
//      TMA                    W20 prefetch.tensormap, W21 2SM multicast load, W22 2SM load, W23 store, W24 commit_group, W25 wait_group.read
//      tcgen05                W26-W28 alloc/dealloc/relinquish, W29 mma, W30 commit (multicast), W31 ld 32x32b.x16, W32 wait::ld
//      CLC                    W33 try_cancel (the query), W34 decode (is_canceled, get_first_ctaid)
//      GDC                    W35 griddepcontrol.wait, W36 launch_dependents; W37 = __syncwarp()
//    A wrapper does exactly one thing; the protocol (who calls it, on which barrier, with which count/parity) lives in sections 5-10.
```

Three consequences shape everything below.

1. **One asm string per wrapper, copied from CUTLASS.** The explicit kernel's claim is "same PTX, no abstraction". Copying the strings (rather than retyping them from the PTX ISA) is what let the note's `check_sass.py` verify the emitted PTX row by row (note G.3: 93 PASS, 0 FAIL). When the CUTLASS function does more than emit one instruction (an election, an `if (pred)`, a fence, an address mask), the extra work is moved to the call site in C++ so that the wrapper stays a single instruction. Four kinds of relocation occur: W10 (the `if (pred)` of `ClusterBarrier::arrive(ptr, cta_id, pred)`, barrier.h:489), W21/W22 (the `& Sm100MmaPeerBitMask` that `SM100_TMA_2SM_LOAD_3D::copy` and `SM100_TMA_2SM_LOAD_MULTICAST_3D::copy` apply to the barrier address, copy_sm100_tma.hpp:115 and :292, hoisted by the kernel to `full_masked_base`, explicit.cu:770), W29/W30 (the `elect_one_sync()` of `fma` and of `umma_arrive_multicast_2x1SM`, mma_sm100_umma.hpp:570 and barrier.h:851) and W34 (the `fence_view_async_shared()` of `work_tile_info_from_clc_response`, sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp:430). W11 is the one wrapper that keeps a non-asm step inside: its `& kPeerBitMask` stays in the wrapper because `umma_arrive_2x1SM_sm0` applies it inside (barrier.h:909) and the call site is a single per-thread arrive with nothing to hoist.

2. **The address-space rule.** Every asm operand that names shared memory is a 32-bit `shared::cta` address `smem_base + OFF_*`; every C++ dereference uses the generic pointer `smem + OFF_*` (explicit.cu:22-23). The wrappers therefore take `uint32_t` addresses, never pointers. `smem_u32` (Section 6.1) is the only bridge.

3. **Convergence is the caller's problem.** Several instructions (`elect.sync`, every `.sync.aligned`, `barrier.cluster.*.aligned`, `bar.sync`) require the whole warp to execute them together. The wrappers do not check this; the role functions are written so that every branch around a wrapper is warp-uniform (`is_leader`, `is_cta0`, `warp_idx == k`, `e == 7`) and the only lane-divergent predicates are election results (a fresh `elect_one_sync()`, or the prologue's `lane_pred` reused as `is_leader_lane` around W12 at explicit.cu:736 and around the prefetches at :1113-1119) and the `lane < 4` that W13 turns into a PTX predicate inside its asm.

### 6.0.2 Anatomy of an `asm volatile` statement

Every wrapper has the GCC/nvcc form

```
asm volatile("template string" : output operands : input operands : clobbers);
```

- **Template string.** PTX text. `%0`, `%1`, ... are operand placeholders numbered in order of appearance in the operand lists, outputs first. A literal `%` (needed for PTX special registers such as `%cluster_ctarank` and for PTX register names such as `%rx`) must be written `%%`. `\n\t` separates PTX statements; adjacent string literals are concatenated by the compiler (translation phase 6 of C/C++, after preprocessing), which is why a PTX template can be split across source lines.
- **`{ ... }`.** A PTX statement block. Register declarations (`.reg .pred P1;`) and labels (`LAB_WAIT:`) inside the braces are local to the block. This is what allows W6 to be inlined at a dozen call sites without ptxas complaining about duplicate symbols (note E.6.2: "write the blocking wait and the election with PTX labels/registers inside `{ }` so they can be inlined many times"). Braces are *required* only where the template declares local registers or labels: W2, W6, W7, W8, W10, W13, W29, W34. The brace-less asm statements are W3/W4, W16-W26, W28, W31, W35/W36 (W1 and W37 are intrinsics, not asm). W5, W9, W11, W12, W14, W15, W27, W30, W32 and W33 carry braces around a single instruction with no local name, simply because the CUTLASS source does; they are harmless.
- **Constraint letters** (note E.6.2, matching the nvcc inline-PTX documentation):

| Constraint | PTX type | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `"r"` | 32-bit `.b32`/`.u32`/`.s32` register | addresses, counts, parities, coordinates, idesc, TMEM address |
| `"l"` | 64-bit `.b64` register | tensor-map generic addresses, UMMA descriptors, cache hint |
| `"h"` | 16-bit `.b16` register | the three multicast masks (W21, W30): the ISA's default `ctaMask` width is 16 bits (`::16b`; a `::32b` form exists, Section 6.6.3) |
| `"n"` | integer immediate | `cp.async.bulk.wait_group.read N` (W25): the ISA wants a constant |
| `"=r"` | write-only output | W3/W4, W7, W8, W31, W34: values the asm always writes (W34's `x0/y0/z0` are the one exception, Section 6.8.3) |
| `"+r"` | read-write output | W2 only (Section 6.2.2 explains why) |

What the constraints become in the emitted PTX (measured, `trace_out_v2/ptx_explicit.txt`, note G.3): the kernel declares four register classes, `.reg .pred %p<92>; .reg .b16 %rs<7>; .reg .b32 %r<1014>; .reg .b64 %rd<29>;` (ptx_explicit.txt:7-10), and `"r"` operands become `%r` (`.b32`), `"l"` operands `%rd` (`.b64`), `"h"` operands `%rs` (`.b16`), while `"n"` is pasted into the instruction text as a literal (`cp.async.bulk.wait_group.read 1`). The `.b16` class is tiny and fully accounted for: `%rs6` is `a_mcast_mask` at both A-load sites (:556, :658), `%rs3` is the constant 15 = `kMainloopReleaseMask` (`mov.b16 %rs3, 15;` at :1384, used by the mainloop commit at :1387), `%rs4` is `acc_commit_mask` (the accumulator commit at :1415), and `%rs1`, `%rs2`, `%rs5` carry the `is_leader` flag as a 16-bit value for `setp.ne.b16` (:34-35, :406-407, :1112); the baseline declares `%rs<16>` for the same reason plus its C path.

- **`volatile`.** Tells the compiler the statement has side effects it cannot see: it must not be deleted when its outputs are unused, must not be merged with an identical statement (two consecutive `elect.sync` must stay two instructions), must not be hoisted out of a loop. For a wait (`mbarrier.try_wait`) this is essential: without `volatile` the compiler could evaluate the "pure" asm once and spin on a stale token. Every wrapper in Section 3 is `volatile`; the CUTLASS originals are too.
- **`"memory"` clobber.** Tells the compiler the asm may read or write any memory: pending C++ stores must be issued before it, and values loaded from memory before it must be reloaded after it. It is a *compiler* fence, not a hardware one. Section 3 follows the CUTLASS origin exactly (note E.6.2):

| Has `"memory"` | Lacks `"memory"` |
|---|---|
| W5-W15 (all mbarrier operations and both fences), W18/W19 (`bar.sync`/`bar.arrive`), W20 (prefetch), W21-W23 (TMA load/store), W25 (`wait_group.read`), W30 (`tcgen05.commit`), W32 (`tcgen05.wait::ld`), W34 (CLC decode), W35 (`griddepcontrol.wait`) | W2 (`elect.sync`), W3/W4 (special registers), W16/W17 (`barrier.cluster.*`), W24 (`commit_group`), W26-W28 (TMEM alloc/dealloc/relinquish), W29 (`tcgen05.mma`), W31 (`tcgen05.ld`), W33 (`try_cancel`), W36 (`launch_dependents`) |

Why the right column is safe (my analysis, following the CUTLASS authors' choices): W2-W4 only produce register values; W29, W31 and W33 only consume registers (the shared memory they touch belongs to the async proxy and is synchronised by mbarrier waits, which do carry the clobber); W24 merely groups prior bulk operations whose issuing asm (W23) already has the clobber; W36 is a scheduling hint; W16/W17 provide the cluster rendezvous but the memory ordering of the preceding `mbarrier.init`s is carried by W14, which has the clobber and sits between the inits and W16. The one subtle case is W26: `tcgen05.alloc` writes the TMEM base address into shared memory, and the kernel then reads it with a plain C++ load (explicit.cu:888). The ordering is guaranteed because W19 (`bar.arrive`, with the clobber) sits between the alloc and the load, which is the argument of note E.6.4 (`mma_role` paragraph: the load "is guaranteed by the `"memory"` clobber of the intervening `bar.arrive 6,160` (W19, barrier.h:308), which W19 must keep per E.6.2"); W37 (`__syncwarp()`, also a compiler barrier) sits there too and would suffice on its own (my addition to the note's argument). In the left column, the clobber matters most for W25: after `wait_group.read 1` the epilogue overwrites the just-released smem stage with ordinary `st.shared` through a C++ pointer (explicit.cu:1047); without the clobber the compiler could legally hoist those stores above the wait.

### 6.0.3 The family map and the dynamic counts you will see

The per-tile counts quoted below are for one CTA on the executed path of the fixed run (beta = 0, 128 k-tiles per tile), derived from the role code (Chapters 7-10) and matching the note's inventory (note B.5, 7.5-7.7). "Pair leader" means the even rank, which alone issues MMAs and `expect_tx`; "rank 0" means the single CTA of each cluster that runs the scheduler warp. Measured quantities (SASS mnemonics, instruction counts) come from note D.2 and G.3.

---

## 6.1 Family 0: the address bridge, `smem_u32`

```
// cute::cast_smem_ptr_to_uint (cute/arch/util.hpp:93-108): the 32-bit shared::cta address of a generic pointer
__device__ __forceinline__ uint32_t smem_u32(void const* p) { return static_cast<uint32_t>(__cvta_generic_to_shared(p)); }
```
(explicit.cu:257-258)

**Purpose.** Convert the generic pointer of the dynamic shared buffer into the 32-bit address that every `shared::cta` / `shared::cluster` asm operand needs.

**Decomposition.** `__cvta_generic_to_shared` is the CUDA intrinsic for the PTX `cvta.to.shared` conversion: it subtracts the shared window base from the generic address and returns the offset inside the CTA's shared window. The cast to `uint32_t` drops the upper half, which is zero for a `shared::cta` address. There is no `asm` here: nvcc knows the intrinsic and, in this kernel, folds it into `mov.b32 %r, smem` plus the constant offset (note B.6: "no `cvta.to.shared` instruction occurs in the compiled kernel").

**Source.** `cute::cast_smem_ptr_to_uint`, cute/arch/util.hpp:93-108; the `return static_cast<uint32_t>(__cvta_generic_to_shared(ptr));` is at util.hpp:108. Verified.

**Caller.** explicit.cu:1098, once per thread: `uint32_t const smem_base = smem_u32(smem);`. Every other shared address in the kernel is `smem_base + OFF_*`.

**What the value is.** Measured (note D.1 item D5): `0x400 + (rank << 24)`. The low 24 bits are the same in every CTA (the 1 KiB of system-reserved shared memory precedes the dynamic buffer), and the cluster rank sits in byte 3. The kernel never assumes this (the comment at explicit.cu:1098 says "computed, never assumed"), but two wrappers rely on the *structure* of it: W11 clears bit 24 (Section 6.3.7), and `mapa` (W10, W13) is lowered by ptxas to a byte-3 insert (note D.2: `PRMT ..., 0x654`).

**Pitfall.** A generic pointer passed where a 32-bit address is expected compiles (both are integers after a cast) and faults or silently addresses garbage at run time. The address-space rule of Section 6.0.1 is the defence: the wrappers take `uint32_t`, the C++ dereferences take `char*`.

---

## 6.2 Family 1: warp and cluster identity, W1-W4

These four wrappers answer "who am I?" at warp and cluster granularity. They run once per thread in the prologue (explicit.cu:1101-1104, 1173-1174) and nowhere in the tile loop.

### 6.2.1 W1 `warp_idx_sync`: a warp-uniform warp index

```
// W1 [warp]  cutlass::canonical_warp_idx_sync (cutlass.h:127-133)
__device__ __forceinline__ int warp_idx_sync() { return __shfl_sync(0xffffffff, static_cast<int>(threadIdx.x / 32), 0); }
```
(explicit.cu:260-261)

**Purpose.** Produce the warp index 0..7 in a form the compiler can prove is identical in all 32 lanes.

**Decomposition.** `threadIdx.x / 32` is already the same in every lane, but the compiler does not know that: each lane computed it from its own `threadIdx.x`. `__shfl_sync(0xffffffff, v, 0)` broadcasts lane 0's value to all lanes with the full mask (all 32 lanes must participate, so the warp must be converged, which it is at kernel entry). The result is marked uniform, so every `if (warp_idx == k)` below becomes a uniform branch and the value lives in a uniform register. In the SASS it is one `SHFL.IDX`, and the role dispatch became a three-entry jump table (`BRXU`) that executes once per thread (note G.3).

**Source.** `cutlass::canonical_warp_idx_sync`, cutlass/cutlass.h:127-133: `return __shfl_sync(0xffffffff, threadIdx.x / NumThreadsPerWarp, 0);` at cutlass.h:129. The wrapper adds the `static_cast<int>` only. Verified.

**Caller.** explicit.cu:1101 `int const warp_idx = warp_idx_sync();`. Count: once per thread.

### 6.2.2 W2 `elect_one_sync`: one lane, deterministically

```
// W2 [warp]  cute::elect_one_sync (cluster_sm90.hpp:180-197): pred is 1 in exactly one lane of the converged warp, 0 elsewhere
__device__ __forceinline__ uint32_t elect_one_sync() {
  uint32_t pred = 0;
  uint32_t laneid = 0;
  asm volatile(
    "{\n"
    ".reg .b32 %%rx;\n"
    ".reg .pred %%px;\n"
    "     elect.sync %%rx|%%px, %2;\n"
    "@%%px mov.s32 %1, 1;\n"
    "     mov.s32 %0, %%rx;\n"
    "}\n"
    : "+r"(laneid), "+r"(pred)
    : "r"(0xFFFFFFFF));
  return pred;
}
```
(explicit.cu:263-278)

**Purpose.** Return 1 in exactly one lane of the warp and 0 in the other 31, so that a warp-wide instruction stream can issue a single TMA, MMA, commit or CLC query.

**Decomposition.**

| Text | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `.reg .b32 %%rx; .reg .pred %%px;` | block-local PTX registers; `%%` escapes the `%` of a PTX register name |
| `elect.sync %%rx\|%%px, %2;` | `elect.sync d\|p, membermask`: among the lanes named in `membermask` that execute the instruction, exactly one is elected; `d` receives its lane id in every lane, `p` is true in the elected lane only. `.sync` is mandatory: the instruction waits until all lanes in the mask have reached it, so the warp must be converged and every executing lane must be in the mask. The ISA guarantees determinism: "Election of a leader thread happens deterministically, i.e. the same leader thread is elected for the same membermask every time", and "The behavior is undefined if the executing thread is not in membermask" (PTX ISA 9.4, section 9.7.15.15). It does not say *which* lane wins, so the kernel must not assume lane 0; what it may rely on is that every W2 call with mask `0xFFFFFFFF` in a given warp elects the same lane, which is what makes the re-election before `tcgen05.commit` safe (Section 6.7.4). |
| `%2` = `"r"(0xFFFFFFFF)` | the full warp mask, passed as a register: the ISA wants a 32-bit operand and CUTLASS writes it as a register, hence the PTX `mov.b32 %r, -1` the note observed (note 7.2, "Operand form") |
| `@%%px mov.s32 %1, 1;` | predicated: only the elected lane writes 1 into `pred` |
| `mov.s32 %0, %%rx;` | every lane copies the winner's lane id into `laneid` (unused by the kernel; kept for PTX parity) |

**Why `"+r"` with zero-initialised locals.** `pred` is written only in the elected lane. With a write-only `"=r"` constraint the compiler would assume the asm always writes the register and could drop the `pred = 0` initialisation as dead, leaving the 31 non-elected lanes with an indeterminate value. `"+r"` declares the register as read *and* written, so the initial 0 is materialised and survives in every lane the asm does not touch (note E.6.2: "the `+r` plus the zero init is what returns 0 in the non-elected lanes; `"=r"` would leave them indeterminate"). `laneid` gets the same treatment for symmetry with the source.

**`volatile`, no `"memory"`.** `volatile` keeps every election distinct: the kernel calls W2 four times in a row inside the k-tile loop of the MMA warp (one per `tcgen05.mma`, explicit.cu:932), and without `volatile` the compiler could reuse one result for all four. No memory is touched, so no clobber (CUTLASS has none either).

**Source.** `cute::elect_one_sync`, cute/arch/cluster_sm90.hpp:180-197 (the function header at :180, `: "r"(0xFFFFFFFF));` at :194, `return pred;` at :195). Byte-identical. Verified.

**Callers** (explicit.cu, grep of `elect_one_sync`):

| Line | Who | What the election guards |
|---|---|---|
| 1103 | every thread, prologue | `lane_pred`, reused for the tensormap prefetches (1113-1119), the producer's `is_leader_lane` (1192) and the `tmem_dealloc` init (1165) |
| 1125, 1136, 1146, 1156 | warps 0, 4, 5, 3 | one fresh election per `mbarrier.init` group (mirrors `initialize_barrier_array*_aligned`, barrier.h:123/134/146, each of which calls `elect_one_sync()` itself) |
| 740 | warp 2, per k-tile | the A + B TMA pair (one election for both loads, as `sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp:619-622`) |
| 843 | rank-0 warp 1, per tile | the `clusterlaunchcontrol.try_cancel` |
| 932 | leader warp 0, per k-block | each `tcgen05.mma` |
| 942 | leader warp 0, per k-tile | the mainloop `tcgen05.commit` |
| 944 | leader warp 0, per tile | the accumulator `tcgen05.commit` |

**Count per tile per CTA.** Warp 2: 128. Pair leader's warp 0: 4 x 128 + 128 + 1 = 641 (note B.3.2 counts the same 641). Rank-0 warp 1: 1. Peer warp 0 and the epilogue warps: 0.

**What ptxas made of it (measured).** The PTX has 14 `elect.sync` sites in the explicit kernel; the SASS keeps 4 `ELECT` (prologue, two inside the `tcgen05.alloc` lowering, one at the relinquish) and none in the producer, MMA or scheduler loops: `UTMALDG`, `UTCHMMA`, `UTCBAR` and `UGETNEXTWORKID` are uniform-datapath instructions that issue once per warp whatever the lane count, so the election is folded away (note D.6 item 6, G.3). The PTX form remains the contract you write; the hardware makes it free.

**Pitfalls.** (1) Never call W2 under a lane-divergent branch. The ISA's `.sync` rule is that the executing thread waits "until all threads in the membermask execute the elect instruction": lanes that are in the mask but skip the instruction leave the others waiting (a hang), and a lane that executes it while *not* in the mask is undefined behaviour (both sentences in 9.7.15.15). In this kernel every W2 sits under warp-uniform conditions only. (2) Do not merge elections "to save instructions": the note's SASS reading shows they are already free, and merging changes the PTX contract (note E.6.7: "one per TMA A+B pair, per MMA, per commit, per CLC query"; E.6.2's W2 row: "one fresh call per TMA pair, per MMA, per commit, per CLC query"). (3) Conversely, do not "fix" the re-elections by carrying one lane predicate through the loop: because the election is deterministic for a fixed mask, re-electing per instruction is equivalent, and it is the form the baseline uses.

### 6.2.3 W3/W4 `cluster_ctarank`, `cluster_ctaid_x/y`: rank and coordinates

```
// W3/W4 [cluster]  cute::block_rank_in_cluster, cute::block_id_in_cluster (cluster_sm90.hpp:154-158, 126-132)
__device__ __forceinline__ uint32_t cluster_ctarank() { uint32_t r; asm volatile("mov.u32 %0, %%cluster_ctarank;\n" : "=r"(r) :); return r; }
__device__ __forceinline__ uint32_t cluster_ctaid_x() { uint32_t x; asm volatile("mov.u32 %0, %%cluster_ctaid.x;\n" : "=r"(x) :); return x; }
__device__ __forceinline__ uint32_t cluster_ctaid_y() { uint32_t y; asm volatile("mov.u32 %0, %%cluster_ctaid.y;\n" : "=r"(y) :); return y; }
```
(explicit.cu:280-283)

**Purpose.** Read the CTA's linear rank in the cluster and its (x, y) coordinates in the (2,2,1) cluster.

**Decomposition.** `mov.u32 %0, %%cluster_ctarank;` copies a PTX special register into a general register; `%cluster_ctarank` is the linear rank `x + 2y` (x fastest) for a (2,2,1) cluster; `%cluster_ctaid.x/.y` are the per-dimension coordinates. `"=r"` output, no inputs (the empty `:` after the output list), no clobber. The `.z` coordinate of the CuTe original is not needed (cluster z = 1) and is not read.

**Why both forms.** The rank drives the pair arithmetic (`is_leader = (rank & 1) == 0`, `peer = rank ^ 1`, explicit.cu:1106-1107) and the barrier addressing; the coordinates drive the multicast mask `0x5 << x` and the tile halves (`128 tm + 64 y`, `128 tn + 64 x`). For this cluster shape `x == rank & 1` and `y == rank >> 1` (comments at explicit.cu:1173-1174); the kernel reads both because the baseline does.

**Source.** `cute::block_rank_in_cluster`, cute/arch/cluster_sm90.hpp:154-158 (asm at :158); `cute::block_id_in_cluster`, cluster_sm90.hpp:126-132 (asm at :130-131). Verified; the wrapper splits the dim3-returning original into two scalar functions.

**Callers.** explicit.cu:1104 (`rank`), 1173 (`x`), 1174 (`y`); W3 is also read in the trace-only hang record (explicit.cu:648, compiled out). Count: once per thread each.

**Measured lowering.** `%cluster_ctarank` is `S2UR SR_CgaCtaId`; `%cluster_ctaid.x/.y` are not read from a special register but computed from `SR_CTAID.X/Y` and a driver constant table with `I2FP`/`FMUL`/`F2I` (note D.2, D.6 item 14: the only two non-epilogue `FMUL` of the kernel).

---

## 6.3 Family 2: mbarrier, W5-W13

### 6.3.1 Primer: what an mbarrier is and what "parity" means

An mbarrier is a 64-bit object in shared memory (8-byte aligned; the kernel's 344-byte barrier region, offsets 0..343, holds 43 eight-byte slots of which 33 are initialised and used; the ten slots at `OFF_EPI_LOAD_FULL` 128, `OFF_EPI_LOAD_EMPTY` 160 and `OFF_LOAD_ORDER` 192 belong to the beta != 0 path and are never initialised, explicit.cu:141-143; Chapter 5). It carries a **phase**, a **pending arrival count** and a **tx-count**:

```
   init(count)          phase 0, pending = count, tx = 0
   arrive               pending -= 1
   expect_tx(n)         tx += n           (the "arrive.expect_tx" form does both: tx += n, pending -= 1)
   complete_tx(n)       tx -= n           (performed by the hardware: TMA bytes landing, CLC response bytes)
   phase completes when pending == 0 and tx == 0:
                        pending = count (reset), phase ^= 1
```

`try_wait.parity`/`test_wait.parity` take a **phaseParity** operand (0 or 1) and answer "has the phase with that parity completed?", where the operand is the parity of either the current phase or the immediately preceding one (PTX ISA 9.4, 9.7.15.16.19, `mbarrier.test_wait` / `mbarrier.try_wait`: "Indicated by the 32-bit unsigned integer operand phaseParity, whose integer parity denotes either the current phase or the immediately preceding phase of the mbarrier object ... An even phase has integer parity 0 and an odd phase has integer parity of 1"; 9.7.15.16.12, `mbarrier.init`: "The primary and conditional phases are initialized to zero"; the CUDA Programming Guide, "Asynchronous Barriers", says the same in its own words: "The `phaseParity` operand is the integer parity of either the current phase or the immediately preceding phase of the barrier object ... When we initialize a barrier, its phase has parity 0"). A freshly initialised barrier is in phase 0; asking for parity 1 refers to the (fictitious, already complete) preceding phase and returns true at once. This is the whole reason producers start with phase 1 and consumers with phase 0 (explicit.cu:606-609, Chapter 4): the producer's first pass over the `empty[]` ring never blocks, the consumer's first wait on `full[]` blocks until the first arrival plus transaction bytes complete phase 0.

The definition also bounds what a waiter may ask. A parity names only the current phase or the immediately preceding one, so a thread that let a barrier advance two phases past the one it is waiting for would get the answer for the wrong phase (phases k and k + 2 have the same parity). The ring protocol never lets this happen: a producer cannot reuse stage `s` until it has waited on `empty[s]`, and a consumer cannot advance past `full[s]` until it has waited on it, so every barrier is at most one phase ahead of its slowest waiter whatever the ring depth (my analysis; Chapter 4 walks the phases through a full wrap of the 8-stage ring).

Three addressing forms appear across the mbarrier wrappers:

- `.shared::cta` with a 32-bit address of the executing CTA's own barrier (the init W5, the waits W6-W8, the arrives W9 and W12);
- `.shared::cluster` with an address produced by `mapa` (W10, W13): "arrive on CTA `b`'s barrier at my offset";
- `.shared::cluster` with the peer-bit-masked address (W11): "arrive on the pair leader's barrier at my offset" without `mapa`.

The `_` in `mbarrier.arrive... _, [addr]` is the sink for the state token the instruction could return; a remote (`shared::cluster`) arrive cannot return a state at all, and the kernel never uses one, so every arrive discards it.

### 6.3.2 W5 `mbar_init`

```
// W5 [mbarrier]  ClusterBarrier::init (barrier.h:391-403)
__device__ __forceinline__ void mbar_init(uint32_t smem_addr, uint32_t arrive_count) {
  asm volatile(
    "{\n\t"
    "mbarrier.init.shared::cta.b64 [%1], %0; \n"
    "}"
    :
    : "r"(arrive_count), "r"(smem_addr)
    : "memory");
}
```
(explicit.cu:285-294)

**Purpose.** Initialise one barrier with its expected arrival count (phase 0, tx-count 0).

**Decomposition.** `mbarrier.init` / `.shared::cta` (the address is in the executing CTA's window) / `.b64` (the object is 64 bits) / `[%1]` the address / `%0` the count. Note the operand order: the count is `%0` because CUTLASS lists `"r"(arrive_count)` first; the wrapper keeps the order so the PTX text is identical. `"memory"`: the barrier is memory that later asm statements read; the clobber stops the compiler from reordering ordinary smem traffic across the init.

**Source.** `ClusterBarrier::init`, cutlass/arch/barrier.h:391-403 (asm text at :397). Verified; CUTLASS's `CUTLASS_ASSERT(arrive_count != 0)` is a no-op under NDEBUG and is not copied.

**Callers and counts** (explicit.cu:1128-1166, prologue only, elected lane of the initialising warp):

| Lines | Warp | Barriers | Count | Why that count (Chapter 4 derives them; one line each) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1128-1129 | 0 | mainloop full[0..7] / empty[0..7] | 1 / 2 | one `arrive.expect_tx` by the leader lane; two `tcgen05.commit` (one per pair leader, mask 0xF) |
| 1139-1140 | 4 | CLC full[0..1] / empty[0..1] | 1 / 800 | one remote `arrive.expect_tx` per CTA; 32 + 4 x (32 + 32 + 128) consuming threads cluster-wide |
| 1149-1150 | 5 | accumulator full[0..3] / empty[0..3] | 1 / 256 | the leader's commit; 2 x 128 epilogue threads |
| 1159-1160 | 3 | throttle full[0..1] / empty[0..1] | 32 / 32 | one warp arrives on each side |
| 1166 | 0 (lane_pred) | tmem_dealloc | 32 | one warp of the peer, then of the leader |

33 inits per CTA. Measured in the explicit kernel (note G.3; `trace_out_v2/sass_explicit.txt`): 33 `SYNCS.EXCH.64` with the init word `{(0x100000 - count) << 1, (0x100000 - count) << 11}` at the Section 6.2 offsets; 32 of them are unpredicated uniform instructions because ptxas folded each group's election into the warp-index branch, and only the `tmem_dealloc` init keeps a predicate, `@!UP0 SYNCS.EXCH.64 URZ, [UR7+0x150], UR4` at `0x0790` (0x150 = 336 = `OFF_TMEM_DEALLOC`), because it is the one init gated by the prologue `lane_pred` (explicit.cu:1165) instead of by a fresh election inside a warp-uniform block. The baseline has the same shape, 42 of 43 unpredicated with the dealloc init behind `VOTEU.ALL UP0; @!UP0` (note D.2, D.6 item 8). The `0x100000` in the init word is 2^20: the ISA bounds the expected-arrival count of a `.layout::v0` barrier to [1, 2^20 - 1] (PTX ISA 9.4, 9.7.15.16.12 and Table 43), so the hardware word holds the counts as 20-bit fields; that it stores `2^20 - count` rather than `count` is read off the measured word, not documented by the ISA.

**Pitfall.** The inits must be visible cluster-wide before any remote arrive: hence W14 after each group and the W16/W17 rendezvous before any role starts (Section 6.4, 6.5).

### 6.3.3 W6 `mbar_wait`: the blocking wait with a suspend hint

```
// W6 [mbarrier]  ClusterBarrier::wait (barrier.h:410-430): blocking try_wait loop with the suspend-time hint in a register
__device__ __forceinline__ void mbar_wait(uint32_t smem_addr, uint32_t phase) {
  uint32_t ticks = kWaitTicks;
  asm volatile(
    "{\n\t"
    ".reg .pred       P1; \n\t"
    "LAB_WAIT: \n\t"
    "mbarrier.try_wait.parity.shared::cta.b64 P1, [%0], %1, %2; \n\t"
    "@P1 bra DONE; \n\t"
    "bra     LAB_WAIT; \n\t"
    "DONE: \n\t"
    "}"
    :
    : "r"(smem_addr), "r"(phase), "r"(ticks)
    : "memory");
}
```
(explicit.cu:296-311)

**Purpose.** Block until the barrier's phase with the given parity has completed.

**Decomposition.**

| Text | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `mbarrier.try_wait.parity.shared::cta.b64 P1, [%0], %1, %2;` | `try_wait` is the *potentially blocking* test: if the phase is not complete the thread may be suspended until it completes or a time limit expires, then the instruction returns `P1 = false`. `.parity` selects the parity form (operand `%1`). `%2` is the optional **timeHint** (ISA syntax: `mbarrier.try_wait.parity{...}.b64 waitComplete, [addr], phaseParity {, timeHint};`): "The optional 32-bit unsigned integer operand timeHint specifies the time limit, in nanoseconds, that may be used for the time limit instead of the system-dependent limit" (PTX ISA 9.4, 9.7.15.16.19). Earlier ISA versions named it `suspendTimeHint`; CUTLASS's comment calls it the suspend-time hint (barrier.h:414). |
| `kWaitTicks = 0x989680` (explicit.cu:189) | = 10,000,000 ns = 10 ms. CUTLASS's comment: "Arbitrarily large timer value after which try-wait expires and re-tries" (barrier.h:414-415). It is a hint for how long the hardware may park the thread before reporting failure; the loop then retries, so correctness does not depend on the value. |
| `@P1 bra DONE; bra LAB_WAIT; DONE:` | the retry loop, in PTX rather than C++ so that one asm statement is one wait. The labels are block-local (Section 6.0.2), which is why W6 can be inlined at every blocking-wait site. |
| `uint32_t ticks = kWaitTicks;` | a local, exactly as barrier.h:415, so the hint is a register operand (PTX `mov.b32 %r, 10000000`, note 7.2); the SASS turns it into the immediate of `NANOSLEEP.SYNCS 0x989680` |

**Why the retry loop is PTX, not C++.** A C++ `while (!mbar_try_wait(addr, parity)) {}` around a one-shot asm would be semantically equivalent, and the kernel's own trace build proves it: `mbar_wait_traced` (explicit.cu:629-657) loops in C++ around the four-operand `try_wait` with a `selp` and a 4 s bound. Two reasons keep the production wrapper in PTX: (a) fidelity, since `ClusterBarrier::wait` is one asm statement containing the loop and `check_sass.py` compares the emitted PTX row by row with the baseline's; (b) the hint, since there is no CUDA intrinsic for the four-operand `try_wait`, so the `timeHint` can only be passed from asm and a C++ loop would need the same asm anyway.

**Measured lowering** (note D.2, G.3): `SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT P, [addr], R` with the parity in bit 31 of `R`, and the retry placed out of line: `TRYWAIT; @!P NANOSLEEP.SYNCS 0x989680; @!P SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64; @!P BRA`. The explicit kernel has 30 such retry loops in total, 26 placed out of line + 4 inline, against the baseline's 47 + 5 (the 22 missing ones are C-path sites); the SASS counts reconcile as `NANOSLEEP` 31 = 30 retry loops + 1 alloc retry and 32 `PHASECHK.TRANS64` = 30 retry copies + 2 `test_wait` (note G.3; `NANOSLEEP` 31 re-counted in `trace_out_v2/sass_explicit.txt`).

**Source.** `ClusterBarrier::wait`, cutlass/arch/barrier.h:410-430 (`ticks = 0x989680` at :415, `LAB_WAIT:` at :419). Verified.

**Callers.** Every blocking wait goes through the `EXPLICIT_WAIT` macro (explicit.cu:237 with the trace toggle off: `mbar_wait((addr), (parity))`); the extra macro arguments vanish. Sites:

| Line | Role | Barrier (address) | Parity | When it executes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 680 | every consuming warp (`clc_consume`) | `OFF_CLC_FULL + 8 clc_idx` | `clc_phase` | once per tile |
| 735 | warp 2 | `OFF_MAIN_EMPTY + 8 prod_idx` | `prod_phase` | only when the W7 peek failed |
| 784 | rank-0 warp 2 | `OFF_THROTTLE_EMPTY + 8 thr_idx` | `thr_phase` | once per tile, no peek |
| 800 | warp 2 tail | `OFF_MAIN_EMPTY + 8 prod_idx` | `prod_phase` | 8 times at exit |
| 836, 841 | rank-0 warp 1 | throttle full, CLC empty | | once per tile each |
| 861 | rank-0 warp 1 tail | CLC empty | | at exit, only if W8 said not done |
| 918 | leader warp 0 | `OFF_ACC_EMPTY + 8 acc_stage` | `accp_phase` | once per tile, no peek |
| 923 | leader warp 0 | `OFF_MAIN_FULL + 8 cons_idx` | `cons_phase` | only when the W7 peek failed |
| 955 | leader warp 0 tail | accumulator empty | | 4 times at exit |
| 965 | warp 0 (both CTAs) | `OFF_TMEM_DEALLOC` | 0 | once at exit |
| 1034 | warps 4-7 | `OFF_ACC_FULL + 8 acc_stage` | `accc_phase` | first subtile, only when the W7 peek failed |

**Count per tile per CTA.** Unconditional: 6 CLC waits (warps 0, 2, 4-7; 7 in rank 0) + 1 accumulator-empty wait (leader) + 3 throttle/CLC-producer waits (rank 0 only). Conditional: mainloop full/empty and accumulator full, only when the peek failed. Tails at exit: 8 + 4 + 2 + 1.

**Why peek-then-wait.** A `try_wait` with a hint suspends the thread; the one-shot W7 does not. CUTLASS peeks the *next* stage immediately after advancing the state, while the current stage's work is being issued, and only enters W6 if the peek said "not yet" (Chapter 8 and 9 show the pattern). Measured: the MMA warp's blocking wait is reached only via `@!P0 BRA` out of line (note G.3).

### 6.3.4 W7 `mbar_try_wait`: the one-shot peek

```
// W7 [mbarrier]  ClusterBarrier::try_wait (barrier.h:461-478): one peek, no suspend hint; 1 = WaitDone, 0 = WaitAgain
__device__ __forceinline__ uint32_t mbar_try_wait(uint32_t smem_addr, uint32_t phase) {
  uint32_t waitComplete;
  asm volatile(
    "{\n\t"
    ".reg .pred P1; \n\t"
    "mbarrier.try_wait.parity.shared::cta.b64 P1, [%1], %2; \n\t"
    "selp.b32 %0, 1, 0, P1; \n\t"
    "}"
    : "=r"(waitComplete)
    : "r"(smem_addr), "r"(phase)
    : "memory");
  return waitComplete;
}
```
(explicit.cu:313-326)

**Purpose.** Test once whether the phase has completed; return a token (1 = done, 0 = wait again) without spinning.

**Decomposition.** The same `try_wait.parity` as W6 but with the three-operand form: no `timeHint`, so the hardware uses its system-dependent limit before returning false; no loop. `selp.b32 %0, 1, 0, P1;` converts the predicate into a 32-bit value the C++ can branch on (`if (!tok)`). `"=r"` because the asm always writes the token.

**Source.** `ClusterBarrier::try_wait`, barrier.h:461-478 (asm at :470). Verified (CUTLASS returns `static_cast<bool>`; the wrapper returns the `uint32_t`).

**Callers.**

| Line | Role | Barrier | Pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| 732 | warp 2 | mainloop empty | pre-loop peek of each `load_ktiles` call (`producer_try_acquire`, sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp:604) |
| 739 | warp 2 | mainloop empty, next stage | unconditional peek after `advance` (:617) |
| 916 | leader warp 0 | mainloop full | pre-loop peek, skipped (`tok = 1`) if `k_tiles <= 0` |
| 927 | leader warp 0 | mainloop full, next stage | peek after `advance`, skipped on the last k-tile |
| 1030 | warps 4-7 | accumulator full | once per tile, consumed at subtile 0 |

**Count per tile per CTA.** Warp 2: 2 + 128 = 130 (128 consumed; the last peek of each call is discarded, note 7.5). Leader warp 0: 1 + 127 = 128. Epilogue: 1 per warp (4). Measured: `SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT` without a retry loop (note D.2).

### 6.3.5 W8 `mbar_test_wait`: the non-blocking test

```
// W8 [mbarrier]  ClusterBarrier::test_wait (barrier.h:435-457): CLC producer_tail only
__device__ __forceinline__ uint32_t mbar_test_wait(uint32_t smem_addr, uint32_t phase, uint32_t pred) {
  uint32_t waitComplete;
  asm volatile(
    "{\n\t"
    ".reg .pred P1; \n\t"
    ".reg .pred P2; \n\t"
    "setp.eq.u32 P2, %3, 1;\n\t"
    "@P2 mbarrier.test_wait.parity.shared::cta.b64 P1, [%1], %2; \n\t"
    "selp.b32 %0, 1, 0, P1; \n\t"
    "}"
    : "=r"(waitComplete)
    : "r"(smem_addr), "r"(phase), "r"(pred)
    : "memory");
  return waitComplete;
}
```
(explicit.cu:328-343)

**Purpose.** Test the phase without any possibility of suspension; used once, in the CLC producer tail.

**Decomposition.** `mbarrier.test_wait` is the *non-blocking* sibling of `try_wait`: it returns immediately with the current completion status and never parks the thread. `setp.eq.u32 P2, %3, 1; @P2 ...` predicates the test on a C++ argument: CUTLASS's `test_wait(ptr, phase, pred)` lets callers skip the test; the kernel always passes `1u`. (If `pred` were 0, `P1` would be unwritten and the `selp` result indeterminate; the wrapper preserves the CUTLASS interface rather than fixing this, and the single caller never hits it.)

**try_wait vs test_wait vs the hint, in one table.**

| Wrapper | Instruction | May suspend the thread? | Loop? | Where used |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| W6 | `try_wait.parity ... , hint` | yes, up to the hint (10 ms) then retries | PTX loop | every blocking wait |
| W7 | `try_wait.parity` (no hint) | yes, up to the system limit, once | no | peeks that decide whether to call W6 |
| W8 | `test_wait.parity` | never | no | CLC `producer_tail` (`sm100_pipeline.hpp:1041-1050`) |

Measured: the two forms stay distinguishable in SASS, `SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64` without `.TRYWAIT` for W8 (note D.2).

**Source.** `ClusterBarrier::test_wait`, barrier.h:435-457 (asm at :446). Verified.

**Caller.** explicit.cu:860, rank-0 warp 1, `mbar_test_wait(smem_base + OFF_CLC_EMPTY + 8u * clp_idx, clp_phase, 1u)`, twice at exit (`kClcStages = 2`); W6 follows only if the result is 0. Count per tile: 0.

### 6.3.6 W9/W10: local and remote arrive

```
// W9 [mbarrier]  ClusterBarrier::arrive (local, barrier.h:509-518)
__device__ __forceinline__ void mbar_arrive_local(uint32_t smem_addr) {
  asm volatile(
    "{\n\t"
    "mbarrier.arrive.shared::cta.b64 _, [%0];\n\t"
    "}"
    :
    : "r"(smem_addr)
    : "memory");
}

// W10 [mbarrier]  ClusterBarrier::arrive(cta_id, pred) (barrier.h:486-499): remote arrive through mapa; the `if (pred)` stays in C++
__device__ __forceinline__ void mbar_arrive_remote(uint32_t smem_addr, uint32_t cta_id) {
  asm volatile(
    "{\n\t"
    ".reg .b32 remAddr32;\n\t"
    "mapa.shared::cluster.u32  remAddr32, %0, %1;\n\t"
    "mbarrier.arrive.shared::cluster.b64  _, [remAddr32];\n\t"
    "}"
    :
    : "r"(smem_addr), "r"(cta_id)
    : "memory");
}
```
(explicit.cu:345-367)

**Purpose.** W9: one arrival on a barrier of the executing CTA. W10: one arrival on the barrier at the same offset in CTA `cta_id` of the cluster.

**Decomposition of W10.** `mapa.shared::cluster.u32 d, a, b` maps the `shared::cta` address `a` to the `shared::cluster` address of the same offset in the CTA with rank `b`. `mbarrier.arrive.shared::cluster.b64 _, [d]` then arrives on that remote barrier; `.shared::cluster` is the state space that makes a cross-CTA address legal, and `_` discards the state (a remote arrive cannot return one). Calling W10 with `cta_id == rank` is a legal local arrive by another name (the dealloc handshake does the opposite: `peer`).

**The `if (pred)` moved out.** CUTLASS's `arrive(ptr, cta_id, pred)` wraps the asm in `if (pred)` (barrier.h:489). The wrapper drops the parameter; the kernel calls W10 only where it should fire (`is_cta0`, `!is_leader`, `is_leader`), so the predicate is a C++ branch at the call site.

**Source.** W9: `ClusterBarrier::arrive(ValueType const*)`, barrier.h:509-518 (asm at :514). W10: `ClusterBarrier::arrive(ValueType const*, uint32_t cta_id, uint32_t pred)`, barrier.h:486-499 (`mapa` at :493). Verified.

**Callers.**

| W | Line | Role | Barrier | Target CTA | Lanes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| W9 | 785 | rank-0 warp 2 | `OFF_THROTTLE_FULL + 8 thr_idx` | own | 32 (count 32) |
| W10 | 684 | every consuming warp (`clc_consume`) | `OFF_CLC_EMPTY + 8 clc_idx` | 0 | all lanes of each consuming warp: 32 + 4 x (32 + 32 + 128) = 800 cluster-wide |
| W10 | 837 | rank-0 warp 1 | `OFF_THROTTLE_EMPTY + 8 thc_idx` | 0 | 32 |
| W10 | 964 | peer warp 0, exit | `OFF_TMEM_DEALLOC` | `peer` (= the leader) | 32 |
| W10 | 970 | leader warp 0, exit | `OFF_TMEM_DEALLOC` | `peer` (= the peer) | 32 |

Why the CLC release always targets CTA 0: the CLC pipeline's `consumer_release` arrives on `params_.producer_blockid` (sm100_pipeline.hpp:1132-1134), which is 0, because only rank 0's scheduler produces responses and only its `clc_empty[]` is ever waited on (Chapter 7).

**Count per tile per CTA.** W9: 1 (rank 0 only). W10: 192 thread-arrivals (6 warps x 32) per CTA, 224 in rank 0 (the scheduler warp also consumes), plus 32 for the throttle release in rank 0; at exit 32 + 32 per pair. Measured lowering: `mapa` produces no instruction (a `PRMT ..., 0x654` byte-3 insert, confirming that the rank lives in address bits [24,32)); the arrive is `SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED.A1T0 RZ, [addr], RZ` for the remote form and `SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.A1T0` for the local one (note D.2).

### 6.3.7 W11 `mbar_arrive_cluster_masked`: the peer-bit arrive

```
// W11 [mbarrier]  cutlass::arch::umma_arrive_2x1SM_sm0 (barrier.h:905-921): arrive on the pair leader's barrier through the peer-bit-masked address
__device__ __forceinline__ void mbar_arrive_cluster_masked(uint32_t smem_addr) {
  uint32_t bar_intptr = smem_addr & kPeerBitMask;
  asm volatile (
    "{\n\t"
    "mbarrier.arrive.shared::cluster.b64 _, [%0];\n\t"
    "}"
    :
    : "r"(bar_intptr)
    : "memory");
}
```
(explicit.cu:369-379)

**Purpose.** Arrive on the **pair leader's** barrier at my offset, whether I am the leader or the peer, without `mapa`.

**The peer-bit mechanism.** `kPeerBitMask = 0xFEFFFFFF` (explicit.cu:187; `cute::Sm100MmaPeerBitMask`, copy_sm100_tma.hpp:45) clears bit 24. The 32-bit shared address of rank r is `0x400 + (r << 24)` (measured, note D.1 D5); bit 24 is therefore rank bit 0, the position of the CTA inside its pair. Clearing it maps rank 1 to rank 0 and rank 3 to rank 2, and leaves the even ranks unchanged:

```
  rank 0  0x00000400 + off  --&0xFEFFFFFF-->  0x00000400 + off   (itself)
  rank 1  0x01000400 + off  --&0xFEFFFFFF-->  0x00000400 + off   (its leader, rank 0)
  rank 2  0x02000400 + off  --&0xFEFFFFFF-->  0x02000400 + off   (itself)
  rank 3  0x03000400 + off  --&0xFEFFFFFF-->  0x02000400 + off   (its leader, rank 2)
```

A `shared::cta` address is also a valid `shared::cluster` address of the executing CTA, so the masked value can be used directly with `.shared::cluster` (note B.6). The same trick is applied by the 2SM TMA loads (Section 6.6.2). Colfax states the rule the same way: "a CTA can find the address of its leader CTA's mbarrier by taking its own mbarrier address and setting the 24th bit to 0" (Chapter 14 reference list).

**What nvcc emits.** The source constant is `0xFEFFFFFF`; the PTX carries `and.b32 %r, %r, -16777224` = `0xFEFFFFF8` and the SASS `LOP3 ... 0xfefffff8` (note D.6 item 2, G.3): the compiler folded the three always-zero alignment bits of an 8-byte-aligned barrier address into the mask. Semantically identical. In the producer the fold goes further, to `0xfefffff0` on the hoisted base (note G.3), which is why the literal `0xfefffff8` survives only at W11's call site.

**Why this is a plain `mbarrier.arrive` and not a `tcgen05.commit`.** This is the accumulator *consumer* release (note 13 item 1 corrects the draft that had it as a commit). The consumer's asynchronous work is `tcgen05.ld` into registers, and the thread has already executed `tcgen05.wait::ld` (W32) when it arrives: there is nothing in flight to track, so a plain arrive is correct. The *producer* side (the MMAs, W30) is the opposite case.

**Source.** `cutlass::arch::umma_arrive_2x1SM_sm0`, barrier.h:907-921 (signature at :907, the mask applied at :909, the asm text at :912, `#else`/`#endif` at :918-920, closing brace at :921); the wrapper comment's 905-921 adds the one-line comment "Always arrive on even SM of collaborating 2 SMs." at :905 and `CUTLASS_HOST_DEVICE` at :906. Verified.

**Caller.** explicit.cu:1039, every epilogue thread, after the 8th `tcgen05.ld` and W32: `mbar_arrive_cluster_masked(acc_empty_base + 8u * acc_stage);` -> 128 arrivals from the leader + 128 from the peer = the leader's `acc_empty[st]` count 256 (explicit.cu:184). The peer's `acc_empty[]` barriers are initialised but never arrived on or waited for.

**Count per tile per CTA.** 128 (one per epilogue thread). Measured in the explicit kernel (`trace_out_v2/sass_explicit.txt`): `ULOP3.LUT UR24, UR24, 0xfefffff8, URZ, 0xc0, !UPT` at `0x44c0` (the only surviving `0xfefffff8` literal, note G.3), then `SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED.A1T0 RZ, [UR24], RZ` at `0x44f0`, placed between subtile 7's `LDTM.x16` and its first `FMUL`; the masked address is warp-uniform (`acc_empty_base + 8 acc_stage` has no lane term), so it lives in a uniform register. The baseline's equivalent is `SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED.A1T0 RZ, [R62], RZ` with `R62 = (base + 0x110 + 8 acc_stage) & 0xFEFFFFF8` at `0xb090` (note D.2; 0x110 = 272 = `OFF_ACC_EMPTY`).

### 6.3.8 W12/W13: arrive with transaction bytes

```
// W12 [mbarrier]  ClusterTransactionBarrier::arrive_and_expect_tx (local, barrier.h:588-598)
__device__ __forceinline__ void mbar_arrive_expect_tx_local(uint32_t smem_addr, uint32_t transaction_bytes) {
  asm volatile(
    "{\n\t"
    "mbarrier.arrive.expect_tx.shared::cta.b64 _, [%1], %0; \n\t"
    "}"
    :
    : "r"(transaction_bytes), "r"(smem_addr)
    : "memory");
}

// W13 [mbarrier]  ClusterTransactionBarrier::arrive_and_expect_tx(bytes, cta_id, pred) (barrier.h:606-620): every lane executes, lanes with pred == 1 act
__device__ __forceinline__ void mbar_arrive_expect_tx_remote_pred(uint32_t smem_addr, uint32_t cta_id, uint32_t pred, uint32_t transaction_bytes) {
  asm volatile(
    "{\n\t"
    ".reg .pred p;\n\t"
    ".reg .b32 remAddr32;\n\t"
    "setp.eq.u32 p, %2, 1;\n\t"
    "@p mapa.shared::cluster.u32  remAddr32, %0, %1;\n\t"
    "@p mbarrier.arrive.expect_tx.shared::cluster.b64  _, [remAddr32], %3;\n\t"
    "}"
    :
    : "r"(smem_addr), "r"(cta_id), "r"(pred), "r"(transaction_bytes)
    : "memory");
}
```
(explicit.cu:381-405)

**Purpose.** Tell a transaction barrier how many bytes of asynchronous data to expect for this phase and count one arrival at the same time. W12 on my own barrier; W13 on CTA `cta_id`'s barrier, from lanes whose `pred` is 1.

**Decomposition.** `.expect_tx` adds `transaction_bytes` to the barrier's tx-count and then performs the arrive-on (pending -= 1). Doing both in one instruction matters: the phase can complete only when pending == 0 *and* tx == 0, so arming the byte count before (or atomically with) the single arrival guarantees that the phase cannot complete before the bytes have landed. Transaction bytes are debited by `complete_tx` operations the hardware performs as a TMA box or a CLC response lands. In W12 the byte count is `%0` and the address `%1` (CUTLASS's operand order, kept). W13 builds the remote address with a predicated `mapa` and uses `.shared::cluster`; `setp.eq.u32 p, %2, 1` turns the C++ `pred` into a PTX predicate so that **all 32 lanes execute the same asm statement** and only the predicated lanes act, without a divergent C++ branch.

**The two byte counts.**

| Site | Bytes | Why |
|---|---|---|
| W12, explicit.cu:736 | `kMainloopTxBytes = 49152` (explicit.cu:180) | 2 CTAs x (16384 B of A + 8192 B of B) = the six 8192-byte TMA boxes that land in the two CTAs of a pair per stage; all six credit the **leader's** `full[s]` (Section 6.6.2), so the leader expects the pair's total, and the peer's `full[s]` expects nothing |
| W13, explicit.cu:842 | `kClcTxBytes = 16` (explicit.cu:181) | one `.b128` CLC response (Section 6.8) |

**Who, exactly.** W12: `if (is_leader_lane)` (explicit.cu:736) where `is_leader_lane = lane_pred != 0 && is_leader` (explicit.cu:1192): the prologue-elected lane of the pair leader's warp 2, once per k-tile, before the loads are issued. W13: rank-0 warp 1, all 32 lanes execute it with `cta_id = lane` and `pred = lane < 4` (explicit.cu:842): lanes 0..3 arm CTAs 0..3's `clc_full[idx]` (count 1, explicit.cu:183) with 16 bytes each, one lane per CTA (note 13 item 6).

**Source.** W12: `ClusterTransactionBarrier::arrive_and_expect_tx(ValueType const*, uint32_t)`, barrier.h:588-598 (asm at :593). W13: the four-argument overload at barrier.h:606-620 (`@p mapa` at :615, `@p mbarrier.arrive.expect_tx` at :616). Verified.

**Count per tile per CTA.** W12: 128 in a pair leader, 0 in a peer. W13: 1 per tile (rank 0, 4 acting lanes). Measured in the explicit kernel: W12 is `@!P0 SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64 RZ, [UR10], R5` with `R5 = 0xc000` (= 49152) in both producer loops (`0x0ee0`, `0x11b0`; note G.3, `trace_out_v2/sass_explicit.txt`; the baseline's form is `@P0 SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64 RZ, [UR17], R2`, note D.2, the opposite predicate polarity for the same leader-lane condition); W13 is `@!P2 SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED RZ, [PRMT(lane)], R9` with `R9 = 0x10` (note D.2, G.3).

**Why bytes may land before the `expect_tx`, and why that is fine.** Nothing orders the peer's or the other pair's TMA issue after the leader lane's W12: each CTA's producer issues as soon as *its own* `empty[s]` wait passes, so rank 2's multicast box can credit rank 0's `full[s]` before rank 0 has armed it. The ISA makes this harmless: the phase completes only when the pending count *and* the tx-count are both zero, the single arrival of count 1 is still outstanding, and the tx-count is signed with range -(2^20 - 1) .. 2^20 - 1 for `.layout::v0` (PTX ISA 9.4, Table 43), so early `complete_tx` operations drive it negative until the `expect_tx 49152` brings it back to zero. "Arm before you issue" is therefore a within-thread convention (the leader's own loads follow its arrive, as in CUTLASS's `producer_acquire`), not a cross-CTA requirement; Chapter 4 ("Why this works whoever lands first") works the numbers, including a two-arrival variant.

## 6.4 Family 3: fences, W14-W15

### 6.4.1 Primer: proxies and why two fences

Blackwell distinguishes the **generic proxy** (ordinary `ld`/`st`, including `st.shared`) from the **async proxy** (TMA `cp.async.bulk.*`, `tcgen05.*`, the CLC response write). Operations in different proxies on the same memory are not ordered by program order alone; a `fence.proxy.async` establishes the ordering (PTX ISA, "membar/fence"; the CUTLASS and Colfax material cited in Chapter 14 describe the TMA-store case). Separately, `mbarrier.init` writes need a release fence before other CTAs may use the barriers; the ISA provides a lightweight fence just for that.

### 6.4.2 W14 `fence_mbarrier_init_release_cluster`

```
// W14 [fence]  cutlass::arch::fence_barrier_init (barrier.h:712-720)
__device__ __forceinline__ void fence_mbarrier_init_release_cluster() {
  asm volatile(
    "{\n\t"
    "fence.mbarrier_init.release.cluster; \n"
    "}"
    ::
    : "memory");
}
```
(explicit.cu:407-415)

**Purpose.** Make the preceding `mbarrier.init` operations visible, with release semantics at cluster scope, so that the cluster rendezvous (W16/W17) can publish them.

**Decomposition.** `fence.mbarrier_init` is a restricted fence that orders only prior `mbarrier.init` operations (cheaper than a full `fence.acq_rel.cluster`); `.release.cluster` are the only semantics/scope the ISA allows for it. The `::` (empty outputs and inputs) followed by `"memory"` is the clobber-only operand list. CUTLASS's comment (barrier.h:707-710) says it "must be composed with an appropriate sync instruction with the right scope ... e.g. `__syncthreads()` or a `cluster_arrive()` + `cluster_wait()`": W14 is the release half, W17's default acquire is the other half.

**Per-thread scope, per the ISA.** "When .op_restrict is .mbarrier_init, the synchronizing effect of the fence only applies to the prior mbarrier.init operations executed by the same thread on mbarrier objects in .shared::cta state space" (PTX ISA 9.4, 9.7.15.4, `membar` / `fence`). Only the elected lane of the initialising warp executed inits, so only its W14 orders anything; the other 255 threads' fences are harmless no-ops, which is consistent with ptxas emitting no instruction for the PTX statement. The cluster-wide publication is completed by release-by-fence (W14) plus acquire-by-wait (W17: "If the optional .acquire qualifier is absent for barrier.cluster.wait, .acquire is assumed by default", PTX ISA 9.4, 9.7.15.3, `barrier.cluster`).

**Source.** `cutlass::arch::fence_barrier_init`, barrier.h:712-720 (asm at :717). Verified.

**Callers.** explicit.cu:1133, 1144, 1154, 1164: every thread, once after each of the four init groups (CUTLASS calls it once per pipeline constructor, so the 33-init explicit kernel has 4 fences where the 43-init baseline has 6; note E.6.3). Count: 4 per thread, prologue only. Measured: it emits no SASS instruction of its own; seven bare `FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S` precede the init groups in the baseline and the attribution is inferred (note D.2, D.6 item 8).

### 6.4.3 W15 `fence_proxy_async_shared_cta`

```
// W15 [fence]  cutlass::arch::fence_view_async_shared (barrier.h:728-736)
__device__ __forceinline__ void fence_proxy_async_shared_cta() {
  asm volatile (
    "{\n\t"
    "fence.proxy.async.shared::cta; \n"
    "}"
    ::
    : "memory");
}
```
(explicit.cu:417-425)

**Purpose.** Order generic-proxy shared-memory accesses before subsequent async-proxy accesses of the same CTA's shared memory (and vice versa).

**Decomposition.** `fence.proxy.async` = a bidirectional proxy fence between the generic and the async proxy; `.shared::cta` restricts it to objects in the CTA's shared memory (the other forms are `.global`, `.shared::cluster`, or no state space for all). `"memory"` is essential here: the fence's whole purpose is to sit *after* the C++ `st.shared` stores (explicit.cu:1047) and the clobber forbids the compiler from sinking those stores below it. The note points out that CUTLASS has a clobber-less twin, `cute::tma_store_fence` (copy_sm90_tma.hpp:1214-1221: `asm volatile ("fence.proxy.async.shared::cta;");`), and that the kernel deliberately copies the `barrier.h` form with the clobber (note E.6.2 W15).

**Source.** `cutlass::arch::fence_view_async_shared`, barrier.h:728-736 (asm at :733). Verified.

**Callers.**

| Line | Role | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 683 | every consuming warp (`clc_consume`), after W34 | the response slot was just read by the generic proxy (`ld.shared.b128`) and will be rewritten by the async proxy (the next `try_cancel`) after the release; CUTLASS fences at the same point (sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp:430). The ISA gives the primary reason: the response "is asynchronously written using weak async-proxy writes to the corresponding local shared memory addr of each CTA in the requesting cluster" (PTX ISA 9.4, 9.7.15.18), so the *next* query's write to this slot is an async-proxy write that must be ordered after this generic-proxy `ld.shared.b128`; the fence establishes that write-after-read order across proxies (Chapter 7 traces the two-round reuse of the slot). |
| 1050 | warps 4-7, every subtile, after the 16 `st.shared` | the TMA store (W23, async proxy) must observe the generic-proxy stores into the C/D stage |

**Count per tile per CTA.** One per consuming warp (6; 7 in rank 0) + 8 per epilogue warp (32). Measured: `MEMBAR.ALL.CTA; FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S` pairs (12 in the explicit kernel's SASS, note G.3).

## 6.5 Family 4: cluster and named barriers, W16-W19

**Two barrier kinds that are not mbarriers.** A *cluster barrier* (`barrier.cluster.*`) is one hardware rendezvous of all threads of all CTAs in the cluster: no address, no count operand, no transaction bytes; every thread arrives once per phase. A *named barrier* (`bar.sync` / `bar.arrive`, `barrier{.cta}` in the ISA) is one of the 16 per-CTA hardware barriers 0..15, counted in *threads* (a multiple of 32), with no transaction bytes, no cross-CTA addressing and no parity to track: it completes when the stated number of threads has arrived and resets itself. Neither lives in shared memory, so neither needs an init or a fence. The epilogue uses named barrier 1 rather than an mbarrier because what it needs is exactly a thread-count rendezvous of the 128 epilogue threads of one CTA, twice per subtile, with no asynchronous bytes to count and nothing remote: one instruction, no state in smem, no phase bookkeeping and no arrive/wait split (Chapter 2, Section 2.10.2 quotes the ISA rules).

### 6.5.1 W16/W17 `cluster_arrive_relaxed`, `cluster_wait`

```
// W16/W17 [cluster]  cute::cluster_arrive_relaxed, cute::cluster_wait (cluster_sm90.hpp:48-51, 66-69)
__device__ __forceinline__ void cluster_arrive_relaxed() { asm volatile("barrier.cluster.arrive.relaxed.aligned;\n" : : ); }
__device__ __forceinline__ void cluster_wait()           { asm volatile("barrier.cluster.wait.aligned;\n" : : ); }
```
(explicit.cu:427-429)

**Purpose.** The cluster-wide rendezvous of the prologue, split into its two halves so that work can be done between them.

**Decomposition.**

| Qualifier | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `barrier.cluster.arrive` | mark this thread's arrival at the cluster barrier without waiting |
| `.relaxed` | no memory ordering is attached to the arrive (the default would be `.release`); the ordering of the inits is already provided by W14, so the release here would be redundant work |
| `.aligned` | all threads of the warp execute the same `barrier.cluster` instruction; the warp must be converged (it is: the prologue has no divergence yet) |
| `barrier.cluster.wait` | block until every thread of every CTA in the cluster has arrived; default `.acquire` semantics make the released inits visible |

(PTX ISA 9.4, 9.7.15.3, `barrier.cluster`: "If the optional .acquire qualifier is absent for barrier.cluster.wait, .acquire is assumed by default", and for the arrive ".release is assumed by default" unless `.relaxed` is written; quoted from the local text copy, see Chapter 14.)

**Why split.** Between explicit.cu:1170 (arrive) and :1179 (wait) the kernel computes `x`, `y`, `tm`, `tn` (W4 and pure arithmetic, no shared memory): the latency of the slowest CTA's arrival is overlapped with useful work, exactly as the baseline does (kernel :580 and :615). No remote barrier operation may precede the wait (comment at explicit.cu:1178), because a peer CTA might not have initialised its barriers yet.

**No `"memory"` clobber.** CuTe's originals have none (`: : );`). This is safe because the shared-memory writes that must be ordered (the inits) are asm statements with their own clobber, W14 with its clobber sits between them and W16, and no C++ shared-memory access occurs before W17.

**Source.** `cute::cluster_arrive_relaxed`, cluster_sm90.hpp:48-51; `cute::cluster_wait`, cluster_sm90.hpp:66-69. Verified.

**Callers.** explicit.cu:1170 and 1179, once per thread. Measured: `UCGABAR_ARV` and `UCGABAR_WAIT; CCTL.IVALL`, both behind a ptxas-inserted "launched as a cluster" guard with a `BAR.SYNC 0x0` fallback (note D.2, G.3).

### 6.5.2 W18/W19 `named_bar_sync`, `named_bar_arrive`

```
// W18/W19 [named barrier]  NamedBarrier::arrive_and_wait_internal / arrive_internal (barrier.h:285-288, 305-309)
__device__ __forceinline__ void named_bar_sync(uint32_t barrier_id, uint32_t num_threads) {
  asm volatile("bar.sync %0, %1;" : : "r"(barrier_id), "r"(num_threads) : "memory");
}
__device__ __forceinline__ void named_bar_arrive(uint32_t barrier_id, uint32_t num_threads) {
  asm volatile("bar.arrive %0, %1;" : : "r"(barrier_id), "r"(num_threads) : "memory");
}
```
(explicit.cu:431-437)

**Purpose.** Synchronise a *subset* of the CTA's warps through one of the 16 hardware named barriers.

**Decomposition.** `bar.sync a, b`: barrier id `a` (0..15), `b` = number of participating threads (a multiple of 32); the thread arrives and waits until `b` threads have arrived. `bar.arrive a, b`: arrive without waiting (the barrier completes when `b` arrivals, counting both kinds, have happened). Both are warp-wide. Barrier 0 is what `__syncthreads()` uses, so CUTLASS reserves ids 1-7 (`ReservedNamedBarriers`, barrier.h:169-178): `EpilogueBarrier = 1`, `TmemAllocBarrier = 6` (explicit.cu:190). The ids and counts are `"r"` registers because CUTLASS passes them as run-time values; nvcc still emits immediates in SASS (`BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING 0x1, 0x80`).

**The two populations.**

| Call | Id | Threads | Who | Why that number |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| explicit.cu:887 `named_bar_arrive(6, 160)` | 6 | 160 = 32 + 128 | warp 0 arrives after `tcgen05.alloc` wrote the TMEM base | only the warps that need the TMEM address participate: warp 0 (producer of the value) + warps 4-7 (consumers); warps 1-3 never read T |
| explicit.cu:997 `named_bar_sync(6, 160)` | 6 | 160 | warps 4-7 wait at the top of `epilogue_role` | after it, `T = *(smem + OFF_TMEM_BASE_PTR)` is safe (explicit.cu:998) |
| explicit.cu:1051, 1071 `named_bar_sync(1, 128)` | 1 | 128 = 4 x 32 | warps 4-7, twice per subtile | (1) after the fence: all 128 threads' stores to the C/D stage are in before warp 4 issues the TMA store; (2) after the store/commit/wait: nobody overwrites the stage until the store that read it one subtile earlier is done |

`"memory"` on both (barrier.h:287, :308): the barrier is exactly where C++ smem stores must be complete (before `bar.sync 1,128` the epilogue's `st.shared`; after `bar.arrive 6,160` the load of T must not be hoisted; note E.6.4, `mma_role` paragraph).

**Source.** `NamedBarrier::arrive_and_wait_internal`, barrier.h:285-288 (asm at :287); `NamedBarrier::arrive_internal`, barrier.h:305-309 (asm at :308). Verified.

**Count per tile per CTA.** W18: 16 (`bar.sync 1,128`, 2 per subtile); plus 1 `bar.sync 6,160` per CTA at start. W19: 1 per CTA at start. Measured: 16 `BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING 0x1, 0x80`, 1 `0x6, 0xa0`, 1 `BAR.ARV 0x6, 0xa0` (note G.3).
