## Checkpoint

1. A colleague proposes to save work by having the peer CTA skip its `arrive.expect_tx` *and* letting the leader expect only its own 24576 bytes. What breaks?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
The peer already skips the arrive (only <code>is_leader_lane</code> arrives, explicit.cu:736). The byte count cannot be halved: the peer's A boxes and B box carry the leader's <code>full[s]</code> as their barrier through the peer-bit mask (<code>full_masked_base + 8 s</code>, explicit.cu:747/754), so 49152 bytes will complete on it per stage whatever the leader expects. With <code>expect_tx = 24576</code> the outcome depends on how many of the six boxes land before the leader's <code>arrive.expect_tx</code>: tx-count starts at 0 and each early <code>complete_tx</code> drives it to <code>-8192 k</code> (Section 8.4.4). If 0..3 boxes landed first, the expect brings tx-count to <code>24576 - 8192 k &gt;= 0</code> and the phase completes as soon as three boxes in total have landed — possibly before the peer's half of the stage is in smem — so the leader's <code>tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2</code> reads stale peer smem: silent wrong results. If 4 or more landed first, the expect leaves tx-count at <code>24576 - 32768 = -8192</code> or lower with the pending-arrival count already 0, the remaining boxes only drive it further negative, and it never returns to 0: the leader's warp 0 hangs on <code>full[s]</code> — the "mainloop deadlock at <code>q = 0</code> -&gt; <code>expect_tx != 49152</code>" row of the note's failure-mode table (E.7.2). Silent corruption or a hang, depending on landing order. The 49152 is the sum of everything that lands in the pair (Section 8.5.3).
</details>

2. Derive the parity the producer waits for on `empty[3]` at k-tile `q = 19` of tile `t = 5`, and the parity of tail step `i = 3` after `n_tiles = 31` tiles.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
Step number <code>n = 128 x 5 + 19 = 659</code>; slot <code>659 % 8 = 3</code> (consistent); parity <code>1 ^ ((659 / 8) &amp; 1) = 1 ^ (82 &amp; 1) = 1</code>. Tail: <code>n = 128 x 31 + 3 = 3971</code>; slot <code>3</code>; <code>3971 / 8 = 496</code>, even, parity <code>1 ^ 0 = 1</code>. Every tail step has parity 1 for every <code>n_tiles</code> because <code>128 n_tiles / 8 = 16 n_tiles</code> is even (Section 8.6.8; measured in all 1518 <code>K_TAIL</code> records, note G.1).
</details>

3. Why is `a_dst_base` offset by `8192 y` but `b_dst_base` is not offset by `8192 x`?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
A is <em>replicated</em>: the two CTAs with equal <code>x</code> each load one 64-row half of the same 128 x 64 stage and multicast it to both, so the half loaded by the <code>y = 1</code> CTA must land in the upper 8192 bytes of the stage in both receivers (<code>a_row = 128 tm + 64 y</code>, destination <code>+ 8192 y</code>). B is <em>split</em>: each CTA of a pair loads only its own 64 columns (<code>b_col = 128 tn + 64 x</code>) into its own 8192-byte B stage, and the 2SM MMA reads the other 64 columns from the peer's smem at the same CTA-relative address. There is no second half to place, so no offset (Sections 8.5.4-8.5.5).
</details>

4. The producer issues 130 `try_wait` peeks per tile but only 128 blocking-wait sites are ever reached. Where do the two extra peeks come from, and are they harmful?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
Each <code>load_ktiles</code> call peeks once before its loop and once per iteration after advancing the state (explicit.cu:732, 739); the last in-loop peek of a call targets the slot the <em>next</em> call will use, and that token is a local that dies with the call. With two calls (8 + 120) that is <code>(8 + 1) + (120 + 1) = 130</code> peeks for 128 acquisitions. A <code>try_wait</code> has no side effect on the barrier, so the cost is two <code>SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT</code> per tile; CUTLASS does the same (<code>sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp:604, 617</code>, no <code>skip_wait</code>), so the explicit kernel keeps it (Section 8.4.5).
</details>

5. The explicit kernel passes the constant `0` as the third TMA coordinate and `kCacheHintEvictNormal` as the cache policy. Which of the two could you change for this fixed run without changing D, and what would you have to prove first?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
The cache hint: EVICT_NORMAL is the default policy of CUTLASS's <code>with()</code> and only steers L2 replacement; EVICT_FIRST/EVICT_LAST (<code>copy_sm90_desc.hpp:193-197</code>) would change timing, never values — but it is a deviation from the baseline, so you would have to re-measure (note Section 12) and show no regression before calling it semantics-preserving at the performance level. The batch coordinate must stay 0: the maps are rank 3 with an L extent of 1 (note Section 5.3), and the explicit kernel is an <code>L = 1</code> kernel by construction (its <code>run()</code> rejects <code>l != 1</code>; note G.3 "Generality"). Changing it would address out-of-range coordinates (zero-filled by TMA) and corrupt D.
</details>

6. Why does `load_ktiles` take `smem_base` *and* `full_masked_base`, when the second is derived from the first?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
They name different barriers. <code>smem_base + OFF_MAIN_FULL + 8 s</code> is this CTA's <em>own</em> <code>full[s]</code>, the operand of the leader's local <code>arrive.expect_tx</code> (W12 is a <code>shared::cta</code> instruction and must address the executing CTA). <code>full_masked_base + 8 s = (smem_base &amp; 0xFEFFFFFF) + 8 s</code> is the <em>pair leader's</em> <code>full[s]</code>, the operand of both TMA loads (<code>cta_group::2</code> allows the peer's barrier). On a leader the two coincide (bit 24 is already 0); on a peer they differ by <code>1 &lt;&lt; 24</code>, and the peer never executes the arrive. Hoisting the mask out of the loop is legal because <code>8 s &lt;= 56</code> cannot carry into bit 24 (Section 8.6.2).
</details>

7. Explain in two sentences why a CTA that exits right after its last TMA issue (no tail) can corrupt its pair leader's result even though all its own loads have completed.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
The leader's <code>tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2</code> reads the peer's A and B stages directly out of the peer's shared memory for up to eight more k-tiles after the peer's last issue; if the peer has exited, that smem may already belong to another CTA. The eight tail waits on <code>empty[0..7]</code> return only after both pair leaders' final commits — which are issued after their last MMAs read each stage — so they are the only thing that keeps the peer alive until its leader is done reading (Section 8.6.8; note Section 7.10).
</details>

8. The producer never computes a swizzled address. Name the two hardware units that do, the one number the kernel must get right for them to agree, and the line that checks it.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
The TMA unit on write (tensor map <code>CU_TENSOR_MAP_SWIZZLE_128B</code>) and the UMMA unit on read (descriptor <code>layout_type = 2</code>). Both XOR address bits [4,7) with bits [7,10), so the stage bases must be 1024-byte aligned: <code>OFF_SMEM_A = 33792</code> and <code>OFF_SMEM_B = 164864</code> are multiples of 1024, checked by <code>static_assert(OFF_SMEM_A % 1024 == 0 &amp;&amp; OFF_SMEM_B % 1024 == 0, ...)</code> at explicit.cu:162, on top of the dynamic base's measured <code>0x400</code> (Section 8.8.3).
</details>

# Chapter 9. The Engine: mma_role (Warp 0)

**What you will learn**

- What warp 0 of every CTA does from the first instruction (`tcgen05.alloc`) to the last (`tcgen05.dealloc`), line by line against explicit.cu:871-975, and why every number in those 105 lines is what it is.
- How one `tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2` instruction of shape 256 x 128 x 16 is assembled from the shared memory of two CTAs (the pair leader and its peer) and writes two separate 128-row accumulators into two separate TMEMs, and why both CTAs must therefore have byte-identical shared-memory layouts.
- How the engine uses the 64-bit UMMA shared-memory descriptor (bit map in Chapter 5): why the start address lives in a 14-bit field, why that field makes the leader's and the peer's descriptors identical, how the low word is advanced per stage and per k-block, and the worked values `0x4000404000011484` (rank 0, s = 3, kb = 2) and `0x4000404000012482` (rank 3, s = 7, kb = 1).
- The exact barrier protocol of the engine: peek-then-wait on `full[s]`, the blocking wait on `acc_empty[st]` (count 256), the `tcgen05.commit` to `empty[s]` of all four CTAs (mask 0xF, count 2) and to `acc_full[st]` of the pair (mask `0x3 << 2y`, count 1), and what breaks if any of these masks or counts is changed.
- The `scale_c` predicate (`D = A*B` for the first MMA of a tile, `D = D + A*B` for the other 511) and why no separate TMEM-zeroing pass exists.
- Why the CLC response is consumed *before* the current tile is computed, why the peer's warp 0 still runs the loop although it issues no MMA, and how the two warps stay in step for the termination tail.
- The termination sequence: `griddepcontrol.launch_dependents`, `tcgen05.relinquish_alloc_permit`, the leader's four-step accumulator tail with its tile-count-dependent parities, the two-arrival deallocation handshake (with a proof of why it is ordered the way it is), and the pair-collective `tcgen05.dealloc`.
- The TMEM map (128 lanes x 512 columns, four 128-column accumulator stages, `(lane << 16) | column`) and which TMEM rows belong to which CTA of the pair.
- What ptxas made of the k-tile loop (47 SASS instructions, 37 of them uniform-datapath, four `UTCHMMA.2CTA`, one `UTCBAR`, peek-then-wait) and why its issue cost disappears behind the tensor core.

Notation (Chapter 1): rank `r = x + 2y` with `(x, y) = %cluster_ctaid`; the MMA pair is `{2y, 2y+1}`; the even rank is the *pair leader*, the odd rank its *peer* (`r ^ 1`); `(tm, tn)` are tile coordinates in 128 x 128 units; `q` is the k-tile (0..127), `s` the smem stage (0..7), `kb` the k-block (0..3), `st` the accumulator stage (0..3); `smem_base = 0x400 + (r << 24)` (measured, note D.1 row D5); `T` is the TMEM base returned by `tcgen05.alloc` (measured 0, note D.1 row D6). Every CUTLASS line number below uses the numbering of commit cb424739, which is what the comments in explicit.cu cite. Two of the files cited here carry trace probes in the working tree (`git diff cb424739 --stat -- include/`). `sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp` has three insertions (hunks `@@ -614,6 +614,34 @@`, `@@ -729,6 +757,12 @@`, `@@ -870,6 +904,12 @@`), so its working-tree lines are unshifted up to :614, +28 for :615-:731, +34 for :732-:872 and +40 from :873; for this chapter's range :726-:805 that means +28 for :726-:731 and +34 for :732-:805 (anchors: `tmem_allocator.allocate` cb :728 = working tree :756, the `__syncwarp()` :729 = :757, the handshake comment :793 = :827, `tmem_allocator.free` :804 = :838). `mma_sm100_umma.hpp` has one 6-line insertion after :571 (hunk `@@ -569,6 +569,12 @@`), so :570 (`elect_one_sync`) and :571 (`mask[8]`) are unshifted and everything from :572 on is +6 (the `tcgen05.mma` asm line cb :576 = working tree :582; the operand line :579 = :585). Verify with `git show cb424739:<path>`. The two other modified headers, `sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp` (+31) and `copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp`, are not cited in this chapter; every other CUTLASS file cited here is unmodified.

## 9.1 Where the engine sits

Chapter 8 left the mainloop producer (warp 2) filling an 8-stage ring of A and B tiles in shared memory and signalling the pair leader's `full[s]` barrier with 49152 transaction bytes per stage. Chapter 10 will take the finished accumulator out of TMEM. Between them sits warp 0: the only warp that talks to the tensor core. Its job is simple to state and exacting to get right:

1. once per CTA: allocate the whole TMEM of the pair, publish the base address to the epilogue warps, build the two descriptor bases;
2. once per tile, leader only: wait until an accumulator stage is free, then for each of the 128 k-tiles wait for the stage to be full, issue four 2SM MMAs, release the stage to all four producers; finally hand the accumulator stage to both CTAs' epilogues;
3. once per tile, both CTAs: consume one CLC response and advance the accumulator state;
4. at the end: release the allocation permit, drain the accumulator pipeline, shake hands with the peer, deallocate.

The whole role is explicit.cu:871-975. We read it in that order.

---

| 871 | `[PROD] tcgen05 MMA role: warp 0 of every CTA` | The legend tags (explicit.cu:26-36): production code, hardware family tcgen05. Warp 0 of *every* CTA runs this function, not only the leader's; the leader/peer split is inside (line 915). The four citations are the note's protocol section (7.6), the note's per-call trace (B.3.2), the CUTLASS kernel branch (`sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:726-805`) and the collective's `mma()` (`sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp:651-712`) that this function de-abstracts. |
| 872-873 | `tcgen05.alloc 512 TMEM columns (cta_group::2: one allocation for the pair, the result written to smem + 384 of both CTAs)` | TMEM has 512 columns per SM (`tmem_allocator_sm100.hpp:120`, `Sm100TmemCapacityColumns = 512`); the kernel takes all of them because 4 accumulator stages x 128 columns = 512 (Section 9.3). With `.cta_group::2` the allocation is one operation performed by both CTAs' warp 0 together and the resulting base address is written to the same shared-memory offset (384 = `OFF_TMEM_BASE_PTR`, explicit.cu:152) in both CTAs (Section 9.4.1). |
| 873 | `bar.arrive 6,160 to release the epilogue warps` | Named barrier 6 with 160 participating threads: the 32 lanes of warp 0 arrive, the 128 epilogue threads `bar.sync` on it in Chapter 10 (explicit.cu:997). Section 9.4.2 derives both numbers. |
| 873 | `and the accumulator producer state; at the end relinquish + dealloc` | Both CTAs keep the 4-stage accumulator producer state in step (line 946), and both execute `tcgen05.relinquish_alloc_permit` and `tcgen05.dealloc` (lines 951, 971). |
| 874 | `The PAIR LEADER only, per tile: wait acc_empty[st] (count 256 = 2 x 128 epilogue threads released stage st)` | Only the even rank issues tensor-core work. Before reusing TMEM stage `st` it must know that *both* CTAs' epilogues finished reading it: 128 threads x 2 CTAs arrive on the leader's `acc_empty[st]` (Chapter 10, explicit.cu:1039), hence count 256 (explicit.cu:184). |
| 875 | `wait full[s] (count 1 + 49152 tx bytes, section 6)` | The mainloop full barrier: one `arrive.expect_tx` from the leader's producer lane plus six 8192-byte TMA boxes landing in the pair (Chapter 8). |
| 875-876 | `4 x tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2 (one per 16-k block; the first of the tile with scale_c = 0 overwrites the accumulator, the rest accumulate)` | A k-tile is 64 wide in K; one f16 MMA consumes K = 16 (256 bits of a row, `mma_traits_sm100.hpp:1175`), so 4 MMAs per k-tile (`kKBlocks = kTileK / kMmaK`, explicit.cu:106). `scale_c` is the instruction's enable-input-D predicate (Section 9.5.3). |
| 876 | `tcgen05.commit to empty[s] of all four CTAs (mask 0xF, count 2 per CTA)` | The release of a smem stage must reach every CTA whose smem the MMA read *and* every CTA whose producer wrote into it; Section 9.5.3 derives why that is all four, and why each CTA's `empty[s]` therefore needs two arrivals. |
| 877 | `tcgen05.commit to acc_full[st] of the pair (mask 0x3 << 2y)` | The accumulator is complete for both CTAs of the pair at the same instant (one instruction wrote both halves), so one multicast commit tells both epilogues; the other pair has its own accumulators and must not be touched (Section 9.5.4). |
| 877 | `advance the accumulator stage (both CTAs advance the state)` | The peer's warp 0 issues nothing, but it advances `{accp_idx, accp_phase}` exactly as the leader does because the source does (`:773` is outside the leader branch); nothing reads the peer's state, the line is kept for PTX parity (Section 9.5.5). |
| 878 | `TMEM address = (lane << 16) \| column; tmem_c = T + 128 st with T = 0 measured` | TMEM is addressed as a 32-bit word whose upper 16 bits select the datapath lane (0..127) and lower 16 bits the column (0..511) (`cute/pointer.hpp:314-316`, note 6.3). The D operand of the MMA names lane 0, column `128 st`; the instruction fills all 128 lanes from there (Section 9.3). |
| 879 | `The MMA tile is 256 (M) x 128 (N): rows [0,128) come from the leader's A stage, [128,256) from the peer's; N from both B halves.` | The 2SM instruction's operand split (Section 9.3): each CTA supplies 128 rows of A and 64 columns of B at the *same CTA-relative addresses*, and receives the 128 rows of D that belong to its own A rows. |
