## 9.3 The pair, the 2SM instruction, and the TMEM map

### 9.3.1 What one `tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2` computes

CUTLASS's description of the atom this kernel instantiates is `MMA_Traits<SM100_MMA_F16BF16_2x1SM_SS<...>>` (`cute/atom/mma_traits_sm100.hpp:1160-1219`). Its thread and value layouts, verified in the source, are:

```
1177:  using Shape_MNK = Shape<Int<M>,Int<N>,Int<K>>;
1178:  using ThrID   = Layout<_2>;
1179:  using ALayout = Layout<Shape <      _2,Shape <Int<M/2>,Int<K>>>,
1180:                         Stride<Int<M/2>,Stride<      _1,Int<M>>>>;
1181:  using BLayout = Layout<Shape <      _2,Shape <Int<N/2>,Int<K>>>,
1182:                         Stride<Int<N/2>,Stride<      _1,Int<N>>>>;
1183:  using CLayout = Layout<Shape <      _2,Shape <Int<M/2>,Int<N>>>,
1184:                         Stride<Int<M/2>,Stride<      _1,Int<M>>>>;
```

Read with `M = 256, N = 128, K = 16` (the fixed instantiation, note Section 4 and explicit.cu:105): `ThrID = 2` means the atom is executed by two "threads" `v = 0, 1`, which are the two CTAs of the pair (`v = x = r % 2`; `sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:427-428` reads `int cta_coord_v = cta_rank_in_cluster % size<0>(typename TiledMma::AtomThrID{});` and `bool is_mma_leader_cta = cta_coord_v == 0;`, where `size<0>(AtomThrID)` evaluates to 2 for `ThrID = Layout<_2>`). CTA `v` supplies A rows `[128 v, 128 v + 128)` (ALayout, stride `M/2 = 128` in the thread mode), B columns `[64 v, 64 v + 64)` (BLayout, stride `N/2 = 64`), and receives D rows `[128 v, 128 v + 128)` (CLayout, stride `M/2 = 128`). In words, from the Colfax cluster tutorial (reference [C2]): "Pair-UMMA must be launched from one thread in one of the CTAs that we elect as the leader CTA; in CUTLASS, we will always choose the even CTA as the leader." and "The accumulator is always split between the two CTAs in the M direction." What the PTX ISA itself says is narrower (reference [P], `tcgen05.mma`): "The qualifier `.cta_group::2` specifies that the matrix multiply and accumulate operation is performed on the Tensor Memory of the executing thread's CTA and its peer CTA", and the instruction "has single thread semantics"; it defines the pair as "Any 2 CTAs within the cluster whose %cluster_ctarank differs by the last bit only" (section 9.7.18.5.1), but its text does not say how A and B are divided between the two shared memories (the operand-split pictures are in the Matrix Shape figures). The split used below is therefore *derived from source*, not from the ISA: it is the `ALayout`/`BLayout`/`CLayout` of the atom above (`mma_traits_sm100.hpp:1179-1184`), restated in note B.6 ("A rows [0,128) and B columns [0,64) of the 256x128 instruction come from the leader's smem and the remaining halves from the peer's smem at the same CTA-relative addresses; each CTA's TMEM receives its 128 rows of D") and in Colfax [C2] ("Each CTA in the pair loads half of each MMA operand tile"). Everything below is consistent with these descriptions.

```
            one tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2 of the fixed run (M 256, N 128, K 16), issued by the LEADER's elected lane

   A operand (K-major, from smem stage s, k-block kb)        B operand (K-major, same s, kb)
   +------------------------------+                           +------------------+------------------+
   | rows   0..127  LEADER smem   |  <- A rows 128 tm_L ..    | cols 0..63       | cols 64..127     |
   |        (OFF_SMEM_A + 16384 s |                           | LEADER smem      | PEER smem        |
   |         + 32 kb)             |                           | (OFF_SMEM_B      | (same CTA-local  |
   +------------------------------+                           |  + 8192 s + 32kb)|  offset)         |
   | rows 128..255  PEER smem     |  <- A rows 128 tm_P ..    +------------------+------------------+
   |        (same CTA-local       |     with tm_P = tm_L + 1     = B columns 128 tn .. 128 tn + 127
   |         offset)              |
   +------------------------------+

   D operand (fp32, TMEM column 128 st, lane 0): the LEADER's TMEM receives rows 0..127 (its own 128 x 128 tile (tm_L, tn)),
                                                 the PEER's TMEM receives rows 128..255 (its own tile (tm_P, tn)), both in lanes 0..127.
```

Why the A rows of the pair are *adjacent* tiles: Chapter 7 derived `tm = 2 (y0 >> 1) + (x0 & 1) + x` and `tn = 2 (x0 >> 1) + (y0 & 1) + y`, so `tm` depends on the CTA only through `x` and `tn` only through `y`. The pair `{2y, 2y+1}` shares `y` (hence `tn`) and differs in `x` (hence `tm` by exactly 1): the leader holds the even 128-row tile and the peer the odd one, which together are the 256 rows of the cluster tile's M half. Each CTA's B stage holds its 64 columns `128 tn + 64 x .. +64` (Chapter 8, explicit.cu:778), and the instruction's N = 128 sees both halves. This is exactly why the instruction only works if the leader's and the peer's `SharedStorage` layouts coincide: the descriptor the leader issues carries *one* CTA-relative start address, and the hardware applies it in both CTAs' shared memory (Section 9.4.4; note B.6; reference [C2] states the same requirement for the multicast TMA copy that fills the stages: "using `cute::copy` for this TMA copy requires all CTAs in a cluster to have the same shared storage layout").

Why N = 128 and not 256 per instruction: the CTA tile is 128 x 128 (`CtaShape_MNK (128, 128, 64)`, explicit.cu:132) and the pair's tile is 256 x 128 (`TileShape (256, 128, 64) per pair`); the 2 x 2 cluster covers 256 x 256 of output per work tile by giving the two pairs different `tn`: `tn = 2 (x0 >> 1) + (y0 & 1) + y` (explicit.cu:693), and since every valid first-CTA id `y0` is even (note 7.4) this is `2 (x0 >> 1) + y`, so the pairs `y = 0` and `y = 1` take adjacent `tn`. The design reasons (A multicast across `y`, TMEM capacity, epilogue width) are Chapter 3's topic; here it suffices that the instruction shape is fixed to 256 x 128 x 16 by the instantiation and encoded once in the instruction descriptor (Section 9.4.4).

### 9.3.2 The TMEM map

TMEM is "256KB per SM in size, and is organized 2-dimensionally in 512 columns and 128 rows, or lanes, of 32-bit cells", addressed with "bits 31-16 denote the lane ID while 15-0 denote the column" (Colfax TMEM tutorial, reference [C1]; the same encoding is in `cute/pointer.hpp:314-316`: "The upper 16 bits, the 0x007F portion, refers to the 128 DP lanes. The lower 16 bits, the 0x01FF portion, refers to the 512 COL lanes"). The accumulator fragment type of the 2SM atom is `UMMA::tmem_frg_2sm<c_type>` (`mma_traits_sm100.hpp:1172`); the note (B.3.2 step 3) traces it to the per-CTA layout `((128,128),1,1,4):((65536,1),0,0,128)`: element `(m, n)` of stage `st` is at `T + (m << 16) + 128 st + n`. With `T = 0` (measured in all 264 K2 records, note D.1 row D6):

```
   TMEM of ONE CTA (the leader's and the peer's look identical; each holds its own 128 x 128 tile per stage)

   column:  0        127 128       255 256       383 384       511
            +-----------+-----------+-----------+-----------+
   lane   0 | st = 0    | st = 1    | st = 2    | st = 3    |   lane m  <->  row m of this CTA's 128 x 128 tile
   lane   1 | tile t    | tile t+1  | tile t+2  | tile t+3  |              = global row 128 tm + m
     ...    | (t%4 == 0)| (t%4 == 1)| (t%4 == 2)| (t%4 == 3)|   column 128 st + n  <->  global column 128 tn + n
   lane 127 |           |           |           |           |
            +-----------+-----------+-----------+-----------+
   address of (m, n) in stage st:  (m << 16) | (128 st + n)        e.g. (lane 64, st 1, n 48) -> 0x0040_00B0

   MMA D operand per tile:  tmem_c = T + 128 st  (lane field 0; the instruction writes lanes 0..127)
   Epilogue warp w (Chapter 10) reads lanes [32 w, 32 w + 32) from  T + ((32 w) << 16) + 128 st + 16 e
```

Which TMEM rows belong to which CTA: by `CLayout`, CTA `v` of the pair owns rows `[128 v, +128)` of the 256-row instruction tile. Those rows are *its own* CTA tile, so each CTA's 128 TMEM lanes map one-to-one onto its 128 output rows; there is no cross-CTA TMEM traffic in the epilogue (Chapter 10 reads only its own TMEM). The fourfold column split is the accumulator pipeline: `kAccStages = 4` (explicit.cu:108) because 512 / 128 = 4 is the most stages the TMEM can hold for a 128-column fp32 tile, and more stages let the epilogue of tile `t` overlap the mainloop of tiles `t+1 .. t+3` (Chapter 3 and 4 discuss the depth; here it fixes `kTmemColumns = 512`, explicit.cu:114).

---

## 9.4 Setup: allocation, publication, descriptor bases, masks, states (explicit.cu:881-908)

```
881:__device__ __forceinline__ void mma_role(char* smem, uint32_t smem_base, uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t rank, bool is_leader,
882:                                         uint32_t peer, uint32_t lane_pred, int k_tiles, int tm, int tn) {
883:  (void)tm; (void)tn;   // the MMA warp needs no tile coordinates (the TMEM stage and the smem stages are tile-independent)
884:  // TMEM allocation: whole warp 0 of both CTAs of the pair, same dst offset (tmem_allocator_sm100.hpp:124-133); result lands in smem
885:  tmem_alloc_2sm(smem_base + OFF_TMEM_BASE_PTR, kTmemColumns);
886:  __syncwarp();                                                                                // (kernel :729)
887:  named_bar_arrive(kBarTmemAlloc, kTmemAllocBarThreads);                                       // bar.arrive 6, 160 (:730)
888:  uint32_t const T = *reinterpret_cast<uint32_t const*>(smem + OFF_TMEM_BASE_PTR);             // tmem_base_ptr (:731); measured 0, never assumed (TMEM address = lane << 16 | column)
```

The signature (881-882) receives both views of shared memory that the file's address-space rule demands (explicit.cu:22-23): `smem` (generic pointer, for C++ dereferences) and `smem_base` (32-bit `shared::cta` address, for every asm operand). `x, y, rank, is_leader, peer` are the cluster identity computed once in the prologue (explicit.cu:1104-1107; `is_leader = ((rank & 1u) == 0u)`, `peer = rank ^ 1u`); `lane_pred` is the prologue's election result, used here only under the trace toggle (893: `(void)lane_pred; (void)rank;` in the production branch); `k_tiles = (params.k + 63) >> 6 = 128`; `tm, tn` are the launch tile.

Line 883 states a fact that distinguishes this warp from the producer and the epilogue: **the MMA warp needs no tile coordinates.** Its inputs are smem stages whose addresses depend only on `s` and `kb`, and its output is a TMEM stage whose address depends only on `st`. Where in the matrix the tile lives is the producer's business (TMA coordinates) and the epilogue's (store coordinates). The `(void)` casts silence unused-parameter warnings; `tm_next/tn_next` are still threaded through `clc_consume` (line 913) because the shared helper writes them, but nothing reads them here. In the baseline's SASS ptxas eliminated the `get_first_ctaid` decode in this warp accordingly ("in the MMA warp only the valid bit survives", note D.2, which describes `sass_gemm.txt`); the same elimination is expected for the explicit kernel, since `tm_next/tn_next` are dead in `mma_role`, but note G.3 does not separately record it.

### 9.4.1 `tcgen05.alloc` by the whole warp 0 of both CTAs (885)

The wrapper W26 (explicit.cu:498-503) is `tcgen05.alloc.cta_group::2.sync.aligned.shared::cta.b32 [dst], num_columns;` copied from `cute::TMEM::Allocator2Sm::allocate` (`tmem_allocator_sm100.hpp:134-145`); Chapter 6, Section 6.7.2 decomposes every qualifier. What matters for this role is why each qualifier is right *here*:

- `.cta_group::2`: the allocation is for the pair. The CUTLASS preconditions (`tmem_allocator_sm100.hpp:124-133`) are the contract: "Must be issued by a single fully active warp of the CTA", "The 2 warps from participating CTAs have the same logical warp ID" (warp 0 in both), and "Both CTAs _must_ provide the exact same dst_ptr for correctness" (line 128). That is why both CTAs' warp 0 execute line 885 (no `if (is_leader)`) and why both pass the same CTA-relative destination `smem_base + OFF_TMEM_BASE_PTR` (the rank bits in `smem_base` differ, but a `shared::cta` operand is interpreted in the executing CTA's window, so both name offset 384 of their own smem).
- `.sync.aligned`: all 32 lanes execute it convergently (it is a warp-collective instruction).
- `.shared::cta.b32 [dst]`: the result, a 32-bit TMEM address, is written to shared memory rather than to a register, because the value must reach other warps (the epilogue) and, with `.cta_group::2`, the other CTA.
- `num_columns = kTmemColumns = 512`: the PTX ISA requires that `nCols` "must be a power of 2, in the range [32, 512]" (non-exclusive form) and that "The unit of allocation and de-allocation is 32 columns and all of lanes per column" (reference [P], `tcgen05.alloc`; CUTLASS repeats it at `tmem_allocator_sm100.hpp:126`, "Must be 32 <= num_columns <= 512 and power of 2"; reference [C1]). 512 is `Sm100TmemCapacityColumns` (`tmem_allocator_sm100.hpp:120`), and the kernel uses exactly that: 4 stages x 128 columns. A smaller request would make a 4-stage accumulator impossible; a second resident CTA that could use the rest cannot exist anyway because 230400 bytes of dynamic smem allow one CTA per SM (note 6.2).

What the hardware actually does (measured on the baseline's SASS, note D.2; note G.3 reports the explicit kernel's 69-instruction allocation sequence as instruction-identical): ptxas lowers this one PTX instruction to a sequence in which **the leader's elected lane** performs the atomic `UTCATOMSWS.2CTA.FIND_AND_SET.ALIGN UP0, UR4, UR4` with `UR4 = 0x10` (allocation units are 32 columns, `ColumnsPerAllocationSlice = 32` at `tmem_allocator_sm100.hpp:119`, so 0x10 = 16 units = 512 columns), retries with `NANOSLEEP 0x64` if TMEM is not free (this loop is the ISA's "The tcgen05.alloc blocks if the requested amount of Tensor Memory is not available and unblocks as soon as the requested amount of Tensor Memory becomes available for allocation", reference [P]), stores the result locally as `STS [UR29+0x180], R9<<5` (0x180 = 384: the atomic returns the allocation in 32-column units and ptxas shifts it by 5 into a column address, which is one concrete reason `T` is a hardware return value and must not be hard-coded, Section 9.4.3) and forwards it to the peer's `smem + 384` with an `STAS` (st.async) that completes a barrier in the peer's system-reserved shared memory; the peer's elected lane waits for it and acknowledges; both warps reconverge (`WARPSYNC.ALL`). The lesson for a kernel writer: the PTX statement "whole warp, both CTAs, same destination" is the contract; the leader-does-the-atomic choreography is the compiler's and must not be hand-written.

Why TMEM must be allocated at all: TMEM is a shared SM resource partitioned among resident CTAs at run time by the allocator, and a CTA may only use the columns it has been granted (that is the whole point of the alloc/dealloc protocol; reference [C1]). The allocation also serialises CTAs on an SM: a CTA whose predecessor has not deallocated spins in the alloc (the retry loop above).

### 9.4.2 `__syncwarp()` and `bar.arrive 6, 160` (886-887)

`__syncwarp()` (W37, the `bar.warp.sync -1` intrinsic, explicit.cu:601) mirrors `sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:729`. Why any synchronisation is needed between the allocation and the reads of its result is stated by the PTX ISA (reference [P], `tcgen05.alloc`): the instruction "writes the address of the allocated Tensor Memory into shared memory at the location specified by address operand dst", and "The store operation in tcgen05.alloc is treated as a weak memory operation in the Memory Consistency Model". A weak store becomes visible to other threads only through a synchronisation that carries memory ordering, and two of them sit between line 885 and every read of `tmem_base_ptr`: `__syncwarp()` orders it for the other 31 lanes of warp 0 (which read `T` at line 888), and the `bar.arrive 6, 160` / `bar.sync 6, 160` pair orders it for warps 4-7 (the ISA guarantee is quoted below). My analysis of the `__syncwarp()` itself: after a `.sync.aligned` instruction the warp is already converged, so its purpose here is ordering rather than convergence, and in the source it is also the natural place to re-establish convergence before a named-barrier instruction. In the baseline's SASS ptxas kept a `WARPSYNC.ALL` at its position (note D.2, attribution inferred; G.3 does not re-check this detail for the explicit kernel, whose allocation sequence it reports as instruction-identical).

The wrapper W19 (explicit.cu:435-437) is `bar.arrive %0, %1;` with `barrier_id = kBarTmemAlloc = 6` and `num_threads = kTmemAllocBarThreads = 160` (explicit.cu:190-191), from `NamedBarrier::arrive_internal` (`barrier.h:305-309`).

- **Who the 160 are.** CUTLASS constructs the barrier as `NamedBarrier tmem_allocation_result_barrier(NumMMAThreads + NumEpilogueThreads, ReservedNamedBarriers::TmemAllocBarrier)` (`sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:558`) with `NumMMAThreads = NumThreadsPerWarp = 32` (`:138`) and `NumEpilogueThreads = CollectiveEpilogue::ThreadCount = 128` (`:141`). The PTX named-barrier model counts *all* participating threads, arrivers and waiters alike, in whole warps (reference [P], `barrier{.cta}`: "Each CTA instance has sixteen barriers numbered 0..15"; "Operand b specifies the number of threads participating in the barrier ... When specifying a thread count, the value must be a multiple of the warp size. Note that a non-zero thread count is required for barrier{.cta}.arrive"; 160 = 5 warps). So: 32 lanes of warp 0 arrive here, 128 threads of warps 4-7 `bar.sync 6, 160` in the epilogue (explicit.cu:997), and the barrier completes when all 160 have reached it.
- **Why `bar.arrive` and not `bar.sync`.** The ISA: "barrier{.cta}.arrive does not cause executing thread to wait for threads of other participating warps", whereas `.sync` "causes executing thread to wait for non-exited threads of all other warps participating in the barrier to arrive" (reference [P]; this is also why CUTLASS names the two forms `arrive_internal` and `arrive_and_wait_internal`, `barrier.h:285, 305`). Warp 0 has nothing to wait for: it is the producer of the information (the TMEM base), and the next thing it will do, waiting on `full[0]` for the first TMA data, is independent of the epilogue warps. A `bar.sync` would stall the first MMA until all four epilogue warps had passed their prologue. The consumers of the information (warps 4-7) are the ones that must wait, and they use `bar.sync`.
- **What publishes `T`.** The ISA guarantees that the `.sync`, `.red` or `.arrive` "instruction guarantees that when the barrier completes, prior memory accesses requested by this thread are performed relative to all threads participating in the barrier" (reference [P]). Warp 0's arrive is program-ordered after the allocation's weak store (and after `__syncwarp()`), so when the 128 epilogue threads leave their `bar.sync` the value at offset 384 is visible to them; this, not the `bar.sync` by itself, is what makes Chapter 10's plain load of `tmem_base_ptr` correct.
- **Why id 6.** Named barriers 0..15 are per-CTA hardware resources; 0 is `__syncthreads`. CUTLASS reserves `EpilogueBarrier = 1` (used by the epilogue's `bar.sync 1, 128`, Chapter 10) and `TmemAllocBarrier = 6` (`barrier.h:169-178`). Two barriers with different participant sets must have different ids; the explicit kernel keeps CUTLASS's numbers so that the PTX matches row for row (note G.3).

### 9.4.3 Reading `T` (888)

`T` is read through the **generic** pointer `smem + OFF_TMEM_BASE_PTR` (the C++-dereference half of the address-space rule, explicit.cu:22-23), mirroring `uint32_t tmem_base_ptr = shared_storage.tmem_base_ptr;` (`sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:731`). The comment says "measured 0, never assumed". Both halves are deliberate:

- *Measured 0*: all 264 K2 records of the traced run (both sites, all 132 CTAs) and the 16 CTAs of the K0 probe kernel report `tmem_base_ptr = 0` (note D.1 row D6). With one CTA per SM and the whole TMEM requested, no other allocation can precede this one, so 0 is what one expects (my analysis).
- *Never assumed*: the base is a hardware return value. If the kernel were ever run with a configuration that lets two CTAs share an SM, or allocated fewer than 512 columns, a non-zero base would be legal (reference [C1] describes allocation as dynamic; the Blackwell blog of reference [G1] remarks "From my experience, `taddr` is always zero, at least when doing only 1 allocation in the kernel's lifetime", an observation carrying exactly the qualifier that matters, not a guarantee; and Section 9.4.1 showed the hardware returning the base in 32-column units that ptxas rescales, i.e. a value computed at run time). The note's target list makes this explicit: "TMEM base read from tcgen05.alloc's result (0 here; do not hard-code)" (note D.7). Every TMEM address in the kernel is `T + ...` (lines 919; Chapter 10's 1031).

Ordering of this plain load after the allocation: on the compiler side the `tcgen05.alloc` asm has no `"memory"` clobber (W26), but the intervening `bar.arrive` asm does (W19, `: "memory"`) and `__syncwarp()` is a compiler barrier as well, so the load cannot be hoisted above either; on the hardware side the allocation's store is weak (Section 9.4.2) and the `__syncwarp()` is what orders it for the lanes of warp 0 (note E.6.4 discusses this point; CUTLASS itself does the plain load at `:731`).

### 9.4.4 The descriptor low words (895-897)

```
895:  // UMMA smem descriptors from this CTA's own stage bases; the 14-bit start-address field drops the rank bits (mma_sm100_desc.hpp:754-755)
896:  uint32_t const desc_lo_a = kSmemDescLo0 | (((smem_base + OFF_SMEM_A) >> 4) & 0x3FFFu);      // expected 0x10880 (D.7)
897:  uint32_t const desc_lo_b = kSmemDescLo0 | (((smem_base + OFF_SMEM_B) >> 4) & 0x3FFFu);      // expected 0x12880 (D.7)
```

A `tcgen05.mma` with both operands in shared memory ("SS") takes two 64-bit *shared-memory descriptors* (A and B) and one 32-bit *instruction descriptor*. Chapter 5, Section 5.8.1 gives the full bit map of the shared-memory descriptor (`union SmemDescriptor`, `mma_sm100_desc.hpp:101-127`) field by field with the reason for every value, and Section 5.8.2 does the same for the instruction descriptor; this section covers only what the engine does with them. The constant halves are (explicit.cu:171-173):

```
171:constexpr uint32_t kSmemDescHi  = 0x40004040u;   // SBO = 64 (1024 B) at [32,46), version = 1 at [46,48), layout_type = 2 (SWIZZLE_128B) at [61,64)
172:constexpr uint32_t kSmemDescLo0 = 0x00010000u;   // LBO = 1 (16 B) at [16,30); start address (addr >> 4) & 0x3FFF is OR'ed in at run time
173:constexpr uint32_t kInstrDesc   = kInstrDescConst;   // 0x10200010: c_format F32 (bit 4), n_dim 128 >> 3 = 16 at [17,23), m_dim 256 >> 4 = 16 at [24,29)
```

In one sentence each: `kSmemDescHi` is bits [32,64) of the 64-bit word, with SBO = 64 (1024 B, the distance between consecutive 8-row swizzle groups) at [32,46), version 1 at [46,48) and `SWIZZLE_128B` = 2 at [61,64) (the TMA wrote the stage with that pattern, explicit.cu:133, so the UMMA unit must read it with the same one); `kSmemDescLo0` is bits [0,32), with LBO = 1 (16 B, the canonical placeholder for a swizzled K-major layout) at [16,30) and the 14-bit start-address field at [0,14) left open for the run-time OR. The file asserts both constants (explicit.cu:174-175), and the first-MMA descriptors measured in the trace, `0x4000404000010880` / `0x4000404000012880` (note D.1 row D7), confirm them.

**Why the start address lives in a 14-bit field and what that buys.** `make_umma_desc` writes `desc.start_address_ = static_cast<uint16_t>(start_address >> 4);` into a `uint16_t start_address_ : 14` bit-field (`mma_sm100_desc.hpp:107, 754-755`). The `shared::cta` address of this CTA's smem is `0x400 + (r << 24) + OFF` (measured, note D.1 row D5): the cluster rank sits in address byte 3. Shifting right by 4 moves the rank to bits [20,22); the 14-bit field keeps bits [0,14) only. So the rank is dropped and `desc_lo_a`, `desc_lo_b` are the *same* in all four CTAs:

```
   rank r:  smem_base + OFF_SMEM_A = 0x0r00_0400 + 0x8400 = 0x0r00_8800     >> 4  = 0x00r0_0880     & 0x3FFF = 0x0880
            smem_base + OFF_SMEM_B = 0x0r00_0400 + 0x28400 = 0x0r02_8800    >> 4  = 0x00r0_2880     & 0x3FFF = 0x2880
   desc_lo_a = 0x10000 | 0x880  = 0x10880          desc_lo_b = 0x10000 | 0x2880 = 0x12880           (for every r = 0..3)
```

The file asserts the two values for the measured base (explicit.cu:177) and the trace confirmed them at the first MMA of both leaders (`desc_a = 0x4000404000010880`, `desc_b = 0x4000404000012880`, note D.1 row D7). This rank-independence is not a convenience, it is a requirement of `cta_group::2`: the one descriptor the leader issues is applied by the hardware at the same CTA-relative offset in the peer's shared memory (Section 9.3.1), so a descriptor that encoded "rank 0's buffer" would be meaningless to the peer's half of the instruction. Note what the worked example proves and what it does not: it proves that the *field* is the same number in every CTA; that the peer's bytes are nevertheless the ones read is a property of the instruction, namely that with `.cta_group::2` the CTA-relative start address is resolved in each CTA's own shared-memory window (derived from the atom layouts and note B.6, "at the same CTA-relative addresses"; the ISA text does not spell this out, Section 9.3.1). It is the same convention the ISA does state for multicast deliveries, whose data and mbarrier signal land "at the same CTA-relative offset" in every masked CTA (reference [P], `cp.async.bulk.tensor`; Chapter 8), and for the multicast commit of Section 9.5.3. The kernel therefore also needs the whole buffer to fit under the field's 256 KiB: `static_assert(kSmemBaseLow24 + kSmemBytes < (1u << 18), ...)` (explicit.cu:165; `0x400 + 230400 = 231424 < 262144`).

Why the explicit kernel masks with `& 0x3FFFu` instead of relying on a bit-field: the file builds descriptors from plain integers (no CuTe at run time), so the truncation that the bit-field performed implicitly must be written out. It is also the reason `desc_lo_*` can be formed once per CTA and advanced with 32-bit adds (Section 9.5.3).

The **instruction descriptor** `kInstrDesc = 0x10200010` (line 173 above; bit map `union InstrDescriptor`, `mma_sm100_desc.hpp:416-443`, derived field by field in Chapter 5, Section 5.8.2: F32 accumulate `0x10`, F16 inputs, K-major A and B, `n_dim = 128 >> 3 = 16` at [17,23), `m_dim = 256 >> 4 = 16` at [24,29)) fixes the 256 x 128 x 16 shape and the formats once; it is asserted at explicit.cu:176 and was measured in every K3 record (note D.1 row D7). It is a run-time `"r"` register in the asm (W29 line 526), as in CUTLASS (`mma_sm100_umma.hpp:579` in cb424739 numbering, `"r"(uint32_t(idescE>>32))`), so the PTX form matches; ptxas materialises it with `UMOV UR29, 0x10200010` in the loop (note G.3).

### 9.4.5 Barrier bases and the accumulator commit mask (898-902)

```
898:  uint32_t const full_base = smem_base + OFF_MAIN_FULL;
899:  uint32_t const empty_base = smem_base + OFF_MAIN_EMPTY;
900:  uint32_t const acc_full_base = smem_base + OFF_ACC_FULL;
901:  uint32_t const acc_empty_base = smem_base + OFF_ACC_EMPTY;
902:  uint16_t const acc_commit_mask = static_cast<uint16_t>(0x3u << (2u * y));                    // the pair: 0x3 for ranks {0,1}, 0xC for {2,3} (calculate_umma_peer_mask)
```

Four barrier arrays, all addressed as `base + 8 i` (8-byte mbarriers at the note's Section 6.2 offsets 0, 64, 240, 272; Chapter 5). All four are this CTA's **own** barriers; no peer-bit masking appears in this role because (i) the leader is the only CTA that waits on `full[s]` and `acc_empty[st]`, and the producers and epilogues of both CTAs already direct their signals at the leader's barriers (Chapters 8 and 10), and (ii) the two `tcgen05.commit` sites use *multicast*, which names the same offset in every masked CTA (the operand is interpreted CTA-relatively in each destination).

`acc_commit_mask` is CUTLASS's `calculate_umma_peer_mask` (`sm100_pipeline.hpp:94-110`): with `AtomThrShape_MNK = (2,1,1)` it sets one bit per CTA of the atom, i.e. ranks `2y` and `2y+1` (column-major cluster layout, rank = `x + 2y`), so `0x3 << 2y` = `0x3` for the pair `{0,1}` (y = 0) and `0xC` for `{2,3}` (y = 1). The mask is 16 bits because `tcgen05.commit ... multicast::cluster` takes a `.b16` cta mask operand (`"h"` constraint, W30 line 538). It is **never 0xF**: the other pair's TMEM stage `st` belongs to a different tile on different SMs, and its `acc_full[st]` has count 1 (explicit.cu:184); a stray arrival would complete a phase of that barrier before that pair's MMAs are done, and its epilogue would read a half-finished accumulator (Section 9.5.4).

### 9.4.6 The pipeline states (903-908)

```
903:  uint32_t cons_idx = 0, cons_phase = 0;     // mainloop consumer state (8 stages), leader only
904:  uint32_t accp_idx = 0, accp_phase = 1;     // accumulator producer state (4 stages), both CTAs
905:  uint32_t clc_idx = 0, clc_phase = 0, clc_count = 0;
906:  int tm_next = tm, tn_next = tn;
907:  uint32_t tile = 0;
908:  bool valid;
```

Three pipeline states, following the rule of explicit.cu:606-609 (producers start `{0, 1}`, consumers `{0, 0}`; `make_producer_start_state`, `sm90_pipeline.hpp:254-260`):

| State | Role of warp 0 | Start | Depth | Who uses it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cons_idx/cons_phase` | consumer of the mainloop ring (`full[s]`) | `{0, 0}` | 8 | leader only (lines 916-927) |
| `accp_idx/accp_phase` | producer of the accumulator pipeline (`acc_empty[st]` acquire, `acc_full[st]` commit) | `{0, 1}` | 4 | both CTAs (914, 918, 944, 946, 955) |
| `clc_idx/clc_phase/clc_count` | consumer of the CLC response slots | `{0, 0, 0}` | 2 | both CTAs (913) |

Why the consumer starts at phase 0 and the producer at phase 1: a freshly initialised mbarrier is in phase 0, and the PTX ISA (reference [P], `mbarrier.test_wait` / `mbarrier.try_wait`) says "The test_wait and try_wait operations are valid only for: the current incomplete phase, for which waitComplete returns False; the immediately preceding phase, for which waitComplete returns True." Parity 1 names the phase immediately preceding the fresh phase 0, so a producer's first pass over an empty ring passes at once; parity 0 names the current incomplete phase, so a consumer blocks until the first fill completes it (explicit.cu:607-609). The same rule is what makes the continued parities of the tail in Section 9.6.3 mandatory rather than merely convenient. The `advance<Stages>` helper (explicit.cu:610-613) is `operator++` of `PipelineState` (`sm90_pipeline.hpp:204-213`) without the `count_` member:

```
610:template <uint32_t Stages>
611:__device__ __forceinline__ void advance(uint32_t& idx, uint32_t& phase) {
612:  if (++idx == Stages) { idx = 0; phase ^= 1; }
613:}
```

A useful consequence for the mainloop state: 128 k-tiles per tile is a multiple of 2 x 8 = 16, so every tile starts at `cons_idx = 0, cons_phase = 0` and k-tile `q` always reads stage `q % 8` with parity `(q >> 3) & 1` (note 7.2). For the accumulator state, tile `t` uses stage `t % 4` with acquire parity `1 ^ ((t >> 2) & 1)` (Section 9.6.3 uses this).

---

## 9.5 The tile loop (explicit.cu:909-949)

```
909:  do {
910:#if defined(CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE)   // [TRACE]
911:    heartbeat(tile, HB_TILE_START);
912:#endif
913:    valid = clc_consume<K_CLC_MMA_KIND>(smem_base, x, y, clc_idx, clc_phase, clc_count, tm_next, tn_next, tile);   // BEFORE computing the current tile (:742-750)
914:    uint32_t const acc_stage = accp_idx;
915:    if (is_leader) {                                                                            // mma() (:762-770)
916:      uint32_t tok = (k_tiles <= 0) ? 1u : mbar_try_wait(full_base + 8u * cons_idx, cons_phase);   // consumer_try_wait(skip_wait) (:670-671)
917:      uint32_t scale_c = 0;                                                                     // ScaleOut::Zero (:676)
918:      EXPLICIT_WAIT(acc_empty_base + 8u * acc_stage, accp_phase, WAIT_ACC_EMPTY, tile, 0u);    // accumulator producer_acquire, blocking (:678)
919:      uint32_t const tmem_c = T + 128u * acc_stage;                                             // lane 0, columns [128 st, 128 st + 128): 0, 128, 256, 384 for T = 0
920:      int k = k_tiles;
921:      #pragma unroll 1                                                                          // CUTLASS_PRAGMA_NO_UNROLL (:680)
922:      while (k > 0) {
923:        if (!tok) { EXPLICIT_WAIT(full_base + 8u * cons_idx, cons_phase, WAIT_MAINLOOP_FULL, tile, uint32_t(k_tiles - k)); }   // consumer_wait (:684)
924:        uint32_t const rs = cons_idx;                                                           // read_stage
925:        advance<kStages>(cons_idx, cons_phase);
926:        --k;
927:        tok = (k <= 0) ? 1u : mbar_try_wait(full_base + 8u * cons_idx, cons_phase);             // peek the next stage; skipped on the last k-tile (:694-696)
928:        uint32_t const lo_a = desc_lo_a + 1024u * rs;                                           // + 16384 B per stage in 16-byte units (32-bit low-word add, mma_sm100_desc.hpp:861-874)
929:        uint32_t const lo_b = desc_lo_b + 512u * rs;                                            // +  8192 B per stage
930:        #pragma unroll                                                                          // (:699)
931:        for (int kb = 0; kb < kKBlocks; ++kb) {
932:          if (elect_one_sync()) {
933:            uint64_t const desc_a = desc64(kSmemDescHi, lo_a + 2u * uint32_t(kb));              // + 32 B per k-block
934:            uint64_t const desc_b = desc64(kSmemDescHi, lo_b + 2u * uint32_t(kb));
935:#if defined(CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE)   // [TRACE]
936:            if (TRACE_IN_FIRST_CLUSTER()) { TRACE_RECORD(K_MMA, 32, desc_a, desc_b, tmem_c, kInstrDesc, scale_c, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0); }   // K3
937:#endif
938:            umma_f16_2sm(tmem_c, desc_a, desc_b, kInstrDesc, scale_c);
939:          }
940:          scale_c = 1u;                                                                          // ScaleOut::One after every gemm (:706)
941:        }
942:        if (elect_one_sync()) { umma_commit_mcast_2sm(empty_base + 8u * rs, kMainloopReleaseMask); }   // consumer_release, mask 0xF (:708)
943:      }
944:      if (elect_one_sync()) { umma_commit_mcast_2sm(acc_full_base + 8u * acc_stage, acc_commit_mask); }   // accumulator producer_commit (:771)
945:    }
946:    advance<kAccStages>(accp_idx, accp_phase);                                                  // both CTAs (:773)
947:    tm = tm_next; tn = tn_next;                                                                 // (:774-775)
948:    ++tile;
949:  } while (valid);
```

In the production build `K_CLC_MMA_KIND` is `0u` and `EXPLICIT_WAIT(addr, parity, ...)` is `mbar_wait(addr, parity)` (explicit.cu:237-239), so the `[TRACE]` lines 910-912 and 935-937 vanish and every `EXPLICIT_WAIT` is the blocking W6 loop.

### 9.5.1 Consume the CLC response first (913)

`clc_consume` (Chapter 7, explicit.cu:677-706) waits on this CTA's `clc_full[clc_idx]`, decodes the 16-byte response, fences, arrives remotely on CTA 0's `clc_empty[clc_idx]` (count 800, written `32 + 4 * (32 + 128 + 32)` at explicit.cu:183 without labelling the terms; by Chapter 7's accounting the leading 32 is rank 0's scheduler warp, the 128 is warps 4-7, and the two 32s inside the parenthesis are warp 2 and this warp, in each of the four CTAs), advances the 2-slot state, and, if the response was a cancelled cluster, writes the next tile into `tm_next, tn_next`. It returns `valid`.

Why it comes **before** the current tile is computed: the loop mirrors `sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:738-776` exactly, where `scheduler.fetch_next_work` (`:742-746`) precedes `collective_mainloop.mma` (`:763`), and the fetched tile is installed only at the bottom (`work_tile_info = next_work_tile_info;` `:774`). The response consumed during tile `t` is response `t`, which names tile `t+1` (or the terminator); tile `t` itself is already known (it is the launch tile for `t = 0`, or the previous response's tile). Three consequences follow (note 7.4):

1. The initial tile is also preceded by a consume: the first thing warp 0 does in the loop is wait for response 0, which the scheduler warp of rank 0 issued at its own start (Chapter 7). Measured: rank 0's first consume preceded its first `tcgen05.mma` by 1.25 us, rank 2's by 0.58 us (note 7.6).
2. The last valid tile is computed *after* the not-cancelled terminator has been consumed, so the response that ends the loop never makes the last tile's compute wait.
3. The loop exits at `while (valid)` (949) only after lines 914-948 have run for the tile that was current, which is why `tm = tm_next` (947) and `++accp` (946) sit *below* the leader branch.

For warp 0 the consume also serves as the "go" for the tile in a subtler way: by participating in the 800-count it guarantees the scheduler cannot re-arm slot `clc_idx` until this warp has read it, which keeps the two response slots from being overwritten under a slow MMA warp (Chapter 7).

### 9.5.2 The leader's entry into a tile (914-920)

`acc_stage = accp_idx` (914) is read **before** the `is_leader` branch because both CTAs will advance the same state at 946; the leader uses it for its barrier and TMEM addresses, the peer only to stay in step.

**The skip-wait peek (916).** `consumer_try_wait(state, skip_wait)` in CUTLASS returns `WaitDone` without touching the barrier when `skip_wait` is set, else one `mbarrier.try_wait.parity` (`sm90_pipeline.hpp:590-597`); `skip_wait = k_tile_count <= 0` (`sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp:670-671`). The explicit kernel writes this as `tok = (k_tiles <= 0) ? 1u : mbar_try_wait(full_base + 8u * cons_idx, cons_phase)`. For the fixed run `k_tiles = 128`, so the ternary always takes the peek; it is kept because it is what the source does and because it protects a kernel with zero k-tiles from peeking a barrier it will never wait on. W7 (explicit.cu:313-326) is the single `try_wait` without a suspend-time hint, returning 1 for `WaitDone`. Note the order: the peek on `full[0]` is issued *before* the blocking accumulator wait (918) because that is CUTLASS's order (`:671` before `:678`). The peek has no side effect and a `WaitDone` token cannot become stale (a completed phase stays completed until this consumer releases the stage, which it has not). What the early position does *not* do is help the data arrive: `mbarrier.try_wait.parity` reports the phase state at the instant it executes and `tok` is never re-evaluated, so a peek can only observe data that has already landed, and a later peek would succeed at least as often. For this first peek the order is immaterial in practice: the producer issued stage 0 right after the cluster barrier, and warp 0 spent the allocation sequence plus its first CLC consume before reaching line 916 (rank 0's first consume preceded its first MMA by 1248 ns, note 7.6), so stage 0 has long landed (my analysis).

**`scale_c = 0` (917)** is `tiled_mma.accumulate_ = UMMA::ScaleOut::Zero` (`:676`): the first MMA of the tile will *overwrite* the TMEM stage. Section 9.5.3 explains the predicate.

**The blocking wait on `acc_empty[st]` (918)** is `accumulator_pipeline.producer_acquire(state)` (`:678`), which for `PipelineUmmaAsync` forwards to `PipelineAsync::producer_acquire` with the default `WaitAgain` token (`sm100_pipeline.hpp:207-209`, `sm90_pipeline.hpp:1110-1112, 1185-1190`): a plain blocking `wait(phase)`, no peek. Why blocking and not peek-then-wait: there is nothing useful the leader could do while TMEM is full; the only work left is this tile's MMAs, which need the stage. Why count 256 (explicit.cu:184, `kAccEmptyCount = 256`; CUTLASS `consumer_arv_count = size(AtomThrShapeMNK{}) * NumEpilogueThreads = 2 x 128`, `sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:530`): stage `st` of the *pair's* accumulator is free only when the epilogue of the leader (128 threads) **and** the epilogue of the peer (128 threads) have both finished their `tcgen05.ld`s of tile `t-4` from their own TMEMs. The MMA writes both TMEMs at once, so the leader must hold proof from both. Every one of those 256 threads arrives on the **leader's** `acc_empty[st]` through the peer-bit-masked address (Chapter 10, explicit.cu:1039; W11), and the peer's own `acc_empty[]` barriers, though initialised (explicit.cu:1150), are never waited on. Why the first four tiles never block here: the producer start phase is 1 and the barriers are fresh, so `try_wait.parity(1)` passes at once (Section 9.4.6); tile 4 is the first to wait, for the release of tile 0.

**`tmem_c = T + 128u * acc_stage` (919)**: the D operand. The column field is `128 st` (0, 128, 256, 384 for `T = 0`), the lane field is 0. The instruction writes 128 lanes starting at lane 0 in each CTA (Section 9.3.2). It is a run-time value because `T` is.

### 9.5.3 The k loop (921-943)

`#pragma unroll 1` (921) is `CUTLASS_PRAGMA_NO_UNROLL` (`:680`): the body is executed 128 times per tile, and unrolling would multiply code size and the number of live uniform registers for no gain, since the loop's issue cost is already hidden behind the tensor core (Section 9.8); ptxas kept it a real loop in both kernels with no peeled first iteration (note D.2, G.3).

**Wait, advance, peek (923-927).** `if (!tok) wait(full[cons_idx], cons_phase)` is `consumer_wait(state, token)` (`:684`): the blocking W6 loop only when the earlier peek said `WaitAgain`. Then `rs = cons_idx` (the stage to read, `read_stage`, `:687`), `advance<8>` (`:692`), `--k` (`:693`), and the peek for the *next* stage (`:694-696`) with the skip when `k <= 0`. Why the peek sits here, before the four MMAs, rather than at the top of the next iteration (my analysis): the test is side-effect-free and is issued as soon as the next `{index, phase}` is known (CUTLASS `:694-696`). Its result is fixed at the instant the `try_wait` executes, so the placement cannot make the data "arrive in time"; what it buys is pipelining of the test itself. The `TRYWAIT`'s predicate is produced here and consumed only by the branch at the loop top (note G.3: `@P0 BRA` skips the out-of-line wait when the peek succeeded), so the instruction's own latency hides behind the four MMA issues instead of sitting on the path to the next k-tile's first MMA. In steady state the producer runs up to 8 stages ahead (Chapter 8), so the peek almost always returns `WaitDone`; when it returns `WaitAgain`, the only cost is one more `TRYWAIT` at the loop top, which then finds the data present or enters the blocking loop. The peek count is structural, not measured: `k` runs 128..1, the peek at line 927 executes for `k = 127..1` and is predicated off once (`k = 0`), so a tile performs 1 (line 916) + 127 (line 927) = 128 peeks; note B.3.2 derives the same count from the source and G.3 confirms that the SASS keeps exactly this predication, while how often a peek *failed* at run time was not measured. The skip on the last k-tile avoids a redundant peek: the next thing the warp does with `full[cons_idx]` is the fresh peek of line 916 in the next tile.

**Descriptor arithmetic (928-929, 933-934).**

```
   lo_a = desc_lo_a + 1024 rs + 2 kb         1024 = 16384 B / 16 B  (one A stage: 128 rows x 64 fp16 x 2 B)
   lo_b = desc_lo_b +  512 rs + 2 kb          512 =  8192 B / 16 B  (one B stage:  64 rows x 64 fp16 x 2 B)
                                                 2 =    32 B / 16 B  (one k-block: 16 fp16 along K)
```

These are `DescriptorIterator::operator+` on the *low 32-bit word only* (`mma_sm100_desc.hpp:861-874`: for CUDA 13.3 the `#else` branch `ret.lo = desc_.lo + uint32_t(offset); ret.hi = desc_.hi;` is compiled), which is why the kernel keeps `desc_lo_*` as 32-bit integers and forms the 64-bit operand only at the asm boundary with `desc64(kSmemDescHi, lo)` (explicit.cu:616). The add can never carry out of the 14-bit field: the largest low-14-bit value is B's `0x2880 + 7 x 512 + 6 = 13958 < 16384` (note B.3.2 step 8 states the bound as `13894 + (smem >> 4)` with `smem >> 4 = 64`), so a plain add is exact. ptxas lowers the stage term with `ULEA` (shift-add by `rs << 10` and `rs << 9`) and the k-block term with `UIADD3 +0x2/+0x4/+0x6`, re-materialising the high word with `UMOV URn, 0x40004040` (note D.2 and G.3, measured).

Why `+32 B per k-block` is the right address inside a swizzled stage: the K-major SW128 canonical layout is `Swizzle<3,4,3> o ((8,n),2):((8,SBO),1)` in 16-byte units (`mma_sm100_desc.hpp:807`); a row holds 64 fp16 = 128 B = eight 16-byte chunks, and k-block `kb` is chunks `[2 kb, 2 kb + 2)` of every row before swizzling. The UMMA unit applies the same XOR of address bits [4,7) with bits [7,10) that the TMA applied on write, so advancing the start address by 2 chunks selects the right pre-swizzle columns in every row of the 8-row group; the SBO (1024 B) steps between groups. The kernel never computes the swizzle (explicit.cu:203).

**The four MMAs (930-941).** The k-block loop is fully unrolled (`CUTLASS_PRAGMA_UNROLL`, `:699`; the source comment at `:698` says why: "Unroll the K mode manually so we can set scale C to 1") so that `scale_c` is a compile-time 1 for `kb = 1..3` and only the `kb = 0` instruction carries a live predicate (note D.2: "only the k-block-0 MMA has a live scale_c register"), and so that the `+2 kb` adds become immediates. Each iteration is `if (elect_one_sync()) { ... umma_f16_2sm(...); }`: one lane issues, as in `SM100_MMA_F16BF16_2x1SM_SS::fma` (`mma_sm100_umma.hpp:570`, `if (cute::elect_one_sync())`), whose body is W29 verbatim (explicit.cu:517-529):

```
517:__device__ __forceinline__ void umma_f16_2sm(uint32_t tmem_c, uint64_t desc_a, uint64_t desc_b, uint32_t idesc, uint32_t scaleC) {
518:  uint32_t mask[8] = {0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0};
519:  asm volatile(
520:    "{\n\t"
521:    ".reg .pred p;\n\t"
522:    "setp.ne.b32 p, %4, 0;\n\t"
523:    "tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2.kind::f16 [%0], %1, %2, %3, {%5, %6, %7, %8, %9, %10, %11, %12}, p; \n\t"
524:    "}\n"
525:    :
526:    : "r"(tmem_c), "l"(desc_a), "l"(desc_b), "r"(idesc), "r"(scaleC),
527:      "r"(mask[0]), "r"(mask[1]), "r"(mask[2]), "r"(mask[3]),
528:      "r"(mask[4]), "r"(mask[5]), "r"(mask[6]), "r"(mask[7]));
529:}
```

Chapter 6, Section 6.7.3 decomposes every qualifier of this instruction; here are the operands under the ISA's own names (reference [P], `tcgen05.mma`, whose syntax is `tcgen05.mma.cta_group.kind [d-tmem], a-desc, b-desc, idesc, { disable-output-lane }, enable-input-d {, scale-input-d};`). `[%0]` is `d-tmem`, the TMEM D address; `%1, %2` are `a-desc`, `b-desc`, the 64-bit shared-memory descriptors (`"l"`); `%3` is `idesc`; `p` is **`enable-input-d`**, computed by `setp.ne.b32 p, scaleC, 0`: "The operation of the form D = A*B is issued when the input predicate argument enable-input-d is false", otherwise `D = A*B + D` (reference [C1]: the parameter switches between "zeroing out the accumulators before executing MMA (the operation D = A * B) and retaining the accumulators (D = A * B + D)"; reference [M1]: "false computes D=A x B, while true computes D=A x B+D"). The eight zero `.b32` operands `{%5, ..., %12}` are the **`disable-output-lane`** vector: "a mask where each bit corresponds to a lane of the Tensor Memory ... If a bit in the mask is 1, then the corresponding lane in the Tensor Memory for the resultant matrix D will not be updated"; the vector has 4 elements for `.cta_group::1` and 8 for `.cta_group::2` (8 x 32 = 256 bits, one per TMEM lane of the pair), so all zero means every lane of both CTAs is written (CUTLASS's `uint32_t mask[8]`, `mma_sm100_umma.hpp:571`). They are registers in the PTX and vanish from the SASS (`UTCHMMA.2CTA` has no mask operands, note D.2). The optional immediate `scale-input-d` (`D = A*B + D * 2^-s`, `s` in [0, 15], valid for `.kind::f16` and `.kind::tf32`) is absent, so `D` enters unscaled. `.kind::f16` selects the FP16/BF16-input family; the F16 input and F32 accumulate choices are in the instruction descriptor.

**What `scale_c = 0` then `1` achieves (917, 940).** The first instruction of each tile (`q = 0, kb = 0`) writes `A x B` into TMEM stage `st` without reading it, so the stage needs no separate zeroing pass before a tile and the stale accumulator of tile `t-4` is simply overwritten. The other 511 instructions accumulate. Line 940 `scale_c = 1u` after *every* MMA is `tiled_mma.accumulate_ = UMMA::ScaleOut::One` (`:706`); setting it inside the loop rather than once after `kb = 0` keeps the source structure (and lets the compiler see the constant for `kb >= 1`). Measured: K3 recorded `scale_c = 0` in the first MMA of each leader and `1` in the following 15 (note 7.6); in the SASS the first `UTCHMMA` is predicated by a uniform predicate cleared once per tile and set right after that instruction, and the other three by the constant-true predicate (note D.2, G.3).

Why issue through `elect_one_sync()` and not `if (lane == 0)`: `tcgen05.mma` is issued by a single thread (the ISA: the instruction "has single thread semantics, unlike the collective instructions mma.sync or wgmma.mma_async. So, a single thread issuing the tcgen05.mma will result in the initiation of the whole matrix multiply and accumulate operation", reference [P]; reference [C1]: "Only one thread is used to launch UMMA"), the warp is converged at this point, and `elect.sync` is CUTLASS's idiom whose result ptxas recognises as warp-uniform issue: every `ELECT` in the producer, MMA and scheduler loops is folded away and the `UTCHMMA.2CTA` is issued once per warp as a uniform-datapath instruction (note D.6 item 6, G.3). The explicit kernel keeps one election per issue site (4 MMAs + 1 commit per k-tile, 1 accumulator commit per tile: 641 per tile in the PTX, note B.3.2) because that is the PTX contract the baseline writes; a `lane == 0` test would be semantically equivalent but would not reproduce the baseline's PTX.

**The commit to `empty[rs]` with mask 0xF (942).** After the fourth MMA the elected lane issues W30 (explicit.cu:532-540), `tcgen05.commit.cta_group::2.mbarrier::arrive::one.shared::cluster.multicast::cluster.b64 [empty_base + 8 rs], 0xF`, copied from `umma_arrive_multicast_2x1SM` (`barrier.h:848-861`), which is what `consumer_release` becomes for a 2SM pipeline (`sm100_pipeline.hpp:740-745`). Semantics (reference [P], `tcgen05.commit`; Chapter 6, Section 6.7.4 defines each qualifier): `tcgen05.commit` is itself asynchronous; "the instruction tcgen05.commit.cta_group::2 tracks for the completion of all prior asynchronous tcgen05 operations with .cta_group::2 issued by the current thread"; `.mbarrier::arrive::one` "indicates that upon the completion of the prior asynchronous tcgen05 operation issued by the current thread, an arrive-on operation, with the count argument of 1, is signaled on the mbarrier object", at cluster scope; and `.multicast::cluster` "allows signaling on the mbarrier objects of multiple CTAs in the cluster", each bit of the 16-bit `ctaMask` corresponding to the `%cluster_ctarank` of a destination CTA, at the same CTA-relative barrier offset. Two of these qualifiers do work that the chapter relies on. `.cta_group::2` is not a per-instruction choice: "All tcgen05 instructions within a kernel must specify the same value for the .cta_group qualifier" (stated under `tcgen05.mma`, `tcgen05.commit` and `tcgen05.alloc`), which is why alloc, dealloc, relinquish, mma and commit in explicit.cu all carry `::2` although only the MMA needs the pair; and because the commit tracks the pair's `::2` operations, the one commit issued by the leader's thread covers the writes into *both* CTAs' TMEM. `.mbarrier::arrive::one` is what makes the barrier counts add up: exactly one arrive-on per destination barrier per commit, so `acc_full[st]` (one leader) needs count 1 and `empty[s]` (two leaders) needs count 2. Three design facts follow:

- It must be issued by the **same thread** that issued the MMAs (the tracking is per issuing thread), right after them, with no wait; the arrival happens later, when the tensor core has finished reading stage `rs`. A plain `mbarrier.arrive` from that thread would fire immediately and release the stage while it is still being read (note 7.6).
- **Why mask 0xF (`kMainloopReleaseMask`, explicit.cu:186) and not the pair's 0x3/0xC.** Stage `s` in the smem of CTA `r` is *read* by the MMA of `r`'s pair leader, but it is *written* by two producers: `r`'s own warp 2 (its B half and its A half) and the warp 2 of CTA `r ^ 2` (the CTA with the same `x` and the other `y`, i.e. the one that shares this CTA's `tm` and receives the same A rows; the words row and column are avoided here because CUTLASS's comments at `sm100_pipeline.hpp:60-61` call equal `x` "same MMA cluster col" and equal `y` "same MMA cluster row"), whose A multicast with mask `0x5 << x` lands its 64-row half at `OFF_SMEM_A + 16384 s + 8192 y'` in both CTAs `x` and `x + 2` (Chapter 8, explicit.cu:747, 772). Before CTA `r ^ 2`'s producer may overwrite stage `s`, it waits on **its own** `empty[s]`, so that barrier must be released not only when `r ^ 2`'s pair has finished reading `s` but also when `r`'s pair has, because the multicast write also lands in `r`. Symmetrically for `r`. Hence every leader's release must reach all four CTAs, and every CTA's `empty[s]` receives one arrival from each of the two leaders: **count 2** (`kMainEmptyCount = 2`, explicit.cu:182; CUTLASS `multicast_consumer_arrival_count = size<0>(cluster)/size<0>(atom) + size<1>(cluster)/size<1>(atom) - 1 = 2/2 + 2/1 - 1 = 2`, `sm100_pipeline.hpp:565-566`; `calculate_multicast_mask<kRowCol>` yields the CTAs in the same MMA column *or* the same MMA row, which for a 2 x 2 cluster with a 2 x 1 atom is everyone, `sm100_pipeline.hpp:57-91`).
- **What mask 0x3 would break.** With the pair mask, CTA `r`'s `empty[s]` would get one arrival per use (from its own leader) against a count of 2, so its producer would block forever at the second use of the ring: a deadlock after 8 k-tiles. If one "fixed" that by lowering the count to 1, CTA `r`'s producer would reuse stage `s` as soon as its own pair was done, and its A multicast would overwrite the half of stage `s` in CTA `r ^ 2` while the other pair's MMA might still be reading it: a silent data race on A, i.e. wrong results in the other pair's tile.

```
   stage s of CTA r is written by:  r's TMA (B half, A half)  and  (r ^ 2)'s TMA (A half, multicast 0x5 << x)
   stage s of CTA r is read by:     the 2SM MMA issued by leader(r) = r & ~1   (reads both CTAs of the pair)
   so before ANY producer rewrites stage s anywhere, BOTH leaders' MMAs on stage s must be done:
       leader 0 --commit 0xF--> empty[s] of ranks 0,1,2,3        leader 2 --commit 0xF--> empty[s] of ranks 0,1,2,3
       each empty[s]: count 2 = one arrival from each leader  -> producer of that CTA may refill s (and multicast into its partner)
```

### 9.5.4 The accumulator commit and the shared state advance (944-948)

Line 944 is `accumulator_pipeline.producer_commit(state)` (`sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:771` -> `sm100_pipeline.hpp:212-214, 259-265` -> `umma_arrive_multicast_2x1SM(&full_barrier_[st], tmem_sync_mask_)`): the same W30, now on `acc_full_base + 8 acc_stage` with `acc_commit_mask = 0x3 << 2y`. It is issued once per tile by the same elected lane after the 512th MMA, so it arrives when the whole tile's accumulation has completed in both TMEMs. The pair mask delivers one arrival to the leader's *and* the peer's `acc_full[st]`, each with count 1 (`kAccFullCount = 1`, explicit.cu:184; `producer_arv_count = 1`, `:529`), and each CTA's epilogue waits on **its own** `acc_full[st]` (Chapter 10, explicit.cu:1030, unmasked `acc_full_base`). This is the only way the peer's epilogue can learn that its TMEM is ready: no instruction of the peer's warp 0 ever touches the tensor core, so completion is known only to the leader's issuing thread, and the multicast carries it across.

Line 946 advances the accumulator producer state in **both** CTAs (`++accumulator_pipe_producer_state;` at `:773` is outside the `if (is_mma_leader_cta)`), and 947-948 install the fetched tile and count tiles. The peer's state is never used for a barrier inside the loop; Section 9.5.5 explains why it is kept.

### 9.5.5 What the peer's warp 0 does, and why it must exist

For the odd rank the loop body is lines 913, 914, 946, 947, 948 only: one CLC consume, one state advance, one tile update per tile. In the baseline's SASS ptxas emits a branch around the entire leader section for it (`BRA.U UP3, 0x3b90`, note D.2: "The peer CTA's warp 0 skips the whole leader section and executes per tile only the CLC consume and the state increments"); the explicit kernel's loop has the same structure (note G.3), but G.3 does not separately record the peer branch. The peer's warp 0 is nevertheless indispensable, and the PTX ISA's Issue Granularity table (reference [P], section 9.7.18.5, Table 55) is the normative reason behind items 1 and 4:

1. **Allocation and deallocation are pair operations.** For `.alloc`, `.dealloc` and `.relinquish_alloc_permit` with `::2` the ISA requires an "Issue from two warps, one in each of the current CTA and its Peer CTA, in order to collectively perform the operation, i.e., the first warp to perform the operation could block until the the second warp in the Peer CTA also performs the operation" [sic], and adds that "the issuing warp must make sure that peer CTA is launched and its warps eventually participate in collective operations". CUTLASS states the same as preconditions (`tmem_allocator_sm100.hpp:129-132, 152-154`: a full warp with the same logical warp id in *both* CTAs). Without the peer's warp 0 the leader's allocation could not complete (the SASS handshake in Section 9.4.1 waits for the peer).
2. **The named barrier.** The peer's epilogue warps `bar.sync 6, 160` and need 32 arrivals from their own CTA's warp 0 (Section 9.4.2); `T` must be present in the peer's smem, which the pair allocation guarantees.
3. **The CLC count.** `clc_empty` of CTA 0 expects 800 arrivals per response, 32 of them from each CTA's warp 0 (explicit.cu:183). A missing consumer would deadlock the scheduler at its second query.
4. **Loop termination and residency.** The peer learns that the kernel is over only from the terminator response (`valid == 0`), and it must run exactly as many iterations as the leader so that it reaches the handshake of Section 9.6.4 only after the leader's last tile. The ISA adds a residency rule for the MMAs themselves: for `.mma` and `.commit` with `::2`, "When the current CTA issues the operation, the peer CTA should be active and should not have exited". So the peer *CTA*, not only its warp 0, must stay resident until the leader's last MMA and commit have completed; the peer's warp 0 running the full loop and then blocking in the handshake is what keeps it there (its epilogue warps are kept by the accumulator pipeline, Chapter 10).
5. **The state advance is kept for parity with the source, not because anything reads it.** Items 1-4 are the operational reasons the peer's warp 0 exists. The unconditional `++accumulator_pipe_producer_state` (`:773`, outside the `if (is_mma_leader_cta)`) is a different matter: no CUTLASS variant uses the peer's state either. In the `IsOverlappingAccum` path (`:753-756`) the peer also only computes `acc_stage = phase ^ 1`, while `mma()` and `producer_commit` stay under `is_mma_leader_cta` (`:762-772`) and the overlapping tail (`:799-801`) only waits on the deallocation barrier. The explicit kernel keeps line 946 unconditional so that the PTX matches the source (note G.3); the handshake of Section 9.6.4 is one phase of one barrier and would work with any peer state (my analysis).

---

## 9.6 Termination (explicit.cu:950-975)

```
950:  griddep_launch_dependents();                                                                  // launch_dependent_grids (:781)
951:  tmem_relinquish_2sm();                                                                        // release_allocation_lock (:784)
952:  if (is_leader) {                                                                              // accumulator producer_tail (:789; sm90_pipeline.hpp:1129-1134) (Section 7.10 tail 3)
953:    #pragma unroll
954:    for (int i = 0; i < kAccStages; ++i) {
955:      EXPLICIT_WAIT(acc_empty_base + 8u * accp_idx, accp_phase, TAIL_ACC, tile, uint32_t(i));
956:#if defined(CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE)   // [TRACE]
957:      heartbeat(tile, HB_TAIL);
958:      trace_tail(TAIL_ACC, accp_idx, accp_phase, tile);
959:#endif
960:      advance<kAccStages>(accp_idx, accp_phase);
961:    }
962:  }
963:  // TMEM deallocation handshake (:794-796): the peer arrives on the leader's barrier, both wait phase 0, the leader arrives on the peer's (Section 7.10 tail 4)
964:  if (!is_leader) { mbar_arrive_remote(smem_base + OFF_TMEM_DEALLOC, peer); }
965:  EXPLICIT_WAIT(smem_base + OFF_TMEM_DEALLOC, 0u, WAIT_TMEM_DEALLOC, tile, 0u);
966:#if defined(CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE)   // [TRACE]
967:  heartbeat(tile, HB_TAIL);
968:  trace_tail(WAIT_TMEM_DEALLOC, 0u, 0u, tile);
969:#endif
970:  if (is_leader) { mbar_arrive_remote(smem_base + OFF_TMEM_DEALLOC, peer); }
971:  tmem_dealloc_2sm(T, kTmemColumns);                                                            // (:804), both CTAs
972:#if defined(CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE)   // [TRACE]
973:  heartbeat(tile, HB_EXIT);
974:#endif
975:}
```

### 9.6.1 `griddepcontrol.launch_dependents` (950)

W36 (explicit.cu:600) is `cutlass::arch::launch_dependent_grids()` (`:781`), emitted because the fixed build defines `CUTLASS_ENABLE_GDC_FOR_SM100=1` (explicit.cu:597-598; note D.1 row D14). This is Programmatic Dependent Launch: the primary kernel signals that a dependent kernel may be *scheduled*; the dependent must still execute `griddepcontrol.wait` (`cudaGridDependencySynchronize`), which "block[s] until all primary kernels the secondary kernel is dependent on have completed and flushed results to global memory", and "The CUDA driver can launch the secondary kernel when all primary thread blocks have launched and executed cudaTriggerProgrammaticLaunchCompletion" (CUDA Programming Guide, reference [N1]). CUTLASS's comment at `:778-780` says the rest: "Hint on an early release of global memory resources. The timing of calling this function only influences performance, not functional correctness." Why warp 0 and why here: by the time warp 0 leaves its loop, the last MMA of this CTA has been issued, so the remaining work is draining (epilogue stores) and a dependent grid's prologue can start overlapping it; all 32 lanes execute it (one `PREEXIT` per CTA in the SASS, note D.2). Why not earlier (my analysis): a dependent grid is launched only once *every* CTA of this grid has executed `griddepcontrol.launch_dependents` or exited (the Programming Guide sentence above), so one CTA triggering early changes nothing by itself; if all CTAs triggered at their start, a dependent's CTAs could be scheduled while this kernel still computes, but with one 230400-byte CTA per SM they could occupy only the 16 SMs this launch leaves idle (note D.3). CUTLASS places the trigger after the last MMA has been issued because from then on this CTA holds its SM only to drain the epilogue. In this harness there is no dependent grid, so the instruction is inert.

### 9.6.2 `tcgen05.relinquish_alloc_permit` (951)

W28 (explicit.cu:512-514), `release_allocation_lock()` (`:784`; `tmem_allocator_sm100.hpp:172-179`). It promises that this CTA will perform no further TMEM allocation, which lets another CTA queue for the SM's TMEM (reference [C1], with the author's hedge: "apparently, this is a guarantee that the CTA will not perform any further TMEM allocation, allowing future CTAs to queue up for the same SM"). CUTLASS places it *before* the deallocation on purpose (`:783`: "Release the right to allocate before deallocations so that the next CTA can rasterize"): the successor CTA can begin its allocation attempt while this CTA drains, and will be admitted the moment the columns are freed. It is `.cta_group::2.sync.aligned`, so both CTAs' warp 0 execute it. ptxas lowered it to bookkeeping in the reserved shared memory (`UVIRTCOUNT.DEALLOC.SMPOOL 0x80` and an `STS.U8`), and placed the former *before* the `PREEXIT` of line 950, swapping the two relative to the PTX (note D.2, D.6 item 9; attribution inferred).

### 9.6.3 The leader's accumulator tail (952-962)

`producer_tail` for a `PipelineAsync` is `for (count = 0; count < Stages; ++count) { producer_acquire(state); ++state; }` (`sm90_pipeline.hpp:1129-1134`), reached through `PipelineUmmaAsync::producer_tail` (`sm100_pipeline.hpp:219-221`): four more blocking acquires that **continue** the producer state where the loop left it, each followed by an advance. Its purpose (CUTLASS comment, `:787`: "Leader MMA waits for leader + peer epilogues to release accumulator stage") is to make sure no epilogue thread of either CTA is still reading TMEM when the pair deallocates, and that no remote arrival on the leader's `acc_empty[]` is still in flight when the leader exits (a CTA must not exit while peers may still arrive on its barriers, note 7.10 and B.6).

Why four waits and why their parities differ: tile `t` acquires stage `t % 4` with parity `1 ^ ((t >> 2) & 1)`, and that acquire passes when the epilogues have released tile `t - 4` (for `t < 4` it passes on the fresh barrier). After `T` tiles the state is `{T % 4, 1 ^ ((T >> 2) & 1)}`, so tail step `i` is exactly the acquire that tile `T + i` would have made, i.e. it waits for the release of tile `T + i - 4`. Steps 0..3 therefore cover the last four tiles `T-4 .. T-1`, and nothing else is needed because every earlier tile's release was already consumed by a later acquire inside the loop. The parity is **not** the same for all four barriers unless `T % 4 == 0` (note 7.2); from the measured tile counts (note D.3: 32, 31, or 19 tiles per cluster):

| T | step i = 0 | i = 1 | i = 2 | i = 3 | derivation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | `acc_empty[0]`, parity 1 | `acc_empty[1]`, 1 | `acc_empty[2]`, 1 | `acc_empty[3]`, 1 | `(32+i) % 4 = i`; `((32+i) >> 2) & 1 = 0` for all i, so `1 ^ 0 = 1` |
| 31 | `acc_empty[3]`, parity 0 | `acc_empty[0]`, 1 | `acc_empty[1]`, 1 | `acc_empty[2]`, 1 | `31 >> 2 = 7` (odd) gives 0; `32..34 >> 2 = 8` gives 1 |
| 19 | `acc_empty[3]`, parity 1 | `acc_empty[0]`, 0 | `acc_empty[1]`, 0 | `acc_empty[2]`, 0 | `19 >> 2 = 4` gives 1; `20..22 >> 2 = 5` gives 0 |

These match note 7.6 step 3, and the traced run recorded exactly these `{idx, phase}` pairs in its `TAIL_ACC` records for every cluster's `T` (note G.1). A kernel that waited with one fixed parity on all four barriers would hang or pass early for most `T`, and worse: by the ISA rule quoted in Section 9.4.6, `try_wait.parity` is "valid only for" the current incomplete phase or the immediately preceding one, so for some `T` a fixed parity would name a phase two steps back, for which the instruction's behaviour is undefined rather than merely wrong. This is why the tail must *continue the state* rather than restart it. The loop is `#pragma unroll` (953) so that each step's address and parity update is straight-line code (SASS: four unrolled waits with the index-wrap/phase-XOR between them, note 7.2).

### 9.6.4 The deallocation handshake (963-970) and its proof

The barrier is `tmem_dealloc` at `OFF_TMEM_DEALLOC = 336` (explicit.cu:150), one per CTA, initialised by warp 0's elected lane with count `kTmemDeallocCount = 32` (explicit.cu:185, 1165-1166; CUTLASS `tmem_deallocation_result_barrier.init(NumMMAThreads)`, `sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:565`). It mirrors `:794-796` (the three statements `arrive(mma_peer_cta_rank, not is_mma_leader_cta); wait(dealloc_barrier_phase); arrive(mma_peer_cta_rank, is_mma_leader_cta)`), whose comment at `:793` reads "Leader does wait + arrive, follower does arrive + wait". The hardware rules this handshake satisfies are the PTX ISA's (reference [P], `tcgen05.dealloc`): "If .cta_group::2 is specified, issuing warp and peer CTA warp must synchronize Tensor Memory accesses before attempting to collectively deallocate the Tensor Memory, and tcgen05.dealloc may block to collectively performs the deallocation with the other peer CTA's warp" [sic], and "All of the Tensor Memory that was allocated using tcgen05.alloc instruction in a kernel, must be explicitly deallocated using tcgen05.dealloc before the kernel exits." The first sentence is what Claims 1 and 2 below establish; the second is why both CTAs' warp 0 must reach line 971 at all:

```
   PEER (odd rank), warp 0, all 32 lanes                      LEADER (even rank), warp 0, all 32 lanes
   ----------------------------------------                   ----------------------------------------
   964: mapa + mbarrier.arrive.shared::cluster on               (952-962: 4 tail waits on own acc_empty[])
        the LEADER's tmem_dealloc  (32 arrivals -> completes
        phase 0 of the leader's barrier)
   965: wait parity 0 on OWN tmem_dealloc  ..................  965: wait parity 0 on OWN tmem_dealloc
        (blocks: nobody has arrived yet)                             (passes once the peer's 32 arrivals landed)
                                                               970: mapa + mbarrier.arrive.shared::cluster on the
                                                                    PEER's tmem_dealloc (32 arrivals -> phase 0 completes)
        (unblocks)                                             971: tcgen05.dealloc.cta_group::2  T, 512
   971: tcgen05.dealloc.cta_group::2  T, 512
```

`mbar_arrive_remote` (W10, explicit.cu:357-367) is `mapa.shared::cluster.u32 rem, addr, cta_id; mbarrier.arrive.shared::cluster.b64 _, [rem];` from `ClusterBarrier::arrive(cta_id, pred)` (`barrier.h:486-499`), with the predicate expressed as the C++ `if (!is_leader)` / `if (is_leader)`; `peer = rank ^ 1` is the `mapa` target, and every lane executes it, which is why the count is 32 and no election is used. Parity 0 for both waits because each barrier is used exactly once: it starts in phase 0 and `try_wait.parity(0)` completes when 32 arrivals finish that phase.

*Claim 1: the peer cannot deallocate before the leader has finished its accumulator tail.* The peer's `tcgen05.dealloc` (971) is program-ordered after its wait (965); that wait completes only when phase 0 of the peer's barrier completes, which requires 32 arrivals, and the only arrivals ever made on the peer's `tmem_dealloc` are the leader's at line 970 (the peer arrives on the *leader's* barrier, not its own). The leader's line 970 is program-ordered after its tail (952-962). Hence peer-dealloc happens-after leader-tail-complete. The tail, in turn, completes only when both CTAs' epilogues have arrived 256 times per stage for the last four tiles, and each epilogue thread arrives only after `tcgen05.wait::ld` (Chapter 10, explicit.cu:1038-1039), so at that point no TMEM read of either CTA is outstanding. Deallocating earlier would free columns the peer's own epilogue might still be loading.

*Claim 2: the leader must not deallocate before the peer has arrived.* The rule being protected, in one line: `tcgen05.dealloc.cta_group::2.sync.aligned` is a pair-collective instruction that both CTAs' warp 0 must execute ("The 2 warps from participating CTAs have the same logical warp ID", `tmem_allocator_sm100.hpp:154`; the ISA: the first warp "could block until the the second warp in the Peer CTA also performs the operation"), so the leader may not reach its half of the deallocation until the peer's warp 0 has left the tile loop, and the arrival at line 964 is the only message that tells the leader this. In the SASS the instruction is `UTCATOMSWS.AND` in both CTAs preceded by two ptxas-inserted consistency checks on the reserved words whose failure path traps (`BPT.TRAP`, note D.2; the explicit kernel carries the same two stubs, note G.3), the hardware-side guard against violating the rule. The peer's arrival (964) is its statement "I have left the tile loop and executed `relinquish`; I am at the deallocation point". Without the leader's wait, the leader could run its half of the collective deallocation while the peer's warp 0 was still consuming CLC responses, which violates the pair-collective contract (and, in the SASS, the bookkeeping check). The two-phase shape (peer announces, leader confirms) gives each side exactly the one fact it lacks: the leader lacks "peer is ready", the peer lacks "TMEM is quiescent". One barrier per CTA and one phase each is the minimum that carries both facts.

Why the leader's wait does not deadlock the peer's arrive: the peer's arrive (964) is unconditional and happens *before* its own wait (965), so the peer never waits for the leader before signalling it; the dependency graph is acyclic (peer-arrive -> leader-wait -> leader-arrive -> peer-wait).

### 9.6.5 `tcgen05.dealloc` in both CTAs (971)

W27 (explicit.cu:504-511): `tcgen05.dealloc.cta_group::2.sync.aligned.b32 T, 512;` from `Allocator2Sm::free` (`tmem_allocator_sm100.hpp:157-170`), executed by the whole warp 0 of both CTAs with the base `T` and the same column count as the allocation (`kTmemColumns`). SASS: `UTCATOMSWS.AND URZ, UR5` with `UR5 = ~(0xffff << (T >> 5))`, i.e. the 16 allocation units of 32 columns are cleared (note D.2 for the baseline; note G.3 reports the explicit kernel's 40-instruction dealloc sequence as instruction-identical). After it the warp falls off the end of `mma_role` and exits; the exit is safe because (i) the tail of 9.6.3 has absorbed every remote arrival that could target the leader's barriers, and (ii) the handshake has absorbed the one remote arrival on each `tmem_dealloc` (note 7.10, tails 3 and 4). The CTA's other tails (warp 2's eight mainloop waits, Chapter 8; rank 0 warp 1's two CLC waits, Chapter 7) are independent of warp 0.

---

## 9.7 Worked examples

### 9.7.1 Descriptors

*Rank 0, stage s = 3, k-block kb = 2.* `smem_base = 0x0000_0400`.

```
   A start (bytes) = 0x400 + 33792 + 16384 x 3 + 32 x 2 = 1024 + 33792 + 49152 + 64 = 84032 = 0x14840
   >> 4 = 0x1484 ;  & 0x3FFF = 0x1484 ;  lo_a = 0x10000 | 0x1484 = 0x11484          (= 0x10880 + 1024 x 3 + 2 x 2)
   desc_a = 0x40004040_00011484

   B start (bytes) = 0x400 + 164864 + 8192 x 3 + 32 x 2 = 1024 + 164864 + 24576 + 64 = 190528 = 0x2E840
   >> 4 = 0x2E84 ;  lo_b = 0x12E84                                                  (= 0x12880 + 512 x 3 + 4)
   desc_b = 0x40004040_00012E84
```

Both values are the ones the file's own comment predicts (explicit.cu:170) and the trace measured `+0x400` (A) / `+0x200` (B) per stage and `+2` per k-block from `0x...10880` / `0x...12880` (note D.1 row D7).

*Rank 3, stage s = 7, k-block kb = 1.* `smem_base = 0x0300_0400`.

```
   A start (bytes) = 0x03000400 + 0x8400 + 7 x 0x4000 + 0x20 = 0x0302_4820
   >> 4 = 0x0030_2482 ;  & 0x3FFF = 0x2482   <- the rank (0x30_0000 after the shift) is gone
   lo_a = 0x12482 ;  desc_a = 0x40004040_00012482

   B start (bytes) = 0x03000400 + 0x28400 + 7 x 0x2000 + 0x20 = 0x0303_6820
   >> 4 = 0x0030_3682 ;  & 0x3FFF = 0x3682
   lo_b = 0x13682 ;  desc_b = 0x40004040_00013682      (0x3682 = 13954; the largest value for kb = 3 is 0x3686 = 13958 < 16384)
```

Rank 3 never issues an MMA (it is a peer), which is the point: if it did, or if the leader's descriptor is applied in rank 3's smem by the hardware, the CTA-relative 14-bit start address is the same number the leader computed for the same `(s, kb)`.

### 9.7.2 The K order

MMA number `n = 4 q + kb` within a tile (0..511) consumes `k = 64 q + 16 kb .. +16` of the 8192-wide reduction: q-major, kb-minor, because the smem ring delivers one 64-wide k-tile per stage and the four 16-wide instructions of a stage are issued back to back before the stage is released. The whole K is covered once: `64 x 128 = 8192`. Per pair and tile: 512 MMAs = 128 k-tiles x 4, of which 1 overwrites and 511 accumulate; FLOP per MMA `2 x 256 x 128 x 16 = 1,048,576 = 2^20`; per pair tile `512 x 2^20 = 2^29 = 536,870,912 = 2 x 256 x 128 x 8192`. A 256 x 256 cluster work tile holds *two* pair tiles (one per MMA pair, Section 9.3.1), so per cluster per tile the two leaders issue `2 x 512 = 1024` MMAs and `2 x 129 = 258` commits (128 mainloop + 1 accumulator each), and a cluster tile is `2 x 2^29 = 2^30` FLOP. Over the 1024 cluster tiles: `1024 x 2 x 512 = 1,048,576 = 2^20` instructions and `2^20 x 2^20 = 2^40 = 1,099,511,627,776 = 2 x 8192^3` FLOP (note Section 9, operation ledger: "tcgen05.mma | 512 per pair per tile | 1048576"; counting one pair per cluster tile would give 2^39, which is 8192^3 and not the GEMM). Cross-check against the measurement: `2^40 / 0.889354 ms = 1.236 x 10^15 FLOP/s`, which is the harness's `GFLOPS` line (1.23498e6-1.23687e6 over the five explicit runs, note G.2; note D.4 states that the harness computes `GFLOPS = 2 x 8192^3 / Avg runtime` exactly), so the ledger and the timing agree.

### 9.7.3 Why the result is order-independent for the harness data (note Section 8)

The accumulator is FP32 and the inputs are FP16. The harness fills A and B with integer values in [-8, 8]: `initialize_block` (70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.cu:293-312) sets `scope_max = Element(8)`, `scope_min = Element(-8)` for element types wider than 8 bits and calls `BlockFillRandomUniform(block.get(), block.size(), seed, scope_max, scope_min, 0)`, whose last argument `bits = 0` is forwarded as the functor's `int_scale` (`tensor_fill.h:922-936`), and with `int_scale >= 0` every sample is rounded with `std::llround` (`tensor_fill.h:536-538`), so every element is an integer (note Section 3 traces the same path); every product is an integer of magnitude at most 64 and every partial sum over K <= 8192 is an integer of magnitude at most 64 x 8192 = 2^19, far below 2^24, the largest integer range in which FP32 is exact. So every intermediate value is exactly representable, the hardware's internal summation order inside one instruction (which is hardware-defined, note Section 8 `[R]`) and the q-major/kb-minor order across instructions cannot change the result, and `alpha = 1, beta = 0` leaves `D = acc` exactly. This is why the harness's exact compare can pass for *any* correct kernel, and also why passing it does not by itself prove that the explicit kernel issues the same instruction sequence as CUTLASS; that equivalence is established structurally (the PTX inventory and SASS comparison of note G.3, Chapter 12).
