## 11.5 Step 3: the 33 `mbarrier.init` calls (explicit.cu:1122-1167)

```cpp
// explicit.cu:1122-1167
  // 7.3 step 3: barrier initialisation in the baseline's constructor order (33-init variant, E.10 item 6):
  // the elected lane of the initialising warp issues the inits (initialize_barrier_array*_aligned, barrier.h:120-150), every thread fences once per group
  if (warp_idx == 0) {                                                                         // mainloop pipeline (kernel :457-472; sm100_pipeline.hpp:555-573)
    if (elect_one_sync()) {
      #pragma unroll
      for (uint32_t i = 0; i < uint32_t(kStages); ++i) {
        mbar_init(smem_base + OFF_MAIN_FULL + 8u * i, kMainFullCount);
        mbar_init(smem_base + OFF_MAIN_EMPTY + 8u * i, kMainEmptyCount);
      }
    }
  }
  fence_mbarrier_init_release_cluster();
  // (epi_load pipeline, warp 1, and load_order barrier, warp 3: beta != 0 only; not initialised, E.10 item 6)
  if (warp_idx == 4) {                                                                         // CLC pipeline (kernel :501-518)
    if (elect_one_sync()) {
      #pragma unroll
      for (uint32_t i = 0; i < uint32_t(kClcStages); ++i) {
        mbar_init(smem_base + OFF_CLC_FULL + 8u * i, kClcFullCount);
        mbar_init(smem_base + OFF_CLC_EMPTY + 8u * i, kClcEmptyCount);
      }
    }
  }
  fence_mbarrier_init_release_cluster();
  if (warp_idx == 5) {                                                                         // accumulator pipeline (kernel :520-536)
    if (elect_one_sync()) {
      #pragma unroll
      for (uint32_t i = 0; i < uint32_t(kAccStages); ++i) {
        mbar_init(smem_base + OFF_ACC_FULL + 8u * i, kAccFullCount);
        mbar_init(smem_base + OFF_ACC_EMPTY + 8u * i, kAccEmptyCount);
      }
    }
  }
  fence_mbarrier_init_release_cluster();
  if (warp_idx == 3) {                                                                         // CLC throttle pipeline (kernel :538-550)
    if (elect_one_sync()) {
      #pragma unroll
      for (uint32_t i = 0; i < uint32_t(kThrottleStages); ++i) {
        mbar_init(smem_base + OFF_THROTTLE_FULL + 8u * i, kThrottleCount);
        mbar_init(smem_base + OFF_THROTTLE_EMPTY + 8u * i, kThrottleCount);
      }
    }
  }
  fence_mbarrier_init_release_cluster();
  if (warp_idx == 0 && lane_pred) {                                                            // tmem_dealloc barrier (kernel :562-565), no fence of its own
    mbar_init(smem_base + OFF_TMEM_DEALLOC, kTmemDeallocCount);
  }
```

`mbar_init` is W5 (explicit.cu:286-295), the asm string of `ClusterBarrier::init` (`barrier.h:391-403`): `mbarrier.init.shared::cta.b64 [addr], count;`. A freshly initialised mbarrier is in phase 0 with `count` pending arrivals (and, for transaction barriers, a zero transaction count that `arrive.expect_tx` later raises); Chapter 4 explained why producers start at parity 1 and consumers at parity 0 against such a barrier. Two ISA constraints on the operands (PTX ISA, `mbarrier.init` and "Size and alignment of mbarrier object"): `count` must lie in `[1, 2^20 - 1]` for the default `.layout::v0` object (the SASS init word `{(0x100000 - count) << 1, (0x100000 - count) << 11}` of note D.2 is exactly this 20-bit field, stored as its complement against `0x100000 = 2^20`), so 800 and 256 are nowhere near the limit; and the object is an opaque `.b64` that must be 8-byte aligned in `.shared`, which every `OFF_*` below satisfies (all multiples of 8).

### 11.5.1 The map of the 512-byte control region

Every init writes 8 bytes at `smem_base + OFF_* + 8 i`. The region (note, Section 6.2; constants at explicit.cu:139-152):

```
offset  bytes  object                         count     init warp   this kernel
   0     64    main full[0..7]                1 (+tx)   0           yes
  64     64    main empty[0..7]               2         0           yes
 128     32    epi_load full[0..3]            32 (+tx)  1           NO  (beta != 0 only)
 160     32    epi_load empty[0..3]           128       1           NO
 192     16    load_order[0..1]               32        3           NO
 208     16    clc full[0..1]                 1 (+tx)   4           yes
 224     16    clc empty[0..1]                800       4           yes
 240     32    acc full[0..3]                 1         5           yes
 272     32    acc empty[0..3]                256       5           yes
 304     16    throttle full[0..1]            32        3           yes
 320     16    throttle empty[0..1]           32        3           yes
 336      8    tmem_dealloc                   32        0           yes
 344      8    (pad: PipelineStorage is aligned_struct<16>)
 352     32    clc_response[0..1]             16-byte CLC responses (written by hardware)
 384      4    tmem_base_ptr                  written by tcgen05.alloc
 388    124    (pad to 512: tensors need 512-byte alignment)
 512 ...       smem_C/D, smem_A, smem_B       (Chapters 8-10)
```

The 43 mbarrier slots occupy bytes 0..343 (344 bytes); CUTLASS's `PipelineStorage` is 352 bytes including its pad (note D.1 D2, `PipelineStorage 352`); the control objects end at 388 (`OFF_TMEM_BASE_PTR + 4`); the pad to 512 gives the first tensor stage its 512-byte alignment. (The file header at explicit.cu:56 writes "barriers 0..391": that is 388 rounded up to the next multiple of 8, my reading; the number is not derived anywhere in the note.) Count of initialised barriers: `8 + 8 + 2 + 2 + 4 + 4 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 33`. The baseline initialises `33 + 4 + 4 + 2 = 43` (note D.2: 43 `SYNCS.EXCH.64`).

### 11.5.2 Each count in one line

| Barrier | Count | Why exactly this number |
|---|---|---|
| main full[s] | 1 (+ 49152 tx) | one `mbarrier.arrive.expect_tx` by the pair leader's elected warp-2 lane per use of stage s (explicit.cu:736; Chapter 8); the phase completes when that arrival **and** 49152 transaction bytes (six 8192-byte TMA boxes landing in the pair, credited to the LEADER's barrier through the peer-bit mask) have been counted |
| main empty[s] | 2 | `cluster_m / atom_m + cluster_n / atom_n - 1 = 2/2 + 2/1 - 1 = 2` (`sm100_pipeline.hpp:565-566`): the two pair leaders each `tcgen05.commit` with mask `0xF` after reading stage s, and every CTA must hear from **both** before overwriting the stage, because its multicast A half lands in the other pair's CTA too (Chapter 4, note 7.2) |
| clc full[i] | 1 (+ 16 tx) | one remote `mbarrier.arrive.expect_tx` of 16 bytes by lane i of rank 0's scheduler warp (explicit.cu:842; W13); the 16-byte CLC response multicast into every CTA completes it |
| clc empty[i] | 800 | `NumSchedThreads + cluster_size * (NumMainloopLoadThreads + NumEpilogueThreads + NumMMAThreads) = 32 + 4 * (32 + 128 + 32)` (kernel `:511-512`); every thread of every consuming warp (`clc_consume`, explicit.cu:684) arrives remotely on **CTA 0's** barrier; the baseline adds `4 * 32 = 128` (928) only when `is_epi_load_needed` (`:513-515`) |
| acc full[st] | 1 | the leader's single `tcgen05.commit` with the pair mask `0x3 << 2y` (explicit.cu:944; `producer_arv_count = 1`, kernel `:529`) |
| acc empty[st] | 256 | `size(AtomThrShapeMNK) * NumEpilogueThreads = 2 * 128` (kernel `:530`): every epilogue thread of **both** CTAs of the pair arrives on the LEADER's barrier via the peer-bit-masked address (explicit.cu:1039; W11) |
| throttle full[i] / empty[i] | 32 / 32 | `NumMainloopLoadThreads` / `NumSchedThreads` (kernel `:546-547`): whole-warp arrivals (all 32 lanes of rank 0's warp 2 locally, explicit.cu:785; all 32 lanes of rank 0's warp 1 remotely to CTA 0 = itself, explicit.cu:837) |
| tmem_dealloc | 32 | `NumMMAThreads` (kernel `:565`): the peer's 32 warp-0 lanes arrive on the leader's barrier, then the leader's 32 lanes on the peer's (explicit.cu:964-970; Chapter 9) |

The constants and their one-line derivations are at explicit.cu:180-185; `static_assert(kMainloopTxBytes == 49152 && kClcEmptyCount == 32 + 4 * (32 + 128 + 32))` at explicit.cu:192 pins the two that are easiest to get wrong.

### 11.5.3 Why 33 and not 43

The baseline's `epi_load` pipeline (`PipelineTransactionAsync<4>`, counts 32/128, initialising warp 1, kernel `:474-487`) and `load_order` barrier (`OrderedSequenceBarrier<1,2>`, count 32, warp 3, kernel `:494-499`) exist for the C-load path (`beta != 0`), which this kernel omits (Chapter 3). Their ten barriers are **initialised but never arrived on or waited for** when `beta = 0` (note 7.2 table, rows "initialized but never used"). The explicit kernel leaves those ten 8-byte slots as reserved, uninitialised space (comment at explicit.cu:1134) and consequently hard-codes the CLC empty count to 800 rather than computing `is_epi_load_needed ? 928 : 800` at run time (the baseline's `selp.b32 928, 800`, note D.2). Nothing reads an uninitialised slot: the K1 trace record deliberately reports `OFF_LOAD_ORDER` and `OFF_EPI_LOAD_FULL` addresses (explicit.cu:1186) only so that `check_trace.py` can confirm the layout, not because the kernel uses them. Fence count follows: 4 groups here, 6 in the baseline (note E.6.3 step 3). Note E.10 item 6 recorded this as the recommended variant; D.7 accepts either.

The constant 800 is correct **only because warp 3 never consumes a CLC response when `beta = 0`**. The rule behind the baseline's formula: every warp that executes `clc_consume` (and therefore arrives once per response on CTA 0's `clc_empty[i]`) is counted once per CTA in which it consumes; rank 0's warp 1 consumes in one CTA (32), warps 0, 2, 4-7 consume in all four (4 x 192). If a rewrite ever adds a consuming warp, for example a C-load warp 3, the count must grow by `cluster_size x 32 = 128` to 928, which is what the baseline computes at run time with `selp.b32 928, 800` on the `is_epi_load_needed` predicate (note D.2). The failure modes are asymmetric (my analysis): an under-count completes the phase before every consumer has released the slot, so the surplus arrivals spill into the next phase and a response slot can be re-armed while a warp is still decoding it; an over-count never completes the phase and hangs CTA 0's scheduler warp at its next `clc_empty` wait (Chapter 7).

### 11.5.4 Why the fence is executed by all 256 threads, and what it orders

```cpp
// explicit.cu:408-415 (W14)
__device__ __forceinline__ void fence_mbarrier_init_release_cluster() {
  asm volatile(
    "{\n\t"
    "fence.mbarrier_init.release.cluster; \n"
    "}"
    ::
    : "memory");
}
```

(copied from `cutlass::arch::fence_barrier_init`, `barrier.h:711-724`, whose comment says: "Helps with visibility of barrier init operations across warps / cta / cluster ... It must be composed with an appropriate sync instruction with the right scope to ensure visibility eg. `__syncthreads()` or a `cluster_arrive()` + `cluster_wait()`".)

**What it orders.** `fence.mbarrier_init` is a lightweight fence whose synchronising effect is restricted to the executing thread's **prior `mbarrier.init` operations** on shared-memory barriers, made visible at cluster scope with release semantics. PTX ISA (`membar/fence`, the `.op_restrict` qualifier): "When `.op_restrict` is `.mbarrier_init`, the synchronizing effect of the fence only applies to the prior `mbarrier.init` operations executed by the same thread on mbarrier objects in `.shared::cta` state space" (LLVM's NVPTX documentation restates the same sentence, 11.11). It pairs with the acquire of `barrier.cluster.wait` in step 6: init (release.cluster) -> arrive -> every CTA waits (acquire) -> every CTA's threads may now arrive on any CTA's barriers. This is the ISA's own recommended shape for a relaxed cluster barrier: the `barrier.cluster` example in the ISA is captioned "use memory fence prior to arrive for relaxed barrier" and reads `fence.cluster.acq_rel; barrier.cluster.arrive.relaxed.aligned; ... barrier.cluster.wait.aligned;`. The rule is "publish with a fence, then arrive relaxed", and `fence.mbarrier_init.release.cluster` is the cheapest fence that satisfies it for `mbarrier.init` stores: it covers nothing else and, as shown below, emits no SASS instruction.

**Why all threads execute it although one lane per group did the inits (derived from source + my analysis).** In every CUTLASS pipeline constructor the fence sits **outside** the `if (warp_idx == initializing_warp)` test: `sm100_pipeline.hpp:559-573` (mainloop), `:139-149` (accumulator, `PipelineUmmaAsync`), `:963-979` / `:981-1000` (CLC), `sm90_pipeline.hpp:1040-1055` (throttle, `PipelineAsync`). So all 256 threads of every CTA execute it once per constructor; the explicit kernel copies that shape (four unconditional calls at explicit.cu:1133, 1144, 1154, 1164). Three reasons it is written this way: (1) the fence is a per-thread operation; for a thread that issued no init it is a no-op, so making it unconditional costs nothing and avoids a second election or a divergent branch; (2) a thread that *did* init must fence **before** its `barrier.cluster.arrive`, and placing the fence straight after each init group guarantees that for whichever lane was elected; (3) in SASS the instruction emits nothing at all (note D.2 and G.3: "`fence.mbarrier_init.release.cluster` emits no instruction"; the bare `FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S` seen before the init groups are attributed to the init lowering, inferred). The `tmem_dealloc` init at explicit.cu:1165-1167 has no fence of its own because the baseline has none there (kernel `:562-576` is followed directly by `pipeline_init_arrive_relaxed` at `:580`). Note that this init comes *after* the fourth fence, so no `fence.mbarrier_init` covers it, and the arrive is `.relaxed`; it is the one init for which the ISA's "fence prior to arrive" pattern above is **not** followed, so as far as I can read the PTX memory model its visibility to the peer's remote arrive at explicit.cu:964 is not formally established by the prologue (unverified). What is certain: the ordering is the baseline's own (derived from source), the explicit kernel copies it, the first remote arrive on this barrier happens at kernel exit, roughly 0.9 ms after the init, and no run of either kernel has ever hung there (measured, note G.1). If you want a provably ordered variant when you rewrite the kernel, move the `tmem_dealloc` init before the fourth fence; the protocol does not change.

### 11.5.5 Why this order and these warps

The groups appear in the order of the baseline's constructors: mainloop (kernel `:457-472`), [epi_load `:474-487`, load_order `:494-499`, omitted], CLC (`:501-518`), accumulator (`:520-536`), throttle (`:538-550`), tmem_dealloc (`:562-565`). The initialising warp of each pipeline is the baseline's `initializing_warp` parameter: 0 (`:467`), 4 (`:517`), 5 (`:531`), 3 (`:549`), and warp 0's `lane_predicate` for `tmem_dealloc` (`:564`).

**Functionally none of this matters.** An `mbarrier.init` is one 8-byte write of the encoded init word by whichever thread executes it (SASS `SYNCS.EXCH.64 [UR29 + off], R` with `R = {(0x100000 - count) << 1, (0x100000 - count) << 11}`, note D.2: a synchronisation-unit exchange on the opaque mbarrier object, not an `STS`, and the ISA requires the object to be created by `mbarrier.init` and nothing else); what matters here is only that the operation has no cross-thread dependency, so any thread may initialise any barrier as long as (a) each barrier is initialised exactly once before its first arrive, and (b) the init is made visible before any remote CTA can arrive on it, which the fence + cluster rendezvous guarantee for all of them together. The baseline spreads the 43 inits over warps 0, 1, 3, 4, 5 so that they proceed in parallel instead of serialising 43 stores in one warp (my analysis of the motive; the mapping itself is derived from source). The explicit kernel keeps the mapping for parity so that the prologue's SASS can be compared row by row (note G.3: "33 `SYNCS.EXCH.64` inits with the same init words at the same Section 6.2 offsets as the baseline's corresponding 33 of 43"). If you rewrite the kernel, you may put all 33 inits in one elected lane of warp 0 followed by one fence; the protocol does not change.

## 11.6 Steps 4-6: the split cluster rendezvous and the initial tile (explicit.cu:1169-1179)

```cpp
// explicit.cu:1169-1179
  // 7.3 step 4: cluster rendezvous, part 1 (kernel :580)
  cluster_arrive_relaxed();

  // 7.3 step 5: warp-uniform setup; the initial tile from the launch coordinate (swizzle_and_rasterize + AlongN transpose, sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp:365-371, 666-677)
  uint32_t const x = cluster_ctaid_x();                                                        // == rank & 1
  uint32_t const y = cluster_ctaid_y();                                                        // == rank >> 1
  int tm = static_cast<int>(2u * (blockIdx.y >> 1) + (blockIdx.x & 1u));
  int tn = static_cast<int>(2u * (blockIdx.x >> 1) + (blockIdx.y & 1u));

  // 7.3 step 6: cluster rendezvous, part 2 (kernel :615); no remote barrier operation before this point
  cluster_wait();
```

W16/W17 (explicit.cu:428-429) are `barrier.cluster.arrive.relaxed.aligned;` and `barrier.cluster.wait.aligned;`, copied from `cute::cluster_arrive_relaxed` / `cute::cluster_wait` (`cluster_sm90.hpp:48-55, 66-73`). The baseline reaches them through `pipeline_init_arrive_relaxed(cluster_size)` and `pipeline_init_wait(cluster_size)` (`sm90_pipeline.hpp:1377-1384`, `:1364-1371`), which fall back to `__syncthreads()` for a cluster of size 1; the explicit kernel knows its cluster is 4 and calls the cluster forms directly. (ptxas nevertheless inserts a run-time test `c[0x0][0x36c] == 1` around both, with `NOP` / `BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING 0x0` fallbacks, in both kernels: note D.2 and G.3; the PTX carries no guard.)

### 11.6.1 What `barrier.cluster` does, and why `.relaxed` + split

From the PTX ISA (`barrier.cluster`): `barrier.cluster.arrive{.sem}{.aligned}` with `.sem = {.release, .relaxed}` (default `.release`) and `barrier.cluster.wait{.acquire}{.aligned}` (default `.acquire`). "`barrier.cluster.wait` instruction causes the executing thread to wait for all **non-exited** threads of the cluster to perform `barrier.cluster.arrive`"; "When all non-exited threads in the cluster have executed `barrier.cluster.arrive`, the barrier completes and is automatically reinitialized"; "Each thread must arrive at the barrier only once before the barrier completes." (The "non-exited" is what would make early-exiting warps harmless for any later cluster barrier; this kernel has none after the prologue.) The memory guarantee sits on the wait: "The `barrier.cluster.wait` instruction guarantees that when it completes the execution, memory accesses (except asynchronous operations) requested, in program order, prior to the preceding `barrier.cluster.arrive` by all threads in the cluster are complete and visible to the executing thread." The `.relaxed` qualifier on the arrive removes that guarantee for the arriving thread's own prior accesses: "there are no memory ordering and visibility guarantees provided for the memory accesses performed prior to `barrier.cluster.arrive`", which is exactly why the `fence.mbarrier_init.release.cluster` of 11.5.4 is needed to publish the inits.

- **Why `.relaxed`.** The only shared-memory writes that must be visible to the other CTAs before they start are the `mbarrier.init`s, and those were already published at cluster scope by `fence.mbarrier_init.release.cluster` (11.5.4). A `.release` arrive would additionally order every other prior store of the thread (there are none that matter) and cost a heavier fence. CUTLASS chose `.relaxed` and named the helper accordingly (`pipeline_init_arrive_relaxed`); the acquire side stays on the `wait`. (Derived from source and the PTX semantics; the cost judgement is my analysis.)
- **Why split the arrive from the wait.** Between arrive and wait every CTA does **local** work that needs no other CTA: in the baseline `load_init` (the TMA coordinate tensors), the pipeline start states, `%cluster_ctaid`, the two multicast masks, the scheduler object with the initial tile, and the TMEM accumulator tensor (kernel `:582-613`; note B.2 steps 21-25); in the explicit kernel the two `%cluster_ctaid` reads and the two tile-coordinate lines (the rest became compile-time constants or per-role locals). The slowest CTA of the cluster is still finishing its inits while the others compute this, so the latency of the rendezvous overlaps the setup instead of adding to it. For the explicit kernel the window holds only a handful of instructions, but the shape is kept because it is correct, free, and makes the SASS comparable (note G.3: `UCGABAR_ARV` ... `UCGABAR_WAIT; CCTL.IVALL` at the same relative positions).
- **Why `.aligned`.** The ISA: "The optional `.aligned` qualifier indicates that all threads in the warp must execute the same `barrier.cluster` instruction. In conditionally executed code, an aligned `barrier.cluster` instruction should only be used if it is known that all threads in the warp evaluate the condition identically, otherwise behavior is undefined." The prologue satisfies the requirement: all 256 threads execute the same instruction with the warp converged (no divergent branch that any thread fails to rejoin: the `if (warp_idx == N)` bodies are warp-uniform and the `elect_one_sync()` bodies reconverge at their closing brace). What the implementation gains from the promise is not documented; that the arrival is then processed per warp rather than per thread is my inference, not an ISA statement. CUTLASS uses the `.aligned` forms (`cluster_sm90.hpp:48-55, 66-73`), so the explicit kernel does too.
- **What `CCTL.IVALL` is (my analysis; Chapter 12 has the listing).** The SASS pairs `UCGABAR_WAIT` with a `CCTL.IVALL` (note G.3). The mnemonic reads as cache control, invalidate all: it invalidates the SM's L1 data-cache lines, and issued right after the cluster wait it is the hardware realisation of the wait's default `.acquire`, so that loads issued after it cannot hit stale L1 copies and therefore observe the other CTAs' released stores. Expect it after any acquire-scoped cluster or GPU-scope synchronisation in SASS; it is not specific to this kernel.

### 11.6.2 `(x, y)` from `%cluster_ctaid`

W4 (explicit.cu:282-283) reads `%cluster_ctaid.x` and `%cluster_ctaid.y` (`cute::block_id_in_cluster`, `cluster_sm90.hpp:126-137`). The PTX ISA defines `%cluster_ctaid` as "the CTA identifier in a cluster in each dimension", unique per CTA and bounded by `0 <= %cluster_ctaid.x < %cluster_nctaid.x` (likewise y, z), and `%cluster_ctarank` as the "unique CTA identifier across all dimensions". For the (2,2,1) cluster `x, y` are each 0 or 1 and `rank = x + 2y` (measured; note B.6, D.1 D5: the four bases `0x400 + (rank << 24)` matched `mapa(base, t)` for every rank). The second identity this chapter relies on, `x = blockIdx.x & 1`, `y = blockIdx.y & 1` (i.e. `%cluster_ctaid == blockIdx mod clusterDim`), follows from the CUDA Programming Guide's description of how clusters are formed ("Specifying clusters groups adjacent thread blocks into clusters", "Thread blocks within a cluster are always adjacent to each other within the grid", "Specifying clusters does not change the grid dimensions or the indices of a thread block within a grid"; Programming Guide 1.2.2.1.1 "Thread Block Clusters") together with the divisibility of the grid by the cluster that `check_cluster_dims` enforces (11.8.3): the grid is tiled by 2 x 2 blocks of adjacent `blockIdx`, so the position inside a tile is `blockIdx mod 2`. Neither document writes the modular relation as a formula; it is confirmed by measurement (note D.1 D5 and B.6: the rank derived from `(x, y)` matched `%cluster_ctarank` and the measured bases in every CTA; note D.3: all 1024 CLC first-CTA ids were even in both coordinates, i.e. every cluster starts at an even `blockIdx`). The comments `// == rank & 1` and `// == rank >> 1` record the identity; the kernel still reads the special registers rather than deriving `x, y` from `rank`, as the baseline does (the SASS computes them from `SR_CTAID.X/Y` and a constant-bank table, note D.2 and D.6 item 14 — "irrelevant to the protocol"). `x` and `y` are used for: the A multicast mask `0x5 << x` and the A/B coordinates and destinations (Chapter 8), the accumulator commit mask `0x3 << 2y` (Chapter 9), and the CLC tile mapping (Chapter 7, explicit.cu:692-693).

### 11.6.3 Deriving `tm`, `tn` from the launch coordinate

The two formulas at explicit.cu:1175-1176 are the end of a chain that starts on the host. Each link is in source. (Line numbers for `sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp` below are those of the working tree, which carries 31 lines of trace probes in two hunks (`git diff cb424739 -- include/cutlass/gemm/kernel/sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp`: `@@ -443,6 +443,12 @@` and `@@ -462,11 +468,36 @@`): 6 lines inserted after cb424739's `:445` (the K5a probe inside the CLC election) and 25 lines inserted within cb424739's `:462-:472` (the K5b/K5c probes). So lines up to `:445` are the same in both trees, cb424739's `:446-:462` are 6 higher in the tree (`:452-:468`), and everything from cb424739's `:473` on is 31 higher: `possibly_transpose_work_tile` is `:699-708` here and `:668-677` there, which is the `666-677` cited by the comment at explicit.cu:1172. Lines before `:445`, such as `possibly_transpose_grid` and `initial_work_tile_info`, are identical in both.)

**Link 1: the logical CTA grid is (M tiles, N tiles, L).** `GemmUniversalAdapter::run` calls `get_grid_shape(params)` (`gemm_universal_adapter.h:381`) -> `GemmUniversal::get_grid_shape` (`sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:383-396`) -> `TileScheduler::get_grid_shape` (`sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp:220-232`) -> `get_tiled_cta_shape_mnl` (`:624-636`):

```cpp
// sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp:628-631 (verbatim)
    auto [tiles_m, tiles_n, tiles_l] = product_each(ceil_div(select<0,1,3>(problem_shape_mnkl), take<0,2>(tile_shape_mnk)));
    auto ctas_m = round_nearest(tiles_m * size<0>(atom_thr_shape_mnk), size<0>(cluster_shape_mnk));
    auto ctas_n = round_nearest(tiles_n * size<1>(atom_thr_shape_mnk), size<1>(cluster_shape_mnk));
    auto ctas_l = tiles_l;
```

With `tile_shape_mnk = (256, 128, 64)` (the **pair's** MMA tile, Chapter 3), `atom_thr_shape = (2, 1, 1)` and `cluster = (2, 2, 1)`: `tiles_m = ceil(8192/256) = 32`, `ctas_m = round_nearest(32 * 2, 2) = 64`; `tiles_n = ceil(8192/128) = 64`, `ctas_n = round_nearest(64 * 1, 2) = 64`; `ctas_l = 1`. Logical grid `(64, 64, 1)` indexed (M, N, L). (Note 13 item 5 records that this is "`ceil_div(M, 256) * 2`, not `ceil_div(M, 128)`"; identical here.)

**Link 2: the launched grid is transposed for AlongN.** `possibly_transpose_grid` (`:235-250`):

```cpp
// sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp:238-248 (verbatim)
    if (raster_order == RasterOrder::AlongN) {
      // Swap grid.x and grid.y for AlongN rasterization order, since the CLC scheduler
      // will schedule in AlongM order by default.
      //
      // Each grid dimension must also be a multiple of the corresponding cluster dimension,
      // so we convert the untransposed x into the number of clusters along the M mode,
      // and multiply this by cluster.n (and vice-versa for y).
      auto tmp = grid.x;
      grid.x = divmod_cluster_shape_n.divide(grid.y) * divmod_cluster_shape_m;
      grid.y = divmod_cluster_shape_m.divide(tmp) * divmod_cluster_shape_n;
    }
```

`grid.x = (64 / 2) * 2 = 64`, `grid.y = (64 / 2) * 2 = 64`. The numbers do not change for a square problem, but the **meaning** does: after this, `blockIdx.x` walks the N tiles and `blockIdx.y` the M tiles. `raster_order` is `AlongN` here because the heuristic `tiles_n > tiles_m ? AlongM : AlongN` (`tile_scheduler_params.h:338-343`, under `RasterOrderOptions::Heuristic`) gives `AlongN` for equal counts (note 13 item 4; measured `raster_order AlongN 1`, note D.1 D10). **Why AlongN is the right answer for this GEMM (my analysis, built on measured D.3).** The CLC hands out cluster ids roughly in increasing launch-linear order (note D.3: "ascending except for a few local swaps"), and with the grid transposed, launch-linear id `L` is the cluster tile `(m, n) = (L / 32, L % 32)` (note D.3): consecutive ids walk along **N** inside one row of cluster tiles, so the 33 resident clusters work on at most two adjacent rows at any moment and share the same 256 A rows (one 256 x 8192 fp16 A panel, 4 MB) while each reads its own B panel. A is therefore re-read from HBM about once per row of 32 cluster tiles instead of once per tile; that is the L2 reuse argument of Chapter 3, and Chapter 7 shows the same `(tm, tn)` map applied to CLC responses. The heuristic's general rule is to raster along the shorter tile axis (`tiles_n > tiles_m` -> `AlongM`): the wave of resident clusters then cycles through the panels of the smaller operand, which has the better chance of staying L2-resident as a whole, while each panel of the larger operand is reused by a run of consecutive clusters; for a square problem both axes are equal and `AlongN` is the tie-break. `enum class RasterOrder { AlongM, AlongN }` (`tile_scheduler_detail.hpp:38-41`) is why the host guard compares against the literal 1 (`kRasterOrderAlongN = 1`, util.hpp:36). The explicit host function hard-codes the result, `dim3 grid(64, 64, 1)` (explicit.cu:1282; util.hpp:32 `kGridX = kFixedN / kCtaTileN, kGridY = kFixedM / kCtaTileM`: note that x is computed from N and y from M, i.e. the transposed order).

**Link 3: on the device, `initial_work_tile_info` feeds `blockIdx` through `swizzle_and_rasterize`.**

```cpp
// sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp:366-371 (verbatim)
  template <class ClusterShape>
  CUTLASS_DEVICE
  WorkTileInfo
  initial_work_tile_info(ClusterShape cluster_shape) {
    return swizzle_and_rasterize(blockIdx.x, blockIdx.y, blockIdx.z, /*valid=*/true, /*cluster_offset_m=*/0, /*cluster_offset_n=*/0);
  }
```

In `swizzle_and_rasterize` (`:728-845`) the whole swizzle block (`:742-826`) is skipped because `divmod_swizzle_size_.divisor == 0` ("Swizzling is enabled if the swizzle size is greater than 0", `:741`; measured `swizzle_divisor 0`, note D.1 D10; the host guard at explicit.cu:1269 enforces it). What remains is the transpose:

```cpp
// sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp:827-833 (verbatim)
    // Since we swap the grid x and y modes if raster order is AlongN, swap the M and N tile offsets when
    // raster order is AlongN.
    auto [new_cta_coord_m, new_cta_coord_n] = possibly_transpose_work_tile(
      params_.raster_order_, cta_coord_m, cta_coord_n, params_.divmod_cluster_shape_m_, params_.divmod_cluster_shape_n_);

    new_cta_coord_m += cta_in_cluster_offset_m;
    new_cta_coord_n += cta_in_cluster_offset_n;
```

with the two in-cluster offsets 0 for the initial tile, and

```cpp
// sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp:699-708 (verbatim)
  possibly_transpose_work_tile(RasterOrder raster_order, int32_t M_idx, int32_t N_idx, FastDivmod divmod_cluster_shape_m, FastDivmod divmod_cluster_shape_n) {
    if (raster_order == RasterOrder::AlongN) {
      int cluster_m, remainder_m, cluster_n, remainder_n;
      divmod_cluster_shape_m(cluster_m, remainder_m, M_idx);
      divmod_cluster_shape_n(cluster_n, remainder_n, N_idx);
      M_idx = cluster_n * divmod_cluster_shape_m.divisor + remainder_m;
      N_idx = cluster_m * divmod_cluster_shape_n.divisor + remainder_n;
    }
    return cute::make_tuple(M_idx, N_idx);
  }
```

Substitute `M_idx = blockIdx.x`, `N_idx = blockIdx.y`, both cluster divisors 2:

```
cluster_m   = blockIdx.x / 2      remainder_m = blockIdx.x % 2
cluster_n   = blockIdx.y / 2      remainder_n = blockIdx.y % 2
tm = M_idx' = cluster_n * 2 + remainder_m = 2 (blockIdx.y >> 1) + (blockIdx.x & 1)
tn = N_idx' = cluster_m * 2 + remainder_n = 2 (blockIdx.x >> 1) + (blockIdx.y & 1)
```

which is explicit.cu:1175-1176 exactly (note B.4, first row). Read it as: **the cluster index** comes from the transposed grid axis (`blockIdx.y / 2` picks the cluster row in M, `blockIdx.x / 2` the cluster column in N), and **the position inside the cluster** stays with the original axis (`blockIdx.x % 2 = x` picks the M half, `blockIdx.y % 2 = y` the N half). That is why `tm % 2 == x` for every tile a CTA ever receives (also for CLC tiles, Chapter 7), which is what makes "CTAs x and x+2 share tm, hence the A rows" true (Chapter 8).

### 11.6.4 Worked examples

| `blockIdx` (x, y) | `x = bx & 1`, `y = by & 1` -> rank | `by >> 1`, `bx >> 1` | `tm = 2 (by >> 1) + (bx & 1)` | `tn = 2 (bx >> 1) + (by & 1)` | D rows / columns |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (5, 2) | x = 1, y = 0 -> rank 1 | 1, 2 | 2 * 1 + 1 = **3** | 2 * 2 + 0 = **4** | rows [384, 512), cols [512, 640) |
| (4, 2) | x = 0, y = 0 -> rank 0 | 1, 2 | 2 | 4 | rows [256, 384), cols [512, 640) |
| (4, 3) | x = 0, y = 1 -> rank 2 | 1, 2 | 2 | 5 | rows [256, 384), cols [640, 768) |
| (5, 3) | x = 1, y = 1 -> rank 3 | 1, 2 | 3 | 5 | rows [384, 512), cols [640, 768) |
| (0, 0) | rank 0 | 0, 0 | 0 | 0 | rows [0, 128), cols [0, 128) |
| (63, 63) | x = 1, y = 1 -> rank 3 | 31, 31 | 63 | 63 | rows [8064, 8192), cols [8064, 8192) |
| (1, 0) | rank 1 | 0, 0 | 1 | 0 | rows [128, 256), cols [0, 128) |
| (0, 1) | rank 2 | 0, 0 | 0 | 1 | rows [0, 128), cols [128, 256) |

The first four rows are the four CTAs of one cluster (the cluster containing `blockIdx` (4..5, 2..3)). Together they cover the 256 x 256 cluster tile at cluster coordinates (M cluster 1, N cluster 2):

```
                 N tiles:   tn = 4            tn = 5
                          cols 512..639     cols 640..767
              +------------------+------------------+
 tm = 2       |  rank 0 (x0,y0)  |  rank 2 (x0,y1)  |   rows 256..383
 rows 256..   |  blockIdx (4,2)  |  blockIdx (4,3)  |
              +------------------+------------------+
 tm = 3       |  rank 1 (x1,y0)  |  rank 3 (x1,y1)  |   rows 384..511
 rows 384..   |  blockIdx (5,2)  |  blockIdx (5,3)  |
              +------------------+------------------+
                 pair {0,1}: tn = 4         pair {2,3}: tn = 5
                 (same y, adjacent tm)      (same y, adjacent tm)
```

The MMA pairs `{0,1}` and `{2,3}` are the two **columns** of this picture (same y, hence same tn, adjacent tm): one `tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2` covers the pair's 256 rows x 128 columns (Chapter 9). The A rows of rank 0 and rank 2 are the same (tm = 2), which is the multicast relation `0x5 << x` (Chapter 8).

### 11.6.5 The 4096 launch coordinates cover the 4096 CTA tiles exactly once

Both maps below are well defined on `{0..63} x {0..63}` because `2 (v >> 1) + (w & 1)` lies in `{0..63}` whenever `v, w` do. Define

```
F : (bx, by) -> (tm, tn) = (2 (by >> 1) + (bx & 1),  2 (bx >> 1) + (by & 1))
G : (tm, tn) -> (bx, by) = (2 (tn >> 1) + (tm & 1),  2 (tm >> 1) + (tn & 1))
```

Apply G after F: `bx' = 2 (tn >> 1) + (tm & 1) = 2 (bx >> 1) + (bx & 1) = bx` (since `tn >> 1 = bx >> 1` and `tm & 1 = bx & 1`), and `by' = 2 (tm >> 1) + (tn & 1) = 2 (by >> 1) + (by & 1) = by`. So `G o F = id`; by the same computation `F o G = id`. F is therefore a bijection of the 64 x 64 grid onto the 64 x 64 tile space: every one of the 4096 CTA tiles is the **initial** tile of exactly one CTA. (The CLC hand-out later re-uses the same map on cancelled clusters' first-CTA ids, Chapter 7; its exactly-once coverage of the 1024 cluster tiles was measured, note D.7 "CLC".)

### 11.6.6 The invariant: no remote operation before `cluster_wait`

Until every CTA of the cluster has passed `barrier.cluster.wait`, a CTA may not touch another CTA's shared memory or barriers: the other CTA might not have executed its `mbarrier.init`s yet (its warps may not even be running), and an arrive on an uninitialised mbarrier is undefined. The explicit kernel's remote operations, all inside the role functions (after explicit.cu:1179):

| Operation | Wrapper | Sites | Target |
|---|---|---|---|
| remote `mbarrier.arrive` via `mapa` | W10 | explicit.cu:684 (CLC release), 837 (throttle release), 964/970 (dealloc handshake) | CTA 0's `clc_empty`, CTA 0's `throttle_empty`, the peer's `tmem_dealloc` |
| arrive on the pair leader's barrier via the peer-bit mask | W11 | explicit.cu:1039 | leader's `acc_empty[st]` |
| remote `arrive.expect_tx` via `mapa` | W13 | explicit.cu:842 | CTAs 0..3's `clc_full[i]` |
| 2SM TMA loads (data into the peer / multicast CTAs; tx bytes to the leader's `full[s]`) | W21, W22 | explicit.cu:747, 754 | ranks `x`, `x+2` (A data); the pair leader's `full[s]` |
| `tcgen05.commit ... multicast::cluster` | W30 | explicit.cu:942, 944 | all four CTAs' `empty[s]`; the pair's `acc_full[st]` |
| `clusterlaunchcontrol.try_cancel ... multicast::cluster::all` | W33 | explicit.cu:847 | every CTA's `clc_response[i]` and `clc_full[i]` |
| `tcgen05.alloc/dealloc.cta_group::2` | W26, W27 | explicit.cu:885, 971 | the pair's TMEM (the SASS handshake uses the peer's reserved smem, note D.2) |

Everything before line 1179 is CTA-local: parameter reads, special registers, 33 local inits, the fences, the relaxed arrive. That is the sentence at explicit.cu:1178 ("no remote barrier operation before this point") and note B.2 step 26.

## 11.7 Step 7: dispatch and the fall-through warps (explicit.cu:1190-1203)

```cpp
// explicit.cu:1190-1203
  // 7.3 step 7: role dispatch in the baseline's branch order (kernel :617, 681, 726, 807, 869); warp 3 and warp 1 of ranks 1-3 fall through and exit
  if (warp_idx == 2) {
    producer_role(params, smem_base, x, y, is_cta0, lane_pred != 0u && is_leader, k_tiles, tm, tn);
  }
  else if (warp_idx == 1 && is_cta0) {
    scheduler_role(smem_base, x, y, lane, tm, tn);
  }
  else if (warp_idx == 0) {
    mma_role(smem, smem_base, x, y, rank, is_leader, peer, lane_pred, k_tiles, tm, tn);
  }
  else if (warp_idx >= 4) {
    epilogue_role(params, smem, smem_base, x, y, rank, is_leader, warp_idx, lane, alpha, beta, tm, tn);
  }
}
```

The baseline's chain is `if (is_participant.main_load) ... else if (is_participant.sched) ... else if (is_participant.mma) ... else if (is_participant.epi_load) ... else if (is_participant.epilogue)`, with `is_participant = {mma: warp 0, sched: warp 1 && rank 0, main_load: warp 2, epi_load: warp 3 && is_epi_load_needed, epilogue: warps 4-7}` (kernel `:449-455`). At cb424739 the five branches are at `:617, :681, :726, :807, :869`, as the comment says; in the working tree they sit at `:645, :709, :754, :841, :903` because the tree carries trace probes inserted after cb424739's `:614` (28 lines, the K1 record) and after `:729` and `:870` (6 lines each; `git diff cb424739 --stat`: 40 insertions). Lines up to `:614` (the whole prologue) are identical in both. The explicit kernel drops the `epi_load` branch (never taken for `beta = 0`) and keeps the other four in the same order.

| Branch | Warps | Role (chapter) | Arguments worth noticing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `warp_idx == 2` | 2 of every CTA | `producer_role` (8) | `is_cta0` (throttle producer only in CTA 0); `lane_pred != 0 && is_leader` = the one lane of the pair leader's warp that issues `arrive.expect_tx 49152` |
| `warp_idx == 1 && is_cta0` | 1 of rank 0 | `scheduler_role` (7) | `lane` (lanes 0..3 arm the four CTAs' `clc_full`) |
| `warp_idx == 0` | 0 of every CTA | `mma_role` (9) | `smem` (generic, for the TMEM base read), `is_leader`, `peer`, `lane_pred` (trace only) |
| `warp_idx >= 4` | 4-7 of every CTA | `epilogue_role` (10) | `smem`, `warp_idx` (-> `w = warp_idx - 4`), `lane`, `alpha`, `beta` |
| (none) | 3 of every CTA; 1 of ranks 1-3 | fall through to `}` at 1203 and exit | |

Every argument is a value computed in the prologue; the roles receive no pointers to prologue state and share nothing but shared memory. `tm, tn` are the initial tile; each role carries its own copy forward through the CLC loop (Chapter 7).

### 11.7.1 Why the fall-through warps may exit early

One warp per CTA (warp 3), and a second in ranks 1-3 (warp 1), leave at line 1203 while the others run for ~0.9 ms: rank 0 loses one warp, ranks 1-3 lose two, so `7 + 3 x 6 = 25` of the cluster's 32 warps stay, which is exactly the `25 x 32 = 800` of the CLC empty count (11.5.2): every warp that stays consumes CLC responses, and no warp that consumes leaves. This is safe because **no synchronisation object counts the leavers**:

| Object | Population | Includes warp 3? warp 1 of ranks 1-3? |
|---|---|---|
| `bar.sync 6, 160` / `bar.arrive 6, 160` (TMEM alloc hand-off, explicit.cu:887, 997; `kTmemAllocBarThreads = 160` at explicit.cu:191) | 32 (warp 0 arrives) + 128 (warps 4-7 sync) = 160 = `NumMMAThreads + NumEpilogueThreads` (kernel `:558`) | no |
| `bar.sync 1, 128` (epilogue subtile barrier, explicit.cu:1051, 1071) | the 128 epilogue threads | no |
| `barrier.cluster` | all 1024 threads of the cluster, **already passed** at 1179 before anyone exits (and the ISA counts only non-exited threads anyway, 11.6.1) | (passed) |
| `clc_empty` 800 | `32 + 4 * (32 + 32 + 128)`: rank 0's warp 1, every CTA's warps 0, 2, 4-7 | no: `NumSchedThreads` is counted once, not `cluster_size` times, and `NumEpilogueLoadThreads` only when `is_epi_load_needed` |
| `main full/empty`, `acc full/empty`, `throttle`, `tmem_dealloc` | see 11.5.2 | no |

A warp that exits does not end the CTA (the CTA stays resident until its last warp exits), does not release the shared memory, and does not disturb the named barriers, which count only the threads whose `bar.sync`/`bar.arrive` name them. The only exit hazard in this kernel is the one of note Section 7.10: a CTA must not exit while remote CTAs may still arrive on **its** barriers, and that is handled by the four tails inside the roles (Chapters 7-9), not here. Warp 1 of ranks 1-3 does its only useful work, the A/B prefetch, at 1113-1116 before it leaves; warp 3 likewise prefetches C/D (1117-1120) and initialises the throttle barriers (1155-1163).

### 11.7.2 What ptxas made of the dispatch

Note G.3 (measured): the explicit binary carries a three-entry jump table in constant bank 2 (`CONSTANT[2]:12`): `UISETP.LT.U32 UP0, UR20, 0x2; USEL UR4, UR20, 0x2, UP0; USHF.L.U32 UR4, UR4, 0x2; LDCU UR10, c[0x2][UR4]; BRXU UR10` at `0x0a60-0x0ae0`, i.e. index `min(warp_idx, 2) * 4` selects the target for warp 0, warp 1 or warp >= 2, and the warp >= 2 target is split again by `UISETP.NE.U32.AND UP0, UPT, UR20, 0x2; BRA.U` (warp 2 vs the rest); a further `warp_idx >= 4` test must then separate the epilogue warps from the `EXIT` at `0x1f00` that G.3 attributes to warps 1 of ranks 1-3 and warp 3 (inferred from the source, explicit.cu:1200; G.3 does not quote that compare for the explicit kernel, whereas note D.2 does quote the baseline's: warp 1 of ranks 1-3 and warp 3 "traverse the dispatch chain to `UISETP.GE.AND UP0, UR18, 0x4; @!P0 EXIT`" at `0x6580`/`0x65a0`; where the `warp_idx == 1 && is_cta0` test lands behind jump-table entry 1 is likewise inferred; the listing is in Chapter 12). The CUTLASS kernel compiles the same chain to compare-and-branch; both execute once per thread in the prologue, so the cost class is identical. Chapter 12 has the listing.

## 11.8 Section 11: the host launch mirror `run()` (explicit.cu:1265-1329)

The harness calls `explicit_gemm::run(gemm)` where it used to call `gemm.run()` (`70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.cu:416` warm-up, `:439` inside the timed loop); the template bridge in explicit.hpp:130-132 turns that into `run(make_params(gemm))`, where `make_params` (explicit.hpp:100-127) copies the four tensor maps, the problem shape, `alpha`/`beta` and the validation fields out of `gemm.params()` (Chapter 5). What follows is the non-template function, quoted in full in pieces.

### 11.8.1 The guards (explicit.cu:1265-1272)

```cpp
// explicit.cu:1265-1272
cutlass::Status run(ExplicitGemmParams const& params) {
  // E.5.1 guards: the kernel hard-codes the Section 0 configuration; refuse anything else loudly (device code has no checks)
  if (params.mode != kModeGemm) { return cutlass::Status::kErrorInvalidProblem; }
  if (params.m != kFixedM || params.n != kFixedN || params.k != kFixedK || params.l != kFixedL) { return cutlass::Status::kErrorInvalidProblem; }
  if (params.raster_order != kRasterOrderAlongN || params.swizzle_divisor != 0) { return cutlass::Status::kErrorInvalidProblem; }
  if (params.tiles_m != kProblemTilesM || params.tiles_n != kProblemTilesN || params.tiles_l != kProblemTilesL) { return cutlass::Status::kErrorInvalidProblem; }
  if (params.alpha_ptr != nullptr || params.beta_ptr != nullptr) { return cutlass::Status::kErrorNotSupported; }   // no pointer path (D.6 item 13)
  if (params.beta != 0.0f) { return cutlass::Status::kErrorNotSupported; }   // the C path is omitted (Section 0; E.10 item 5); -0.0f passes like is_zero()
```

| Guard | Rejects | Why the kernel cannot handle it | Status (string printed by `CUTLASS_CHECK`, `examples/common/helper.h:43-52`; `cutlass.h:74-77`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode != 0` | anything but `GemmUniversalMode::kGemm` | batched/array modes change the parameter semantics | `kErrorInvalidProblem` ("Error Invalid Problem") |
| shape != (8192, 8192, 8192, 1) | any other M, N, K, L | the grid is hard-coded to (64,64,1); the device never reads M, N, L; the TMA store has a literal 0 batch coordinate; partial tiles are not handled | `kErrorInvalidProblem` |
| `raster_order != 1` or `swizzle_divisor != 0` | AlongM raster, any swizzle | the `tm, tn` formulas of 11.6.3 and the CLC mapping (Chapter 7) are the AlongN, swizzle-0 specialisation | `kErrorInvalidProblem` |
| tiles != (32, 32, 1) | an inconsistent scheduler state | consistency check on the host-only fields | `kErrorInvalidProblem` |
| `alpha_ptr` or `beta_ptr` non-null | scalars passed by device pointer | the explicit kernel has no `ld.global` path for them (note D.6 item 13: compiled but never taken in the baseline) | `kErrorNotSupported` ("Error Not Supported") |
| `beta != 0.0f` | a real C term | the C load path (`epi_load` pipeline, 32 C TMA loads per tile, `load_order`) is omitted; the epilogue computes `fmaf(beta, 0.0f, t)` with a literal-zero C fragment | `kErrorNotSupported` |

`alpha` is deliberately **not** guarded: any value is handled identically to the baseline (`alpha * acc`). `-0.0f` passes the `beta` test because `-0.0f != 0.0f` is false under IEEE comparison, which matches the baseline's `is_zero()` test (`is_C_load_needed = !beta.is_zero()`, note B.2 step 11, Section 8). With `beta = -0.0f` both kernels then compute `fmaf(-0.0f, 0.0f, t)` with the same run-time `beta`, so `D` stays bit-identical to the baseline's; the only input where the sign of `beta` is observable is `t = -0.0f` (`-0.0 + -0.0 = -0.0` against `+0.0 + -0.0 = +0.0`), which is exactly why the C term is kept as an FFMA with the run-time `beta` instead of being dropped (Chapter 10, note D.7). The baseline's `run()` has no guards at all (they live in `can_implement`, which the harness still calls on the CUTLASS side at `70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.cu:407`); these six are the documented deviation (b) of 11.8.6.

### 11.8.2 The kernel pointer and step 1: the dynamic-smem opt-in (explicit.cu:1274-1279)

```cpp
// explicit.cu:1274-1279
  // E.5.2: the run() mirror (gemm_universal_adapter.h:375-575 -> cluster_launch.hpp:260-296)
  void const* kernel = reinterpret_cast<void const*>(&explicit_blackwell_fp16_gemm_kernel);
  cutlass::Status launch_result = cutlass::Status::kSuccess;

  // 1. MaxDynamicSharedMemorySize opt-in on the explicit kernel (initialize() does it for the CUTLASS kernel, :342-352); every call, not hoisted (E.5.4)
  launch_result = status_from_cuda(cudaFuncSetAttribute(kernel, cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize, static_cast<int>(kSmemBytes)));
```

- **Why needed.** By default a kernel may be launched with at most 48 KB of dynamic shared memory; "kernels relying on shared memory allocations over 48 KB per block are architecture-specific ... and require an explicit opt-in using `cudaFuncSetAttribute`" (CUDA Programming Guide, section 3.2.6 of the v13 guide; the Runtime API reference adds that the value plus the static `sharedSizeBytes` cannot exceed `cudaDevAttrMaxSharedMemoryPerBlockOptin`, which is 227 KB = 232448 bytes on CC 10.0 per the Blackwell Tuning Guide; `static_assert(kSmemBytes <= 232448)` at util.hpp:46). Without this call `cudaLaunchKernelExC` with `dynamicSmemBytes = 230400` is rejected and nothing runs (the exact error code was not measured).
- **Who does it for the CUTLASS kernel.** `GemmUniversalAdapter::initialize()` (`gemm_universal_adapter.h:342-352`): `if (smem_size >= (48 << 10)) cudaFuncSetAttribute(device_kernel<GemmKernel>, cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize, smem_size)`. The harness still calls `gemm.initialize()` before every `explicit_gemm::run()` (`70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.cu:410, 438`), so that call keeps happening, but on a kernel that is never launched. The explicit kernel is a different function and needs its own opt-in.
- **Why every call, not hoisted behind a `static bool`.** Note E.5.4: the baseline makes two attribute calls per iteration on the kernel it launches (the opt-in inside `initialize()` and `NonPortableClusterSizeAllowed` inside `run()`); doing the opt-in on every call keeps the explicit path at two attribute calls on the launched kernel per iteration, so the per-iteration host sequence stays the same **in kind** (23 non-synchronising runtime calls against 22). A `cudaFuncSetAttribute` is a host-side table update costing low microseconds (inferred, note E.5.4), hidden behind the previous ~0.889 ms kernel for iterations 1-9 and exposed only in iteration 0; hoisting it would save nothing measurable and would make the comparison harder to argue.
- `status_from_cuda` (util.hpp:51-53) maps `cudaSuccess -> kSuccess`, anything else `-> kInvalid`, mirroring `ClusterLauncher`'s `Return_Status` macro (`cluster_launch.hpp:73-78`).

### 11.8.3 Steps 2-4: geometry, `check_cluster_dims`, the non-portable-cluster attribute (explicit.cu:1281-1295)

```cpp
// explicit.cu:1281-1295
  // 2. launch geometry (Section 5.4): grid (64,64,1) = the AlongN-transposed (N/128, M/128, 1); block (256,1,1); 230400 bytes of dynamic smem
  dim3 const grid(kGridX, kGridY, kGridZ);
  dim3 const block(kBlockThreads, 1, 1);
  dim3 const cluster(kClusterX, kClusterY, kClusterZ);

  // 3. check_cluster_dims (cluster_launch.hpp:103-112)
  if (launch_result == cutlass::Status::kSuccess) {
    bool const ok = (cluster.x * cluster.y * cluster.z <= 32u) && (grid.x % cluster.x == 0u) && (grid.y % cluster.y == 0u) && (grid.z % cluster.z == 0u);
    if (!ok) { launch_result = cutlass::Status::kInvalid; }
  }

  // 4. ClusterLauncher::init: NonPortableClusterSizeAllowed on every launch (cluster_launch.hpp:141-143, called from :280)
  if (launch_result == cutlass::Status::kSuccess) {
    launch_result = status_from_cuda(cudaFuncSetAttribute(kernel, cudaFuncAttributeNonPortableClusterSizeAllowed, 1));
  }
```

- **Geometry.** `grid = (64, 64, 1)` (util.hpp:32, the transposed order of 11.6.3), `block = (256, 1, 1)` (`GemmKernel::get_block_shape()` = `dim3(MaxThreadsPerBlock, 1, 1)`, kernel `:399-401`), `cluster = (2, 2, 1)` (util.hpp:31). In the baseline `grid` comes from `get_grid_shape(params)` at run time (`gemm_universal_adapter.h:381`); here it is a constant because the guards have already pinned the shape (deviation (b)).
- **`check_cluster_dims`** is a copy of `cluster_launch.hpp:103-112`: cluster size `<= MaxClusterSize = 32` (`:82`) and each grid dimension divisible by the cluster dimension. For this run `4 <= 32`, `64 % 2 == 0`, `64 % 2 == 0`, `1 % 1 == 0`; the same conditions are also `static_assert`ed at util.hpp:42-43, so the run-time test can never fail here. It is kept because `launch_with_fallback_cluster` performs it on every launch (`:274-278`) and returns `kInvalid` when it fails.
- **`NonPortableClusterSizeAllowed`.** `ClusterLauncher::init` (`:141-144`) sets `cudaFuncAttributeNonPortableClusterSizeAllowed = 1` on every launch (`:280`). It is only *needed* for clusters larger than the portable maximum of 8 ("the maximum portable cluster size supported is 8; however, NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPU allows for a nonportable cluster size of 16 by opting in. Launching a kernel with a nonportable cluster size requires setting the `cudaFuncAttributeNonPortableClusterSizeAllowed` function attribute", Blackwell Tuning Guide). A cluster of 4 does not need it; it is kept for parity with the baseline's call sequence (note E.5.2 item 4 marks the "functionally irrelevant" judgement as inferred).

### 11.8.4 Steps 5-6: the launch configuration and `cudaLaunchKernelExC` (explicit.cu:1297-1313)

```cpp
// explicit.cu:1297-1313
  // 5.-6. make_cluster_launch_config (:151-213): one attribute, cudaLaunchAttributeClusterDimension = {2,2,1}; legacy default stream; then cudaLaunchKernelExC (:294)
  if (launch_result == cutlass::Status::kSuccess) {
    cudaLaunchConfig_t launch_config = {};
    launch_config.gridDim = grid;
    launch_config.blockDim = block;
    launch_config.dynamicSmemBytes = kSmemBytes;
    launch_config.stream = nullptr;
    cudaLaunchAttribute launch_attribute[1];
    launch_attribute[0].id = cudaLaunchAttributeClusterDimension;
    launch_attribute[0].val.clusterDim.x = cluster.x;
    launch_attribute[0].val.clusterDim.y = cluster.y;
    launch_attribute[0].val.clusterDim.z = cluster.z;
    launch_config.attrs = launch_attribute;
    launch_config.numAttrs = 1;
    void* kernel_params[] = { const_cast<void*>(static_cast<void const*>(&params)) };
    launch_result = status_from_cuda(cudaLaunchKernelExC(&launch_config, kernel, kernel_params));
  }
```

This is `ClusterLauncher::make_cluster_launch_config` (`cluster_launch.hpp:150-213`) evaluated for this build and this call:

| `make_cluster_launch_config` | Value here | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `launch_attribute[0] = {cudaLaunchAttributeClusterDimension, {2,2,1}}` (`:166, :177`) | the one attribute kept | no fallback cluster (`have_fallback = false`, `:168`, since `fallback_cluster_dims = {0,0,0}` from `gemm_universal_adapter.h:400`) |
| `numAttrs` starts at 3 (`CUDA_ENABLE_PREFERRED_CLUSTER` is defined for nvcc >= 12.8, `cluster_launch.hpp:55-57`; `:89`) | 3 -> 2: `numAttrs--` because there is no fallback (`:192-194`) | the preferred-cluster attribute is dropped |
| `launch_attribute[numAttrs - 1] = PDL` (`:199-200`) | written but not counted: `numAttrs = launch_with_pdl ? numAttrs : numAttrs - 1 = 1` (`:206`) | `launch_with_pdl = false` (default argument at `gemm_universal_adapter.h:378`, the harness never sets it); so the kernel's `griddepcontrol.wait` returns immediately and `launch_dependents` has no dependent (Chapter 8, 9; note E.5.4 "absence of PDL", inferred) |
| `gridDim, blockDim, dynamicSmemBytes` (`:202-204`) | (64,64,1), (256,1,1), 230400 | |
| `stream` (`:205`) | `nullptr` = the legacy default stream | `gemm.run()` is called with its default `stream = nullptr` (`gemm_universal_adapter.h:612`); the harness's `GpuTimer` records its events on stream 0 (`examples/common/helper.h:79, 93-96`), so the timed launches must be on that stream |

`cudaLaunchKernelExC(&config, func, args)` (CUDA Runtime API, "Execution Control") enqueues the kernel asynchronously with the attributes in `config`; `args` is an array of pointers to the kernel's parameters, here one pointer to the 640-byte `ExplicitGemmParams`, which the runtime copies into the launch's parameter buffer (the baseline copies its 2048-byte `Params`, note D.1 D2). The call is `cluster_launch.hpp:293-294` (`synclog_setup()` is a no-op without `CUTLASS_ENABLE_SYNCLOG`, note D.1 D14).

**Where the parameter-size limit comes from.** Kernel parameters "are passed to the device through constant memory and have been limited to 4,096 bytes"; "CUDA 12.1 increases this parameter limit from 4,096 bytes to 32,764 bytes on all device architectures including NVIDIA Volta and above" (NVIDIA developer blog, "CUDA 12.1 Supports Large Kernel Parameters"; an R530 or newer driver is required, and the limit stays 4,096 bytes below Volta). That constant-memory placement is what 11.2.2 showed: the block lands in constant bank 0 at `c[0x0][0x380]`, so the resource line reads `CONSTANT[0]:1536 = 0x380 + 640` (note G.3). explicit.hpp:76 keeps the classic bound as a guard, `static_assert(sizeof(ExplicitGemmParams) <= 4096, "kernel parameter block limit");`; the 640-byte block (and the baseline's 2048) is far below either limit, so the assert documents the constraint rather than guarding a live risk.

### 11.8.5 Step 7: `cudaGetLastError` and the Status mapping (explicit.cu:1315-1329)

```cpp
// explicit.cu:1315-1329
  // 7. cudaGetLastError -> kSuccess / kErrorInternal (gemm_universal_adapter.h:564-574)
  cudaError_t const result = cudaGetLastError();
#if defined(CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE)   // [TRACE]
  if (result != cudaSuccess || launch_result != cutlass::Status::kSuccess) {
    std::printf("TRACE_HOST explicit_run_launch_error %d %s status %d\n", int(result), cudaGetErrorString(result), int(launch_result));
  }
  if (g_explicit_trace_armed && result == cudaSuccess && launch_result == cutlass::Status::kSuccess) {
    return explicit_trace_wait_and_check();   // toggle-on warm-up only: bounded wait, hang records, heartbeats (E.7.2 B1/B2)
  }
#endif
  if (cudaSuccess == result && cutlass::Status::kSuccess == launch_result) {
    return cutlass::Status::kSuccess;
  }
  return cutlass::Status::kErrorInternal;
}
```

The last four lines are `GemmUniversalAdapter::run` `:564-574` verbatim in logic: `cudaGetLastError()` "returns the last error that has been produced by any of the runtime calls in the same instance of the CUDA Runtime library in the host thread and resets it to `cudaSuccess`" (CUDA Runtime API, Error Handling). The reset applies to the **non-sticky** error state: a launch rejection is non-sticky and is cleared here, so a stale error is not picked up by some later unrelated `cudaGetLastError` (note E.5.2 item 7: "clears the per-thread error variable so that a stale non-sticky error is not picked up"); a device fault (an illegal address, or the `__trap()` that 11.9's watchdog path ends in) is sticky, leaves the context unusable and is returned by every later call regardless. Every failure path (`kInvalid` from any step, or a non-success `result`) collapses to `kErrorInternal`, exactly as the adapter does. On the `[PROD]` path the function therefore returns in one of two ways: `kSuccess` with the kernel **enqueued, not finished**, or an error status with nothing launched.

### 11.8.6 Side by side with `GemmUniversalAdapter::run()` and `ClusterLauncher`

| # | `explicit_gemm::run` (explicit.cu) | CUTLASS | Same? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | six guards (1267-1272) | none in `run()`; `can_implement()` on the host side | **deviation (b)**: documented, affects only arguments outside the fixed configuration |
| 1 | `cudaFuncSetAttribute(kernel, MaxDynamicSharedMemorySize, 230400)` (1279) | in `initialize()` `:342-352`, on `device_kernel<GemmKernel>` | **deviation (a)**: the same attribute, on the kernel that is actually launched; the baseline's call still runs on the never-launched kernel |
| 2 | `grid(64,64,1)`, `block(256,1,1)`, `cluster(2,2,1)` (1282-1284) | `block = get_block_shape()`, `grid = get_grid_shape(params)` (`:380-381`), `cluster` from `ClusterShape` (`:395-397`) | same values; grid hard-coded (part of deviation (b)) |
| 3 | `check_cluster_dims` (1287-1290) | `cluster_launch.hpp:103-112` via `:274-278` | same |
| 4 | `cudaFuncSetAttribute(kernel, NonPortableClusterSizeAllowed, 1)` (1294) | `ClusterLauncher::init` `:141-144` via `:280` | same |
| 5 | `cudaLaunchConfig_t` with one `ClusterDimension` attribute, stream `nullptr` (1299-1310) | `make_cluster_launch_config` `:151-213` (3 -> 2 -> 1 attributes) | same configuration |
| 6 | `cudaLaunchKernelExC(&cfg, kernel, {&params})` (1311-1312) | `:293-294` | same API; 640-byte vs 2048-byte parameter copy |
| 7 | `cudaGetLastError` -> `kSuccess` / `kErrorInternal` (1316, 1325-1328) | `:564-574` | same |

Path through the adapter for this configuration (`gemm_universal_adapter.h:388-521`), naming the compile-time tests it falls through so that you can trace it in the header: `kMinComputeCapability >= 90` -> extended launch API; `if constexpr (kEnableCudaHostAdapter)` (`:418`; `kEnableCudaHostAdapter = CUTLASS_ENABLE_CUDA_HOST_ADAPTER` at `:145`, false in this build) -> the `else` at `:455` takes `kernel = device_kernel<GemmKernel>` (`:458`); `static constexpr bool kClusterLaunch = GemmKernel::ArchTag::kMinComputeCapability == 90` (`:459`) is false for SM100, so `if constexpr (kClusterLaunch)` (`:460`) is skipped and control reaches the `kMinComputeCapability == 100 || 101 || 120 || 103` branch (`:486-490`); inside it `is_static_1x1x1` is false (cluster size 4) -> `ClusterLauncher::launch_with_fallback_cluster(grid, cluster, fallback_cluster, block, smem_size, stream, kernel, kernel_params, launch_with_pdl)` (`:509-518`) -> `cluster_launch.hpp:260-296`.

**Why nothing synchronises.** `cudaFuncSetAttribute` and `cudaGetLastError` are host-side; `cudaLaunchKernelExC` enqueues and returns. There is no `cudaDeviceSynchronize`, `cudaStreamSynchronize`, `cudaMemcpy`, `cudaFuncGetAttributes`, occupancy query or `printf` on the `[PROD]` path (note E.5.2 "Not in the function"). This is what the harness's timing method requires: `GpuTimer::start()` records an event, ten iterations of `gemm.initialize()` + `explicit_gemm::run()` enqueue ten kernels (plus six `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled` and three attribute calls of host work each), `stop()` records a second event, and `elapsed_millis()` is the GPU-side span (`helper.h:106-112`; `70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.cu:435-445`). The GPU is idle when the timer starts because `verify()` ends with `cudaDeviceSynchronize()` (`70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.cu:375`) and the reference compare drains the stream, so iteration 0's host work is exposed in both binaries and iterations 1-9 hide theirs behind the previous kernel (note E.5.4, with the "hidden" part marked inferred). A synchronising call anywhere in `run()` would turn the measured number into kernel time **plus** host time ten times over and break the comparison (note Section 12 item 1).

The result of all this (measured, note G.2): median `Avg runtime` 0.889354 ms for the explicit path against 0.889917 ms for the pristine binary on the same day, ratio 0.99937; 23 runtime calls per iteration against 22.

## 11.9 Section 12 in brief: the bring-up instruments (explicit.cu:1212-1263, 1331-1449)

Everything in this section sits inside `#if defined(CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE)` and is compiled only when line 1 of util.hpp is uncommented (`// #define CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE 1`). With the toggle off, two independent builds produced byte-identical SASS (note G.3 "D6"), so none of it exists in the performance binary. It is here because a kernel of this kind fails in only a few ways (a hang on a barrier, a wrong tile mapping, a wrong epilogue address), and each of them is far faster to diagnose with a purpose-built instrument than with a debugger that cannot stop a `tcgen05`/TMA pipeline without perturbing it.

| Instrument | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **Sentinel fill of D** (B3) | `trace_begin`, explicit.cu:1348-1351 | `cudaMemset(D, 0xFF)` before the warm-up launch: every float of D becomes a NaN pattern, so any tile the kernel never stores shows up as `N` in the mismatch map instead of as stale zeros |
| **K0 probe kernel** | `trace_begin`, 1347 (`trace_probe_kernel_k0`, `deabstraction_trace_probes.hpp:79-98`) | a tiny (2,2,1)-cluster kernel launched with the same 230400-byte / non-portable attributes that records each rank's shared-memory base, `mapa` results and TMEM base (`TRACE_K0`), i.e. measures the `0x400 + (rank << 24)` fact of 11.2.3 independently of the GEMM kernel |
| **Hang records + 20 s watchdog** (B1/B2) | `explicit_trace_wait_and_check`, 1222-1261; `EXPLICIT_WAIT` -> `mbar_wait_traced` (Section 2 and 4 of the file) | every blocking wait of the roles becomes a bounded loop reading `%globaltimer`; after 4 s the stuck warp writes a 64-byte `HangRec` (site, `blockIdx`, rank, warp, lane, barrier address and offset, parity, tile, k-tile) into a host-mapped pinned buffer, spins 1 s so that every stuck warp records, then `__trap()`s; lane 0 of each role warp also writes heartbeats (tile counter, phase marker) at tile start, tail, TMEM alloc and exit (`enum HbPhase : uint32_t { HB_TILE_START = 1, HB_TAIL = 2, HB_ALLOC = 3, HB_EXIT = 4 };`, explicit.cu:228). `run()` under the toggle (1321-1323), **only for the armed warm-up launch**, polls `cudaEventQuery` every 10 ms for up to 20 s, then prints `TRACE_HANG` / `TRACE_HANG_HB` lines and `_Exit(3)`s on timeout |
| **Record buffer** (K1-K5, K_TAIL) | `trace_reset`/`trace_dump`/`trace_disable` (`deabstraction_trace.hpp:178-230`), `TRACE_RECORD` probes in the roles | 128-byte records of every TMA/MMA/CLC operand of the first cluster, dumped to `launch0.csv` and checked by `check_trace.py` against Parts A-E (4112 PASS for the explicit kernel, note G.1) |
| **Mismatch classifier** (B4) | `trace_mismatch_dump`, 1360-1438 | if the compare fails: counts value vs bitwise vs sentinel vs sign-of-zero mismatches; prints a 64 x 64 per-tile map (`.` clean, `#` all wrong, `x` partial, `N` sentinel); for the first bad tile, the mismatch fraction per 64-row half, 32-row quarter (= epilogue warp), 16-column subtile and `(row % 32, col % 4)` class; a histogram of `D/ref` ratios in 1/128 steps (a wrong `scale_c` or a missed k-tile shows up as a ratio of `k/128`); and whether the bad tile holds the reference of some *other* tile (a tile-mapping error). Each of these classes points at one chapter's code |
| **H3 attributes and occupancy** | `trace_end`, 1443 (`trace_host_post_run_fn`) | `cudaFuncGetAttributes` and `cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters` on the explicit kernel (`numRegs`, `sharedSizeBytes 0`, `maxDynamicSharedSizeBytes 230400`, `max_active_clusters 33`) |

The harness calls them under the same toggle: `trace_begin(block_D.get(), bytes)` before the warm-up (`70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.cu:389-392`), `trace_end("launch0.csv", passed, D, ref_D, m, n)` right after `verify()` (`:421-424`), and `trace_end` disarms the watchdog (`g_explicit_trace_armed = false`, explicit.cu:1442) and disables recording (`trace_disable()`, 1445) **before** the ten timed launches. The timed launches of the trace binary are nevertheless **not** quiet: `trace_disable()` only clears `g_trace_enabled`, i.e. stops the `TRACE_RECORD` appends (`deabstraction_trace.hpp:189-193`), while the `EXPLICIT_WAIT` bounded waits (explicit.cu:232 -> `mbar_wait_traced`, which reads `%globaltimer` at entry and after every failed `try_wait`) and the `heartbeat()` writes to host-mapped pinned memory (explicit.cu:624-626; `g_explicit_hang_buf` is never reset to null) stay compiled in and active. That is why the trace binary's number is discarded: its `Avg runtime` is 1.13341 ms, about 27% slower than the performance binary's 0.889354 ms, and about 12.6% slower than the CUTLASS kernel's own toggle-on build (1.00684 ms), the comparison note H.1 rounds to "about 12%" (note G.2). Only the toggle-off binary is ever timed.

## 11.10 The frame as a timeline, and a rewriting checklist

```
 host (one call of explicit_gemm::run)           device (every CTA, 256 threads; t ->)
 ------------------------------------------      --------------------------------------------------------
 guards (6 compares)                             entry: smem_base = cvta(smem)            [all threads]
 FuncSetAttribute MaxDynSmem 230400              step 1  shfl -> warp_idx; elect -> lane_pred;
 grid/block/cluster constants                            %cluster_ctarank -> rank, is_cta0, is_leader, peer
 check_cluster_dims                              step 2  alpha, beta, k_tiles = (k+63)>>6
 FuncSetAttribute NonPortableCluster 1                   warp 1 lane: prefetch A, B; warp 3 lane: prefetch C, D
 cudaLaunchConfig_t {64x64x1, 256, 230400,       step 3  w0: 16 inits | fence | w4: 4 inits | fence |
   stream 0, [ClusterDimension 2x2x1]}                   w5: 8 inits | fence | w3: 4 inits | fence | w0 lane: 1 init
 cudaLaunchKernelExC  ---- enqueue ---->         step 4  barrier.cluster.arrive.relaxed.aligned
 cudaGetLastError -> Status                      step 5  x, y = %cluster_ctaid; tm, tn from blockIdx
 return (kernel still running)                   step 6  barrier.cluster.wait.aligned   <- first point at which
                                                                                            remote smem may be touched
                                                 step 7  w2 -> producer | w1&rank0 -> scheduler | w0 -> mma |
                                                         w4-7 -> epilogue | w3, w1 of ranks 1-3 -> exit
```

If you rewrite this frame from a blank file, the order of decisions is:

1. **Parameter block.** A POD struct with the `CUtensorMap`s first (alignment 64/128), scalars after; pass it `const __grid_constant__`; take addresses of the maps only.
2. **Shared memory.** One `extern __shared__ char smem[]`, no static `__shared__`, every object at a fixed `OFF_*`; `static_assert` the alignments (1024 for SW128 stages, 512 for the SW128_32B epilogue stages, 16 for the CLC responses) and the total; compute `smem_base` once; never mix it with the generic pointer.
3. **Identity.** Warp index through `shfl`, one election you may reuse for one-off work, `%cluster_ctarank` and `%cluster_ctaid`; derive leader/peer/cta0 from the rank.
4. **Prefetch** every descriptor you will use, from an idle warp, before the rendezvous.
5. **Barriers.** Initialise every barrier you will arrive on with the exact count of arrivals per phase (one line of justification each), fence, and only then the cluster rendezvous; leave unused barriers uninitialised and keep their counts out of the others (800, not 928).
6. **Rendezvous.** `arrive.relaxed` -> local setup -> `wait`; no remote operation before the wait; derive the initial tile from `blockIdx` by inverting whatever raster/transposition the host applied.
7. **Dispatch** on the warp-uniform index; let non-participating warps exit; make sure no `bar.sync` population or mbarrier count includes them.
8. **Host.** Opt in to the dynamic smem, set the cluster attribute, launch with `cudaLaunchKernelExC` on the stream the timer watches, map errors, never synchronise.

Chapter 13 generalises this list to other operators.

- NVIDIA Blackwell Tuning Guide (228 KB per SM, 227 KB per block, 1 KB reserved per block, 64 K registers per SM, portable cluster size 8 / non-portable 16): https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/blackwell-tuning-guide/index.html
- NVIDIA Hopper Tuning Guide (same cluster-size statements for CC 9.0): https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/hopper-tuning-guide/index.html
- PTX ISA 9.4 (`barrier.cluster` 9.7.15.3, `membar`/`fence` with `.op_restrict = .mbarrier_init` 9.7.15.4, `elect.sync` 9.7.15.15, "Size and alignment of mbarrier object" 9.7.15.16.1, `mbarrier.init` 9.7.15.16.12, `prefetch.tensormap` 9.7.10.16, Tensor-map 5.5.8, `%cluster_ctaid` 10.14): https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/index.html (the quotations in this chapter are taken from the text of that page)
- LLVM NVPTX usage guide (`nvvm.fence.mbarrier_init.release.cluster`, restating the ISA sentence on `.mbarrier_init`): https://llvm.org/docs/NVPTXUsage.html
- Local sources cited inline: explicit.cu, explicit.hpp, util.hpp, `70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.cu`, `deabstraction_trace.hpp`, `examples/common/helper.h`, `include/cutlass/device_kernel.h`, `include/cutlass/gemm/kernel/sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp` (cb424739 line numbers, identical to the working tree up to `:614`; the tree carries trace probes after `:614`, `:729` and `:870`), `include/cutlass/gemm/kernel/sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp` (working-tree line numbers; identical to cb424739 up to `:445`, 6 higher for cb424739's `:446-:462`, 31 higher from `:473` on, see 11.6.3), `include/cutlass/gemm/kernel/tile_scheduler_detail.hpp`, `include/cutlass/gemm/kernel/tile_scheduler_params.h`, `include/cutlass/cluster_launch.hpp`, `include/cutlass/gemm/device/gemm_universal_adapter.h`, `include/cutlass/arch/barrier.h`, `include/cutlass/pipeline/sm100_pipeline.hpp`, `include/cutlass/pipeline/sm90_pipeline.hpp`, `include/cute/arch/cluster_sm90.hpp`, `include/cute/arch/copy_sm90_desc.hpp`, `include/cute/arch/copy_sm100_tma.hpp`, `include/cute/arch/util.hpp`, `include/cutlass/cutlass.h`, `include/cutlass/detail/helper_macros.hpp`; the note (Sections 5.4, 6.2, 7.1-7.3, 7.10, 12, 13; B.2, B.4, B.5, B.6; D.1, D.2, D.3, D.5, D.6, D.7; E.5, E.6; G.1-G.3; H).

## Checkpoint

**Q1.** The kernel takes `params` by value. Why does it need `__grid_constant__`, and what observable artefact in the compiled binary tells you it worked?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

Seven expressions at three kinds of site take the address of a member: `&params.tma_a/b/c/d` at the four `prefetch.tensormap` (explicit.cu:1114-1115, 1118-1119), `&params.tma_a/b` at the two TMA loads (747, 754) and `&params.tma_d` at the TMA store (1066); the PTX ISA requires the tensor map to live in `.const`, `.param` or `.global` space. `__grid_constant__` guarantees the compiler makes no per-thread copy and that the address is the parameter-space object (CUDA Programming Guide 5.4.1.5). Without it, taking the address would force a local-memory copy of the 640-byte struct. The evidence: `LOCAL:0 STACK:0` in `cuobjdump --dump-resource-usage` (note G.3) and the descriptor addresses appearing as `c[0x0][0x348] + 0x180` in the SASS.
</details>

**Q2.** Compute the `shared::cta` address of rank 2's `acc_full[1]` and of its A stage 3, and state why both are correctly aligned.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

`smem_base = 0x400 + (2 << 24) = 0x02000400`. `acc_full[1] = smem_base + OFF_ACC_FULL + 8 = 0x02000400 + 240 + 8 = 0x020004F8` (8-byte aligned, as every mbarrier must be). A stage 3 = `smem_base + OFF_SMEM_A + 3 * 16384 = 0x02000400 + 33792 + 49152 = 0x02000400 + 82944 = 0x02014800`; `0x14800 % 1024 = 0` because the base `0x400` and `OFF_SMEM_A = 33792 = 33 * 1024` are both 1024-multiples and the stage stride 16384 is too. The alignment of the base is a property of the launch (no static `__shared__`), measured as `0x400`, not something the declaration can enforce.
</details>

**Q3.** Why is `kClcEmptyCount` 800 and not 928 or 896, and which warps' threads make up the 800?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

`consumer_arv_count = NumSchedThreads + cluster_size * (NumMainloopLoadThreads + NumEpilogueThreads + NumMMAThreads) = 32 + 4 * (32 + 128 + 32) = 800` (kernel `:511-512`): rank 0's warp 1 (32), plus in each of the 4 CTAs warp 2 (32), warps 4-7 (128) and warp 0 (32). 928 would add `cluster_size * NumEpilogueLoadThreads = 128` for warp 3, which only consumes CLC responses when `is_epi_load_needed` (`beta != 0`, kernel `:513-515`; the baseline's run-time `selp.b32 928, 800`). 896 would count `NumSchedThreads` `cluster_size` times, `4 * (32 + 32 + 128 + 32)`, i.e. warp 1 in every CTA; only rank 0's warp 1 consumes (the others exit at the dispatch). As warp counts:

| Count | Warps counted | Arithmetic |
|---|---|---|
| 800 | rank 0's warp 1 + 4 x {0, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7} = 1 + 24 = 25 warps (exactly the warps that do not exit at the dispatch) | 25 x 32 |
| 896 | 800 + warp 1 of ranks 1-3 (3 more warps, which exit at 1203 and never consume) | 28 x 32 |
| 928 | 800 + warp 3 of every CTA (4 more warps, consumers only when `beta != 0`) | 29 x 32 |

Every one of the 800 threads arrives remotely on CTA 0's `clc_empty[i]` (explicit.cu:684).
</details>

**Q4.** The arrive of the cluster rendezvous is `.relaxed`. Where does the release that publishes the `mbarrier.init`s come from, and what would go wrong if a thread issued a remote `mbarrier.arrive` before `barrier.cluster.wait`?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

From `fence.mbarrier_init.release.cluster`, executed by every thread after each init group (explicit.cu:1133, 1144, 1154, 1164); it orders the thread's prior `mbarrier.init`s at cluster scope with release semantics, and `barrier.cluster.wait` carries the acquire (PTX ISA defaults). The arrive therefore needs no release of its own, which is cheaper and is what `pipeline_init_arrive_relaxed` does. Before the wait, another CTA may not yet have executed its inits (or even started), so a remote arrive on its barrier would hit uninitialised memory: undefined behaviour, in practice a hang or a corrupted phase. Hence the invariant: all remote operations (11.6.6) are inside the role functions, after explicit.cu:1179.
</details>

**Q5.** Derive `(tm, tn)` for `blockIdx = (6, 1)`, name the rank, and state which other CTA of its cluster shares its A rows.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

`x = 6 & 1 = 0`, `y = 1 & 1 = 1`, rank `= x + 2y = 2`. `tm = 2 * (1 >> 1) + (6 & 1) = 0 + 0 = 0`; `tn = 2 * (6 >> 1) + (1 & 1) = 6 + 1 = 7`. Tile (0, 7): D rows [0, 128), columns [896, 1024). The CTA sharing its A rows is the one with the same tm and the other y, i.e. rank `x + 2(1-y) = 0`, `blockIdx = (6, 0)` -> `(tm, tn) = (0, 6)`. The A multicast mask of both is `0x5 << x = 0x5` (ranks 0 and 2).
</details>

**Q6.** Warp 3 exits at line 1203 in every CTA. List the synchronisation objects in the kernel and show that none of them waits for warp 3.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

`bar.sync/arrive 6, 160`: 32 (warp 0) + 128 (warps 4-7). `bar.sync 1, 128`: the four epilogue warps. `barrier.cluster`: all 256 threads, but warp 3 participates and it is passed before anyone exits. mbarrier counts: main full 1 (leader lane of warp 2), main empty 2 (two leaders' commits), clc full 1 (scheduler lane), clc empty 800 (warps 0, 2, 4-7 of every CTA and rank 0's warp 1), acc full 1 (leader commit), acc empty 256 (warps 4-7 of both CTAs), throttle 32/32 (rank 0's warps 2 and 1), tmem_dealloc 32 (warp 0). Warp 3 appears nowhere, so its exit cannot block anything; its only duties (prefetch C/D, init the throttle barriers) are done before the rendezvous.
</details>

**Q7.** Why does `run()` call `cudaFuncSetAttribute(MaxDynamicSharedMemorySize)` on every call instead of once, and what would change in the measurement if it did not?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

The opt-in is required (230400 > 48 KB) and must be on the launched kernel, so it cannot be left to `gemm.initialize()`, which sets it on the never-launched CUTLASS kernel. Doing it on every call keeps the number of attribute calls on the launched kernel at two per iteration, as in the baseline (`initialize()`'s opt-in + `run()`'s `NonPortableClusterSizeAllowed`), so the per-iteration host sequence is the same in kind (23 vs 22 non-synchronising calls). Hoisting it would save low microseconds hidden behind the previous kernel in iterations 1-9 and make the per-iteration sequences differ in kind, so the timing comparison would need `nsys` kernel-only durations to stand (note E.5.4, Section 12). The kernel itself would be unaffected.
</details>

**Q8.** `run()` returns `kSuccess`. Has the GEMM finished? What does `verify()` rely on, and why must `run()` itself never synchronise?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

No: `cudaLaunchKernelExC` enqueues asynchronously, and `run()` contains no synchronising call; `kSuccess` only means the launch was accepted. `verify()` runs the reference GEMM on the same stream and ends with `cudaDeviceSynchronize()` (`70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.cu:375`) before comparing. `run()` must not synchronise because the harness times ten back-to-back iterations between two events on stream 0 (`GpuTimer`); any synchronisation inside `run()` would add host latency to every iteration and make `Avg runtime` incomparable with `gemm.run()`'s, which never synchronises either (`gemm_universal_adapter.h:372-575`).
</details>
