# Chapter 12. The Artifact: What ptxas Made of It, and What Was Measured

**What you will learn**

- What the compiled kernel actually is: a 1553-line PTX entry, a 1640-instruction `sm_100a` cubin, and one resource line (`REG:26 STACK:0 SHARED:1024 LOCAL:0 CONSTANT[2]:12 CONSTANT[0]:1536`), and how each number is produced.
- The three things you must be able to read before any SASS listing makes sense: the control word and its scoreboards (where `tcgen05.wait::ld` went and what `DEPBAR.LE SBn, k` means), the truth-table immediates of `LOP3`/`PLOP3` (why `0x80, 0x8` is "true" and `0x40, 0x4` is "false"), and the byte selectors of `PRMT` (how `mapa` and the multicast mask were lowered).
- The PTX-to-SASS dictionary for every instruction family the kernel uses (tcgen05, TMA, mbarrier, CLC, GDC, named/cluster barriers, fences, arithmetic), with the lesson each lowering teaches about the hardware, and the PTX ISA rules that make the kernel's single `tcgen05.wait::ld` and its elections necessary.
- What the uniform datapath (`UR`/`UP` registers, `U*` mnemonics) is, why one warp-uniform `UTMALDG`/`UTCHMMA`/`UTCBAR`/`UGETNEXTWORKID` costs one issue slot regardless of lane count, why every `elect.sync` inside the role loops vanished from the SASS, and what that means for how you write issue code.
- Why the kernel needs 26 vector registers where the CUTLASS kernel needs 68, and why neither number matters here (and when it would).
- The exact shape of the four hot loops in the binary (47, 37, 50 and 674/696 instructions) and a quantitative argument for why their issue cost is invisible behind the 426-cycle k-tile.
- What was measured: the five interleaved timing pairs (ratio 0.99937), the correctness evidence (value-equal D and why the comparison is exact, sentinel fill, 4112 checks as committed and 4116 with the later self-check section, 1518 tail records), the record-level trace equivalence with the CUTLASS kernel (6864 identical non-CLC records), and the CLC dynamics (33 clusters on 132 SMs, 16 idle SMs, 32/31 tiles per cluster, hand-out order, latency distribution).
- How to reproduce and inspect everything yourself: build, run, flip the trace toggle, `cuobjdump` the binary, read a `SYNCS`/`UTC*`/`UTMA*` line, and which Nsight Compute metrics would attribute the remaining distance to the speed of light.
- What "performance-equivalent" required structurally, and what was free to change.

Evidence tags used in this chapter: **[M]** measured (note Parts D and G, or my own reading of the committed dumps in `trace_out_v2/`), **[S]** derived from source (explicit.cu, the CUTLASS headers, or the documents named in the references), **[H]** my analysis or hypothesis. Every SASS line quoted below is copied from `trace_out_v2/sass_explicit.txt` with the trailing `/* 0x... */` control-word comment removed; every C++ line is copied from explicit.cu with `sed`.

---

## 12.1 Three artifacts, one toolchain

The kernel you studied in Chapters 5-11 is a C++ file. What runs on the B200 is a cubin that `ptxas` produced from the PTX that `nvcc`'s front end produced from that file. The asm strings of the 37 wrappers (Chapter 6) are copied into the PTX verbatim; everything else, including the lowering of every `tcgen05.*`, `cp.async.bulk.tensor.*` and `mbarrier.*` instruction into machine instructions, is `ptxas`'s decision. This chapter is about those decisions and about what the finished binary did when it ran.

```
 explicit.cu ──nvcc front end──> PTX (compute_100a, embedded in the fatbin)
                                   │  1553 instruction lines, 92 predicates, 1014 .b32 regs       [M]
                                   └──ptxas──> SASS (sm_100a cubin)
                                                 1640 instructions, REG 26, LOCAL 0, STACK 0     [M]
```

The build is the fixed Section 0 command of the note (two `--generate-code` clauses, `arch=compute_100a,code=[sm_100a]` and `arch=compute_100a,code=[compute_100a]`, so the fatbin carries both the cubin and the PTX; note D.5). The dumps the chapter reads were produced by `cuobjdump` on the saved toggle-off binary `trace_out_v2/70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.explicit` (note Part H.2.2).

### 12.1.1 The PTX entry header [M]

```
.visible .entry _ZN13explicit_gemm35explicit_blackwell_fp16_gemm_kernelENS_18ExplicitGemmParamsE(
.param .align 128 .b8 ..._param_0[640]
.maxntid 256
.minnctapersm 1
.reg .pred %p<92>;
.reg .b16 %rs<7>;
.reg .b32 %r<1014>;
.reg .b64 %rd<29>;
```

Why each line is what it is:

| PTX line | Comes from | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `.param .align 128 .b8 [640]` | `const __grid_constant__ ExplicitGemmParams params` (explicit.cu:1096) | `sizeof(ExplicitGemmParams)` is 640 because `alignof(CUtensorMap)` is 128 in the CUDA 13.3 headers: four 128-byte maps (512) + 12 ints/floats (48) + two pointers (16) = 576, padded to the next multiple of 128 (explicit.hpp byte map; note G.3). |
| `.maxntid 256` / `.minnctapersm 1` | `__launch_bounds__(256, 1)` (explicit.cu:1095) | 256 threads = 8 warps (Chapter 11); 1 CTA per SM is forced anyway by 230400 B of dynamic shared memory. |
| `%p<92> %rs<7> %r<1014> %rd<29>` | virtual registers before allocation | The CUTLASS kernel's entry declares `%p<248> %rs<16> %r<1635> %rd<55>` (note D.2); the explicit kernel carries fewer live values (no C path, no scheduler bookkeeping). Of the seven `.b16` registers six are used and only three carry mask operands: `%rs3` (`mov.b16 %rs3, 15`, `kMainloopReleaseMask`, the `"h"` operand of W30), `%rs4` (`cvt.u16.u32` of `3 << 2y`, the accumulator commit mask, W30) and `%rs6` (`cvt.u16.u32` of `5 << x`, the A multicast mask, W21); `%rs2 = cvt.u16.u32 %cluster_ctarank`, `%rs1 = %rs2 & 1` (`rank & 1`: 1 on the peer, 0 on the pair leader) and `%rs5 = %rs1 & 255` are rank bookkeeping that the front end narrowed to 16 bits and re-tests with `setp.ne.b16` in the role tests (`trace_out_v2/ptx_explicit.txt` lines 34-35, 406-407, 419, 1104, 1112, 1384-1387, 1415, 1430, 1516) [M]. |

The only parameter reads the device performs are two: `ld.param.v2.b32 {%r5, %r6}, [..._param_0+528]` (alpha and beta) and `ld.param.b32 %r36, [..._param_0+520]` (k) [M]. The four tensor-map addresses are formed with `cvta.param` and passed to `prefetch.tensormap` and the TMA instructions; `m`, `n`, `l` are never read (note G.3). In SASS the parameter block begins at constant-bank offset `c[0x0][0x380]`, so k is read by `LDCU UR14, c[0x0][0x588]` (0x380 + 520 = 0x588) and alpha/beta by `LDCU.64 UR26, c[0x0][0x590]` (0x380 + 528 = 0x590) [M]; `c[0x0][0x348]` is read as a 64-bit value at four sites (`@!UP1 LDCU.64 UR4` at 0x00d0 and `LDCU.64 UR6` at 0x0130 for the prefetches, `LDCU.64 UR22` at 0x0c10 in the producer, `LDCU.64 UR30` at 0x1f50 in the epilogue) and offset by `+0x0`, `+0x80`, `+0x100`, `+0x180`, exactly the explicit.hpp byte offsets of the four maps (`+0x100`/`+0x180` feed the `UTMACCTL.PF` of C and D, `+0x80` is `tma_b` in the producer, `+0x180` is `tma_d` in the epilogue) [M]. Since the PTX forms those operands with `cvta.param`, I read the slot as the generic address of the parameter block, which note D.2 calls the "descriptor base" [H: the constant-bank layout itself is not documented in any source I used].

### 12.1.2 The resource line [M]

```
Function _ZN13explicit_gemm35explicit_blackwell_fp16_gemm_kernelENS_18ExplicitGemmParamsE:
  REG:26 STACK:0 SHARED:1024 LOCAL:0 CONSTANT[2]:12 CONSTANT[0]:1536 TEXTURE:0 SURFACE:0 SAMPLER:0
```

(`trace_out_v2/resources.txt`; the CUDA Binary Utilities manual states that `REG`, `TEXTURE`, `SURFACE`, `SAMPLER` are counts and the other fields are bytes.)

| Field | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `REG` | 26 | The SASS names 24 distinct vector registers, `R0..R23` (the epilogue's 16 `LDTM` destinations `R4..R19` plus four lane-dependent store bases `R20..R23` set the maximum), and ptxas reports 26, two more than the number named; the CUTLASS kernel names `R0..R65` (66) and reports 68 [M]. The reason for the +2 is not documented in the sources I used (unverified). `nvcc -Xptxas -v` (or `--resource-usage`) prints the same figure at compile time, the quicker check after a rebuild than `cuobjdump --dump-resource-usage`. Section 12.4. |
| `STACK` / `LOCAL` | 0 / 0 | No spills (`LDL`/`STL` count 0 [M]), no local arrays that survived (the `mask[8]` of W29 and `r[16]` of the epilogue are fully promoted to registers). |
| `SHARED` | 1024 | **Not** static `__shared__` of this kernel: it is the system-reserved kilobyte below the dynamic buffer, reported for every kernel in the binary; `cudaFuncGetAttributes` reports `sharedSizeBytes 0` (`TRACE_HOST kernel_sharedSizeBytes 0` in `trace_out_v2/host.txt`) and the device attribute `cudaDevAttrReservedSharedMemoryPerBlock` reports the same 1024 (`TRACE_HOST device_reserved_smem_per_block 1024`) [M] (note D.6 item 4, G.3). It is also why `smem_base` is `0x400 + (rank << 24)` and not 0 (Chapter 5). |
| `CONSTANT[0]` | 1536 | 0x380 + 640: the kernel's parameter block sits at `c[0x0][0x380]` in constant bank 0, so the bank holds 896 bytes of driver/launch data plus the 640-byte block (explicit.hpp header; note G.3). The CUTLASS kernel's is 2944 = 0x380 + 2048. |
| `CONSTANT[2]` | 12 | A three-entry jump table that ptxas built for the role dispatch (Section 12.2, row "role dispatch"); the CUTLASS kernel has none (it uses a compare-and-branch chain) [M]. |

### 12.1.3 Three decoding prerequisites: control words, truth-table immediates, byte selectors [S, H where marked]

The dictionary in Section 12.2 and the listings in Section 12.5 use three pieces of SASS literacy that no CUDA course teaches. Read them once here.

**Control words and scoreboards.** `cuobjdump` prints every instruction as a 128-bit encoding in two `/* 0x... */` comments, the first on the instruction's line and the second alone on the next line (`/*5410*/ UTCHMMA.2CTA ... ; /* 0x00ff1c0c0a0075ea */` followed by `/* 0x0009e20008200024 */` in `sass_explicit.txt`). Part of that encoding is **control information** that the compiler, not the hardware's dependency logic, fills in: a stall count (cycles to wait before the next instruction issues), a yield flag, a write-scoreboard index and a read-scoreboard index (which of six dependency barriers this instruction sets when its result is written, or when its operands have been read), and a wait mask (which barriers must be clear before this instruction may issue). The field list is documented by the reverse-engineering literature: for Maxwell by the maxas wiki ("Control Codes": "There are 6 barrier resources"; write barriers for "variable latency instructions"; read barriers so that a later instruction does not "overwrite the operand values" before they are read; a wait mask so that an instruction "waits on a previously set barrier"; one 64-bit control word per three instructions), and for Volta by Jia et al. (2018), where the control word moved into each 128-bit instruction. That `sm_100a` keeps the same scheme is my inference from the `SB0..SB5` names that appear in the listing [H]. Fixed-latency ALU instructions need only the stall count. **Variable-latency instructions** (`LDTM`, `LDS`, `LDCU`, `S2UR`, `SYNCS.*`, `UTMA*`, and the TC-pipe operations) set a scoreboard, and their consumers carry the matching wait bit: this is where `tcgen05.wait::ld` went (Section 12.2, row `tcgen05.wait::ld`). The one explicit form you will meet is `DEPBAR.LE SBn, k` ("Dependency Barrier" in the Blackwell instruction table of the CUDA Binary Utilities manual): block until scoreboard n has at most k outstanding operations. So `DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x1` is `cp.async.bulk.wait_group.read 1` (at most one bulk store group still reading shared memory), `DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x0` would be `wait_group.read 0` (absent here), and the two `DEPBAR.LE SB1, 0x36` at 0x4b20/0x4b80 inside the alloc sequence drain scoreboard 1 down to 54 before the TMEM allocator atomic, a compiler-inserted ordering inside the `tcgen05.alloc` lowering whose exact purpose is not documented [H].

**Truth-table immediates.** `LOP3.LUT d, a, b, c, LUT` computes, bit by bit, the three-input Boolean function whose truth table is the 8-bit immediate: bit `(a << 2) | (b << 1) | c` of `LUT` is the result for inputs `(a, b, c)`. This is the same convention as PTX `lop3.b32 d, a, b, c, immLut` (`immLut = F(0xF0, 0xCC, 0xAA)`), so `0xc0` = `a & b`, `0x3c` = `a ^ b`, `0x33` = `~b`, `0xf6` = `a | (b ^ c)`, `0xf8` = `a | (b & c)`, `0xf4` = `a | (b & ~c)` [S]. Worked examples from this kernel: `LOP3.LUT R9, R9, UR11, RZ, 0x3c, !PT` (0x52f0) is `cons_phase ^= flip`; `LOP3.LUT P2, RZ, R6, 0x1, RZ, 0xc0, !PT` (0x1ce0) writes the predicate `P2 = (R6 & 1) != 0` with the register result discarded into `RZ`; in the epilogue entry (0x1f30-0x2000) `R20 = l << 2`, `R0 = ((w << 11) | ((l & 7) << 2))`, `R21 = R20 & 0x60 = ((l >> 3) & 3) << 5`, and the four store bases are `LOP3.LUT R23, R0, 0x60, R20, 0xf8` = `R0 | R21`, `LOP3.LUT R22, R0, 0x20, R21, 0xf6` = `R0 | (0x20 ^ R21)`, `LOP3.LUT R21, R0, 0x40, R21, 0xf6` = `R0 | (0x40 ^ R21)`, `LOP3.LUT R20, R0, 0x60, R20, 0xf4` = `R0 | (0x60 ^ R21)`: the `Swizzle<2,5,2>` XOR of the column class `c = 0..3` into bits 5-6 of the lane term (Chapter 10), one `LOP3` per class [M for the listing, S for the decode]. `PLOP3.LUT` and `UPLOP3.LUT` are the same idea on predicates: with three constant-true inputs the index is 7, so LUT `0x80` (bit 7 set) writes **true** and LUT `0x40` (bit 6 set) writes **false**; `PLOP3.LUT P2, PT, PT, PT, UP2, 0x80, 0x8` copies the uniform predicate `UP2` into the vector predicate `P2` (inputs `11x` select bit 7 or bit 6 of `0x80`). The trailing second immediate (`0x8` with `0x80`, `0x4` with `0x40`) is a further encoding field that I have not decoded (unverified). This is what the annotations `P0 = true`, `P2 = UP2`, `UP0 = false` / `UP0 = true` in Section 12.5.1 mean.

**Byte selectors.** `PRMT d, a, sel, b` (and `UPRMT`) assembles each of the four result bytes from the eight bytes of the pair `{b, a}`: "The bytes in the two source registers are numbered from 0 to 7: {b, a} = {{b7, b6, b5, b4}, {b3, b2, b1, b0}}" and "the 3 lsbs of the selection value specify which of the 8 source bytes should be moved into the target position" (PTX ISA, `prmt`), nibble k of the selector (least significant first) naming the source of result byte k. That the SASS operand order is `a, sel, b` is my reading of the listing [H], but it is the only reading under which the three uses make sense: `PRMT R4, RZ, 0x654, R4` = `{R4.b0, R4.b1, R4.b2, RZ.b0}`, the shared::cta address with byte 3 replaced by 0 = `mapa(addr, 0)`; `UPRMT UR6, UR9, 0x654, UR8` = the address in `UR8` with byte 3 = `UR9` = the target rank; `UPRMT UR34, URZ, 0x5410, UR25` = `{0, 0, UR25.b0, UR25.b1}`, the 16-bit multicast mask moved into bits [16, 32) of the `UTMALDG` mask operand.

---

## 12.2 The PTX-to-SASS dictionary

The table covers every instruction family the kernel emits. "Sites" are counts in the explicit kernel's SASS (my recount of `trace_out_v2/sass_explicit.txt`, which agrees with note G.3); the CUTLASS kernel's counts, where different, are in note D.2. "Uniform" means a uniform-datapath instruction (Section 12.3): `U*` mnemonic, `UR`/`UP` operands, issued once per warp.

| PTX (wrapper, explicit.cu line) | SASS in the explicit kernel (sites) | What the lowering teaches |
|---|---|---|
| `tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2.kind::f16 [tmem], descA, descB, idesc, {8 masks}, p` (W29, :517) | `UTCHMMA.2CTA gdesc[UR10], gdesc[UR12], tmem[UR36], tmem[UR28], idesc[UR29], UP0` (4: 0x5410, 0x5440, 0x5460, 0x5470) | Uniform, unpredicated: the `elect.sync` around it is folded away. The 64-bit descriptors are UR pairs whose high words are `UMOV URn, 0x40004040` (8 per k-tile). The scale-c predicate `p` becomes the uniform predicate `UP0` on the first MMA and the constant-true `UPT` on the other three (`scale_c = 1u` after k-block 0 is a compile-time fact for kb 1..3). The eight zero mask registers do not appear. `UR28` is held at 0 by `UMOV UR28, 0x0`; which of the PTX operands it carries I cannot verify. |
| `tcgen05.commit.cta_group::2.mbarrier::arrive::one.shared::cluster.multicast::cluster.b64 [bar], mask` (W30, :532) | `UTCBAR.2CTA.MULTICAST [UR32], URZ, UR37` (2: 0x5480 with `UR37 = 0xf`; the accumulator commit with `UR33 = 0x3 << 2y`, note G.3) | Uniform; the commit is a TC-pipe barrier instruction, not a memory op. The mainloop commit is the instruction after the fourth `UTCHMMA`. The compile-time mask 0xF becomes `UMOV UR37, 0xf` inside the loop; the run-time pair mask stays in a UR computed once. |
| `tcgen05.alloc.cta_group::2.sync.aligned.shared::cta.b32 [smem+384], 512` (W26, :498) | `UTCATOMSWS.2CTA.FIND_AND_SET.ALIGN UP0, UR6, UR6` with `UR6 = 0x10` (2 copies: 0x4b30 and the retry 0x4b90 after `NANOSLEEP 0x64`) inside a 69-instruction sequence 0x4a90-0x4ed0 [M] | One allocation unit = 32 TMEM columns, so 512 columns = `0x10` units. The "whole warp, both CTAs" PTX op is executed as: the **leader's** elected lane does the atomic, stores the result (`STS [UR7+0x180], R6` with `R6 = R2 << 5`, i.e. units -> columns), forwards it to the peer with `STAS [R4.64], R2` (st.async) which completes a barrier in the peer's reserved shared memory at `(rank << 24) + 0x48`, keeps bookkeeping words at `+0x50/+0x54/+0x58` with `ATOMS.OR/XOR`; the peer's elected lane waits (`SYNCS...TRYWAIT [UR4+0x8]`), rescales and acknowledges; `WARPSYNC.ALL` twice; then `BAR.ARV 0x6, 0xa0`. The reserved kilobyte (`SHARED:1024`) is where this handshake lives. The sequence is instruction-identical to the CUTLASS kernel's (note G.3). |
| `tcgen05.dealloc.cta_group::2.sync.aligned.b32 T, 512` (W27, :504) | `UTCATOMSWS.AND URZ, UR4` (1: 0x5ae0) + `ATOMS.AND` clears of the reserved words + two ptxas-inserted consistency checks whose failure paths `CALL` stubs containing `BPT.TRAP 0x1` (0x6530, 0x6560) | Both CTAs execute it. `UR4 = ~(0xffff << (T >> 5))` clears the 16 unit bits of the allocation. The PTX has no `trap`; the two `BPT.TRAP` are ptxas's own sanity checks on the reserved words [M]. |
| `tcgen05.relinquish_alloc_permit.cta_group::2.sync.aligned` (W28, :512) | no `UTC*` mnemonic; `UVIRTCOUNT.DEALLOC.SMPOOL 0x80` (0x55f0) and an `ELECT`-guarded `STS.U8 [UR6+0x1c], R2` (0x5630) bracket `PREEXIT` | Attribution inferred (note D.2): these are the only otherwise unexplained instructions at the PTX position. ptxas emitted it **before** `PREEXIT`, the reverse of the PTX order (`griddep_launch_dependents()` at :950 precedes `tmem_relinquish_2sm()` at :951). |
| `tcgen05.ld.sync.aligned.32x32b.x16.b32 {16 regs}, [addr]` (W31, :543) | `LDTM.x16 R4, tmem[UR29+0x10*e]` (8: 0x2290, 0x2760, 0x2c40, 0x3120, 0x3600, 0x3ae0, 0x3fc0, 0x44d0) | The TMEM address `T + ((32w) << 16) + 128 st` is warp-uniform (`UR29`, built by `ULEA UR17, UR16, UR17, 0x15` = `w << 21` plus the base); the subtile term `16e` is folded into the immediate `0x10*e`. Sixteen vector destination registers `R4..R19` per lane. |
| `tcgen05.wait::ld.sync.aligned` (W32, :558) | **no instruction** | The asynchronous register writes of `LDTM` are tracked by scoreboards in the control words: the first `FMUL R4` after an `LDTM` waits on the scoreboard the `LDTM` set, the next `LDTM` waits on the `STS` read scoreboard (WAR), and the subtile-7 `SYNCS.ARRIVE` at 0x44f0 waits on the eighth `LDTM` (0x44d0). The absence of a wait opcode is measured; the scoreboard decode is inferred (note D.2, G.3; Section 12.1.3). Why the PTX still needs exactly one `wait::ld`, before the release: the ISA (9.7.18.6.4.5, "Register dependencies, same thread") guarantees that "an intra-thread ordering through true register dependency will be respected regardless of the presence or absence of other forms of synchronization", so the `FMUL`s of every subtile are legal without any wait; but that dependency "does not imply any other form of ordering", and "to enforce such memory orderings and avoiding anti-dependency hazards around tcgen05.ld, tcgen05.wait::ld must be used". The `mbarrier.arrive` that releases the accumulator stage (explicit.cu:1039) is not a register consumer, so without the `wait::ld` at explicit.cu:1038 the release could precede the completion of the eighth load. |

| `cp.async.bulk.tensor.3d.cta_group::2.shared::cluster.global.mbarrier::complete_tx::bytes.L2::cache_hint` (W22, :463) | `UTMALDG.3D.2CTA [UR8], [UR30], desc[UR32]` (2: 0x1000, 0x12e0) | Same form without the mask operand; `UR8 = base + 0x28400 + (s << 13)`, `UR9..UR12` = `{UR17, UR18, b_col, UR20}` copied by `UMOV UR9, UR17; UMOV UR10, UR18; UMOV UR12, UR20` [M for the copies, H for the block reading]. Four rows deserve the long form.

### 12.2.1 `UTCHMMA` and its operands [M]

```
        /*5410*/                   UTCHMMA.2CTA gdesc[UR10], gdesc[UR12], tmem[UR36], tmem[UR28], idesc[UR29], UP0 ;
        /*5440*/                   UTCHMMA.2CTA gdesc[UR16], gdesc[UR18], tmem[UR36], tmem[UR28], idesc[UR29], UPT ;
        /*5460*/                   UTCHMMA.2CTA gdesc[UR20], gdesc[UR22], tmem[UR36], tmem[UR28], idesc[UR29], UPT ;
        /*5470*/                   UTCHMMA.2CTA gdesc[UR24], gdesc[UR26], tmem[UR36], tmem[UR28], idesc[UR29], UPT ;
        /*5480*/                   UTCBAR.2CTA.MULTICAST [UR32], URZ, UR37 ;
```

Compare with the PTX source of the wrapper (explicit.cu:517-529):

```
__device__ __forceinline__ void umma_f16_2sm(uint32_t tmem_c, uint64_t desc_a, uint64_t desc_b, uint32_t idesc, uint32_t scaleC) {
  uint32_t mask[8] = {0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0};
  asm volatile(
    "{\n\t"
    ".reg .pred p;\n\t"
    "setp.ne.b32 p, %4, 0;\n\t"
    "tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2.kind::f16 [%0], %1, %2, %3, {%5, %6, %7, %8, %9, %10, %11, %12}, p; \n\t"
    "}\n"
    :
    : "r"(tmem_c), "l"(desc_a), "l"(desc_b), "r"(idesc), "r"(scaleC),
      "r"(mask[0]), "r"(mask[1]), "r"(mask[2]), "r"(mask[3]),
      "r"(mask[4]), "r"(mask[5]), "r"(mask[6]), "r"(mask[7]));
}
```

- `gdesc[UR10]` is the 64-bit A descriptor in `{UR10, UR11}`: `UR10 = ULEA UR8, UR30, 0xa` (= `desc_lo_a + 1024 s`, the `+16384 B per stage` in 16-byte units of explicit.cu:928), `UR11 = 0x40004040` (`kSmemDescHi`). The three later k-blocks use `UR16/18/20/22/24/26 = UR10/12 + 0x2/0x4/0x6` (`+ 2 kb`, explicit.cu:933-934) with their own `0x40004040` high words `UR17/19/21/23/25/27`: that is why eight `UMOV URn, 0x40004040` appear per k-tile.
- `tmem[UR36]` = `tmem_c = T + 128 st` (explicit.cu:919), computed once per tile.
- `idesc[UR29]` = `0x10200010` (`kInstrDesc`), re-materialised per k-tile by `UMOV UR29, 0x10200010`.
- `UP0` / `UPT`: the `setp.ne.b32 p, scaleC, 0` of the wrapper. In the loop `scale_c` is 0 only for `kb = 0` of the first k-tile of a tile (explicit.cu:917, :940), so ptxas keeps a uniform predicate `UP0`: it is cleared (set false) once per tile by `UPLOP3.LUT UP0, UPT, UPT, UPT, UPT, 0x40, 0x4` at 0x51c0, before the k-tile loop, and set true by `UPLOP3.LUT UP0, UPT, UPT, UPT, UPT, 0x80, 0x8` at 0x54b0 after the first k-tile's four MMAs have issued, so every later k-tile's first `UTCHMMA` runs with `scale_c = 1` (LUT decode in Section 12.1.3; entry sequence and loop listing in Section 12.5.1); the other three MMAs are hard-wired to `UPT`. The CUTLASS kernel shows the same two-site pattern on `UP2` at 0x3860 / 0x3a90 (note D.2).
- The `if (elect_one_sync())` around the call (explicit.cu:932) is gone. The whole warp reaches the instruction; the hardware executes it once (Section 12.3).

### 12.2.2 The barrier wait, inline and out of line [M]

The wrapper (explicit.cu:297-311) is a `bra` loop:

```
__device__ __forceinline__ void mbar_wait(uint32_t smem_addr, uint32_t phase) {
  uint32_t ticks = kWaitTicks;
  asm volatile(
    "{\n\t"
    ".reg .pred       P1; \n\t"
    "LAB_WAIT: \n\t"
    "mbarrier.try_wait.parity.shared::cta.b64 P1, [%0], %1, %2; \n\t"
    "@P1 bra DONE; \n\t"
    "bra     LAB_WAIT; \n\t"
    "DONE: \n\t"
    "}"
    :
    : "r"(smem_addr), "r"(phase), "r"(ticks)
    : "memory");
}
```

ptxas emits the first attempt inline and moves the loop out of the hot path. In the MMA loop:

```
        /*51f0*/               @P0 BRA 0x5240 ;                                   <- peek succeeded: skip the wait
        /*5200*/                   ULEA UR4, UR8, UR7, 0x3 ;                       <- full[s] = smem_base + 8 s
        /*5210*/                   SHF.L.U32 R2, R9, 0x1f, RZ ;                    <- parity -> bit 31
        /*5220*/                   SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT P0, [UR4], R2 ;
        /*5230*/              @!P0 BRA 0x6350 ;                                    <- not yet: go to the out-of-line retry loop
```

and the out-of-line shape (this copy is the producer tail's last wait, which ends in `EXIT`):

```
        /*1950*/                   SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT P0, [R3+URZ], R0 ;
        /*1960*/              @!P0 NANOSLEEP.SYNCS 0x989680 ;
        /*1970*/              @!P0 SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64 P0, [R3+URZ], R0 ;
        /*1980*/               @P0 EXIT ;
        /*1990*/                   BRA 0x1940 ;
```

Lessons: (1) the parity operand is a 32-bit register whose bit 31 is the parity, so `phase ^= 1` in C++ costs a `LOP3 ... 0x3c` (XOR) plus the `SHF`; (2) the `NANOSLEEP.SYNCS 0x989680` carries the 10 ms `timeHint`: the ISA says the suspended thread "resumes execution when the specified phase completes OR before the phase completes following a system-dependent time limit" and that the operand "specifies the time limit, in nanoseconds, that may be used for the time limit instead of the system-dependent limit" (PTX ISA, `mbarrier.try_wait`), so it is an upper bound on the suspension that the barrier completion cuts short, not a sleep; (3) the kernel has 30 such retry loops, one `NANOSLEEP.SYNCS` each: 26 placed out of line after the role code (0x5be0-0x64f0, past warp 0's `EXIT` at 0x5bc0) and 4 kept inline because they end a role's exit path (0x1960 producer tail, 0x1ea0 scheduler tail, 0x5860 and 0x58a0 warp-0 tails), matching note G.3's "26 out-of-line + 4 inline loops against 47 + 5" for the CUTLASS kernel; 30 + the alloc retry's `NANOSLEEP 0x64` = 31 `NANOSLEEP`, and 30 + the 2 `test_wait` = 32 `SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64` without `.TRYWAIT`; the counts are ptxas's and not part of the contract (note D.7).

### 12.2.3 The epilogue element: `LDTM`, `FMUL`, `FFMA`, `STS` [M]

```
        /*2290*/                   LDTM.x16 R4, tmem[UR29] ;
        /*22a0*/                   UISETP.NE.U32.AND UP1, UPT, UR16, URZ, UPT ;
        /*22b0*/                   FMUL R4, R4, UR26 ;
        /*22c0*/                   FMUL R5, R5, UR26 ;
        ...
        /*2300*/                   FFMA R4, RZ, UR27, R4 ;
        ...
        /*23a0*/                   STS [R23+UR7+0x200], R4 ;
        ...
        /*23e0*/                   STS [R22+UR7+0x280], R5 ;
        ...
        /*2420*/                   STS [R21+UR7+0x300], R6 ;
        ...
        /*2460*/                   STS [R20+UR7+0x380], R7 ;
        ...
        /*24a0*/                   STS [R23+UR7+0x400], R8 ;
```

From the source (explicit.cu:1043-1048):

```
      #pragma unroll
      for (int j = 0; j < 16; ++j) {
        float const t = alpha * __uint_as_float(r[j]);
        float const d = fmaf(beta, 0.0f, t);
        *reinterpret_cast<uint32_t*>(smem + st_off[j & 3] + 512u * uint32_t(j >> 2) + kEpiStageBytes * uint32_t(e & 3)) = __float_as_uint(d);   // 16 scalar st.shared.b32 (B.3.3 step 17)
      }
```

Read the `STS` immediates against the formula: `st_off[c]` contributes `OFF_SMEM_CD (0x200) + 128 c (0x80 c)` plus the lane term that lives in `R20..R23`; `512 (j >> 2)` is `0x200 (j >> 2)`; `8192 (e & 3)` is `0x2000 (e & 3)`. For `j = 0..4`: `0x200, 0x280, 0x300, 0x380, 0x400` with base registers `R23, R22, R21, R20, R23`: exactly `0x200 + 0x80 (j & 3) + 0x200 (j >> 2)`. The scheduling interleaves `FMUL`, `FFMA` and `STS` so that each `STS` is issued as soon as its value is final, and the first `FMUL R4` is the instruction that waits (through the scoreboard) for the asynchronous `LDTM`.

### 12.2.4 The CLC query line [M]

```
        /*1b70*/              @!P0 SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED RZ, [R11+URZ], R5 ;     <- lanes 0..3: arm CTA (lane)'s clc_full[idx] with R5 = 0x10 bytes
        ...
        /*1bc0*/                   UGETNEXTWORKID.BROADCAST [UR8], [UR9] ;         <- the try_cancel: response slot UR8, barrier UR9
        ...
        /*1c60*/                   LDS.128 R4, [R4+0x160] ;                        <- the 16-byte response (OFF_CLC_RESPONSE = 352 = 0x160)
        /*1c90*/                   MEMBAR.ALL.CTA ;

        /*1cc0*/                   SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED.A1T0 RZ, [R2+URZ], RZ ; <- consumer release on CTA 0's clc_empty[idx] (R2 = PRMT(.., RZ, 0x654, ..))
        /*1ce0*/                   LOP3.LUT P2, RZ, R6, 0x1, RZ, 0xc0, !PT ;        <- valid = bit 0 of response word 2
```

This is Chapter 7's scheduler loop in five machine instructions plus bookkeeping; the whole loop is 50 instructions (Section 12.5.3).
