## 12.3 The uniform datapath, or why the elections disappeared

### 12.3.1 What `UR`, `UP`, `URZ`, `UPT` are

Since Turing every SM sub-partition has, next to the 32-lane vector datapath, a scalar **uniform datapath**: "this scalar unit executes instructions where all threads use the same input and generate the same output" (Nsight Compute Profiling Guide, pipeline descriptions). Its state is a separate file of **uniform registers** `URn` (one 32-bit value per warp, not per lane) and **uniform predicates** `UPn`; `URZ` is the uniform zero register and `UPT` the constant-true uniform predicate, mirrors of `RZ` and `PT`. Instructions whose mnemonic starts with `U` (`UMOV`, `UIADD3`, `ULEA`, `USHF`, `ULOP3`, `UISETP`, `USEL`, `UPRMT`, `UPLOP3`, `LDCU`, `S2UR`, `R2UR`, `BRA.U`, `BRXU`) read and write that file. There is no PTX-level control over it: ptxas decides, by proving that a value is identical across the warp, whether it lives in `UR` or `R`.

Why this matters for a GEMM kernel: the operands of a TMA load (destination address, barrier, coordinates, mask), of a `tcgen05.mma` (descriptors, TMEM address, instruction descriptor) and of a `tcgen05.commit` (barrier address, mask) are warp-uniform by construction: they depend on the cluster rank, the tile coordinates, the stage index and compile-time constants, never on the lane. ptxas therefore keeps them in `UR`s and issues the instruction itself as a **single warp-level operation**: `UTMALDG`, `UTMASTG`, `UTCHMMA`, `UTCBAR`, `UGETNEXTWORKID`, `UTMACCTL` are all uniform-datapath instructions. "Issued once per warp regardless of how many lanes reach it" (note D.2) is the operational definition: whether 1 or 32 lanes are active, the issue cost is one slot and the hardware performs one operation.

### 12.3.2 Why `elect.sync` vanished from the loops [M]

The PTX contract of CUTLASS (and of explicit.cu, Chapters 8-9) is "one elected lane issues the TMA/MMA/commit/query": `if (elect_one_sync()) { ... }` around W21/W22 (explicit.cu:740), W29 (:932), W30 (:942, :944) and W33 (:843). The PTX has 14 `elect.sync` sites. The SASS has 4 `ELECT` instructions, all outside the role loops (prologue 0x0020, alloc/handshake 0x4a90 and 0x4d60, relinquish 0x55d0). Inside the producer, MMA and scheduler loops there is **none**: the uniform instruction executes once per warp anyway, so predicating it on one lane changes nothing, and ptxas removes the election (note D.6 item 6).

The election survives only where the issue genuinely is per-lane or where a vector side effect depends on it: the prologue's `lane_pred` (it predicates `UTMACCTL.PF` through `VOTEU.ALL UP1, P1`, a vector-to-uniform predicate conversion), the alloc atomics (one lane performs the `STS`/`STAS`/`ATOMS` handshake) and the `STS.U8` of the relinquish lowering.

`elect.sync` is deterministic ("the same leader thread is elected for the same membermask every time", PTX ISA), which is why "leader lane" is a stable identity across the producer's `expect_tx` predicate and its TMA issue (Chapter 8).

The lesson is **not** "drop the `elect.sync`". The PTX ISA gives `tcgen05.mma` "single thread semantics, unlike the collective instructions mma.sync or wgmma.mma_async. So, a single thread issuing the tcgen05.mma will result in the initiation of the whole matrix multiply and accumulate operation": it does not forbid more issuing threads, it means every issuing thread starts a whole MMA, which is why an election (or, as here, a uniform instruction executed once per warp) is needed to avoid issuing it 32 times. CUTLASS's contract is the election; the SASS shows that keeping it costs nothing. The lesson is the converse: **an issue instruction whose operands are not provably uniform will not become a `U*` instruction**, and then the election matters, lane-dependent address arithmetic appears in vector registers, and `R2UR` moves (vector to uniform) are needed before the instruction. The explicit kernel has 13 `R2UR` against the CUTLASS kernel's 150, and 0 `MOV.SPILL`/`R2UR.FILL` against 44 + 44 (note G.3): the uniform file, not the vector file, was the CUTLASS kernel's tight resource (note D.7, inferred).

### 12.3.3 What this implies for how you write issue code [H, grounded in the measurements above]

1. Compute every TMA/MMA/barrier operand from warp-uniform sources only: `%cluster_ctarank`/`%cluster_ctaid`, `blockIdx`, the pipeline `{index, phase}` state, loop counters, compile-time constants, and values read from shared memory by every lane (e.g. `T` at `smem + 384`). Never from `threadIdx.x & 31` or lane-dependent loads.
2. Keep the `elect.sync` as the PTX-level contract; expect it to be free.
3. Keep the number of loop-invariant uniform values small (descriptor bases, barrier bases, masks, map addresses). The explicit kernel's three extra `UMOV` and one extra `ULEA` per k-tile (47 vs 44 in the MMA loop) and five re-materialised invariants per k-tile in the producer (37 vs 31) are ptxas choosing to recompute rather than hold a `UR` (note G.3); harmless here (Section 12.5), but the mechanism is worth knowing.
4. Lane-dependent work belongs to the vector lanes: the epilogue's `STS` bases (`R20..R23`), the per-lane `expect_tx` predicate, the CLC arming by lanes 0..3. ptxas separates the two datapaths cleanly if the code does.
5. A warp-uniform branch becomes `BRA.U UPn` (the loop back-edges at 0x12f0 and 0x54d0 are `BRA.U UP0`/`BRA.U UP1`): the uniform predicate makes the branch provably non-divergent [H: interpretation of the `.U` suffix].

---

## 12.4 Registers: 26 versus 68

### 12.4.1 Where 26 comes from [M]

| Register range | Holds | Why it is needed |
|---|---|---|
| low registers, per role | per-lane pipeline state and scratch, re-used by every role: the MMA warp keeps `cons_phase` in `R9` (`LOP3.LUT R9, R9, UR11, RZ, 0x3c` at 0x52f0) and the shifted parity in `R2` (`SHF.L.U32 R2, R9, 0x1f`), and touches only `R0, R2, R4, R9` in its loop; the producer keeps `prod_phase` in `R0` (`LOP3.LUT R0, R0, UR8, ...` at 0x1190) and uses `R4`, `R5`; the scheduler loop uses `R0` and `R2..R12` (response words `R4..R7`, arming address `R11`, barrier base `R12`); the epilogue uses `R0`, `R2`, `R3`, `R8` and `R9` (its `acc_full` parity: `TRYWAIT P0, [UR24+0xf0], R9` at 0x2180) besides the two ranges below [M] | the phase bits are vector values because the wrappers take them as `"r"` operands; since every role re-uses the low registers, the kernel's maximum is set by the epilogue's live set alone |
| `R4..R19` | the 16 `LDTM.x16` destinations = 16 fp32 accumulator values of one lane for one subtile; also the `FMUL`/`FFMA` results in place | `tcgen05.ld.32x32b.x16` writes 16 registers per lane (W31) |
| `R20..R23` | the four lane-dependent `STS` bases `st_off[c]` (explicit.cu:1011-1014): `R23` for `j & 3 = 0`, `R22` for 1, `R21` for 2, `R20` for 3 | the `Swizzle<2,5,2>` term depends on `l & 7` and `(l >> 3) & 3` (Chapter 10) |
| `R1` | the stack pointer (`LDC R1, c[0x0][0x37c]` at 0x0000) | ABI, unused (STACK 0) |

Everything else (barrier addresses, descriptors, coordinates, alpha, beta, `k_tiles`, pipeline states) lives in uniform registers. The CUTLASS kernel's highest register is `R65`: it additionally carries the zero-filled C fragment (`R21..R36`, 16 registers, the `beta != 0` path's operand that is dead for beta = 0 but still allocated), the `epi_load` pipeline state, the per-tile CLC decode in vector registers for the scheduler bookkeeping, and the 44 `MOV.SPILL`/`R2UR.FILL` uniform-to-vector moves (40 of them in the never-executed C-load path) (note D.2, G.3).

### 12.4.2 Why it does not matter here, and when it would [S, H]

- Occupancy is fixed at **1 CTA per SM** by shared memory: 230400 B of dynamic smem out of 232448 B opt-in (util.hpp `static_assert`), and `__launch_bounds__(256, 1)` says so explicitly. 256 threads x 68 registers = 17408 of the SM's 65536 32-bit registers; even 255 x 256 = 65280 would fit. Register count cannot change occupancy, and it did not change the issue rate (Section 12.5). (Registers are allocated per warp in fixed-size granules, the "register allocation unit size" of the CUDA occupancy calculator, so a difference of a few registers changes nothing until a granule boundary is crossed; the granule for CC 10.0 is not verified here.)
- It would matter in three situations: (a) a kernel designed for 2 or more CTAs per SM (smaller smem footprint), where 256 threads x >128 registers would halve occupancy; (b) a register-hungry epilogue (e.g. `tcgen05.ld.32x32b.x32` = 32 registers per load, plus conversion temporaries and multiple subtiles in flight) where ptxas would start spilling, and a spill (`STL`/`LDL`) inside the per-subtile loop would be on the epilogue's critical path; (c) Hopper-style `setmaxnreg` register reallocation between producer and consumer warps, which this kernel does not use because 1 CTA/SM with 8 warps leaves the register file three-quarters empty anyway.
- The number to watch is therefore not `REG` but `LOCAL` and `STACK` (both 0) and the absence of `LDL`/`STL` in the hot loops; `check_sass.py` makes `LDL`/`STL` = 0 and `LOCAL` = 0 hard rows and `REG <= 68` only a soft row for exactly this reason.

---

## 12.5 The four hot loops

All addresses and counts in this section are my recount of `trace_out_v2/sass_explicit.txt`; they agree with note G.3 except where stated.

### 12.5.1 MMA warp: 47 instructions per k-tile (0x51f0-0x54d0) [M]

How warp 0 reaches the loop, once per tile (0x5180-0x51e0, verbatim; comments mine):

```
/*5180*/                   SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT P2, [UR35+0x110], R2 ;   acc_empty[st] blocking wait (UR35 = base + 8 st, +0x110 = OFF_ACC_EMPTY)
/*5190*/              @!P2 BRA 0x62f0 ;                                             out-of-line retry loop
/*51a0*/                   BRA.U !UP0, 0x54e0 ;                                     UP0 = is_leader here: the non-leader CTA skips the whole MMA section
/*51b0*/                   ULEA UR36, UR5, UR15, 0x7 ;                              tmem_c = T + 128 st   (UR5 = st, UR15 = T)
/*51c0*/                   UPLOP3.LUT UP0, UPT, UPT, UPT, UPT, 0x40, 0x4 ;          UP0 = false: scale_c = 0 for the first MMA of the tile
/*51d0*/                   UMOV UR6, UR14 ;                                         k = k_tiles
/*51e0*/                   UMOV UR8, UR4 ;                                          s = cons_idx
```

Three things to read here. `UP0` is overloaded: at 0x51a0 it still holds `is_leader`, and the non-leader CTA's warp 0 jumps over the four MMAs and the commit to 0x54e0, executing per tile only the CLC consume and the accumulator state advance (Chapter 9); from 0x51c0 on `UP0` is the scale-c predicate, cleared once per tile here and set at 0x54b0 inside the loop (Section 12.2.1). `UR36` (`tmem_c`), the loop counter `UR6 = k_tiles` (`UR14`, loaded once from `c[0x0][0x588]`) and the stage `UR8` are formed once per tile, which is why the loop body below contains none of them. The `acc_empty[st]` wait is on the leader's own barrier (`UR35 = ULEA(st, base, 3)` at 0x5120, unmasked), the one all 256 epilogue threads arrive on (Chapter 4); after the loop, 0x54e0 forms `acc_full[st]` from the same register (`UIADD3 UR6, UR35, 0xf0`) for the accumulator commit.

The loop body, complete and in order, grouped by purpose (the SASS is verbatim; the right-hand comments are mine):

```
--- blocking wait on full[s], skipped when the peek succeeded (4 instructions, off the fast path) ---
/*51f0*/               @P0 BRA 0x5240 ;
/*5200*/                   ULEA UR4, UR8, UR7, 0x3 ;              full[s] = base + 8 s
/*5210*/                   SHF.L.U32 R2, R9, 0x1f, RZ ;           parity -> bit 31
/*5220*/                   SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT P0, [UR4], R2 ;
/*5230*/              @!P0 BRA 0x6350 ;                           out-of-line retry loop
--- pipeline state: rs = s; advance {s, phase}; decide whether to peek (k > 0) ---
/*5240*/                   UISETP.NE.U32.AND UP2, UPT, UR6, 0x1, UPT ;   UP2 = (k != 1): peek the next stage
/*5250*/                   PLOP3.LUT P0, PT, PT, PT, PT, 0x80, 0x8 ;      P0 = true (tok = 1 when no peek)
/*5260*/                   UIADD3 UR4, UPT, UPT, UR8, 0x1, URZ ;          s + 1
/*5270*/                   ULEA UR10, UR8, UR30, 0xa ;                    lo_a = desc_lo_a + 1024 s
/*5280*/                   UISETP.NE.U32.AND UP1, UPT, UR4, 0x8, UPT ;    wrap test (s + 1 == 8)
/*5290*/                   PLOP3.LUT P2, PT, PT, PT, UP2, 0x80, 0x8 ;     P2 = UP2 as a vector predicate
/*52a0*/                   ULEA UR12, UR8, UR31, 0x9 ;                    lo_b = desc_lo_b + 512 s
/*52b0*/                   USEL UR11, URZ, 0x1, UP1 ;                     phase flip bit
/*52c0*/                   USEL UR4, UR4, URZ, UP1 ;                      s = wrap ? 0 : s + 1
/*52d0*/                   ULEA UR32, UR8, UR7, 0x3 ;                     (base + 8 rs) -> empty[rs] after + 0x40
/*52e0*/               @UP2 ULEA UR8, UR4, UR7, 0x3 ;                     full[s + 1] address for the peek
/*52f0*/                   LOP3.LUT R9, R9, UR11, RZ, 0x3c, !PT ;         cons_phase ^= flip
--- descriptor low words for k-blocks 1..3 (+2, +4, +6 = +32, +64, +96 bytes) ---
/*5300*/                   UIADD3 UR16, UPT, UPT, UR10, 0x2, URZ ;
/*5310*/                   UIADD3 UR18, UPT, UPT, UR12, 0x2, URZ ;
/*5320*/               @P2 SHF.L.U32 R2, R9, 0x1f, RZ ;                   peek parity
/*5330*/                   UIADD3 UR20, UPT, UPT, UR10, 0x4, URZ ;
/*5340*/                   UIADD3 UR22, UPT, UPT, UR12, 0x4, URZ ;
/*5350*/               @P2 SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT P0, [UR8], R2 ; the peek of the next stage (predicated off on the last k-tile)
/*5360*/                   UIADD3 UR24, UPT, UPT, UR10, 0x6, URZ ;
/*5370*/                   UIADD3 UR26, UPT, UPT, UR12, 0x6, URZ ;
/*5380*/                   UIADD3 UR32, UPT, UPT, UR32, 0x40, URZ ;        empty[rs] = base + 64 + 8 rs
--- constants the PTX materialises per k-block (mov.b32 idiom) ---
/*5390*/                   UMOV UR28, 0x0 ;
/*53a0*/                   UMOV UR29, 0x10200010 ;                        idesc
/*53b0*/                   UMOV UR11, 0x40004040 ;                        descriptor high words x 8
/*53c0*/                   UMOV UR13, 0x40004040 ;
/*53d0*/                   UMOV UR17, 0x40004040 ;
/*53e0*/                   UMOV UR19, 0x40004040 ;
/*53f0*/                   UMOV UR21, 0x40004040 ;
/*5400*/                   UMOV UR23, 0x40004040 ;
--- the four MMAs and the release ---
/*5410*/                   UTCHMMA.2CTA gdesc[UR10], gdesc[UR12], tmem[UR36], tmem[UR28], idesc[UR29], UP0 ;
/*5420*/                   UMOV UR25, 0x40004040 ;
/*5430*/                   UMOV UR27, 0x40004040 ;
/*5440*/                   UTCHMMA.2CTA gdesc[UR16], gdesc[UR18], tmem[UR36], tmem[UR28], idesc[UR29], UPT ;
/*5450*/                   UMOV UR37, 0xf ;                               kMainloopReleaseMask
/*5460*/                   UTCHMMA.2CTA gdesc[UR20], gdesc[UR22], tmem[UR36], tmem[UR28], idesc[UR29], UPT ;
/*5470*/                   UTCHMMA.2CTA gdesc[UR24], gdesc[UR26], tmem[UR36], tmem[UR28], idesc[UR29], UPT ;
/*5480*/                   UTCBAR.2CTA.MULTICAST [UR32], URZ, UR37 ;      tcgen05.commit -> empty[rs] of all four CTAs
--- loop counter, scale-c, back-edge ---
/*5490*/                   UISETP.GT.U32.AND UP1, UPT, UR6, 0x1, UPT ;    k > 1 ?
/*54a0*/                   UIADD3 UR6, UPT, UPT, UR6, -0x1, URZ ;         --k
/*54b0*/                   UPLOP3.LUT UP0, UPT, UPT, UPT, UPT, 0x80, 0x8 ; UP0 = true: scale_c = 1 from now on
/*54c0*/                   UMOV UR8, UR4 ;                                cons_idx = s
/*54d0*/                   BRA.U UP1, 0x51f0 ;
```

Composition: 12 `UMOV`, 9 `UIADD3`, 5 `ULEA`, 4 `UTCHMMA`, 2 `TRYWAIT`, 2 `SHF`, 2 `UISETP.NE`, 2 `PLOP3`, 2 `USEL`, 1 `LOP3`, 1 `UTCBAR`, 1 `UISETP.GT`, 1 `UPLOP3`, 3 branches = 47. The CUTLASS kernel's loop (0x3890-0x3b40 in `sass_gemm.txt`) is 44 [M]; the +3 is `UMOV UR28/UR29` (hoisted out of the loop only in the CUTLASS kernel), `UMOV UR37, 0xf` (the CUTLASS kernel builds the mask at run time before the tile loop) and the `ULEA` that recomputes `empty[rs]`, minus one loop-counter instruction (note G.3). Two things to notice: the first iteration is **not peeled** (the C++ `tok` of explicit.cu:916 becomes `P0` carried across the back-edge), and the peek at 0x5350 is predicated off on the last k-tile (`k <= 0 ? 1u : mbar_try_wait(...)` at explicit.cu:927), giving exactly 1 + 127 = 128 peeks per tile (Chapter 9).

What runs where: of the 47 instructions, 5 are vector-datapath (2 `SHF`, 1 `LOP3`, 2 `PLOP3` predicate moves), 2 are barrier operations (`TRYWAIT`), 5 are TC-pipe (4 `UTCHMMA`, 1 `UTCBAR`), 3 are branches, and the remaining 32 are uniform-datapath ALU operations (12 `UMOV`, 9 `UIADD3`, 5 `ULEA`, 3 `UISETP`, 2 `USEL`, 1 `UPLOP3`); 5 + 2 + 5 + 3 + 32 = 47. The vector lanes of warp 0 are essentially idle.

### 12.5.2 Producer warp 2: 37 instructions per k-tile (0x10b0-0x12f0), 33 on the fast path [M]

```
/*10b0*/               @P1 BRA 0x1100 ;                                  peek succeeded: skip the blocking wait
/*10c0*/                   ULEA UR4, UR28, UR7, 0x3 ;
/*10d0*/                   SHF.L.U32 R4, R0, 0x1f, RZ ;
/*10e0*/                   SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT P1, [UR4+0x40], R4 ;      empty[s] = base + 64 + 8 s
/*10f0*/              @!P1 BRA 0x5c80 ;
/*1100*/                   UIADD3 UR4, UPT, UPT, UR28, 0x1, URZ ;                   s + 1
/*1110*/              @!P0 MOV R5, 0xc000 ;                                         49152 (leader lane only)
/*1120*/                   VOTEU.ALL UP1, P0 ;
/*1130*/                   USHF.L.U32 UR18, UR13, 0x6, URZ ;                        c0 = 64 q
/*1140*/                   UISETP.NE.U32.AND UP0, UPT, UR4, 0x8, UPT ;              wrap
/*1150*/              @!UP1 ULEA UR10, UR28, UR7, 0x3 ;                             full[s] (unmasked, local) for the expect_tx
/*1160*/                   USEL UR8, URZ, 0x1, UP0 ;
/*1170*/                   USEL UR4, UR4, URZ, UP0 ;
/*1180*/                   UIADD3 UR30, UP0, UPT, UR22, 0x80, URZ ;                 &params.tma_b = param base + 0x80 (low word)
/*1190*/                   LOP3.LUT R0, R0, UR8, RZ, 0x3c, !PT ;                    prod_phase ^= flip
/*11a0*/                   ULEA UR8, UR28, UR7, 0xd ;                               base + (s << 13)
/*11b0*/              @!P0 SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64 RZ, [UR10], R5 ;                    mbarrier.arrive.expect_tx full[s], 49152
/*11c0*/                   ULEA UR9, UR4, UR7, 0x3 ;                                empty[s + 1] for the peek
/*11d0*/                   SHF.L.U32 R4, R0, 0x1f, RZ ;
/*11e0*/                   ULEA UR17, UR28, UR35, 0x3 ;                             masked full[s] = (base & 0xfefffff0) + 8 s
/*11f0*/                   ULEA UR16, UR28, UR24, 0xe ;                             A dst = (base + 0x8400 + 8192 y) + (s << 14)
/*1200*/                   UPRMT UR34, URZ, 0x5410, UR25 ;                          multicast mask (0x5 << x) into bits [16,32)
/*1210*/                   UIADD3 UR8, UPT, UPT, UR8, 0x28400, URZ ;                B dst = base + 0x28400 + (s << 13)
/*1220*/                   UIADD3.X UR31, UPT, UPT, URZ, UR23, URZ, UP0, !UPT ;     &params.tma_b high word
/*1230*/                   UMOV UR20, URZ ;                                         z coordinate = 0
/*1240*/                   UMOV UR32, 0x0 ;                                         cache hint low
/*1250*/                   UMOV UR33, 0x10000000 ;                                  cache hint high -> 0x1000000000000000
/*1260*/                   SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT P1, [UR9+0x40], R4 ;      peek empty[s + 1]
/*1270*/                   UMOV UR9, UR17 ;                                         B's barrier
/*1280*/                   UMOV UR10, UR18 ;                                        B's c0
/*1290*/                   UMOV UR12, UR20 ;                                        B's z
/*12a0*/                   UTMALDG.3D.MULTICAST.2CTA [UR16], [UR22], UR34, desc[UR32] ;   A
/*12b0*/                   UIADD3 UR13, UPT, UPT, UR13, 0x1, URZ ;                  ++q
/*12c0*/                   UMOV UR28, UR4 ;                                         prod_idx = s + 1 (wrapped)
/*12d0*/                   UISETP.NE.U32.AND UP0, UPT, UR13, UR39, UPT ;            q != end ?
/*12e0*/                   UTMALDG.3D.2CTA [UR8], [UR30], desc[UR32] ;              B
/*12f0*/                   BRA.U UP0, 0x10b0 ;
```

The issue order is the one the source dictates (explicit.cu:732-752): wait, `expect_tx`, advance, peek, A load, B load. The CUTLASS kernel's loop (0x1d60-0x1f40 in `sass_gemm.txt`) is 31 (28 fast path). Matching the two bodies instruction by instruction leaves 28 shared, 9 explicit-only and 3 baseline-only, net +6 [M]. Explicit-only: the five re-materialised invariants `@!P0 MOV R5, 0xc000` (the baseline hoists `@P0 MOV R2, 0xc000` in front of each loop, 0x1a10 and 0x1cf0), `UIADD3 UR30` + `UIADD3.X UR31` (the `tma_b` address pair), `UPRMT UR34` (the mask insert) and `UMOV UR20, URZ` (z = 0); the `VOTEU.ALL UP1, P0` that predicates `@!UP1 ULEA UR10`; and two further `full[s]` address formations, `ULEA UR4` for the blocking wait and `ULEA UR17` for the masked TMA barrier, where the baseline forms `full[s]` once (`ULEA UR17, UR4, UR29, 0x3` at 0x1d60, before its `@P1 BRA`, serving both the wait and the `expect_tx`) and masks it in place with `ULOP3.LUT UR17, UR17, 0xfefffff8` (0x1e80). Baseline-only: that `ULEA`, that `ULOP3`, and `UIADD3 UR16, UR16, 0x8400` (0x1e90), which the explicit kernel folds into the hoisted `UR24 = base + 0x8400 + 8192 y`. Note G.3 states the same net as "eight explicit-only in-loop instructions minus two baseline-only ones" by pairing the wait-block `ULEA UR4` with the `0x8400` add. The 8-k-tile prologue loop (0x0de0-0x1020) has the same 37 with its own two `UTMALDG` at 0x0fc0/0x1000.

### 12.5.3 Scheduler warp 1 of CTA 0: 50 instructions per tile (0x1a20-0x1d30) [M]

Head at 0x1a20 (target of `@P2 BRA 0x1a20` at 0x1d30), so the body is `(0x1d30 - 0x1a20) / 16 + 1 = 50`, opcode for opcode the CUTLASS kernel's (note G.3): throttle wait (`TRYWAIT [R5+URZ+0x130]`) and remote release (`PRMT R4, RZ, 0x654, R4; SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED.A1T0 RZ, [R4+URZ], RZ`), CLC empty wait (`TRYWAIT P1, [UR6+0xe0], R6`), arming by lanes 0..3 (`@!P0 SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED RZ, [R11+URZ], R5`, `R5 = 0x10`), `UGETNEXTWORKID.BROADCAST [UR8], [UR9]`, response wait (`TRYWAIT P2, [R12+URZ+0xd0], R5`), `LDS.128`, `MEMBAR.ALL.CTA; FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S`, release to CTA 0, decode. The tail (0x1d40-0x1ec0) is the two `SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64` test-waits with their blocking fallbacks, ending in `@P0 EXIT`.

### 12.5.4 Epilogue warps 4-7: 674 per tile in the loop, 696 in the function [M]

The epilogue role spans 0x1f10 (`BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING 0x6, 0xa0`, the `named_bar_sync(kBarTmemAlloc, ...)` of explicit.cu:997) to 0x4a80 (`EXIT`): 696 instructions, the number note G.3 reports "per tile". My recount splits it: one-time entry 0x1f10-0x2050 (21 instructions: the `LDCU.64` of alpha/beta and of the parameter base, the four `st_off` bases `R20..R23`, `T` from `[UR7+0x180]`, `UR17 = (32 w) << 16`), the tile loop 0x2060-0x4a70 (674 instructions, back-edge `BRA.U UP0, 0x2060` at 0x4a70), and the `EXIT`. Inside the loop:

| Segment | Addresses | Instructions | Content |
|---|---|---|---|
| per-tile setup | 0x2060-0x2280 | 35 | `clc_consume` (CLC wait, `LDS.128`, fence, release to CTA 0, decode to `tm/tn`), the `acc_full[st]` peek, the TMEM address `UR29 = T + ((32w) << 16) + 128 st` |
| subtile 0 | 0x2290-0x2750 | 77 | `LDTM.x16`, 16 `FMUL`, 16 `FFMA`, 16 `STS`, `MEMBAR.ALL.CTA + FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S`, `BAR.SYNC 0x1, 0x80`, the warp-4-only store block (`@P1 BRA` around it: `UIADD3`/`UMOV` bookkeeping for the four `{src, c0, c1, c2}` tuples, 4 `UTMASTG.3D`, `UTMACMDFLUSH`, `DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x1`), `BAR.SYNC 0x1, 0x80` |
| subtiles 1-5 | 0x2760-0x3fb0 | 78 each | same content; the one-instruction difference from subtile 0 is address bookkeeping [H] |
| subtile 6 | 0x3fc0-0x44c0 | 81 | same, plus the `ULOP3 ... 0xfefffff8` and `UIADD3 ... 0x110` that build the masked `acc_empty[st]` address for subtile 7 |
| subtile 7 | 0x44d0-0x4a70 | 91 | `LDTM.x16 R4, tmem[UR29+0x70]; NOP; SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED.A1T0 RZ, [UR24], RZ` (the `tcgen05.wait::ld` + release of explicit.cu:1038-1039, the arrive waiting on the `LDTM` scoreboard), the arithmetic and stores, the accumulator state advance, `tm = tm_next` etc., the loop test |

The store block of subtile 0 (0x25f0-0x2740, verbatim) shows how warp 4 forms the four `{src, c0, c1, c2}` tuples that the `UTMASTG` operand blocks name:

```
        /*25f0*/                   UIADD3 UR36, UP2, UPT, UR30, 0x180, URZ ;
        /*2600*/                   UIADD3 UR20, UPT, UPT, UR7, 0x200, URZ ;
        /*2610*/                   UIADD3.X UR37, UPT, UPT, URZ, UR31, URZ, UP2, !UPT ;
        /*2620*/                   UIADD3 UR9, UPT, UPT, UR21, 0x20, URZ ;
        /*2630*/                   UIADD3 UR8, UPT, UPT, UR7, 0xa00, URZ ;
        /*2640*/                   UIADD3 UR13, UPT, UPT, UR21, 0x40, URZ ;
        /*2650*/                   UIADD3 UR12, UPT, UPT, UR7, 0x1200, URZ ;
        /*2660*/                   UIADD3 UR33, UPT, UPT, UR21, 0x60, URZ ;
        /*2670*/                   UIADD3 UR32, UPT, UPT, UR7, 0x1a00, URZ ;
        /*2680*/                   UMOV UR23, URZ ;
        /*2690*/                   UMOV UR10, UR22 ;
        /*26a0*/                   UMOV UR11, UR23 ;
        /*26b0*/                   UTMASTG.3D [UR20], [UR36] ;
        /*26c0*/                   UMOV UR14, UR22 ;
        /*26d0*/                   UMOV UR15, UR23 ;
        /*26e0*/                   UMOV UR34, UR22 ;
        /*26f0*/                   UMOV UR35, UR23 ;
        /*2700*/                   UTMASTG.3D [UR8], [UR36] ;
        /*2710*/                   UTMASTG.3D [UR12], [UR36] ;
        /*2720*/                   UTMASTG.3D [UR32], [UR36] ;
        /*2730*/                   UTMACMDFLUSH ;
        /*2740*/                   DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x1 ;
```

`UR30:UR31` is the parameter-block address (`LDCU.64 UR30, c[0x0][0x348]` at 0x1f50), so `UR36:UR37 = +0x180` is `&params.tma_d`. `UR7` is `smem_base`, so the four sources are `OFF_SMEM_CD + 2048 i` = `0x200, 0xa00, 0x1200, 0x1a00` (one 32-row x 16-column fp32 box is 2048 B). `UR21 = 128 tm` and `UR22 = 128 tn` are formed once per tile (`USHF.L.U32 UR21, UR21, 0x7` and `USHF.L.U32 UR22, UR29, 0x7` at 0x2120-0x2130), so `c0 = 128 tm + 32 i` is `UR21`, `UR9 = UR21 + 0x20`, `UR13 = UR21 + 0x40`, `UR33 = UR21 + 0x60`; `c1 = 128 tn + 16 e` is `UR22` for subtile 0, copied into `UR10`, `UR14`, `UR34` for boxes 1-3; `c2 = 0` is `UR23 = URZ`, copied into `UR11`, `UR15`, `UR35`. The tuples are thus `{UR20, UR21, UR22, UR23}`, `{UR8, UR9, UR10, UR11}`, `{UR12, UR13, UR14, UR15}`, `{UR32, UR33, UR34, UR35}` [H for the block reading, M for the arithmetic]. For subtile e only two things change: `c1` becomes `UR22 + 16 e` (subtile 1: `UIADD3 UR10, UR22, 0x10` at 0x2ac0, then `UMOV UR9, UR21` for box 0's c0), the sources move to the epilogue smem stage `0x200 + 0x2000 (e & 3) + 0x800 i` (subtile 1: `UR7 + 0x2200, 0x2a00, 0x3200, 0x3a00`), and ptxas re-forms the D-map address into a different register per unrolled subtile (`UIADD3 UR40, UP2, UPT, UR30, 0x180` at 0x2ab0, so subtile 1 stores `UTMASTG.3D [UR8], [UR40]`). A reader comparing `[UR36]` in subtile 0 with `[UR40]` in subtile 1 is looking at the same 64-bit value in two registers, not at an error.

Per subtile both kernels have 1 `LDTM.x16`, 16 `FMUL`, 16 `FFMA`, 16 `STS`, 1 fence pair, 2 `BAR.SYNC`, 4 `UTMASTG`, 1 `UTMACMDFLUSH`, 1 `DEPBAR`; the CUTLASS kernel's 1265 per tile adds its 16 dead `LDS` of C behind a never-taken predicate, three `SYNCS` of the dead `epi_load` pipeline, an `R2UR`, a `NOP` and predicate bookkeeping per subtile, and a 309-instruction setup (note G.3).

### 12.5.5 Why none of this is on the critical path [M for the inputs, H for the model]

The time budget per k-tile, from the measured runtime (note D.4): a cluster on the critical path processes 32 tiles in 0.888 ms, so one tile takes at most 27.75 us and one k-tile 27.75 us / 128 = 216.8 ns = **426 cycles** at 1965 MHz; one 256 x 128 x 16 MMA therefore has 106.5 cycles. (If the 1024 tiles were spread as the mean 31.03 per cluster the figures would be 3.1 % larger: 32 / 31.03 = 1.031, i.e. 28.6 us per tile, 439 cycles per k-tile, 109.8 cycles per MMA, the second figure note D.4 quotes.)

Issue model: an SM has four sub-partitions, each with one warp scheduler; the Nsight Compute Profiling Guide (hardware model) says "From the set of eligible warps the scheduler selects a single warp from which to issue one or more instructions." I take **one instruction per cycle per scheduler** as the issue bound [H: the guide states no per-cycle rate; if more than one instruction can issue per cycle, the utilisation figures below are upper bounds]. Eight warps on four schedulers means two warps per scheduler (which two is `warp_id % 4` on the architectures I know; unverified for this chip).

| Warp | Instructions per k-tile (static, fast path) | Share of one scheduler's 426 slots |
|---|---|---|
| 0 (MMA, leader CTA) | 43 (47 minus the 4 skipped wait instructions) | 10.1 % |
| 2 (producer) | 33 | 7.7 % |
| 4-7 (epilogue), each | 674 per tile / 128 k-tiles = 5.3 | 1.2 % |
| 1 (scheduler, CTA 0 only) | 50 per tile / 128 = 0.4 | 0.1 % |
| 1 (ranks 1-3), 3 | exited | 0 |

Even if warps 0 and 4 share a scheduler, their combined demand is about 11 % of its issue capacity; the busiest scheduler is idle nine cycles out of ten. The uniform-datapath instructions of warp 0 moreover do not compete with the epilogue's `FMUL`/`FFMA`/`STS`, which use the vector pipes. The only way the MMA warp could become the bottleneck is if the tensor core finished four MMAs in fewer than ~43 cycles, i.e. if the hardware were about ten times faster than it is: the loop length is irrelevant as long as the next k-tile's `UTCHMMA`s are issued before the tensor core drains, which the 8-stage ring and the peek-then-wait idiom (the `full[s]` wait almost always succeeds on the inline try) make the common case. The same reasoning applies to the producer: 33 issue slots to put 49152 bytes in flight per k-tile per pair, running up to 8 stages ahead (Chapter 8).

What **is** on the critical path is the dependency chain the loops encode: `full[s]` completion (TMA bytes landed) -> `UTCHMMA` issue -> tensor-core execution -> `UTCBAR` -> `empty[s]` -> next `UTMALDG` into stage s; and per tile `acc_full[st]` -> `LDTM` -> `STS` -> `UTMASTG` -> `acc_empty[st]`. Chapter 3 derives the speed-of-light bound of that chain; Section 12.7.4 lists the counters that measure where it actually waits.

---

## 12.6 What was measured

### 12.6.1 Performance: five interleaved pairs [M]

`trace_out_v2/baseline.txt` and `timing_summary.txt` (five runs of the pristine toggle-off binary of the original example interleaved with five runs of the explicit binary, same day, same GPU, `nvidia-smi` sampling clocks every 100 ms):

| Run (interleaved order) | pristine `Avg runtime` (ms) | explicit `Avg runtime` (ms) | explicit / pristine |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.888653 | 0.889261 | 1.00068 |
| 2 | 0.890288 | 0.890307 | 1.00002 |
| 3 | 0.889411 | 0.888947 | 0.99948 |
| 4 | 0.889990 | 0.889517 | 0.99947 |
| 5 | 0.889917 | 0.889354 | 0.99937 |
| median | **0.889917** | **0.889354** | **0.99937** |
| mean / stdev | 0.889652 / 0.000641 | 0.889477 / 0.000508 | 0.99980 |
| min / max | 0.888653 / 0.890288 | 0.888947 / 0.890307 | |

- The acceptance rule was "replacement median <= same-day pristine median x 1.002" (note E.8 C2); 0.889354 <= 0.891697: accept. The 0.06 % advantage by medians is inside the run-to-run spread ((max - min) / median: 0.15 % for the explicit binary, 0.18 % for the pristine one) and means nothing except "indistinguishable".
- `GFLOPS` is `2 m n k / Avg runtime` exactly (`Options::gflops`, 70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.cu:256-262): 2 x 8192^3 = 1.0995 x 10^12 FLOP; / 0.889354 ms = 1.2363 x 10^15 FLOP/s, printed as `1.2363e+06`.
- What the interval contains: the harness times ten iterations of `gemm.initialize()` + `explicit_gemm::run(gemm)` between `timer.start()` and `timer.stop()` (70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.cu:435-445), so each iteration includes six `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled` calls, one `cudaFuncSetAttribute` on the never-launched CUTLASS kernel, two on the explicit kernel (explicit.cu:1279, :1294), the `cudaLaunchKernelExC` (explicit.cu:1312) and `cudaGetLastError`; nothing synchronises (note G.2 C4). Kernel-only time would need `nsys` (note, Section 12 item 2) and was not measured.
- Clocks: 101 of 101 steady-state samples at 1965 MHz SM / 3996 MHz memory, power 196.5-306.1 W (median 300.0 W) over those 101 samples, temperature 31-37 C over all 108; the seven earlier samples (three at 120 MHz, four at 787 MHz) are the idle ramp before the first kernel, and the 188.6 W floor and 299.9 W median that the note quotes include them (my recount of `clocks.csv`). That the 9 ms timed loops themselves ran at 1965 MHz is inferred from the surrounding samples (note G.2 C1, D.4).
- The machine-state gate: the same-day pristine median 0.889917 ms versus the 2026-09-09 pristine median 0.888659 ms is 1.00142, inside the +-0.3 % gate (note G.2 C3). The 2026-09-09 run was executed on a different physical B200 (PCI bus `9D:00.0` against `43:00.0`, same SKU, driver and toolkit; note G.0), so this gate compares two boards, not one board on two days; it still bounds the drift to 0.14 %, and the acceptance itself rests only on the same-day interleaved pair. The script has since recorded hostname and GPU UUID as `gpu_identity.txt` (note G.6 item 5); that file is not among the committed `trace_out_v2` artefacts, whose GPU identity is in `clocks_query.txt`.
- For the record only: the trace build (toggle on) runs at 1.13341 ms, 27 % slower, because every blocking wait reads `%globaltimer` and the roles write heartbeats to host-mapped memory; it must never be timed (note G.2, H).

### 12.6.2 Correctness [M]

| Evidence | Where it comes from | What it proves |
|---|---|---|
| `Disposition: Passed` in 1 toggle-on + 5 toggle-off runs | `verify()` runs the device reference GEMM with the same alpha/beta/C and compares all M x N outputs with `cutlass::reference::device::BlockCompareEqual` (70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.cu:351-378): **exact** equality, no tolerance | D is value-equal to the reference, and the comparison is exact for an arithmetic reason, not by tolerance: `initialize_block` fills A and B with integers in [-8, 8] (`BlockFillRandomUniform` with `scope_max = 8, scope_min = -8` for 16-bit elements, 70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.cu:307-312), so every product is an integer with abs(ab) <= 64 and every partial sum of the 8192 products satisfies abs(sum) <= 8192 x 64 = 524288 < 2^24; every intermediate is exactly representable in fp32, so the kernel's and the reference's accumulations are exact whatever their order; with alpha = 1 and beta = 0 the epilogue is exact too, and `BlockCompareEqual` is a bit-equality test up to the sign of zero, which `==` ignores [S] |
| sentinel fill | `trace_begin()` fills D with `0xFF` bytes before the traced launch (explicit.cu:1349: `cudaMemset(d_ptr, 0xFF, d_bytes)`), so any element never stored reads as NaN and fails `==` | every one of the 2^26 elements was written by the kernel; a tile skipped by a scheduling bug could not pass |
| `check_trace.py`: 4112 PASS, 0 FAIL (`trace_out_v2/checklist.txt`) | sections 1-7 of the checker as committed: shared-memory addresses, TMEM base, every MMA operand, every TMA load/store operand, CLC slot/parity/coverage, host facts, the explicit kernel's tail records (the 4105 checks of the CUTLASS run plus seven Part-E rows, note G.1); the current `check_trace.py` adds section 8 (trace-infrastructure self-checks: every record from lane 0, `smid` in range, per-kind `seq` contiguous, CSV count equal to the host counter; note G.6 item 6) and reports 4116 PASS, 0 FAIL on the same `launch0.csv` | every address, offset, descriptor, coordinate, slot, parity and count predicted in the note matches what the kernel did |
| 1518 `K_TAIL` records = 46 per cluster x 33 | rank 0: 8 mainloop + 2 CLC + 4 accumulator + 1 dealloc; rank 1: 8 + 1; rank 2: 8 + 4 + 1; rank 3: 8 + 1 (`check_trace.py` `TAIL_EXPECT`) | all four exit tails of Chapter 4 ran to completion in every CTA with the `{index, phase}` the pipeline formulas predict (mainloop tails all waited parity 1; accumulator `((T + i) % 4, 1 ^ (((T + i) / 4) & 1))`; CLC `((T + i) % 2, 1 ^ (((T + i) / 2) & 1))` for a cluster with T tiles) |
| no `TRACE_HANG` / `TRACE_HANG_HB` line | the 4 s bounded wait and the 20 s watchdog of the trace build never fired | no barrier was ever waited on with the wrong parity or count |

### 12.6.3 Record-level equivalence with the CUTLASS kernel [M]

The trace build records, from inside the kernel, one row per probed event into a device buffer dumped to `launch0.csv` (`kind, bx, by, rank, warp, lane, smid, seq, t, v0..v9`). The same probes, with the same payload definitions, exist in the CUTLASS kernel's trace build (the headers under the toggle), so the two runs can be compared record by record.

| kind | Name | Records | Payload | Explicit vs CUTLASS run |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1, 11 | K1a/K1b | 4 + 4 | shared-memory base and barrier addresses per rank | identical multisets |
| 2 | K2 | 264 | TMEM base, rank, leader flag, site (both sites x 132 CTAs) | identical (`T = 0` everywhere) |
| 3 | K3 | 32 | `desc_a`, `desc_b`, `tmem_c`, `idesc`, `scale_c` of the first MMAs | identical: `0x4000404000010880`, `0x4000404000012880`, `+2` per k-block, `+0x400`/`+0x200` per stage, `0x10200010`, `scale_c = 0` only on the first |
| 4 | K4a | 128 | TMA load coordinates, destination, size, barrier | identical |
| 5 | K4b | 256 | TMA store coordinates, source, active lanes (32) | identical |
| 7, 8, 9 | K5a/b/c | 1024 + 1024 + 4096 | CLC state, raw response, valid, decoded tile | differ in 26 / 290 / 1160 tuples: the tile ids the hardware handed out; protocol fields (slot = `count % 2`, parities, barrier addresses) pass in both |
| 10 | K0 | 32 | the standalone K0 probe kernel's view of its own 4 x 4 grid = four 2 x 2 clusters: 16 CTAs x 2 records (`v9 = 0`: smem base, `mapa` to the peer and to rank 0, the masked base, cluster coordinates; `v9 = 1`: the TMEM base from `tcgen05.alloc`), run before the GEMM (note D.1 D6, D.3) | identical |
| 13 | K_TAIL | 1518 | tail site, `{idx, phase}`, tile | explicit kernel only |

Total 8382 rows; 6864 of them are not tail records, the same count the CUTLASS kernel produced (my recount of `trace_out_v2/launch0.csv`; note G.1). The `trace_seq_3 34` and `trace_seq_4 132` counters against 32 and 128 rows are the per-kind record caps doing their job: `TRACE_RECORD(kind, cap, ...)` increments `g_trace_seq[kind]` and stores a record while the count is below `cap`; the first attempt at or past `cap` sets `g_trace_full[kind]`, and every later attempt is skipped before the atomic (deabstraction_trace.hpp:139-152), e.g. `TRACE_RECORD(K_MMA, 32, ...)` at explicit.cu:936. So 34 is 32 stored + 2 attempts that raced in before the full flag became visible, not a count of the 4 x 128 x 1024 MMA issues.

Column meaning, so that you can redo the recounts of Section 12.6.4 (deabstraction_trace.hpp:26-61): `kind,bx,by,rank,warp,lane,smid,seq,t,v0..v9` with `t` = `%globaltimer` in ns and the cluster of a record `(bx / 2, by / 2)`; K3 `v0..v4` = `desc_a, desc_b, tmem_c, idesc, scale_c`; K4a `v0..v5` = `c0, c1, c2, dst, size in elements, mbarrier`; K4b `v0..v4` = `c0, c1, c2, src, popc(activemask)`; K5a (kind 7) `v0..v5` = CLC `state.index, state.phase, state.count, mbarrier address, blockIdx.x / 2, blockIdx.y / 2`; K5b/K5c (kinds 8, 9) `v0..v8` = raw `M_idx, N_idx, L_idx, valid, state.index, state.phase, state.count, swizzled M_idx, swizzled N_idx`; K_TAIL `v0..v3` = `site, index, parity, tile`. Two payload differences that are not protocol differences: for a not-cancelled response the explicit probe writes 0 in the two tile fields where the CUTLASS probe wrote stale values, and in both runs the raw id words of a not-cancelled response equal the **previous** response's: the predicated `get_first_ctaid` leaves its outputs unwritten (explicit.cu:577 comment; note D.3), which is why Chapter 7 insists those fields are read only under `valid`.

### 12.6.4 CLC dynamics [M, with the inferences marked]

**Residency.** 33 clusters launched natively (launch-linear ids 0..32), equal to `cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters` for this configuration (`max_active_clusters 33` in `host.txt`); 132 of 148 SMs host CTAs; SMs 64, 65, 122-129 and 142-147 stay idle for the whole launch (my recount of the `smid` column agrees with note D.3). The naive 148 / 4 = 37 is not reached.

Why 33 (inferred, note D.3): every MMA pair sits on an SM pair `(2j, 2j + 1)`, a TPC, and both pairs of a cluster sit in the same SM-id group:

| Cluster ids | pair {0, 1} on SMs | pair {2, 3} on SMs |
|---|---|---|
| 0-7 | `2k`, `2k + 1` | `+16` |
| 8-15 | `2k + 16`, `2k + 17` | `+16` |
| 16-22 | `66 + 2(k - 16)`, `+1` | `+14` |
| 23-29 | `94 + 2(k - 23)`, `+1` | `+14` |
| 30-31 | `130 + 2(k - 30)`, `+1` | `+6` |
| 32 | 134, 135 | 140, 141 |

A 2 x 2 cluster needs two whole TPCs inside one GPC; the groups above have an even number of usable TPCs and the 8 leftover TPCs (16 SMs) cannot be paired, hence 33 and not 37. For a designer: the cluster shape costs 10.8 % of the machine before the first instruction runs, and the loss depends on the chip's floorsweeping, not on the kernel. A (2,1,1) cluster or a non-clustered kernel would fill more SMs but lose the A multicast; Chapter 3 weighs this.

**Tiles per cluster.** 32 tiles for 13 clusters, 31 for 19, 19 for cluster (0, 0) (the probed cluster, slowed 1.7x by its K3/K4 probes in the trace build); sum 13 x 32 + 19 x 31 + 19 = 1024 (my recount). Dynamic scheduling absorbed the probe-induced slowness automatically: the slow cluster simply received fewer tiles. [H] In the Release binary there is no probed cluster; with 1024 tiles over 33 clusters (33 x 31 = 1023, one tile over) the expected split is 31 or 32 per cluster, faster clusters taking the extra tiles, but the Release runs record only `Avg runtime` and `Disposition`, so this was not measured. Under that expectation the tail imbalance is at most one tile in 31, about 3 % of the runtime, which is the price of 256 x 256 cluster tiles on 33 clusters.

**Hand-out order** (CUTLASS kernel's trace, note D.3). The 991 cancelled ids are 33..1023, each exactly once; within each cluster the successive ids are strictly increasing; sorted by query issue time the ids are ascending except 25 adjacent swaps among 990 pairs (933 of 991 at their sorted position). The first hand-out was id 33 to cluster (0, 0) 1.28 us after the first query; the last was id 1023 at 959.2 us. With `AlongN` and no swizzle, id L is cluster tile `(L / 32, L % 32)`, so a cluster's successive tiles are about 33 ids apart: `m` advances by one per tile while `n` drifts, and at any moment the 33 clusters work on two (834 of 991 hand-outs) or three (157) adjacent 256-row bands of A. That is good L2 behaviour obtained for free from the launch order.

**Query latency** (issue by the scheduler's elected lane to consumption by the same warp):

| Trace | min | p10 | median | p90 | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CUTLASS kernel (note D.3, 1024 queries) | 736 ns | 800 | 1408 | 1536 | 2336 |
| explicit kernel (my recount, 1024 queries) | 928 ns | 960 | 1024 | 1184 | 1408 |

The difference is probe placement in the scheduler warp, not hardware (note G.2). Either way the latency is irrelevant. In the CUTLASS kernel's trace the throttle gap between consuming response n and issuing query n + 1 is 28.8-37.7 us (median 30.8 us, unprobed clusters, note D.3), so with its 1.41 us median latency a query is in flight 4.6 % of the time; in the explicit kernel's trace the gap is 33.7-41.0 us (median 34.4 us over the 973 consume-to-issue pairs of the 32 unprobed clusters, my recount) against a 1.02 us median, about 3 %. Never more than one query is outstanding per cluster, at most 25 GPU-wide (note D.3). Both rows of the table and the tile split above are reproducible from `launch0.csv` with the column map of Section 12.6.3: pair each cluster's kind-7 record (`v2` = count) with the kind-8 record of the same count (`v6`); `t_8 - t_7` is the latency and `t_7(n + 1) - t_8(n)` the gap; the split is the number of kind-8 records with `v3 = 1` per cluster plus the launch tile (13 x 32 + 19 x 31 + 19). A designer takes three lessons: the CLC round trip is about 1 us, so one query per tile (27 us) hides it completely and a deeper CLC pipeline than 2 slots would buy nothing; the throttle (Chapter 7) is what keeps "one outstanding query per cluster" true; and the exactly-once coverage of 1024 tiles must be verified by a checker, because no run-time assertion exists for it.

---

## 12.7 How to reproduce and inspect

### 12.7.1 The full-speed run (note Section 0, Part H.1)

```
export CUDACXX=.../cuda-13.3/bin/nvcc CUDA_HOME=.../cuda-13.3
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER="$CUDACXX" -DCUDAToolkit_ROOT="$CUDA_HOME" \
      -DCUTLASS_NVCC_ARCHS=100a -DCUTLASS_ENABLE_EXAMPLES=ON -DCUTLASS_ENABLE_TESTS=ON -DCUTLASS_ENABLE_PROFILER=ON \
  && cmake --build build --target 70_blackwell_fp16_gemm --parallel 16
./build/examples/70_blackwell_gemm/70_blackwell_fp16_gemm --m=8192 --n=8192 --k=8192
```

Expected: `Disposition: Passed`, `Problem Size: 8192x8192x8192`, `Avg runtime: 0.889 ms` (0.888-0.891 on the B200 at 1965 MHz), `GFLOPS: 1.236e+06`. The target compiles both `70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.cu` and `70_blackwell_fp16_gemm_explicit.cu` (CMakeLists.txt source list); the binary still contains the never-launched CUTLASS kernel because the unchanged `gemm.initialize()` odr-uses it (note E.3.3).

Before timing anything, check the toggle: `head -1 examples/70_blackwell_gemm/70_blackwell_fp16_gemm_explicit_util.hpp` must **begin with** `// #define CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE 1` (the line continues with a long comment). The driver script flips it with `sed -i '1s|^// #define CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE 1|#define CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE 1|'` and back with the inverse pattern, both matching that prefix only, and its `on_exit` warns if line 1 still starts with `#define` (`deabstraction_trace_run.sh:41-49`, `toggle_on`/`toggle_off`/`toggle_state`); both `.cu` files include this header first, so one edit switches both translation units.

Where the evidence lives: `OUT=${TRACE_OUT:-$ROOT/trace_out_v2}` (`deabstraction_trace_run.sh:27`), so `trace_out/` and `trace_out_v2/` are directories at the **repository root**, not under `examples/70_blackwell_gemm/`; every `trace_out_v2/...` path in this chapter is relative to the repository root.

The script's steps (`S=examples/70_blackwell_gemm/deabstraction_trace_run.sh`, always with `TRACE_OUT=<fresh dir>` because `trace_out/` holds the pristine baseline and `trace_out_v2/` the committed evidence):

| Step | What it does | Outputs |
|---|---|---|
| `$S build` | toggle off, fixed build, saves the binary | `70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.explicit`, `build_build.log` |
| `$S inspect` | `cuobjdump` on the saved binary, cuts the explicit kernel out, runs `check_sass.py` | `sass.txt`, `sass_explicit.txt`, `sass_gemm.txt`, `ptx.txt`, `ptx_explicit.txt`, `resources.txt`, `elf.txt`, `config.txt`, `sass_summary.txt`, `sass_checklist.txt` |
| `$S baseline` | 5 pristine + 5 explicit runs interleaved, clocks sampled at 100 ms, GPU identity | `baseline.txt`, `timing_*.txt`, `timing_summary.txt` (medians, ratio, accept/explain/fail tier, machine-state gate), `clocks.csv`, `gpu_identity.txt` |
| `$S trace` | toggle on, rebuild, one traced run | `host.txt`, `launch0.csv` |
| `$S check` | `check_trace.py launch0.csv host.txt` | `checklist.txt` |
| `$S restore` | toggle off, touch both `.cu`, rebuild, prove the SASS equals the `build` step's | `sass_explicit_after.txt`, `build_restore.log` |
| `$S all` | trace, check, stop unless Passed with 0 FAIL, then build, inspect, baseline, restore | all of the above |

### 12.7.2 Dumping the binary yourself (note H.2.2)

```
BIN=./build/examples/70_blackwell_gemm/70_blackwell_fp16_gemm
cuobjdump --dump-sass "$BIN" > sass.txt
cuobjdump --dump-ptx  "$BIN" > ptx.txt
cuobjdump --dump-resource-usage "$BIN"
cuobjdump --list-elf "$BIN"            # two sm_100a cubins expected, one per translation unit
awk '/^Fatbin /{p=0} /Function :/{p=index($0, "explicit_blackwell_fp16_gemm_kernel") > 0} p' sass.txt > sass_explicit.txt
awk '/^Fatbin /{p=0} /^\.visible \.entry|^\.entry/{p=index($0, "explicit_blackwell_fp16_gemm_kernel") > 0} p' ptx.txt > ptx_explicit.txt
python3 examples/70_blackwell_gemm/check_sass.py ptx_explicit.txt sass_explicit.txt resources.txt explicit_blackwell_fp16_gemm_kernel
```

`--dump-sass` "dumps CUDA assembly for a single cubin file or all cubin files embedded in the binary", `--dump-resource-usage` "dumps resource usage for each ELF", `--list-elf` "lists all the ELF files available in the fatbin" (CUDA Binary Utilities manual). The `awk` cut works because `cuobjdump` prints one `Function : <mangled name>` header per kernel and a `Fatbin ...` header per embedded image.

### 12.7.3 The checklist: what to grep for [M]

`check_sass.py` turns the inventory of note E.7.4/G.3 into PASS/FAIL rows (hard rows fail the run, soft rows warn; values that the PTX carries in `mov.b32`-fed registers are checked through the feeding `mov.b32` or the SASS immediate, never by a literal on the instruction line). The executed-path inventory you should see, with the counts I recounted:

| Family | Expected in the explicit kernel | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `UTCHMMA.2CTA` | 4 | the four k-blocks |
| `UTCBAR.2CTA.MULTICAST` | 2 | mainloop release, accumulator commit |
| `UTMALDG.3D.MULTICAST.2CTA` / `UTMALDG.3D.2CTA` / plain `UTMALDG.3D` | 2 / 2 / 0 | one A and one B per rolled producer loop; no C load |
| `UTMASTG.3D` / `UTMACMDFLUSH` / `DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x1` / `DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x0` | 32 / 8 / 8 / 0 | 4 boxes x 8 subtiles; no `store_tail` |
| `LDTM.x16` | 8 | |
| `UGETNEXTWORKID.BROADCAST` | 1 | the CLC query (grep for this, not for "CLC") |
| `ACQBULK` / `PREEXIT` | 2 / 1 | GDC |
| `UTMACCTL.PF` | 4 | A, B, C, D prefetch |
| `UTCATOMSWS.2CTA.FIND_AND_SET` / `UTCATOMSWS.AND` | 2 / 1 | alloc (+ retry copy), dealloc |
| `SYNCS.EXCH.64` | 33 | the 33 `mbarrier.init` |
| `SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT` / `SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64` / `NANOSLEEP` | 65 / 32 / 31 | ptxas's retry structure; not a contract |
| `SYNCS.ARRIVE*` | 14 | 9 remote `.RED.A1T0`, 2 `.RED` (expect_tx remote and alloc handshake), 1 `.A1T0`, 2 plain (expect_tx local) |
| `BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING 0x1, 0x80` / `0x6, 0xa0` / `BAR.ARV 0x6, 0xa0` | 16 / 1 / 1 | plus one `BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING 0x0`, the non-cluster fallback |
| `FMUL` / `FFMA` / `FADD` | 130 / 128 / 0 | 128 + the two of the `%cluster_ctaid` lowering |
| `STS` / `LDS` | 131 / 11 | 128 + 3 bookkeeping; 4 `LDS.128` + 7 reserved/tmem_base reads |
| `LDL` / `STL` / `MOV.SPILL` / `R2UR.FILL` | 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 | |
| `ELECT` | 4 | none between the `UTCHMMA`s (`check_sass.py` tests a window around them) |
| `0xfefffff8` / `UPRMT ..., 0x5410` / `PRMT` or `UPRMT ..., 0x654` | 1 / 2 / 11 | peer mask, mask insert, `mapa` lowering |
| `UMOV URn, 0x40004040` | 8 | the descriptor high words, all in the MMA loop |
| resources | `REG` 26 (<= 68), `STACK` 0, `LOCAL` 0, `SHARED` 1024, `CONSTANT[0]` 1536 | |

Which of these rows `check_sass.py` actually asserts, and how hard (`examples/70_blackwell_gemm/check_sass.py:61-93, 122-145, 167-190, 207-235, 254-258`): **hard rows** (a miss is FAIL and a non-zero exit) are the PTX inventory (4 `tcgen05.mma`, 2 `tcgen05.commit`, 8 `tcgen05.ld`, 1 `tcgen05.wait::ld`, 1 each `alloc`/`dealloc`/`relinquish`, 2 + 2 + 0 TMA loads, 32 TMA stores, 8 `commit_group`, 8 `wait_group.read 1` and 0 `wait_group.read 0`, 1 `try_cancel`, 2 + 1 GDC, 4 `prefetch.tensormap`, 33 `mbarrier.init`, 2 + 1 `expect_tx`, 4 `fence.mbarrier_init`, 1 + 1 cluster barrier, 17 `bar.sync`, 1 `bar.arrive`, 128 `mul.f32`, 128 `fma.rn.f32`, 0 `add.f32`, 128 `st.shared.b32`, 0 generic `st.b32`, the peer-bit `and.b32`, the three CLC-decode consistency rows and the absence list), and in SASS `UTCHMMA.2CTA` 4, `UTCBAR.2CTA.MULTICAST` 2, `UTMASTG.3D` 32, `UTMACMDFLUSH` 8, `DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x1` 8, `DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x0` 0, `LDTM.x16` 8, `UGETNEXTWORKID.BROADCAST` 1, `PREEXIT` 1, `FFMA` 128, `FADD` 0, `LDL`/`STL` 0, and the resource fields `LOCAL` 0, `STACK` 0, `SHARED` 1024. **Soft rows** (WARN): `UTMALDG` 2/2/0, `UTMACCTL.PF` 4, `ACQBULK` 2, `UTCATOMSWS.AND` 1, `UTCATOMSWS.2CTA.FIND_AND_SET` >= 1, `SYNCS.EXCH.64` 33, the three `BAR` rows, `BPT.TRAP` 2, `FMUL` in 128..130, `STS` in 128..131, `0xfefffff8` >= 1, `UPRMT ... 0x5410` >= 1, no `ELECT` in the window from 30 instructions before the first `UTCHMMA` to 6 after the fourth, `UTCBAR` within 3 instructions after the fourth `UTCHMMA`, PTX `elect.sync` >= 9, `mbarrier.try_wait` sites >= 20, `mapa` >= 5, `.b16` mask operands >= 3, the `mov.b32` materialisations, and `REG <= 68`. **Informational** (INFO): the `ELECT` count, `CONSTANT[0]`, other constant banks. The `TRYWAIT`/`PHASECHK`/`NANOSLEEP`, `SYNCS.ARRIVE*`, `R2UR`, `UMOV 0x40004040` and `0x654` counts in the table above are my recounts that the tool does not check.

The committed `trace_out_v2/sass_checklist.txt` shows 89 PASS and 1 FAIL: the one FAIL is a parser bug on the resources line (the fixed-order regex did not expect `CONSTANT[2]:12` between `LOCAL` and `CONSTANT[0]`), fixed afterwards in `check_sass.py` (key-value parsing in any order); the re-run on the same dumps gives 93 PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 WARN (note G.6 item 1). Likewise the committed `checklist.txt` (4112 PASS) predates `check_trace.py`'s section 8 (4116 PASS, Section 12.6.2). Both committed files were produced by the pre-G.6 tool versions; `$S inspect` and `$S check` regenerate them from the saved binary and `launch0.csv`.

### 12.7.4 Reading a SASS line [M, H for the operand-block reading]

```
        /*5220*/                   SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT P0, [UR4], R2 ;
        ^addr   ^predicate slot (empty = always; "@!P0" = if not P0; "@UP2" = uniform predicate)
                                   ^mnemonic.modifiers           ^dst   ^address  ^source
```

- `SYNCS.*`: the barrier unit. `PHASECHK.TRANS64` = phase check of a 64-bit transaction barrier; `.TRYWAIT` = the potentially-blocking form; `EXCH.64` = initialise by exchange; `ARRIVE.TRANS64[.RED][.A1T0]` = arrive (`.RED` on a possibly remote word, `A1T0` = 1 arrival and 0 transaction bytes; without `A1T0` the source register carries the transaction count, as in the `expect_tx` with `R5 = 0xc000`).
- `UTC*`: the tensor-core control (TC) pipe: `UTCHMMA` = the MMA, `UTCBAR` = the commit, `UTCATOMSWS` = the TMEM allocator atomics. The Nsight Compute Profiling Guide: "The TC pipeline executes UTCBAR, UTCCP, UTC*MMA, UTCSHIFT and UTC*SWS instructions"; `UTCCP` (`tcgen05.cp`) and `UTCSHIFT` (`tcgen05.shift`) do not occur in this kernel.
- `UTMA*`: the TMA unit: `UTMALDG` load global-to-shared, `UTMASTG` store shared-to-global, `UTMACMDFLUSH` commit group, `UTMACCTL.PF` descriptor prefetch. The operand in the first bracket names the first register of a block of consecutive uniform registers (`{dst, mbarrier, c0, c1, c2}` for a load, `{src, c0, c1, c2}` for a store); the second bracket is the 64-bit tensormap pointer; `desc[URn]` is the 64-bit cache-hint descriptor [H].
- `LDTM.x16 R4, tmem[UR29+0x70]`: a TMEM load of 16 x 32-bit per lane from the lane group and column in `UR29` plus the immediate column offset.
- `UR`, `UP`, `URZ`, `UPT`, `RZ`, `PT`: uniform register, uniform predicate, uniform zero, uniform true, vector zero, vector true.
- The trailing `/* 0x... */` comments (stripped above) are the 128-bit encoding, including the control fields: stall count, yield, read/write scoreboard indices and wait mask (Section 12.1.3). It is where `tcgen05.wait::ld` went; decoding the fields needs third-party tools and is not needed for this course.

### 12.7.5 Attributing the remaining gap to the speed of light [S for the metric definitions, H for the numbers]

The measured 1.2363 x 10^15 FLOP/s is 4.25 kFLOP per cycle per SM over 148 SMs at 1965 MHz, 4.77 k over the 132 active SMs (note D.4). The vendor's dense FP16/BF16 Tensor Core figure for the 1000 W B200 is 2.25 PFLOPS (Lenovo ThinkSystem product guide for the HGX B200 180 GB 1000 W GPU, "2.25 / 4.5 petaFLOPS" without/with sparsity). The ratio is 55 %, but the datasheet conditions are not this run's: the measured power was about 300 W at 1965 MHz, and the datasheet's clock is unknown (if the 2.25 PFLOPS corresponds to 8192 dense FP16 FLOP/cycle/SM, the implied clock is 1.856 GHz and a 256 x 128 x 16 pair-MMA would take 64 cycles against the 106.5 measured [H]). Chapter 3 derives the bound from first principles; what this chapter can give you is the instrument to settle it. Three practicalities first. (a) "Speed Of Light" in `ncu` is the `GPU Speed Of Light Throughput` section: "For each unit, the throughput reports the achieved percentage of utilization with respect to the theoretical maximum" (Profiling Guide), the busiest unit's share of its peak sustained rate, the same notion Chapter 3 applies analytically. (b) `--launch-skip 1 --launch-count 1` count only launches that match `--kernel-name` ("The number takes into account only launches that match the kernel filters"; "The count is only incremented for launches that match the kernel filters", Nsight Compute CLI manual), so launch 0 of the explicit kernel, the harness's warm-up, is skipped and its first timed launch is profiled; the reference GEMM and the compare kernels are not counted. (c) `ncu` locks the GPU clocks while profiling ("Nsight Compute locks SM clocks by default", Profiling Guide, Clock Control): `--clock-control base` locks GPC and memory clocks to the base frequency, and the current CLI manual (v2026.3.1) documents `boost` as the default with a fallback to `base` where boost locking is unsupported (older releases documented `base` as the default; unverified here). Either way the clock can differ from the 1965 MHz of the timing runs, so cycle-based figures will not line up with the 426-cycle budget of Section 12.5.5 unless you pass `--clock-control none` (the guide's recommendation for comparisons with unlocked measurements is to lock the clocks externally with `nvidia-smi` and use `--clock-control none`) and confirm the clock from `sm__cycles_elapsed` against `gpu__time_duration`. Profile one timed launch (the warm-up is launch 0 of the kernel; the reference GEMM and the compare are other kernels):

```
ncu --kernel-name regex:explicit_blackwell --launch-skip 1 --launch-count 1 \
    --section SpeedOfLight --section ComputeWorkloadAnalysis --section WarpStateStats --section MemoryWorkloadAnalysis \
    ./build/examples/70_blackwell_gemm/70_blackwell_fp16_gemm --m=8192 --n=8192 --k=8192
```

and read, in this order:

| Question | Metric or section | What a designer concludes |
|---|---|---|
| Is the tensor pipe busy? | `sm__pipe_tc_cycles_active.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_elapsed` (the TC pipe that executes `UTC*MMA`/`UTCBAR`); also the `sm__pipe_tensor_*` metrics: NVIDIA staff on the developer forum (thread 355164, in the references) state that "A tcgen05 instruction will result in both sm__pipe_tc_cycles_active (singleton per SM) and sm[sp]__pipe_tensor_cycles_active (per SMSP) counters being updated" and that "The TC unit is also responsible for some of the other tcgen05 (not .mma) instructions so activity of TC could exceed Tensor Cycles Active"; the Profiling Guide itself only lists the TC pipe's instructions | if this is near 100 % on the active SMs, the kernel is at the tensor-core speed of light for its clock and the only lever left is the 16 idle SMs and the tail |
| Are the 16 idle SMs visible? | `sm__cycles_active.avg` vs `.max` and `sm__cycles_elapsed`; the `LaunchStats` section (cluster size, waves) | a 10.8 % gap between average and maximum active cycles is the cluster-packing loss, not a kernel bug |
| Where do warps wait? | `WarpStateStats`: `smsp__average_warp_latency_issue_stalled_*` (barrier, long scoreboard, wait, membar, ...) | a leader warp 0 stalled on the `full[s]` barrier means TMA is late (L2/DRAM bound or multicast imbalance); epilogue warps stalled on `acc_full` means the mainloop is the limiter, as designed |
| Is the issue rate anywhere near the limit? | `smsp__issue_active.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_active`, `smsp__inst_executed.sum` | Section 12.5.5 predicts under 15 % on the busiest sub-partition |
| How much traffic? | `lts__t_bytes.sum`, `dram__bytes.sum`, `dram__throughput.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_elapsed` | the operands need 8 GiB of L2-to-SM traffic (1024 cluster tiles x 128 k-tiles x 64 KiB: 32 KiB of A delivered by multicast and 32 KiB of B per cluster per k-tile) in 0.889 ms = about 9.7 TB/s from L2 [H], but only 128 + 128 MiB of unique A and B plus 256 MiB of D from/to DRAM if L2 reuse is perfect (0.6 TB/s against 7.7 TB/s HBM3e); the measured `dram__bytes` tells you how far from perfect |
| Kernel-only time without the host encodes | `nsys profile --stats=true` on the same command, or `gpu__time_duration.sum` in `ncu` | separates the 23 host API calls per iteration from the kernel |

Metric names other than those quoted from the Profiling Guide follow its `unit__(subunit?)_(pipestage?)_quantity_(qualifiers?)` convention and should be checked with `ncu --query-metrics` on the installed version (unverified for CUDA 13.3's Nsight Compute).

## 12.8 Lessons: what "performance-equivalent" required, and what was free

### 12.8.1 Required (the structural contract) [S, M]

| Requirement | Where the explicit kernel does it | Where CUTLASS does it | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rolled k-tile loops in the producer and the MMA warp | `#pragma unroll 1` at explicit.cu:733 and :921 | `CUTLASS_PRAGMA_NO_UNROLL` at sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp:607 and :680 | an unrolled 128-k-tile loop would be 128 x 47 instructions of straight-line code: instruction-cache misses on every tile and no gain, because the loop is not issue-bound (Section 12.5.5) |
| Unrolled k-blocks | `#pragma unroll` at explicit.cu:930 | `CUTLASS_PRAGMA_UNROLL` at :699 | lets ptxas hard-wire `scale_c` to `UPT` for k-blocks 1..3 and lay the four `UTCHMMA` back to back |
| Fully unrolled epilogue subtiles | `#pragma unroll` at explicit.cu:1032 | `#pragma unroll(UnrollEpiLoop ? NumEpiSubtilesN : 1)` at sm100_epilogue_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:818 | the `16 e` term becomes the `LDTM` immediate, the `8192 (e & 3)` the `STS` immediate, the store coordinates compile-time offsets; the single `tcgen05.wait::ld` and release land in subtile 7 by construction |
| Warp-uniform issue operands | every TMA/MMA/commit/query operand from rank, tile, stage, constants | same | otherwise no `U*` lowering, vector address arithmetic and `R2UR` traffic in the loops (Section 12.3) |
| The same barrier protocol: counts, parities, masks, peer-bit addressing, peek-then-wait, four exit tails | Chapters 4, 7-11 | Chapter 4's sources | the protocol **is** the pipeline; a different count or an extra wait changes the overlap, and a missing tail is a use-after-exit hazard |
| Run-time alpha and beta, `t = alpha * acc; d = fmaf(beta, 0, t)` | explicit.cu:1045-1046, `ld.param +528` | the fusion tree's `FMUL`/`FFMA` | bit-identical D including the sign of zero; constant 1.0f/0.0f would fold the pair away (note D.7) |
| TMA issue order wait -> expect_tx -> peek -> A -> B; MMA order wait -> 4 MMAs -> commit; store order fence -> bar.sync -> 4 stores -> commit_group -> wait_group.read 1 -> bar.sync | Sections 12.5.1-12.5.4 | same | the order is what hides latency: the peek is issued before the loads so that the next iteration's wait is usually satisfied |

### 12.8.2 Free to change (and changed) [M]

| Changed | Explicit | CUTLASS | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vector registers | 26 | 68 | none (1 CTA/SM) |
| Parameter block | 640 B, `CONSTANT[0]` 1536 | 2048 B, 2944 | none |
| Role dispatch | `BRXU` jump table (`CONSTANT[2]:12`) | compare-and-branch chain | once per thread; same cost class |
| Barrier inits | 33 (`epi_load`, `load_order` omitted) | 43 | 10 fewer `SYNCS.EXCH.64` in the prologue |
| Prologue length | 175 instructions to the dispatch | 359 | one `SHFL.IDX` instead of 7, four `ULOP3` for the initial tile instead of the rasterisation arithmetic |
| Dead C path | absent | compiled, never executed (32 `UTMALDG.3D`, 128 `LDS`, 8 `expect_tx`, `DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x0`, a third `ACQBULK`) | SASS 1640 vs 3224 instructions |
| Loop-invariant handling | some re-materialised per k-tile (`UMOV`s, mask insert, `tma_b` address) | hoisted, at the price of 44 spill/fill pairs elsewhere | +3 / +6 instructions per k-tile, invisible |
| `k_tiles` | kept in `UR14` | re-read from `c[0x0][0x38c]` per tile | the accumulator acquire/commit block is 15 vs 18 instructions |
| CLC z coordinate | constant 0 (L = 1 kernel by construction; the host guard rejects `l != 1`) | bound to the response's `L_idx` | an L > 1 kernel would restore it |
| Multicast masks | `0x5 << x` and `0xf` from constants | computed from the cluster shape at run time | same values |
| The `elect.sync` count in PTX | 14 | 19 | both become 4-5 `ELECT` in SASS |

### 12.8.3 The measurement protocol itself [M]

Interleave the two binaries run by run on the same day; log clocks at 100 ms and check that every steady-state sample reads the maximum SM clock; compare medians of at least five runs; use tiers (<= +0.2 % accept, <= +0.5 % explain, else fail) and a machine-state gate against a previous day's median (+-0.3 %; here that median came from a different board of the same SKU, note G.0, which is why the gate only checks machine state and never replaces the same-day pair); record the GPU identity with the run; never time a diagnostics build; and keep the instruction inventory as part of the result, because "a single wall-clock number is not sufficient evidence" (note, Section 12). A 0.06 % difference in medians with a 0.15-0.18 % spread is not a speed-up; it is equality.

## Checkpoint

1. The PTX of the MMA warp has four `elect.sync` around the four `tcgen05.mma` and one around the `tcgen05.commit` per k-tile. How many `ELECT` instructions does the MMA loop contain in SASS, and why is it still correct (and still required) to write the elections?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
Zero. `UTCHMMA.2CTA` and `UTCBAR.2CTA.MULTICAST` are uniform-datapath instructions: their operands are uniform registers and the hardware executes them once per warp regardless of how many lanes are active, so predicating them on one lane changes nothing and ptxas removes the election (note D.6 item 6; Section 12.3.2). The kernel's four `ELECT` are in the prologue (`lane_pred`), the alloc handshake and the relinquish lowering, where a per-lane side effect exists. The PTX-level election is still what guarantees one MMA per k-block at the PTX level (the ISA gives `tcgen05.mma` "single thread semantics": every issuing thread starts a whole MMA, so without an election a 32-lane warp would issue it 32 times) and it costs nothing, so it stays.
</details>

2. Explain the eight `UMOV URn, 0x40004040` in the 47-instruction MMA loop: what are they, why eight, and why are they not hoisted?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
They are the constant high word `kSmemDescHi` of the eight 64-bit UMMA shared-memory descriptors used per k-tile: four k-blocks x (A, B). `desc64(kSmemDescHi, lo)` (explicit.cu:616, :933-934) forms each descriptor at the asm boundary, and ptxas keeps each 64-bit operand in a UR pair `{lo, hi}` (`gdesc[UR10]` = `{UR10, UR11}`), so eight high halves must hold the constant. ptxas chose to re-materialise them per k-tile rather than hold eight loop-invariant URs (the CUTLASS kernel's SASS shows the same eight per k-tile, note D.2); the cost is eight uniform issue slots in a 426-cycle k-tile (Section 12.5.5).
</details>

3. `tcgen05.wait::ld` is in the PTX exactly once per tile but has no SASS instruction. Where did the dependency go, and what would happen if you deleted the PTX instruction?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
Into the control-word scoreboards: `LDTM.x16` sets a scoreboard that its first consumer (`FMUL R4` for subtiles 0..6, the `SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED.A1T0` release for subtile 7) waits on, and the `STS` reads set a scoreboard the next `LDTM` waits on (WAR). This is measured for the absence of a wait opcode and inferred for the scoreboard decode (note D.2, G.3). Deleting the PTX `wait::ld` would not endanger the `FMUL`s: the ISA guarantees that "an intra-thread ordering through true register dependency will be respected regardless of the presence or absence of other forms of synchronization", so the arithmetic of every subtile is legal by the ISA's own rule, not by ptxas's grace. What it would remove is the ordering between the eighth load and the `mbarrier.arrive` that releases the TMEM stage to the MMA warp: a register dependency "does not imply any other form of ordering", and "to enforce such memory orderings and avoiding anti-dependency hazards around tcgen05.ld, tcgen05.wait::ld must be used". The arrive is not a register consumer, so without the wait the release could be issued before the loads completed, letting the leader's next `tcgen05.mma` overwrite an accumulator stage still being read. That ptxas happens to chain the arrive to the `LDTM` scoreboard in this build is not a contract.
</details>

4. The explicit kernel uses 26 registers and the CUTLASS kernel 68. Give the register-by-register reason for 26, and state precisely why the difference is worth zero nanoseconds here.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
`R4..R19` are the 16 `LDTM.x16` destinations (one lane's 16 fp32 values of a subtile), `R20..R23` the four lane-dependent `STS` bases carrying the `Swizzle<2,5,2>` term, the low registers per-role scratch and per-lane phase bits (`R9` is the MMA warp's `cons_phase` and the epilogue's `acc_full` parity, `R0` the producer's `prod_phase`), `R1` the (unused) stack pointer; the SASS names 24 registers `R0..R23` and ptxas reports 26, two more than the number named (`R0..R65` = 66 -> 68 for the CUTLASS kernel). The CUTLASS kernel adds the 16-register zero C fragment for the dead beta != 0 path, the `epi_load` state, scheduler bookkeeping in vector registers and 44 uniform-to-vector spill/fill pairs (`R65` -> 68). Occupancy is 1 CTA/SM because of 230400 B of shared memory (and `__launch_bounds__(256, 1)`), so register count cannot change residency; neither kernel spills (`LOCAL 0`); and the hot loops are not issue-bound, so the extra moves of the CUTLASS kernel cost nothing either. The count would matter for multi-CTA/SM kernels or when spills land in a hot loop.
</details>

5. Derive the 426-cycle k-tile budget and show that the busiest warp scheduler is under 15 % utilised.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
0.888 ms for the 32 tiles of a critical-path cluster gives 27.75 us per tile; / 128 k-tiles = 216.8 ns; x 1.965 GHz = 426 cycles (note D.4). Static fast-path instruction counts per k-tile: warp 0 43 (47 minus the skipped wait block), warp 2 33, each epilogue warp 674 / 128 = 5.3, the scheduler 50 / 128 = 0.4. At one issue per cycle per scheduler, a scheduler hosting warps 0 and 4 needs (43 + 5.3) / 426 = 11.3 % of its slots; one hosting 2 and 6 needs 9.0 %. The uniform-datapath instructions of warp 0 do not even compete with the epilogue's vector `FMUL`/`FFMA`/`STS` for execution units.
</details>

6. Why did only 33 clusters become resident on a 148-SM GPU, and what does the kernel do about the resulting 32-vs-31 tile split?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
Each MMA pair must sit on a TPC (SM pair `(2j, 2j + 1)`) and a 2 x 2 cluster needs two TPCs in one GPC; the measured placement shows SM-id groups with an even number of usable TPCs and 8 leftover TPCs (SMs 64, 65, 122-129, 142-147) that cannot be paired, so 33 clusters, not 37 (note D.3, inferred from the `smid` placement). 1024 cluster tiles over 33 clusters is 31.03 per cluster; the CLC scheduler hands tiles out dynamically, so 13 clusters got 32 and 19 got 31 (and the probe-slowed cluster (0, 0) got 19 in the trace build): the kernel does nothing special, the hardware queue balances by construction, and the residual imbalance is one tile (about 3 %).
</details>

7. A colleague runs `cuobjdump --dump-sass` on the whole binary and reports "it has 40 `UTMALDG` and 151 `LDS`, the explicit kernel is bloated". What went wrong, and what are the right numbers?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
They counted the whole binary, which still contains the never-launched CUTLASS kernel (the unchanged `gemm.initialize()` odr-uses it): 40 = 36 + 4 and 151 = 140 + 11 (my recount of `trace_out_v2/sass.txt`, `sass_gemm.txt`, `sass_explicit.txt`). Of the CUTLASS kernel's 36 `UTMALDG`, 32 are the plain `UTMALDG.3D` of its compiled-but-dead C path (the other 4 are its own A/B pairs in the prologue and main loops), and of its 140 `LDS`, 128 are the dead C reads. Cut the explicit kernel out by its `Function :` header (the `awk` in Section 12.7.2 or `$S inspect`): 2 `UTMALDG.3D.MULTICAST.2CTA` + 2 `UTMALDG.3D.2CTA`, 11 `LDS` (4 `LDS.128` CLC decodes + 7 reads of `tmem_base_ptr` and the reserved alloc words), 1640 instructions in total against the CUTLASS kernel's 3224.
</details>

8. What exactly does `Disposition: Passed` prove, and what did the sentinel fill and the 1518 `K_TAIL` records add that it could not?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
`BlockCompareEqual` (70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.cu:378) is an exact comparison of all 2^26 elements of D against the device reference GEMM with the same alpha, beta and C; with integer inputs in [-8, 8] the fp32 result is exact, so `Passed` means value-equal D. It cannot by itself say *why* an element is wrong, and an element never written would hold whatever the buffer held before (zero or stale data from an earlier launch), which could in principle coincide with the reference; so `trace_begin()` fills D with `0xFF` bytes (NaN) first: a skipped element is then certain to fail the compare and is classified as `sentinel` by the mismatch dump (explicit.cu:1377). The `K_TAIL` records (46 per cluster x 33) prove that every role warp's exit tail waited on the predicted `{index, phase}` of every pipeline before the CTA exited, i.e. that no peer could still arrive on a departed CTA's barriers: a hazard that would not necessarily corrupt D on a given run and that the compare therefore cannot see.
</details>

# Chapter 13. Writing It Yourself: Construction Order, Pitfalls, Generalization, and a SOL Recipe

**What you will learn**

- A ten-step construction order that takes you from a blank file to the passing kernel of explicit.cu, where every step produces something you can test and every step removes one class of bug from the suspect list.
- The five design artifacts (tile table, smem map, barrier table, role table, operation ledger) that you write *before* any code, and why a kernel of this kind cannot be debugged without them.
- A pitfall checklist indexed by symptom: which mistake hangs, which one traps, which one gives wrong values, and which one is silently slow, with the line of explicit.cu that avoids each.
- How to generalize this kernel as deltas against the fixed run: residues, L > 1, beta != 0, other data types, other tile and cluster shapes, 1SM MMA, stream-K, swizzled rasterization. Each delta names the lines that change.
- A speed-of-light (SOL) design recipe with the formulas (roofline, FLOP per smem byte, Little's law, barrier-table-first), applied end to end to a 256 x 256 pair-tile FP16 GEMM.
- How to find the same five artifacts in any CUTLASS SM100 kernel so that you can de-abstract the next kernel yourself.

Notation is the lecture's: rank r = x + 2y, pair leader (even r) and peer (r ^ 1), CTA 0 (r = 0), tile (tm, tn) in 128 x 128 CTA-tile units, k-tile q, stage s, k-block kb, accumulator stage st, subtile e, box i, value j, epilogue warp w = warp_idx - 4, lane l, smem_base = 0x400 + (r << 24) (measured), OFF_* as in explicit.cu, T = TMEM base (measured 0). "Measured" means note Parts D or G; "derived" means read from explicit.cu or the CUTLASS sources at the cited lines; "my analysis" means an inference you should re-check on your machine.

Line-number convention for CUTLASS citations: explicit.cu's comments and the note cite CUTLASS at commit cb424739, and so does this chapter. The working tree (HEAD of `dev/gemm-deabstraction`) carries the committed trace-probe blocks of 24419122, which shift `sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp` by +28 lines after :617 (+34 after :760, +40 after :907), `sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp` by +31 after the `fetch_next_work` probes at :446-:480, `mma_sm100_umma.hpp` by +6 after :572 (the K3 probe) and `copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp` by +7 after :420 (the K4a/K4b probes). Examples: the role dispatch `is_participant.main_load` is :617 in cb424739 and :645 at HEAD; `swizzle_and_rasterize` is :697 and :728; `SM100_MMA_F8F6F4_2x1SM_SS` is :1463 and :1469. Everything before those points (the kernel's `SharedStorage`, the pipeline constructors :455-575 including the CLC count at :511-514 and the `tmem_dealloc` init at :560-575; the scheduler's `initial_work_tile_info` :369, `work_tile_info_from_clc_response` :409-436 and its `fence_view_async_shared()` at :430) has the same number in both trees, and the other CUTLASS headers cited here are identical in both. If you `sed` the checkout, apply the shift or read `git show cb424739:<path>`.
