## 13.6 Worked case: the 256 x 256 pair-tile FP16 GEMM

Apply the recipe at the design-table level to the same 8192^3 problem with `MmaTileShape (256, 256, 64)` and cluster (2,2,1): CTA tile 128 (M) x 256 (N) x 64 (K). Everything below is derived with the formulas above unless marked.

### Tile table

| Quantity | Value | Derivation |
|---|---|---|
| MMA instruction | `tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2.kind::f16`, 256 x 256 x 16 | N <= 256, N % 16 == 0 (mma_sm100_umma.hpp:554-555) |
| Instruction descriptor | `0x10400010` | `c_format 1 << 4`, `n_dim (256 >> 3) = 32 << 17 = 0x400000`, `m_dim 16 << 24` (mma_sm100_desc.hpp:420-443) |
| MMAs per k-tile | 4 (K = 64 / 16) | unchanged |
| CTA tile / cluster tile | 128 x 256 x 64 / 256 x 512 | cluster (2,2,1) |
| Cluster tiles | 32 x 16 = 512 | 8192 / 256 by 8192 / 512 |
| Grid | (32, 64, 1) | `ctas_n = round_up(ceil_div(8192, 256), 2) = 32`, `ctas_m = round_up(ceil_div(8192, 256) * 2, 2) = 64`, AlongN transpose (note Section 7.4) |
| Tile formulas | unchanged: `tm = 2 (by >> 1) + (bx & 1)`, `tn = 2 (bx >> 1) + (by & 1)`; CLC `tm = 2 (y0 >> 1) + (x0 & 1) + x`, `tn = 2 (x0 >> 1) + (y0 & 1) + y` | tn is now in units of 256 columns |
| A coordinates / box / mask | `(64 q, 128 tm + 64 y, 0)`, (64, 64, 1) = 8192 B, `0x5 << x`, destination `OFF_SMEM_A + 16384 s + 8192 y` | unchanged |
| B coordinates / box | `(64 q, 256 tn + 128 x, 0)`, one (64, 128, 1) box = 16384 B (or two (64, 64, 1) boxes), destination `OFF_SMEM_B + 16384 s`, no multicast | each CTA loads its 128 of the pair's 256 N columns |
| Tiles per cluster | 512 / 33 = 15.5 -> 16 or 15 | same 3 % quantization as 32 / 31 |

### Smem map

| Offset | Bytes | Content | Why here |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 40 | mainloop full[5] | 5 stages (below) |
| 40 | 40 | mainloop empty[5] | |
| 80 | 16 + 16 | CLC full[2], empty[2] | |
| 112 | 16 + 16 | acc full[2], empty[2] | 2 TMEM stages |
| 144 | 16 + 16 | throttle full[2], empty[2] | |
| 176 | 8 | tmem_dealloc | |
| 192 | 32 | clc_response[2] (16-aligned) | |
| 224 | 4 | tmem_base_ptr | |
| 512 | 4 x 16384 = 65536 | C/D stages, (128, 32) fp32 subtiles, `Swizzle<2,5,2>` | 512-aligned; StagesC = 4 (`ReuseSmem` for 32-bit C: `max(min(8, 4), 3)`, sm100_builder.inl:1112-1114) |
| 66560 | 5 x 16384 = 81920 | A stages | first 1024-aligned offset at or after 66048: the descriptor's `base_offset` is hard-wired to 0 (mma_sm100_desc.hpp:757-758), so SW128 bases *must* be 1 KiB aligned (my design choice; CUTLASS's own struct padding for this shape was not verified) |
| 148480 | 5 x 16384 = 81920 | B stages | 148480 = 145 x 1024 |
| 230400 | | end | <= 232448; by coincidence the same total as the 128 x 128 kernel |

Stage count check with the builder's formula: carveout = 32 (acc pipeline, 2 stages) + 32 (CLC) + 16 (load order) + 8 (dealloc) + 32 (throttle) + 32 (responses) + 8 (TMEM base pointers) = 160 (sm100_pipeline_carveout.inl:45-83); epilogue smem = 65536 + 512 (fusion pad) + 64 (load pipeline) rounded to 512 = 66560; stages = floor((232448 - 160 - 66560) / (16384 + 16384 + 16)) = floor(165728 / 32784) = 5. A sixth stage is about 31 KB short: 6 x 32784 = 196704 against the 165728 available (30976 B) by the builder's formula, or 66560 + 6 x 32768 = 263168 against 232448 (30720 B) by the hand layout; after five stages 1808 B remain.

Three things about this carveout and map that are easy to get wrong. (a) `SchedulerPipelineStageCount` is the compile-time constant 2 for dense GEMM (8 only for grouped and ragged-contiguous grouped GEMM, sm100_umma_builder.inl:283), so the CLC pipeline (32 B), the throttle (32 B), the responses (2 x 16) and the TMEM base pointers (2 x 4) are tile-shape independent; only `AccumulatorPipelineStorage` (16 B per stage) moves with the accumulator stage count, 64 -> 32 here. (b) The map above drops the beta != 0 slots that explicit.cu keeps reserved (`OFF_EPI_LOAD_FULL`/`EMPTY` 128/160 and `OFF_LOAD_ORDER` 192, explicit.cu:141-143); they return with the Section 13.4.3 delta (2 x 32 + 16 bytes), and the carveout figure of 160 still counts the 16-byte load-order barrier for parity with CUTLASS. The stage count does not care: 165728 and 165744 both give 5. (c) The new B stage has to pass the TMA encoder's limits: the (64, 128, 1) fp16 box is 128 B along the inner dimension, which equals the SW128 span and is the most a 128B-swizzled map allows (the `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled` contract of the CUDA driver API: "CU_TENSOR_MAP_SWIZZLE_128B* require the bounding box inner dimension to be <= 128" bytes, quoted in Chapter 3 reference R8 and Chapter 14 Section 14.4.2), by 128 rows, inside the 256-per-dimension box limit that CUTLASS asserts (copy_traits_sm90_tma.hpp:1005-1013, `smem_box_shape[i] <= 256`). The UMMA descriptor's SBO stays 1024 B because the SW128 atom is 8 rows x 128 B however many rows the stage holds, so the high word `0x40004040` is unchanged.

Descriptors for the measured base 0x400: `desc_lo_a = 0x10000 | ((0x400 + 66560) >> 4) = 0x10000 | 0x1080 = 0x11080`, `desc_lo_b = 0x10000 | ((0x400 + 148480) >> 4) = 0x10000 | 0x2480 = 0x12480`; both advance by +1024 per stage (16384 B) and +2 per k-block; the high word stays `0x40004040` (SBO 1024 B, SWIZZLE_128B). The 14-bit field is safe: `(0x400 + 230400) >> 4 = 0x3880 < 0x4000`.

### TMEM map

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Allocation | 512 columns (`tcgen05.alloc.cta_group::2`), base T |
| Accumulator stage st | columns `[256 st, 256 st + 256)`, lanes 0..127; 2 stages |
| MMA D operand | `T + 256 st` |
| Epilogue load | `tcgen05.ld.sync.aligned.32x32b.x32.b32` at `T + ((32 w) << 16) + 256 st + 32 e`, e = 0..7, 32 registers per thread per subtile (or two `.x16` loads) |

### Barrier table

| Pipeline | St. | Full | Empty | Parity rule (n-th use) | Whose barrier | Init warp | Change vs. the 128 x 128 kernel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mainloop | 5 | 1 + **65536** tx (2 x (16384 + 16384): four A halves of 8192 and two B halves of 16384 landing in the pair) | 2, release mask 0xF | consumer `(n / 5) & 1`, producer `1 ^` that | leader's full (peer-bit mask); own empty | 0 | tx and stage count; 128 % 10 != 0, so tiles no longer start at the same stage and phase: the state *must* be carried across tiles (it already is) |
| Accumulator | **2** | 1, commit mask `0x3 << 2y` | 256 | n = tile: `(n / 2) & 1` | own full (pair-multicast commit); leader's empty (peer-bit mask) | 5 | depth; the MMA of tile t + 2 waits for the epilogue of tile t |
| CLC | 2 | 1 + 16 | 800 | n = tile: `(n / 2) & 1` | own full; CTA 0's empty | 4 | none |
| Throttle | 2 | 32 | 32 | n = tile: `(n / 2) & 1` | CTA 0 (both) | 3 | none |
| TMEM dealloc | 1 | 32 | - | parity 0, once | both (each CTA's own, armed by the other) | 0 | none |

Epilogue per subtile e (0..7, 32 columns): `tcgen05.ld` x32 -> 32 `FMUL` + 32 `FFMA` -> 32 `st.shared.b32` at `OFF_SMEM_CD + 16384 (e % 4) + 4096 w + 128 j + 4 ((l & 7) + 8 (((l >> 3) & 3) ^ (j & 3)))` (same `Swizzle<2,5,2>` on byte offsets: bits [7,9) are `j & 3` because `128 j` keeps them, bits [5,7) are `(l >> 3) & 3`) -> `fence.proxy.async` -> `bar.sync 1, 128` -> four TMA stores of (32, 32, 1) = 4096 B boxes from `+ 4096 i` to `(128 tm + 32 i, 256 tn + 32 e, 0)` -> `commit_group` -> `wait_group.read 1` -> `bar.sync 1, 128`. Tails: 5 + 2 + 2 + 1 waits.

### Expected SOL fraction

| Metric | 128 x 128 kernel (measured) | 256 x 256 design (derived) |
|---|---|---|
| FLOP per smem byte (operands) | 85.3 | 128 (1.5x less smem traffic per FLOP) |
| L2 read per SM per k-tile / per FLOP | 16384 B / 2.1 MFLOP = 128 FLOP/B | 24576 B / 4.2 MFLOP = 171 FLOP/B |
| Ideal k-tile time (8192 FLOP/clk/SM, Chapter 3 R2/R3) | 256 cycles | 512 cycles |
| Ring coverage | 8 x 256 = 2048 ideal cycles | 5 x 512 = 2560 ideal cycles (deeper in time despite fewer stages) |
| Accumulator slack | 3 tiles | 1 tile (epilogue must finish within one mainloop tile; it needs a small fraction of that) |
| Wave quantization | 32 / 31.03 | 16 / 15.52, both 97 % |
| Measured / expected | 60 % of the tensor peak per active SM | if the 40 % gap is operand delivery (MMA warp waiting on `full[s]`), this design recovers part of it; if it is the tensor pipe's own issue rate on dependent accumulations, it recovers nothing. The step-9 attribution decides before you write code (hypothesis; the CUTLASS profiler can run this configuration today). |

## 13.7 Reading CUTLASS with this knowledge

For any CUTLASS SM100 GEMM kernel, the five artifacts live in the same five places. Find them in this order, print what is compile-time (`sizeof`, `offsetof`, the CuTe types via `cute::print`), probe what is run-time (descriptors, masks, addresses: the note's K1-K5 method), and only then write wrappers and roles.

| Artifact | Where it is | How to extract |
|---|---|---|
| **Smem struct** | kernel `SharedStorage` (sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:181-212): `pipelines` (one storage per pipeline, `aligned_struct<16>`), `clc_response[]`, `tmem_base_ptr`, `tensors {epilogue, mainloop}`; mainloop `TensorStorage {smem_A, smem_B}` (sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp:223-231); epilogue `smem_C`/`smem_D` union and `TensorStorage` (sm100_epilogue_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:181-218) | host-side `offsetof` ladder (note D.1 D2: `off_smem_A 33792`, ...); alignments from the swizzle atoms (`Swizzle<3,4,3>` -> 1024, `Swizzle<2,5,2>` -> 512) |
| **Pipeline constructors** (the barrier table) | kernel :455-575: mainloop (:457-472), epi_load and load_order (:474-499), CLC (:501-518, the 800/928 count at :511-514), accumulator (:520-536), throttle (:538-550), `tmem_dealloc` (:560-575); the count and mask formulas in sm100_pipeline.hpp (:57-91 release mask, :96-112 peer mask, :565-566 empty count); the state and parity rules in sm90_pipeline.hpp:170-260 | read the `Params` fields set at each site (`producer_arv_count`, `consumer_arv_count`, `transaction_bytes`, `initializing_warp`); confirm in the SASS `SYNCS.EXCH.64` init words (note D.2) |
| **Role dispatch** | kernel :419-454 (`WarpCategory`, `IsParticipant`), then the branch chain: `main_load` :617, `sched` :681, `mma` :726, `epi_load` :807, `epilogue` :869 (cb424739; :645, :709, :754, :841, :903 at HEAD) | note which warps fall through (here warp 3 and warp 1 of ranks 1-3) and which named-barrier populations result |
| **Load / MMA / store loops** | `CollectiveMma::load` (sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp:589-629) and `::mma` (:651-712); `CollectiveEpilogue::load` (sm100_epilogue_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:461-550), `::store` (:573-956), `::store_tail` (:1269-1291) | the peek/wait/`expect_tx`/issue order, the `CUTLASS_PRAGMA_NO_UNROLL` loops, the `ScaleOut` handling, the `ReuseSmemC` release lag; the PTX strings behind `copy()` and `cute::gemm()` are in cute/arch (copy_sm100_tma.hpp, copy_sm90_tma.hpp, mma_sm100_umma.hpp, mma_sm100_desc.hpp) and cutlass/arch/barrier.h |
| **Scheduler** | sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp: initial tile :365-371, `issue_clc_query` :392-405, `work_tile_info_from_clc_response` :409-436, `advance_to_next_work` :438-451, `swizzle_and_rasterize` :697-814 (remap at :788-789); the CLC pipeline in sm100_pipeline.hpp; the consumption points in the kernel (`fetch_next_work` at :665, :702, :742, :878, and :820 for the C producer; the fetched tile becomes current at :670-671, :774-775, :932-933, note Section 7.4) | the mapping formulas (note B.4), the throttle (kernel :632-636), and the measured dynamics (note D.3) |

Three checks that keep a de-abstraction honest, whatever the kernel: the inventory (Section 13.2 step 9) must match the baseline's *executed* path, not its whole binary (the CUTLASS kernel compiles 32 C loads and 128 C reads it never executes for beta = 0: note D.7); the probes must be guarded and barrier-free (note C.1); and every measured value that the kernel could compute at run time (the smem base, the TMEM base, the number of native clusters, the hand-out order) must be computed, never assumed (note D.7; explicit.cu:1098, 888).

## Checkpoint

**1.** Every leader's warp 0 hangs at `WAIT_MAINLOOP_FULL` with q = 0 in the trace build; the peers' producers are not stuck. Rank the causes and name the probe for each.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
Four candidates, all in the producer's first k-tile (note E.7.2 failure-mode table): (1) the transaction count is not 49152 (for example 24576 = one CTA's share instead of the pair's; explicit.cu:180); (2) the TMA barrier operand is not peer-bit-masked, so the peer's two boxes credit the peer's own, never-armed `full[s]` and the leader's barrier waits for bytes that never come (explicit.cu:770); (3) the A multicast mask is wrong (not `0x5 << x`, explicit.cu:772), so a half lands in the wrong CTA and the pair's byte total is wrong; (4) a non-leader lane performs the `arrive.expect_tx` (explicit.cu:736 requires `is_leader_lane`). The K4a records (coordinates, destination, unmasked barrier address per TMA) and the K1 record (`base & 0xFEFFFFFF` is the even partner's base) separate them; the hang record itself gives the barrier address and parity.
</details>

**2.** The mainloop empty barrier has count 2 and the accumulator empty barrier count 256, although both are "released by the consumer". Why the difference?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
A `tcgen05.commit` arrives *once per issuing thread per CTA in its mask*. The ISA basis: ".mbarrier::arrive::one indicates that upon the completion of the prior asynchronous tcgen05 operation issued by the current thread, an arrive-on operation, with the count argument of 1, is signaled on the mbarrier object. The scope of the arrive-on operation is the cluster scope", and with `.multicast::cluster` "The mbarrier signal is multicast to the same offset as mbar in the shared memory of each destination CTA" named by `ctaMask`, whose bit positions are `%cluster_ctarank`s (PTX ISA 9.4, tcgen05.commit). So the mainloop release is one commit from each of the two pair leaders with mask 0xF, and every CTA's `empty[s]` receives exactly two arrivals (count = 2/2 + 2/1 - 1, sm100_pipeline.hpp:565-566). The accumulator release is not a commit but a plain `mbarrier.arrive.shared::cluster` executed by every one of the 128 epilogue threads of both CTAs on the leader's barrier through the peer-bit-masked address (barrier.h:905-921; note Section 13 item 1), hence 256. Counting the arriving *agents* is the rule of Section 13.5 step 6.
</details>

**3.** Derive the mainloop stage count for the 256 x 256 pair tile with fp32 C/D and cluster (2,2,1).

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
A stage = 128 x 64 x 2 = 16384 B, B stage = 128 x 64 x 2 = 16384 B, plus 16 B of pipeline storage: 32784 B per stage. Epilogue smem: tile (128, 32) (`N_perf = 32` for 32-bit C with CtaN > 128), 4 stages x 16384 = 65536, plus the 512-byte fusion pad and 64 B of load-pipeline storage, rounded to 512: 66560. Carveout 160 (2 accumulator stages). Stages = floor((232448 - 160 - 66560) / 32784) = floor(165728 / 32784) = 5. Laid out with 1 KiB alignment of the A base the total is 66560 + 2 x 81920 = 230400 (Section 13.6).
</details>

**4.** For FP8 e4m3 operands with the same 256 x 128 x 64 MMA tile, what changes in the MMA loop and the descriptors, and what stays?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
Instruction `kind::f8f6f4` (mma_sm100_umma.hpp:1484); K per instruction 32 (32 bytes per operand row), so 2 MMAs per 64-wide k-tile instead of 4; the k-block increment in the descriptor low word stays +2 because a k-block is still 32 B; the instruction-descriptor *value* stays 0x10200010 because E4M3 = 0 in the `MXF8F6F4Format` enum, but it is now read under the f8f6f4 kind; the smem atom falls from SW128 to SW64 because 64 fp8 elements are 64 bytes (`layout_type = 4`, SBO 512 B, bases 512-aligned, TMA swizzle 64B); stage bytes 8192 + 4096, transaction count 24576 per pair; the stage count is recomputed from the budget, and the epilogue is a different design (8-bit output with scaling and amax).
</details>

**5.** Why do producers start at phase 1 and consumers at phase 0, and what is the symptom of swapping them?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
A freshly initialised mbarrier is in phase 0. `try_wait.parity` with parity p returns true when the phase with parity p has *completed*, and the hardware treats "the previous phase" (parity 1 before any completion) as complete, so a producer waiting parity 1 on an empty ring passes immediately, as it should (the stages are free). A consumer starting at parity 1 would also pass immediately and read a stage that has not been filled: wrong values. A producer starting at parity 0 would wait for a completion that requires its own data: a hang at the first wait (Section 13.3 row 2; note Section 7.2; explicit.cu:723-726).
</details>

**6.** Warp 2 consumes the CLC response after issuing the current tile's loads, warps 0 and 4-7 before computing or storing the current tile, and in every role the fetched tile becomes current only at the end of the loop body. What breaks if warp 2 consumed before its loads and switched tiles immediately?

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
Nothing hangs: the 800 arrivals per response are still delivered, one per participating warp. But the producer would load tile t + 1's A and B while the MMA warp commits the result as tile t and the epilogue stores it under tile t's coordinates, so every tile after the launch tile would hold another tile's product: the mismatch map shows `#` tiles with "tile (tm, tn) holds the reference of tile (tm', tn')" (Section 13.3 row 16; note Sections 7.4 and 7.9; explicit.cu:793-794).
</details>

**7.** A kernel passes `Disposition: Passed` on the fixed command. Name three defects that this cannot detect and the check that catches each.

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
(1) A different arithmetic (folded `alpha * acc`, a dropped `fmaf`, a different MMA sequence): the data are integers in [-8, 8], so any summation order is exact; catch it with the PTX/SASS inventory (128 `FMUL` + 128 `FFMA`, 0 `FADD`) and a bitwise compare on non-integer data (Section 13.5 step 8). (2) A coverage defect that writes a tile twice with identical values, or leaves stale correct values from a previous run in D: catch it with the sentinel fill (0xFF -> NaN) and the K5 exactly-once check. (3) A dropped tail or a missing dealloc handshake, which is an intermittent exit race: catch it with five consecutive runs, the "Passed then hang at iteration 2" symptom, and the 46 `K_TAIL` records per cluster.
</details>

**8.** Write the barrier table for the 1SM variant (cluster 1 x 1 x 1, CTA tile 128 x 128 x 64).

<details><summary>Answer</summary>
Mainloop: full count 1 + 32768 tx (A 16384 + B 16384, both loaded by this CTA), empty count 1 (1/1 + 1/1 - 1), released by `tcgen05.commit.cta_group::1.mbarrier::arrive::one.shared::cluster.b64` without multicast; accumulator: full 1 (local commit), empty 128 (plain local arrives of the four epilogue warps); CLC: full 1 + 16 tx, empty 32 + 1 x (32 + 128 + 32) = 224; throttle 32 / 32; no `tmem_dealloc` handshake (no peer); no peer-bit mask anywhere, `tcgen05.alloc/dealloc.cta_group::1`, and the MMA instruction `tcgen05.mma.cta_group::1.kind::f16` with four disable-mask registers (Section 13.4.6).
</details>

- Lenovo Press, *ThinkSystem NVIDIA HGX B200 180GB 1000W GPU Product Guide* (https://lenovopress.lenovo.com/lp2226-thinksystem-nvidia-b200-180gb-1000w-gpu): FP16/BF16 Tensor Core 2.25 / 4.5 PFLOPS (without / with structural sparsity), FP8 4.5 / 9, TF32 1.1 / 2.2, 180 GB HBM3e, 7.7 TB/s, 1000 W.
- Colfax Research, *CUTLASS Tutorial: Writing GEMM Kernels Using Tensor Memory For NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs* (https://research.colfax-intl.com/cutlass-tutorial-writing-gemm-kernels-using-tensor-memory-for-nvidia-blackwell-gpus/): TMEM is 256 KB per SM, 512 columns x 128 lanes of 32-bit cells; each warp of a warpgroup accesses 32 lanes; allocation columns a power of two >= 32 from a single warp; K is 32 bytes wide for dense GEMM.
- Colfax Research, *Dynamic persistent tile scheduling with Cluster Launch Control (CLC) on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs* (https://research.colfax-intl.com/dynamic-persistent-tile-scheduling-with-cluster-launch-control-clc-on-nvidia-blackwell-gpus/): one issuing thread per cluster; the 16-byte response; no further `try_cancel` after a failure.
- CUDA C++ Programming Guide 13.1, *Work Stealing with Cluster Launch Control* (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.1.0/cuda-programming-guide/04-special-topics/cluster-launch-control.html): compute capability 10.0; "Submitting another cancellation request after observing a previously failed request is undefined behavior."
- PTX ISA 9.4 (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/), read from a local text extraction of the single-page document. The passages quoted above are from the sections on `cp.async.bulk.tensor` (the `.cta_group::2` parity routing of the mbarrier signal; the `completeCount` wording), `tcgen05.commit` (`.mbarrier::arrive::one`, `.multicast::cluster`, and "All tcgen05 instructions within a kernel must specify the same value for the .cta_group qualifier"), `tcgen05.alloc` (the two `nCols` forms), 9.7.18.8.1 "Access restrictions" (the 32-lane rule), `clusterlaunchcontrol.try_cancel` (the response written to each CTA's local `addr`, the exit rule and the repeat-after-failure rule) and `barrier{.cta}` (exited threads do not participate).

# Chapter 14. Exercises, Glossary, and References

**What you will learn**

- How to test yourself on the whole lecture: 34 exercises in four grades (RECALL, DERIVE, MODIFY, DESIGN), each with a worked answer that recomputes every number from the formulas in `explicit.cu` and says which facts are measured, which are derived from source, and which are analysis.
- The exact meaning of every term and acronym the lecture uses (TMEM, tcgen05/UMMA, TMA, CLC, mbarrier tx-count, parity, proxies, DSMEM, peer-bit mask, SW128, k-tile/k-block/stage/subtile, bulk group, named barrier, uniform datapath, scoreboard, carveout, ...), one to three precise sentences each.
- Where every fact came from: the PTX ISA sections and CUDA Programming Guide pages that were consulted, the CUTLASS files and line anchors cited throughout the lecture, the note's Parts, and the articles that were opened and found accurate.
- A one-page numbers card: every constant of the kernel (counts, offsets, masks, descriptors, coordinates, byte totals, measured results) in one place, so that you can rewrite the kernel from a blank file without re-deriving the arithmetic.

Provenance tags used in every answer of this chapter:

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **[S]** | derived from source: `explicit.cu`, `explicit.hpp`, `util.hpp`, or the CUTLASS headers at commit cb424739 (file:line cited) |
| **[M]** | measured on the B200, taken from the note Parts D and G (section cited) |
| **[A]** | my analysis or hypothesis: follows from [S]/[M] facts by reasoning, not itself verified by a run |
| **[S/A]** | a source fact plus my inference about its consequence (the sentence says which half is which) |
| **[M/A]** | a measured number plus my arithmetic on it (e.g. a rate derived from `Avg runtime`) |

Notation is the lecture's: rank `r = x + 2y` with `(x, y) = %cluster_ctaid`; "pair leader" = even rank, "peer" = `r ^ 1`; "CTA 0" = rank 0; CTA tile `(tm, tn)` in 128 x 128 units; k-tile `q` (0..127); smem stage `s` (0..7); k-block `kb` (0..3); accumulator stage `st` (0..3); subtile `e` (0..7); store box `i` (0..3); value index `j` (0..15); epilogue warp `w = warp_idx - 4`; lane `l`; `smem_base = 0x400 + (r << 24)` [M]; `T` = TMEM base (measured 0) [M].

---

## 14.1 How to use this chapter

Work the exercises in order inside each grade, but feel free to interleave grades. RECALL exercises check that the kernel's constants and their reasons are in your head (Chapters 4, 5). DERIVE exercises make you run the kernel's address and parity arithmetic by hand for concrete `(rank, tile, q, s, kb, w, l, j, e)` values (Chapters 6-10). MODIFY exercises ask what breaks, hangs, or merely slows down when one line changes (Chapters 4, 7-11, 13). DESIGN exercises re-run the Chapter 3 / Chapter 13 method on a different shape, cluster, or epilogue. Every numeric answer was recomputed with a script from the formulas quoted from `explicit.cu`; where a formula line exists, it is quoted verbatim with its line number.

If you can do all DERIVE exercises without opening the file, and all MODIFY exercises without hesitating about *which* barrier count changes, you are ready to write the kernel from scratch (Chapter 13).

## 14.2 Exercises

### 14.2.1 RECALL

**R1. What does each `OFF_*` constant hold, how large is the region, and why is it at that offset?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

The shared-memory map is `explicit.cu:139-155` [S], quoted verbatim:

```
constexpr uint32_t OFF_MAIN_FULL      =      0;   // 8 x 8 B ClusterTransactionBarrier, count 1
constexpr uint32_t OFF_MAIN_EMPTY     =     64;   // 8 x 8 B ClusterBarrier, count 2
constexpr uint32_t OFF_EPI_LOAD_FULL  =    128;   // 4 x 8 B (beta != 0 only; reserved, not initialised: E.10 item 6)
constexpr uint32_t OFF_EPI_LOAD_EMPTY =    160;   // 4 x 8 B (idem)
constexpr uint32_t OFF_LOAD_ORDER     =    192;   // 2 x 8 B (idem)
constexpr uint32_t OFF_CLC_FULL       =    208;   // 2 x 8 B, count 1 (+16 tx bytes)
constexpr uint32_t OFF_CLC_EMPTY      =    224;   // 2 x 8 B, count 800 (only CTA 0's are used)
constexpr uint32_t OFF_ACC_FULL       =    240;   // 4 x 8 B, count 1
constexpr uint32_t OFF_ACC_EMPTY      =    272;   // 4 x 8 B, count 256
constexpr uint32_t OFF_THROTTLE_FULL  =    304;   // 2 x 8 B, count 32
constexpr uint32_t OFF_THROTTLE_EMPTY =    320;   // 2 x 8 B, count 32
constexpr uint32_t OFF_TMEM_DEALLOC   =    336;   // 1 x 8 B, count 32
constexpr uint32_t OFF_CLC_RESPONSE   =    352;   // 2 x 16 B, alignas(16)
constexpr uint32_t OFF_TMEM_BASE_PTR  =    384;   // 4 B, written by tcgen05.alloc
constexpr uint32_t OFF_SMEM_CD        =    512;   // 4 x 8192 B, Swizzle<2,5,2>, 512-byte aligned
constexpr uint32_t OFF_SMEM_A         =  33792;   // 8 x 16384 B, Swizzle<3,4,3>, 1024-byte aligned
constexpr uint32_t OFF_SMEM_B         = 164864;   // 8 x  8192 B, idem
```

Why these offsets [S, note Section 6.2]: the layout is the CUTLASS `SharedStorage` of `sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:181-212` laid out by the C++ rules. The 8-byte barriers are packed in declaration order (mainloop 16 barriers = 128 B, epi_load 8 = 64 B, load_order 2 = 16 B, CLC 4 = 32 B, accumulator 8 = 64 B, throttle 4 = 32 B, tmem_dealloc 1 = 8 B, total 344 B), padded to 352 because the `PipelineStorage` is a 16-byte-aligned struct; the two 16-byte CLC responses follow (352, 368); the 4-byte `tmem_base_ptr` sits at 384; then the tensor storage needs 512-byte alignment (the `Swizzle<2,5,2>` epilogue atom spans 512 B), so it starts at 512. The epilogue storage is 4 x 8192 = 32768 B plus an empty `FusionStorage` padded to the 512-byte alignment of the epilogue struct (`static_assert` at `explicit.cu:158`: `OFF_SMEM_A == OFF_SMEM_CD + kEpiStages * kEpiStageBytes + 512`), so A begins at 33792 = 33 x 1024, which satisfies the 1024-byte alignment that the SW128 atom (8 rows x 128 B) requires; B follows A's 8 x 16384 = 131072 B at 164864 = 161 x 1024 (`explicit.cu:159`); the end is 164864 + 8 x 8192 = 230400 = `kSmemBytes` (`explicit.cu:160`). The three beta != 0 regions (128..207) are reserved but never initialised in this kernel (33 inits instead of 43).

The whole map is relative to each CTA's own `smem_base = 0x400 + (r << 24)` [M, note D.1 D5]: 0x400 because 1 KiB of system-reserved shared memory precedes the dynamic buffer; `r << 24` because the compiler places the cluster rank in address byte 3.
</details>

**R2. State the arrive count and, where applicable, the transaction byte count of every barrier the kernel initialises, and say why each count is what it is.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

Constants at `explicit.cu:180-185` [S]:

```
constexpr uint32_t kMainloopTxBytes  = 2 * (kStageBytesA + kStageBytesB);   // 49152: six 8192-byte boxes per stage credit the leader
constexpr uint32_t kClcTxBytes       = 16;
constexpr uint32_t kMainFullCount    = 1, kMainEmptyCount = 2;      // 2/2 + 2/1 - 1
constexpr uint32_t kClcFullCount     = 1, kClcEmptyCount  = 800;    // 32 + 4 * (32 + 128 + 32); beta = 0
constexpr uint32_t kAccFullCount     = 1, kAccEmptyCount  = 256;    // 2 x 128 epilogue threads
constexpr uint32_t kThrottleCount    = 32, kTmemDeallocCount = 32;
```

| Barrier (x slots) | Count | tx bytes | Why [S, note 7.2] |
|---|---|---|---|
| mainloop full[8] | 1 | 49152 | One `mbarrier.arrive.expect_tx` by the pair leader's elected lane of warp 2 (`explicit.cu:736`); the bytes are the six 8192-byte TMA boxes that land in the two CTAs of the pair per stage: four A boxes (one from each of the 4 CTAs, each multicast to 2 CTAs, so each pair receives 4) and two B boxes; 2 x (16384 + 8192) = 49152. The peer's boxes credit the leader's barrier through the peer-bit-masked address. |
| mainloop empty[8] | 2 | - | Two `tcgen05.commit ... multicast::cluster` with mask 0xF arrive in every CTA per k-tile: one from each pair leader. CUTLASS writes it as `2/2 + 2/1 - 1` = (cluster M / atom M) + (cluster N / atom N) - 1; the source is `PipelineTmaUmmaAsync::init_barriers` (`include/cutlass/pipeline/sm100_pipeline.hpp:559-573`, formula at `:563-564`: `multicast_consumer_arrival_count = (size<0>(cluster_shape) / size<0>(atom_thr_shape)) + (size<1>(cluster_shape) / size<1>(atom_thr_shape)) - 1`, with cluster (2,2,1) and atom (2,1,1)). Both leaders must release because CTA x multicasts its A half into CTA x+2's smem, which the *other* pair's MMA reads. |
| CLC full[2] | 1 | 16 | One `arrive.expect_tx` per CTA (lanes 0..3 of rank 0's warp 1 arm CTAs 0..3 remotely, `explicit.cu:842`); the 16-byte `try_cancel` response is multicast to all CTAs and completes each CTA's own full barrier. |
| CLC empty[2] | 800 | - | Every consuming thread arrives remotely on CTA 0's barrier: 32 (rank 0 warp 1) + 4 CTAs x (32 warp 0 + 32 warp 2 + 128 warps 4-7) = 800. With beta != 0 warp 3 joins: 928. |
| accumulator full[4] | 1 | - | One `tcgen05.commit` by the leader with the pair mask `0x3 << 2y` (`explicit.cu:944`); it arrives in both CTAs of the pair. |
| accumulator empty[4] | 256 | - | Every epilogue thread of both CTAs (2 x 128) arrives on the LEADER's barrier via the peer-bit mask (`explicit.cu:1039`); the peer's acc_empty barriers are initialised but never used. |
| throttle full[2] / empty[2] | 32 / 32 | - | Whole-warp local arrive by rank 0's warp 2 at tile start / whole-warp remote arrive by rank 0's warp 1 after it consumed the throttle; rank 0 only. |
| tmem_dealloc | 32 | - | One whole-warp remote arrive (32 lanes) by the peer's warp 0, then by the leader's warp 0, in the exit handshake (`explicit.cu:964,970`). |

Total: 8+8+2+2+4+4+2+2+1 = 33 `mbarrier.init` [M, note G.3: 33 `SYNCS.EXCH.64`].

Why the transaction barriers tolerate bytes arriving *before* the `expect_tx` [S, PTX ISA 9.4]: the producer's order is wait `empty[s]` -> `mbarrier.arrive.expect_tx 49152` by the leader lane -> two TMA issues (`explicit.cu:735-748`), but the peer's three boxes, and even the leader's own, may complete before the leader lane's `expect_tx` executes (the peer runs an independent warp). This is safe because of three ISA rules: (1) the tx-count is a signed counter with range `-(2^20 - 1) .. 2^20 - 1` (section 9.7.15.16.3, Table 43), so `complete-tx` operations may drive it negative (down to -49152 here, well inside the range) before the matching `expect-tx` adds the expected bytes back (9.7.15.16.6.1 "expect-tx operation increases the tx-count", 9.7.15.16.6.2 "complete-tx ... tx-count is decremented"); (2) a phase completes only when "the count of the pending arrivals has reached zero" AND "the tx-count has reached zero" (9.7.15.16.8); (3) the single arrival (count 1) is fused with the byte expectation in `arrive.expect_tx`, so the pending-arrival count cannot reach zero until the `expect_tx` has executed, whatever the order of the 48 KiB of completions. The same argument covers the CLC `full[]` (count 1 + 16 bytes: the remote `arrive.expect_tx` from rank 0's lanes 0..3 and the multicast response's 16-byte `complete_tx` may arrive in either order). When the arrival and the expectation are separate operations, as in the C-load pipeline (G2: one bare `expect_tx`, 32 plain arrives), the same rules require only that the last arrival cannot precede the `expect_tx`; CUTLASS orders them TMA issue -> `expect_tx` (one thread) -> 32 arrives within the one issuing warp (`sm100_epilogue_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:528-541`), so the bytes may land early (tx-count negative) but the phase cannot close before the expectation is registered.
</details>

**R3. Which warp plays which role, and why does the kernel have exactly 256 threads?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

Dispatch at `explicit.cu:1191-1203` [S]: warp 2 = producer (TMA loads); warp 1 of rank 0 = CLC scheduler (warp 1 of ranks 1-3 exits); warp 0 = MMA (TMEM alloc, UMMA, commits, dealloc); warps 4-7 = epilogue; warp 3 = the beta != 0 C-load warp, prefetches `tma_c`/`tma_d` and exits. 256 threads = 8 warps because the epilogue needs exactly 4 warps (`tcgen05.ld` lets warp `w % 4` read TMEM lanes `[32 w, 32 w + 32)`, so 4 warps cover the 128 accumulator rows) and the three single-warp roles plus the idle warp 3 fill the first warpgroup; `__launch_bounds__(256, 1)` (`explicit.cu:1095`) tells ptxas the block has at most 256 threads and that it should budget registers for *at least* 1 resident CTA per SM (the second argument is `minBlocksPerMultiprocessor`, a lower bound used for register allocation, up to 255 registers per thread; it does not cap residency). Residency is in fact 1 CTA per SM because two CTAs would need 2 x 230400 B > 232448 B of opt-in shared memory [S, note 6.2]. Named barrier 6 counts 160 = 32 (warp 0 arrives) + 128 (warps 4-7 sync) threads, which is why `kTmemAllocBarThreads = 160` (`explicit.cu:191`).
</details>

**R4. What are the three multicast / commit masks and what does each bit mean?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[S] `explicit.cu:772` `a_mcast_mask = 0x5 << x`: bits for ranks `x` and `x + 2`, the two CTAs that share `tm` and therefore the same 128 A rows; each contributes a 64-row half (`+ 8192 y` destination offset, `explicit.cu:768`). B is not multicast: the pair's 2SM MMA reads both CTAs' B halves directly. `explicit.cu:186` `kMainloopReleaseMask = 0xF`: the leader's `tcgen05.commit` releases `empty[s]` in all four CTAs (see R2). `explicit.cu:902` `acc_commit_mask = 0x3 << (2 y)`: the pair {2y, 2y+1}, i.e. 0x3 for ranks {0,1} and 0xC for ranks {2,3}. Bit `k` of every mask is rank `k` = `x + 2y` (the cluster's row-major CTA layout). All three are 16-bit `"h"` operands [S]; measured register values 0x5/0xA, 0xF, 0x3/0xC [M, note D.2].
</details>

**R5. What is the peer-bit mask, where is it applied, and what is the difference between 0xFEFFFFFF and 0xFEFFFFF8?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

`explicit.cu:187` [S]: `kPeerBitMask = 0xFEFFFFFFu` (= `cute::Sm100MmaPeerBitMask`, `include/cute/arch/copy_sm100_tma.hpp:45` [S]). Clearing bit 24 of a 32-bit `shared::cta` address clears bit 0 of the rank that the compiler stores in byte 3, so the odd CTA's address of barrier X becomes the even CTA's address of the same barrier; the pair leader's address is unchanged. Applied in two places: the TMA barrier operand (`full_masked_base = smem_base & kPeerBitMask`, `explicit.cu:770`, so all six boxes of a stage credit the leader's `full[s]`) and the accumulator release (`explicit.cu:371`, `bar_intptr = smem_addr & kPeerBitMask`, so 256 epilogue threads arrive on the leader's `acc_empty[st]`). 0xFEFFFFF8 is what nvcc emits: the three low bits of an 8-byte-aligned barrier address are known zero, so the compiler folds them into the constant (`and.b32 %r, %r, -16777224`) [M, note 7.2]; in the explicit kernel's SASS the literal survives at the epilogue release, while the producer's copy is folded further to 0xFEFFFFF0 on the 1024-byte-aligned base [M, note G.3]. Validity rests on the measured address convention `smem_base = 0x400 + (r << 24)` and `mapa(base_r, t) == base_t` [M, D.1 D5]; the Colfax cluster tutorial states the same rule ("setting the 24th bit to 0").
</details>

**R6. Why does a producer start at `{index 0, phase 1}` and a consumer at `{0, 0}`?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[S] `explicit.cu:724` `uint32_t prod_idx = 0, prod_phase = 1;` and `explicit.cu:903` `uint32_t cons_idx = 0, cons_phase = 0;` mirror `make_producer_start_state` (`include/cutlass/pipeline/sm90_pipeline.hpp:254-260`). A freshly initialised mbarrier is in phase 0. `mbarrier.try_wait.parity P` succeeds when the phase of parity P has completed, i.e. when the barrier's current phase parity differs from P. Waiting with parity 1 on a fresh barrier therefore succeeds at once (the "previous" phase, of parity 1, counts as complete), so the producer's first pass over the 8 empty stages never blocks; the consumer's parity-0 wait blocks until the first fill completes phase 0. `advance` (`explicit.cu:612`: `if (++idx == Stages) { idx = 0; phase ^= 1; }`) flips the parity at each wrap, so for the n-th use of a stage (n = 0, 1, ...) the consumer waits parity `n & 1` and the producer `1 ^ (n & 1)`.
</details>

**R7. Give the UMMA shared-memory descriptor and instruction descriptor constants and decode their fields.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

`explicit.cu:171-173` [S]:

```
constexpr uint32_t kSmemDescHi  = 0x40004040u;   // SBO = 64 (1024 B) at [32,46), version = 1 at [46,48), layout_type = 2 (SWIZZLE_128B) at [61,64)
constexpr uint32_t kSmemDescLo0 = 0x00010000u;   // LBO = 1 (16 B) at [16,30); start address (addr >> 4) & 0x3FFF is OR'ed in at run time
constexpr uint32_t kInstrDesc   = kInstrDescConst;   // 0x10200010: c_format F32 (bit 4), n_dim 128 >> 3 = 16 at [17,23), m_dim 256 >> 4 = 16 at [24,29)
```

Smem descriptor (bit map `include/cute/arch/mma_sm100_desc.hpp:101-127` [S]): bits [0,14) start address in 16-byte units (`(addr >> 4) & 0x3FFF`, assigned by `static_cast<uint16_t>(start_address >> 4)` at `:755`, which drops the rank bits so the leader and the peer form identical descriptors); [16,30) leading byte offset = 1 (16 B): for a K-major swizzled layout the ISA says the leading-dimension stride is "not used, assumed to be 1" and its example table gives "Encoding of LBO in descriptor: 1 (assumed)" (PTX ISA 9.4 section 9.7.18.3.1.1 "Relative offset mode"; field position bits 16-30 in Table 49, section 9.7.18.4.1), and CUTLASS fixes it to 1 for every swizzled K-major canonical layout (`mma_sm100_desc.hpp:822-832`: `static_assert(stride_10 == expected_stride_10)` with `expected_stride_10 = 1`, then `desc.leading_byte_offset_ = stride_10`); [32,46) stride byte offset = 64 (1024 B: the distance between consecutive 8-row groups of a 128-byte-row SW128 atom); [46,48) version = 1; [61,64) layout type = 2 = SWIZZLE_128B. High word: `64 | (1 << 14) | (2 << 29)` = 0x40004040 (`static_assert` at `explicit.cu:175`). Instruction descriptor (`mma_sm100_desc.hpp:416-443` [S]): bits [4,6) c_format = 1 (F32) -> 0x10; a/b formats 0 (F16); a/b major 0 (K-major); [17,23) n_dim = 128 >> 3 = 16 -> 0x200000; [24,29) m_dim = 256 >> 4 = 16 -> 0x10000000; total 0x10200010 (`static_assert` at `explicit.cu:176`). Measured first-MMA values `desc_a = 0x4000404000010880`, `desc_b = 0x4000404000012880`, `idesc = 0x10200010` [M, D.1 D7].
</details>

**R8. What is the TMA box of each tensor map and why?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[S, note Section 5.3, D.1 D3 (measured encodes)]: A and B: FLOAT16, rank 3, shape (8192, 8192, 1), strides (16384 B, 0), box (64, 64, 1) = 8192 B, SWIZZLE_128B, L2 promotion 128 B. The inner box dimension is 64 fp16 = 128 B, the maximum inner extent of SWIZZLE_128B (CUDA Programming Guide 4.12.2.2.5: inner dimension <= 128 bytes); the outer 64 rows are one CTA's half of the 128-row A stage (multicast assembles the two halves) and one CTA's 64 B columns. C and D: FLOAT32, shape (8192, 8192, 1), strides (32768 B, 0), box (32, 16, 1) = 2048 B, SWIZZLE_128B_ATOM_32B: the inner 32 fp32 = 128 B again fills the swizzle span, 16 columns is the epilogue subtile width, and four boxes `i = 0..3` cover the 128 rows of a subtile (`explicit.cu:1056`: `c0 = 128 * tm + 32 * i`). The coordinates are (innermost, outer, batch) in elements: (k, row, 0) for A/B, (m, n, 0) for D.
</details>

**R9. Why does the kernel read `alpha` and `beta` at run time although they are always 1 and 0?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[S, note Section 0 and 8] The harness compares D bit-exactly with a reference that computes `t = alpha * acc; d = fmaf(beta, c, t)`. `explicit.cu:1045-1046`:

```
        float const t = alpha * __uint_as_float(r[j]);
        float const d = fmaf(beta, 0.0f, t);
```

With run-time operands nvcc emits exactly one FMUL and one FFMA per element (128 + 128 per tile, 0 FADD) [M, G.3], the baseline's own instruction shape. With `constexpr` 1.0f/0.0f the compiler would fold `1.0f * acc` to `acc` and `fmaf(0, 0, t)` to `+0.0f + t` (an FADD; not to `t`, because `+0.0 + (-0.0) = +0.0`), changing the instruction inventory that the equivalence contract (note Section 12, D.7) requires, and the kernel could no longer serve any other alpha/beta. See M5 for what would happen to D itself.
</details>

**R10. List the four exit tails and say what each one protects.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[S, note Section 7.10] (1) warp 2, `explicit.cu:799-806`: 8 blocking waits on `empty[]` continuing the producer state, so that no `tcgen05.commit` from either pair leader can still arrive on this CTA's barriers after it exits; (2) rank 0's warp 1, `explicit.cu:859-867`: 2 `test_wait`-then-`wait` steps on CLC `empty[]`, absorbing the 800 remote arrivals for the last two responses; (3) the leader's warp 0, `explicit.cu:954-961`: 4 waits on `acc_empty[]`, absorbing the 256 arrivals per stage from both epilogues; (4) the TMEM dealloc handshake, `explicit.cu:964-971`: the peer arrives on the leader's `tmem_dealloc`, both wait parity 0, the leader arrives on the peer's, then both `tcgen05.dealloc`, so neither CTA frees the shared TMEM allocation while the other may still read it. Per-rank inventory of blocking tail waits [M, G.1, trace build: 1518 `K_TAIL` records = 46 per cluster x 33]: rank 0 = 8 mainloop + 2 CLC + 4 accumulator + 1 dealloc = 15; rank 1 = 8 + 1 = 9; rank 2 = 8 + 4 + 1 = 13; rank 3 = 8 + 1 = 9; 15 + 9 + 13 + 9 = 46. Only even ranks execute tail (3), only rank 0 tail (2), every rank tails (1) and (4). There is no cluster-wide barrier at exit; these tails are the only thing keeping a CTA's smem alive while remote arrivals can target it. The throttle pipeline is CTA-local and needs no tail; the store pipeline exits with at most one bulk group's smem read un-awaited (`store_tail` is empty for beta = 0) [M, D.1 D15: six of six runs passed].
</details>

### 14.2.2 DERIVE

**D1. Compute `desc_a` and `desc_b` for rank 2, stage s = 5, k-block kb = 3.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

Formulas [S], `explicit.cu:896-897`, `928-929`, `933-934`:

```
  uint32_t const desc_lo_a = kSmemDescLo0 | (((smem_base + OFF_SMEM_A) >> 4) & 0x3FFFu);      // expected 0x10880 (D.7)
  uint32_t const desc_lo_b = kSmemDescLo0 | (((smem_base + OFF_SMEM_B) >> 4) & 0x3FFFu);      // expected 0x12880 (D.7)
```
```
        uint32_t const lo_a = desc_lo_a + 1024u * rs;                                           // + 16384 B per stage in 16-byte units (32-bit low-word add, mma_sm100_desc.hpp:861-874)
        uint32_t const lo_b = desc_lo_b + 512u * rs;                                            // +  8192 B per stage
```
```
            uint64_t const desc_a = desc64(kSmemDescHi, lo_a + 2u * uint32_t(kb));              // + 32 B per k-block
            uint64_t const desc_b = desc64(kSmemDescHi, lo_b + 2u * uint32_t(kb));
```

Rank 2: `smem_base = 0x02000400`. A: `0x02000400 + 33792 = 0x02008800`; `>> 4` = 0x200880; `& 0x3FFF` = 0x0880 (the rank bits fall out of the 14-bit field); `| 0x10000` = 0x10880. Stage 5: + 5 x 1024 = 0x11C80; kb 3: + 6 = 0x11C86. **`desc_a = 0x4000404000011C86`**. B: `0x02000400 + 164864 = 0x02028800`; `>> 4 & 0x3FFF` = 0x2880; `| 0x10000` = 0x12880; + 5 x 512 = 0x13280; + 6 = 0x13286. **`desc_b = 0x4000404000013286`**. Cross-check against the file's own example (`explicit.cu:170`): rank 0, s = 3, kb = 2 gives 0x10880 + 3072 + 4 = 0x11484 and 0x12880 + 1536 + 4 = 0x12E84, matching `0x4000404000011484` / `0x4000404000012E84`. Rank 2's descriptors equal rank 0's for the same (s, kb) [M, D.1 D7: rank 0 and rank 2 identical], which is required because the 2SM MMA reads the peer's halves at the same CTA-relative addresses. The largest low word is `0x10880 + 7 x 1024 + 6 = 0x12486` (A) and `0x12880 + 7 x 512 + 6 = 0x13686` (B). Note what the two adds are: plain 32-bit additions into a word whose bits [0,14) are the start-address field, [14,16) are reserved and [16,30) hold LBO = 1. A carry out of the field would corrupt the reserved bits or LBO, so the construction is only legal because the field cannot overflow: the largest field value is `0x13686 & 0x3FFF = 0x3686 < 0x3FFF`, i.e. no carry is ever generated. The `static_assert` at `explicit.cu:165` (`kSmemBaseLow24 + kSmemBytes < (1u << 18)`) is exactly that guarantee for the whole buffer: `0x400 + 230400 = 0x38800 < 2^18` bytes, so every 16-byte-unit address inside the dynamic smem fits the 14-bit field. The `& 0x3FFF` at `:896-897` is what strips the rank bits [24,26) of `smem_base` (and everything above bit 17), so the per-stage add starts from a rank-independent word.
</details>

**D2. Which barrier address and parity does warp 2 wait on for q = 20 of its 4th tile (tile counter t = 3), and which does the MMA warp wait on for the same k-tile?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[S] The producer state is carried across tiles (`explicit.cu:724`), and 128 k-tiles per tile is a multiple of 8, so the global use count is `n = 128 t + q = 404`. Stage `s = n % 8 = 4`; number of earlier uses of stage 4 = `n / 8 = 50`; producer parity = `1 ^ (50 & 1) = 1` (R6). Address: `empty_base + 8 s = smem_base + OFF_MAIN_EMPTY + 32 = smem_base + 96`, i.e. `0x00000460` for rank 0, `0x01000460` for rank 1, `0x02000460` for rank 2, `0x03000460` for rank 3 (each CTA waits on its own empty barrier; the two leaders' commits with mask 0xF complete all four). In the code the wait is the peek `mbar_try_wait(empty_base + 8u * st.prod_idx, st.prod_phase)` issued one k-tile earlier (`explicit.cu:739`) plus the blocking `EXPLICIT_WAIT` on the same operands only if the peek failed (`explicit.cu:735`). Meaning: parity 1 succeeds once phase 49 (the 50th completion, i.e. the release of use 49 = q = 12 of this tile) is done, i.e. once both leaders committed the MMAs that read stage 4 for q = 12.

The leader's MMA warp waits `full[4]` at `smem_base + 32` with consumer parity `50 & 1 = 0`: phase 50 must complete, i.e. the 51st fill (this k-tile's six boxes plus the leader lane's `expect_tx`) must have landed. The blocking wait is `explicit.cu:923` (`if (!tok) { EXPLICIT_WAIT(full_base + 8u * cons_idx, cons_phase, WAIT_MAINLOOP_FULL, ...) }`); it is normally satisfied in advance by the peek at `:916` (first k-tile of the tile) or `:927` (every later k-tile), and `:924` is where the stage index is captured as `rs`.
</details>

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 (0,0) | (12,6) | (6400, 1536, 0) = 1536..1599 | 99328 in ranks 0, 2 (0x00018800, 0x02018800) | 0x5 | (6400, 768, 0) = 768..831 | 0x00030800 | 0x00000420 |
| 1 (1,0) | (13,6) | (6400, 1664, 0) = 1664..1727 | 99328 in ranks 1, 3 (0x01018800, 0x03018800) | 0xA | (6400, 832, 0) = 832..895 | 0x01030800 | 0x00000420 |
| 2 (0,1) | (12,7) | (6400, 1600, 0) = 1600..1663 | 107520 in ranks 0, 2 (0x0001A800, 0x0201A800) | 0x5 | (6400, 896, 0) = 896..959 | 0x02030800 | 0x02000420 |

The pair {0,1} holds B columns 768..895 = the 128 columns of tn = 6 (64 in each CTA); the pair {2,3} holds tn = 7. The barrier operand is the pair leader's `full[4]` (ranks 0/1 -> rank 0's, ranks 2/3 -> rank 2's), so each leader's barrier receives 2 A boxes landing in the leader + 2 landing in the peer + 2 B boxes = 6 x 8192 = 49152 bytes. **D4. Compute `st_off[0..3]` for epilogue thread (w = 2, l = 17) and the smem byte written for value j = 11 of subtile e = 5. Which stage and which store box does it fall into?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[S] `explicit.cu:1013` and `1047`:

```
    st_off[c] = OFF_SMEM_CD + 2048u * w + 4u * (l & 7u) + 128u * c + 32u * (((l >> 3) & 3u) ^ c);
```
```
        *reinterpret_cast<uint32_t*>(smem + st_off[j & 3] + 512u * uint32_t(j >> 2) + kEpiStageBytes * uint32_t(e & 3)) = __float_as_uint(d);   // 16 scalar st.shared.b32 (B.3.3 step 17)
```

w = 2, l = 17: `l & 7 = 1`, `(l >> 3) & 3 = 2`. `st_off[c] = 512 + 4096 + 4 + 128 c + 32 (2 ^ c)`: c = 0: 4612 + 64 = **4676**; c = 1: 4612 + 128 + 96 = **4836**; c = 2: 4612 + 256 + 0 = **4868**; c = 3: 4612 + 384 + 32 = **5028**. For j = 11, e = 5: `j & 3 = 3`, `j >> 2 = 2`, `e & 3 = 1`: byte = 5028 + 1024 + 8192 = **14244 = 0x37A4**. Stage `e % 4 = 1` (bytes 8704..16895), and within the stage the offset is 14244 - 8704 = 5540, box `i = 5540 / 2048 = 2 = w` (box i always equals w because rows 32 w .. 32 w + 31 of the subtile are box w). Cross-check with the unswizzled form: pre-swizzle byte = `512 + 8192 x 1 + 2048 x 2 + 128 x 11 + 4 x 17 = 14276 = 0x37C4`; `epi_swz` (`explicit.cu:197`: `o ^ ((o & 0x180u) >> 2)`): `0x37C4 & 0x180 = 0x180`, `>> 2 = 0x60`, `0x37C4 ^ 0x60 = 0x37A4`. Both forms agree, as the `static_assert`s at `explicit.cu:199-202` check against `cute::Swizzle<2,5,2>`; the file's own worked example (`explicit.cu:992`: w = 0, l = 9, j = 5, e = 6 -> 17540) recomputes as `st_off[1] = 644`, `+ 512 + 16384 = 17540`. The row written is 32 w + l = 81 of the CTA tile, column 16 e + j = 91. Why the XOR is there at all [S/A]: for one `st.shared.b32` instruction (fixed j and e) the 32 lanes write `4 (l & 7) + 32 (((l >> 3) & 3) ^ (j & 3))` + a warp-uniform base, i.e. the four 32-byte chunks of one 128-byte row in a lane-dependent but bijective order: all 32 banks exactly once. The store is therefore conflict-free with or without the XOR (the XOR only permutes chunks within the same 128-byte row, and `j & 3` is warp-uniform). The kernel must compute the XOR because the D tensor map is encoded with `SWIZZLE_128B_ATOM_32B` [M, D.1 D3]: the TMA unit un-swizzles on read, so the smem image has to be in the swizzled layout, exactly as for A/B where the TMA unit swizzles on write and the UMMA unit un-swizzles on read and the kernel never computes anything (`explicit.cu:203`). The swizzle is dictated by the tensor map; the conflict-free STS pattern is a property of the (32, 16) subtile mapping that happens to hold either way.
</details>

**D6. Compute the global byte address of the D element written by thread (w = 1, l = 20), register j = 9, subtile e = 2, of CTA tile (5, 9); then the smem byte it passes through and the TMA store box that carries it.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[S] Row `m = 128 tm + 32 w + l = 640 + 32 + 20 = 692`; column `n = 128 tn + 16 e + j = 1152 + 32 + 9 = 1193`. D is fp32, M-major (column-major) with leading dimension 8192 (stride 32768 B per column, D.1 D3), so byte offset = `(n x 8192 + m) x 4 = (9773056 + 692) x 4 = 39094992 = 0x2548AD0` from the base of D.           int32_t const c1 = 128 * tn + 16 * e;

box i = 1 has coordinates (672, 1184, 0) and source `cd_base + 8192 x 2 + 2048 x 1`; the element sits at (20, 9) inside the 32 x 16 box; the TMA unit un-swizzles (SWIZZLE_128B_ATOM_32B) on read and writes 16 runs of 128 contiguous bytes (one per column) into D.

**D7. A cluster processes T = 29 tiles. Give the index and parity of every wait in the three tails.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[S] Each tail continues the producer state after N producer steps. The two lines a tail step executes are, for the mainloop (`explicit.cu:800` and `:805`):

```
    EXPLICIT_WAIT(empty_base + 8u * st.prod_idx, st.prod_phase, TAIL_MAINLOOP, tile, uint32_t(i));
```
```
    advance<kStages>(st.prod_idx, st.prod_phase);
```

and the same pair for the CLC tail (`:860-861` test-then-wait on `smem_base + OFF_CLC_EMPTY + 8u * clp_idx` with `clp_phase`, then `:866` `advance<kClcStages>(clp_idx, clp_phase);`) and the accumulator tail (`:955` wait on `acc_empty_base + 8u * accp_idx` with `accp_phase`, then `:960` `advance<kAccStages>(accp_idx, accp_phase);`). Because `advance` (`:612`) increments the index and flips the phase at each wrap, and the producer started at `{0, 1}` and has taken N steps, step i of the tail waits `empty[(N + i) % Stages]` with parity `1 ^ (((N + i) / Stages) & 1)` (the same formula note 7.2 derives for `producer_tail`; tails at `explicit.cu:799-806`, `859-867`, `954-961`). Mainloop: N = 128 x 29 = 3712, Stages 8: indices 0..7, parity `1 ^ ((464 + 0..0) & 1) = 1` for all eight (3712 / 8 = 464 is even; in general 128 T / 8 = 16 T is always even, so the mainloop tail parity is 1 for every T [M, G.1: every K_TAIL mainloop step waited parity 1]). Accumulator: N = 29, Stages 4: i = 0..3 -> indices (29, 30, 31, 32) % 4 = **1, 2, 3, 0**, parities `1 ^ ((29/4 = 7) & 1) = 0`, `1 ^ (7 & 1) = 0`, `1 ^ (7 & 1) = 0`, `1 ^ ((32/4 = 8) & 1) = 1` -> **0, 0, 0, 1**. CLC (rank 0 only): N = 29, Stages 2: indices (29, 30) % 2 = **1, 0**, parities `1 ^ ((14) & 1) = 1`, `1 ^ ((15) & 1) = 0` -> **1, 0**. Sanity check against the measured tile counts [M, G.1]: T = 32 gives accumulator indices 0,1,2,3 all parity 1 and CLC 0,1 parity 1,1; T = 31 gives 3,0,1,2 with 0,1,1,1 and CLC 1,0 with 0,1 - exactly the recorded `{idx, phase}` pairs. This is why a tail must continue the state rather than apply one parity to all barriers.
</details>

**D8. How many bytes cross the L2-to-SM path per cluster per k-tile, how many land in shared memory, and what arithmetic intensity does that give the mainloop?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[S] Per k-tile each of the 4 CTAs issues one A box and one B box of 8192 B: 8 boxes = **65536 B requested from L2** per cluster. Shared memory receives more because every A box is multicast to two CTAs: 4 A boxes x 2 destinations x 8192 + 4 B boxes x 8192 = **98304 B delivered**, i.e. each CTA receives 16384 (A) + 8192 (B) = 24576 B = one full A stage plus its B half, and each pair leader's `full[s]` sees 49152 B [S, R2]. FLOP per k-tile per cluster = 2 x 256 x 256 x 64 = 8388608, so the intensity is 8388608 / 65536 = **128 FLOP per L2 byte** and 8388608 / 98304 = **85.3 FLOP per smem byte** (equivalently per CTA: 2 x 128 x 128 x 64 = 2097152 FLOP against 24576 B delivered = 85.3). Per tile: 128 x 65536 = 8 MiB from L2; whole run: 1024 tiles x 8 MiB = 8 GiB from L2 in 0.889 ms = about 9.7 TB/s aggregate L2-to-SM, 73 GB/s per active SM [M/A, arithmetic on the measured runtime]. Caveat for every rate derived from `Avg runtime` in this chapter: the harness's number is a `GpuTimer` interval around 10 `initialize()` + `run()` pairs and includes, per iteration, six `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled` host encodes, two `cudaFuncSetAttribute` calls and the launch itself (note Section 12 item 1), so the kernel-only time is at most 0.889354 ms and every per-tile / per-k-tile / per-MMA figure below is an upper bound on kernel time (equivalently, the bandwidths are lower bounds). The note's trace-build per-tile time (31.9 us, D.3) is not a substitute: that build is about 13% slower (D.3, G.2). The HBM minimum is A + B + D = 128 + 128 + 256 MiB = 512 MiB (0.6 TB/s over the run), far below HBM bandwidth; the kernel is compute-bound by design (Chapter 3).
</details>

**D9. Which CTA tile does a CLC response with first-CTA id (x0, y0) = (18, 44) give to rank 3, and what are its A rows and D columns?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[S] `explicit.cu:692-693`:

    tn_next = static_cast<int>(2u * (x0 >> 1) + (y0 & 1u) + y);

**D10. The launch coordinate is blockIdx = (41, 26). Which rank is the CTA, who is its pair leader and its A-multicast partner, and what is its initial tile?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[S] `x = blockIdx.x & 1 = 1`, `y = blockIdx.y & 1 = 0` (the cluster is 2 x 2 in grid coordinates, so `%cluster_ctaid = (blockIdx.x % 2, blockIdx.y % 2)`; `explicit.cu:1173-1174` read them and comment `== rank & 1`, `== rank >> 1`); rank `r = x + 2y = 1`, an odd rank, so it is the peer; its pair leader is rank 0 (`peer = rank ^ 1`, `explicit.cu:1107`); its A-multicast partner is rank x + 2 = 3 (mask 0x5 << 1 = 0xA).
