### 14.2.3 MODIFY

**M1. The accumulator empty barrier is initialised with count 128 instead of 256. What happens?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[A, from the [S] protocol] Exactly 256 arrivals land on the leader's `acc_empty[st]` per use (128 from each CTA's epilogue, `explicit.cu:1039`), so with count 128 the barrier completes two phases per use. Two failure modes, depending on timing: (1) the leader's 128 arrivals alone complete the phase, the MMA warp's `producer_acquire` for tile t + 4 passes, and the 2SM MMA (which writes BOTH CTAs' TMEM) overwrites stage st while the peer's epilogue may still be issuing `tcgen05.ld` on it: silently wrong D in the peer; (2) the parity bookkeeping drifts: after both CTAs arrived the barrier is two phases ahead, so the producer's next parity wait either passes without any new arrivals (another overwrite) or, if the interleaving leaves the barrier mid-phase, blocks for 128 arrivals that can only come from an epilogue that is itself waiting on `acc_full`: a hang. With 4 accumulator stages and an epilogue that is far shorter than the 27.8 us mainloop per tile (its wall time was not measured in the note, which records only the whole-tile period and the 77-92 SASS instructions per subtile per warp, G.3; "a few microseconds" is therefore (unverified)), the race window is small and the bug may stay latent in this run; it would surface with fewer stages or a slower epilogue. Count 256 is the only value equal to the number of arrivals per phase.
</details>

**M2. The mainloop release commit uses mask 0x3 << 2y (the pair) instead of 0xF. What happens? And if the empty count were also lowered to 1?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[A] With pair masks, each CTA's `empty[s]` receives one arrival per k-tile (from its own pair leader) against count 2: no phase ever completes, and all four producer warps block at their 9th k-tile (the first 8 pass because the producer starts with parity 1): a hang after one ring pass. Lowering the count to 1 makes the kernel run but breaks the invariant that `0xF` encodes: CTA x multicasts its A half into CTA x + 2's stage s (`a_mcast_mask = 0x5 << x`, `explicit.cu:772`), and stage s of CTA x + 2 is read by the OTHER pair's MMA. With count 1 and pair-local commits, rank 0's producer would be told "stage s is free" by its own pair while pair {2,3} may still be reading rank 2's stage s (which rank 0 is about to overwrite by multicast): silent accumulator corruption in pair {2,3}. That is what `kMainEmptyCount = 2 // 2/2 + 2/1 - 1` and `calculate_multicast_mask<kRowCol>` (`include/cutlass/pipeline/sm100_pipeline.hpp:57-91`) encode: a release must reach every CTA whose smem the releasing MMA has read, including the CTAs that only *wrote into* it by multicast.
</details>

**M3. `fence.proxy.async.shared::cta` is removed (a) from the epilogue, (b) from `clc_consume`.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

(a) [S/A] The 16 `st.shared.b32` per subtile are generic-proxy writes; the TMA store reads shared memory in the async proxy. The CUDA Programming Guide 4.12.2.1 states that to make such writes visible to subsequent bulk-asynchronous copies the proxy fence is required. Without `fence_proxy_async_shared_cta()` at `explicit.cu:1050`, the `bar.sync 1,128` still orders the threads, but the TMA unit may read stale bytes: nondeterministic wrong values in D, most likely in the subtile written just before the store. (b) [S/A] In `clc_consume` (`explicit.cu:683`) the fence sits between the generic `ld.shared.b128` of the response and the remote arrive that lets the scheduler reuse the slot; the next `try_cancel` writes the slot in the async proxy. Removing it violates the proxy memory model (a generic read must be fenced against a later async-proxy write to the same location); in practice the hazard is masked by the 800-count barrier and the two-slot alternation, so the failure probability is far lower than in (a), but CUTLASS keeps it (`sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp:430` `cutlass::arch::fence_view_async_shared();`, the same line at cb424739 and at HEAD; the `:433` quoted in the `explicit.cu:683` comment is the `#endif` three lines below it) and so must you.
</details>

**M4. The cluster becomes (2, 1, 1). Which constants, masks, counts and formulas change?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[A, with the [S] formulas] Ranks are {0, 1} only (y = 0 always), one pair. A has no multicast partner: each CTA loads its full 128 x 64 A stage itself: a single (64, 128, 1) fp16 box of 16384 B is encodable, because `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled` limits each `boxDim` entry to 256 elements ("must be non-zero and less than or equal to 256") and `SWIZZLE_128B` constrains only the inner extent ("CU_TENSOR_MAP_SWIZZLE_128B* require the bounding box inner dimension to be <= 128" bytes; 64 fp16 = 128 B) [S, CUDA Driver API `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled`, 14.4.2], so the leader's `full[s]` expects 2 x (16384 + 8192) = 49152 bytes as before but from 4 boxes instead of 6 (or keep two 64-row boxes and 6 arrivals of bytes; both balance); the TMA A wrapper no longer needs `.multicast::cluster` (or uses mask 0x1 << x trivially). Mainloop empty count becomes `2/2 + 1/1 - 1 = 1` with release mask 0x3 (only the one leader reads either CTA's smem). Accumulator commit mask 0x3. CLC: full arming by lanes 0..1; empty count `32 + 2 x (32 + 32 + 128) = 416`; the (tm, tn) mapping from the launch coordinate and from the first-CTA id must be re-derived from `swizzle_and_rasterize` / `possibly_transpose_work_tile` with cluster divisors (2, 1) (`sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp:666-677, 695-814` at cb424739; +31 lines at HEAD, see 14.4.3) - it is not the 2 x 2 formula of D9/D10. Cluster tiles are 256 x 128, so there are 32 x 64 = 2048 of them. Cost: L2-to-SM traffic per output rises by 1.5x (per k-tile 32768 A + 16384 B = 49152 B for 32768 outputs vs 65536 B for 65536 outputs), while residency could rise to one cluster per TPC (74 clusters, all 148 SMs) instead of 33 clusters on 132 SMs [A; the hardware placement for 2-CTA clusters was not measured]. Whether that is a net win is a Chapter 3 measurement, not a derivation.
</details>

**M5. `alpha` and `beta` become `constexpr float alpha = 1.0f, beta = 0.0f`. Does D change? Does anything else?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[A, from note Section 0/8] D does not change: `1.0f * acc` is an exact identity, and `fmaf(0.0f, 0.0f, t)` folds to `+0.0f + t`, which equals the FFMA result for every t including `t = -0.0f` (both give `+0.0f`; `-0.0` can arise only from `alpha * acc` when alpha < 0 or acc = -0.0, and for integer-valued inputs acc is never -0.0). What changes is the instruction stream: the 128 FMUL + 128 FFMA per tile disappear (an FADD at most, or nothing), the epilogue warps' register footprint shrinks, the `ld.param.v2.b32 [+528]` vanishes, and the kernel can no longer run any other alpha/beta; the host guard `explicit.cu:1272` (`if (params.beta != 0.0f) { return cutlass::Status::kErrorNotSupported; }`) would still reject beta != 0 but alpha != 1 would now silently compute the wrong result. The equivalence contract of note Section 12/D.7 (same arithmetic form, run-time scalars) is what forbids it; performance would be unchanged within noise because the epilogue is not on the critical path [A].
</details>

**M6. The accumulator release (`mbar_arrive_cluster_masked`) is moved from before subtile 7's arithmetic to after subtile 7's TMA stores. Legal? Faster or slower?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[S/A] Legal: the only hard requirement is that `tcgen05.wait::ld` (W32, `explicit.cu:1038`) precedes the arrive so that all eight `tcgen05.ld` of the tile have delivered their registers before the MMA warp may overwrite the stage; moving the arrive later keeps that order. The baseline places the release at the earliest legal point (right after the wait, before subtile 7's FMUL/FFMA/STS and stores) so the MMA warp is unblocked as soon as TMEM is no longer read. Delaying it by one subtile (16 FMUL + 16 FFMA + 16 STS + fence + 2 `bar.sync` + 4 TMA issues) would matter only if the MMA warp were waiting on `acc_empty`; with 4 accumulator stages and a mainloop of 27.8 us per tile against an epilogue that is a small fraction of that (its wall time is not measured in the note; "a few microseconds" is (unverified)), it never is in steady state [A], so no measurable change is expected. Moving it *earlier* (before the last `tcgen05.ld` completes) would be a real bug.
</details>

**M7. Warp 2 consumes the CLC response before issuing its tile's loads instead of after.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[A, with [M] latencies] No deadlock: rank 0's warp 2 arrives on `throttle_full[t]` at tile start (before `load_ktiles`, `explicit.cu:783-786`), which is what allows the scheduler to issue query t, so a consume-before-load would still be satisfied. But it exposes the CLC latency: warp 2 would wait for response t (min 736, median 1408, max 2336 ns from issue to consumption [M, D.3, trace build]) before issuing tile t's loads. Quantify it against the ring: at the tile boundary the producer has run up to 8 stages ahead, so the MMA warp holds at most 8 k-tiles = 8 x 217 ns = 1.74 us of work, and the first new stage becomes consumable one TMA latency after the first new issue. The bubble per tile is therefore `max(0, response latency + first-load TMA latency - 1.74 us)`: about zero at the median latency, and up to about 0.6 us plus the refill latency at the 2.34 us maximum, i.e. **0 to roughly 2-5% of a 27.8 us tile** [A]; a flat "1.4 us = 5%" would be the upper bound that assumes the ring is already drained when the response is awaited. The baseline order lets the response arrive during tile t's 256 loads (the scheduler's measured gap from consuming response n to issuing query n+1, i.e. its throttle wait, is 28.8-37.7 us (median 30.8) in the unprobed clusters of the trace build [M, D.3 and Section 7.4], so the latency is fully hidden) and the fetched tile replaces the current one only at the end of the loop body (`explicit.cu:794`). Why the CUTLASS kernel orders it this way [S, cb424739 `sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:617-679`]: in the producer branch the two `collective_mainloop.load` calls (`:640-647`, `:654-661`) return before `scheduler.fetch_next_work` (`:665-669`), so tile t's TMA issues overlap the CLC round trip; and because the throttle `producer_acquire` + `producer_commit` (`:632-636`) is advanced exactly once per loop iteration, consuming before loading would also delay query t+1 by the whole load phase of tile t. The consume-after also matches the 800-count: the number of arrivals per response does not depend on the order, only their timing does.
</details>

**M8. The producer's `load_tail` (the 8 waits at `explicit.cu:799-806`) is deleted.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[S/A] After the last tile, the two pair leaders still have up to 8 stages of MMAs in flight, each followed by a `tcgen05.commit` with mask 0xF that arrives on every CTA's `empty[s]`, including the CTAs whose warp 2 has already exited. The CTA cannot exit before those arrivals land: the PTX contract for cluster barriers requires that a CTA's shared memory remain valid while remote arrivals target it (note B.6, 7.10); exiting early is undefined behavior, which may show as nothing, as a hang of the leader's `tcgen05.commit`, or as an illegal-address error. Note also that the tail needs the *continued* producer state (D7): it is the only way to know which parity each of the 8 barriers must reach. The CUTLASS chain is `CollectiveMma::load_tail` (`include/cutlass/gemm/collective/sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp:633-641`) -> `PipelineTmaUmmaAsync::producer_tail` (`include/cutlass/pipeline/sm100_pipeline.hpp:702-704`, which only forwards: `impl_.producer_tail(state);`) -> `PipelineTmaAsync::producer_tail` (`include/cutlass/pipeline/sm90_pipeline.hpp:448-454`, the `for (count < Stages) { empty_barrier_ptr_[state.index()].wait(state.phase()); ++state; }` loop), the mainloop pipeline being `PipelineTmaUmmaAsync<8,(2,2,1),(2,1,1)>` [M, D.1 D1].
</details>

**M9. The epilogue's `cp.async.bulk.wait_group.read 1` is changed to `.read 0`; then to `.read 3`.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[S/A] `explicit.cu:1069` `tma_store_wait_read<1>();` is issued by warp 4 right after committing subtile e's group. `.read N` guarantees that all but the most recent N bulk groups have finished reading their smem source. Stage `(e + 1) % 4` is written next and was last read by group e - 3, so the loosest legal value is N = 3; `read 1` is conservative. Where the 1 comes from [S]: the CUTLASS store pipeline is `PipelineTmaStore<4,1>` [M, D.1 D1], i.e. `Stages = 4`, `UnacquiredStages = 1` ("the number of committed TMA store batches that can be in flight upon return of producer acquire", `include/cutlass/pipeline/sm90_pipeline.hpp:650-700`), and `producer_acquire` runs `tma_store_wait<UnacquiredStages>()` when `params_.always_wait || count > UnacquiredStages` (`:698-699`); the kernel sets `epi_store_pipeline_params.always_wait = true` (`sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:491`, the same line at cb424739 and HEAD), which is why every subtile, including the first, executes the `.read 1` instead of skipping it while fewer than two groups are pending. `.read 0` is legal but serialises every subtile behind its own store's smem read, adding one TMA-read latency per subtile to the epilogue (still off the critical path in this kernel, so probably invisible here, visible in an epilogue-bound kernel) [A]. `.read 3` is legal with 4 stages and allows three groups in flight; whether it helps is unmeasured. Whatever N you choose, the exit condition is unchanged: `store_tail` executes nothing for beta = 0, so the CTA exits with the last group's smem read un-awaited [M, D15], which the measured runs show to be safe because the global writes complete as part of kernel completion.
</details>

### 14.2.4 DESIGN

**G1. Size the pipelines for a 256 x 256 pair tile (CTA tile 128 x 256 x 64) with the same fp16 inputs and fp32 TMEM accumulator.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[A, using the builder arithmetic of note Section 6.1 and the [S] constants] Per CTA per stage: A 128 x 64 x 2 = 16384 B (unchanged), B now 128 columns x 64 x 2 = 16384 B (each CTA holds half of the pair's 256 N columns), plus 16 B of barriers: 32784 B. Epilogue storage with the same (128, 16) subtile: 4 x 8192 + pad = 33792 B. Carveout 192 B. Stages = floor((232448 - 192 - 33792) / 32784) = floor(6.05) = **6**, using 192 + 33792 + 6 x 32784 = 230688 B. TMEM: a stage is 128 lanes x 256 fp32 columns, so only **2 accumulator stages** fit in 512 columns (still one full tile of slack between the MMA and the epilogue). Barriers: mainloop full tx = 2 x (16384 + 16384) = **65536 B** (A: 4 x 8192 multicast boxes as before; B: each CTA loads one (64, 128, 1) fp16 box of 16384 B, which the encoder accepts because each `boxDim` entry may be up to 256 elements and the swizzle limit applies only to the 128-byte inner extent [S, CUDA Driver API `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled`, 14.4.2], or two 64-column boxes); empty count stays 2 / mask 0xF; acc full 1 / empty 256; CLC and throttle unchanged. MMA: `tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2` 256 x 256 x 16 (2 MFLOP each), still 4 per k-tile; instruction descriptor n_dim = 256 >> 3 = 32 -> **idesc = 0x10400010**; the B descriptor's start address steps by 16384 B per stage (1024 in 16-byte units) like A's. Epilogue: 16 subtiles of 128 x 16 per tile, TMEM address `T + ((32 w) << 16) + 256 st + 16 e`. Time per k-tile doubles (about 434 ns at the measured MMA rate) so 6 stages buffer about 2.6 us of MMA work against 1.7 us before: deeper in time, shallower in count. The trade: 2x FLOP per L2 byte (A traffic unchanged, B halves per output) against 2 TMEM stages, 6 smem stages and a 2x longer epilogue per tile; the Colfax cluster tutorial makes the same point about the 256 x 256 pair tile ("the same number of FLOPs but transfers half the operand data").
</details>

**G2. Design the barrier table for beta != 0 (C must be read).**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[S, note 7.2 table and 7.8/B.3.5; initialisation already laid out in the smem map] Add warp 3 as the C producer and initialise the three reserved regions:

| Barrier | Count / tx | Who |
|---|---|---|
| epi_load full[4] at 128 | 32 arrivals + 8192 tx bytes | `PipelineTransactionAsync<4>` separates the two: ONE thread's `mbarrier.expect_tx.shared::cta.b64 [full], 8192` (`producer_expect_transaction`, "Must be called by 1 thread", `sm90_pipeline.hpp:941-946` -> `barrier.h:626-637`, no arrival) plus 32 plain `mbarrier.arrive` from warp 3's lanes through `mapa` to `dst_blockid` (`producer_commit`, `:948-951`). If all 32 lanes did `arrive.expect_tx(8192)` the tx-count would be 32 x 8192 = 262144 and the phase would never complete. The 8192 bytes are one 128 x 16 fp32 C subtile = four (32, 16) boxes of 2048 B into the C/D stage. Order in the CUTLASS epilogue (`sm100_epilogue_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:528-541`): `producer_acquire` -> TMA copy -> `producer_expect_transaction` -> `producer_commit` (bytes may land before the expectation, R2). SASS: the bare `expect_tx` is `SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED.A0TR` (8 sites, not executed for beta = 0) [M, D.2] |
| epi_load empty[4] at 160 | 128 | the 128 epilogue threads release after reading C from smem |
| load_order[2] at 192 | 32 each | warp 2 arrives after its first `load()` call (the 8-k-tile prologue) so that C loads do not compete with the A/B prologue; warp 3 waits before its first C load |
| CLC empty[2] | **928** = 32 + 4 x (32 + 32 + 32 + 128) | warp 3 now consumes CLC responses too |

Who initialises them and in what order they are used [S, note 7.2 "Init warp" column; cb424739 `sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp`]: warp 1 initialises the 8 `epi_load` barriers and warp 3 the 2 `load_order` barriers (`OrderedSequenceBarrier<1,2>`, count 32 each), so the init total becomes 43 (`SYNCS.EXCH.64` 43 in the baseline [M, D.2]). Warp 2 arrives on `load_order` once per kernel, between its first `load()` call (the 8-k-tile prologue, `:640-647`) and its second (`:654-661`): `:649-652` `if (do_load_order_arrive) { load_order_barrier.arrive(); do_load_order_arrive = false; }`, so the C loads of the first tile cannot compete with the A/B prologue for TMA bandwidth; warp 3 waits on it once, before its first C load (`:832-834` `if (do_load_order_wait) { load_order_barrier.wait(); do_load_order_wait = false; }`), and never again. The epilogue reads C with 16 `ld.shared.b32` per thread per subtile (one per register; 128 per tile per thread, the 128 static `ld.shared.b32` C reads of the PTX [M, D.2]) into the C fragment, computes `d = fmaf(beta, c, t)` with the real c, and `store_tail` must now execute `cp.async.bulk.wait_group.read 0` because C stages are reused; the C path's `elect.sync`-guarded TMA loads are the only TMA instructions that keep an election predicate [M, D.2]. Everything else (mainloop, accumulator, throttle, tails 1-4) is unchanged. The explicit kernel's host guard rejects beta != 0 precisely because none of this is implemented (`explicit.cu:1272`).
</details>

**G3. Estimate the speed-of-light fraction this kernel would reach on 4096^3 (same tile, same cluster).**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[A, anchored on [M]] Cluster tiles: (4096 / 256)^2 = 256; k-tiles per tile: 4096 / 64 = 64. With 33 resident clusters [M, D.1 D4], 256 / 33 = 7.76 -> 8 waves: 25 clusters do 8 tiles, 8 do 7, a wave-quantisation efficiency of 7.76 / 8 = 0.97. Per-tile time at the measured per-k-tile rate (0.889354 ms / 32 tiles / 128 = 217 ns per k-tile [M/A]; an upper bound on kernel time, D8 caveat) is 64 x 217 ns = 13.9 us, so the mainloop critical path is 8 x 13.9 = 111 us. Two points about the comparison. First, wave quantisation is *not* a differential term: the 8192^3 reference has the same 0.97 (1024 / 33 = 31.03 -> 32 waves), and the 217 ns rate was derived from that run's 32-tile critical path, so at 111 us the 4096^3 run would reproduce the 8192^3 throughput exactly (2 x 4096^3 = 1.374e11 FLOP / 111 us = 1.238 PFLOP/s against 1.236 PFLOP/s [M, G.2]). Second, the only differential term is the fixed cost F (prologue, TMEM allocation, first-tile pipeline fill, the last tile's epilogue, the tails: Chapter 12), amortised over 8 tiles instead of 32. F was not measured in the note (unverified); if it is 2-6 us the run takes 113-117 us, i.e. 1.17-1.22 PFLOP/s, **0.95-0.98 of the 8192^3 throughput**; at F = 9 us (120 us) it would be 0.93 (1.145 PFLOP/s). The ceiling itself is set by 132 of 148 SMs being usable by 2 x 2 clusters [M, D.3], which no tile change recovers; a (2,1,1) cluster might (M4) at the cost of 1.5x L2 traffic per output. A dense-FP16 peak spec number for the B200 was not fetched for this chapter and is therefore not used (unverified).
</details>

**G4. Choose a cluster shape and raster order for M = 1024, N = 65536, K = 8192 (same data types).**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[A, with the [S] scheduler heuristic] FLOP = 2 x 1024 x 65536 x 8192 = 1.0995e12, identical to 8192^3. A is 16 MiB (L2-resident), B is 1 GiB, D 256 MiB. CTA tiles 8 x 512 = 4096 (same count), cluster tiles 4 x 256 = 1024 with (2,2,1). The CUTLASS heuristic `tiles_n > tiles_m ? AlongM : AlongN` (note 7.4) selects **AlongM** here (512 > 8), which is the right choice: the CLC hands out ids in approximately increasing order [M, D.3], and with AlongM four consecutive ids share one 256-column band of B, so each B band is read from HBM about once (about 1 GiB total); with AlongN the 33 clusters would march along n within one m band and each B band would be re-fetched for each of the 4 m bands (about 4 GiB, 0.5 ms of HBM time at 8 TB/s - a number not verified here - against 0.89 ms of compute: tight). Cluster shape: L2-to-SM bytes per k-tile per 1K outputs are 1536 for (2,1,1), **1024 for (2,2,1)**, 1280 for (4,1,1), 768 for (4,2,1) and (2,4,1) (A loaded once per x, B once per y; see Chapter 3's model), so (2,2,1) is the best 4-CTA shape and (4,2,1) would cut traffic a further 25% at the price of 8-CTA clusters (fewer resident clusters: 8 CTAs need 4 TPCs in one GPC [A]) and M = 1024 = only 2 cluster rows of 512. Recommendation: keep (2,2,1) + AlongM (the heuristic's own answer), measure, and try (4,2,1) only if L2-to-SM bandwidth is shown to be the limiter.
</details>

**G5. Replace CLC by a static persistent schedule (as one would on sm_90). What changes, and what does CLC buy on this very problem?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[A, with [M] residency] Static: launch exactly N_resident clusters and let cluster c process tile ids c, c + N, c + 2N, ...; every warp computes the next id locally; delete the CLC pipeline (2 + 2 barriers, 800-count, arming lanes, `try_cancel`, decode, the proxy fence, tail 2), the throttle (4 barriers) and the scheduler warp; keep every other barrier. The subtle part is N_resident: the naive 148 / 4 = 37 is wrong on this machine. Measured: 33 native clusters, 132 SMs busy, 16 idle (64, 65, 122-129, 142-147), every MMA pair on an SM pair (2j, 2j+1), and `cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters` = 33 [M, D.3, D.1 D4]; the explanation - a 2 x 2 cluster needs two whole TPCs in one GPC and the 8 leftover TPCs cannot be paired - is the note's inference [A, D.3 "Inferred"]. Launching 37 statically would make the last 4 clusters run as a second wave after the first 33 finish (each with about 28 tiles of work): the run time would nearly double. With N = 33 a static round-robin gives 1 cluster x 32 tiles + 32 clusters x 31 (1024 = 32 + 992). The CLC hand-out recorded in the TRACE build was 13 clusters x 32 + 19 x 31 + 1 x 19 (the probe-slowed cluster (0,0); 416 + 589 + 19 = 1024, 13 + 19 + 1 = 33) [M, D.3, G.1]: every unprobed cluster received 31 or 32 tiles, i.e. the same balance as the static split up to one tile, and the 13 clusters that got 32 were exactly the 13 with the shortest per-tile time [M, D.3]. (The Release-build hand-out was not recorded; the trace build's per-tile time is 31.9 us against the Release bound of 27.75 us, D.4, and its CLC latency figures are the ones quoted throughout this chapter.) So on this uniform problem CLC buys no balance, only robustness: it does not need to know N_resident, it tolerates another kernel occupying SMs, and its latency (median 1.4 us) is hidden behind the 28.8-37.7 us throttle wait per tile [M, D.3, trace build]. It also costs almost nothing: 8 barriers, one 50-instruction warp loop, a query in flight about 4% of the time [M, D.3]. Where tile costs vary (ragged K, mixed problem sizes, grouped GEMM) its balancing becomes the point (Colfax CLC article).
</details>

---

## 14.3 Glossary

Each entry: what it is, how this kernel uses it, where to look. "W" numbers are the PTX wrappers of `explicit.cu` section 3 (W1 at `explicit.cu:260` ... W37 at `:601`).

**2SM MMA (`cta_group::2`)** - A `tcgen05.mma` issued by one thread of the even CTA of a pair that reads A and B halves from both CTAs' shared memory at identical CTA-relative addresses and writes each CTA's 128 rows of the 256 x 128 result into that CTA's own TMEM. The kernel issues 4 per k-tile (W29, `explicit.cu:516-529`).

**Accumulator stage (`st`)** - One 128-column slice of the 512 TMEM columns: `tmem_c = T + 128 st` (`explicit.cu:919`); 4 stages form the accumulator pipeline (full count 1 by commit, empty count 256 by the epilogues).

**AlongN raster order** - The tile-scheduler rasterisation in which the launch grid's x dimension indexes N and y indexes M after a transpose, giving `tm = 2 (y >> 1) + (x & 1)`, `tn = 2 (x >> 1) + (y & 1)`; chosen by the heuristic `tiles_n > tiles_m ? AlongM : AlongN` on equal counts (note 7.4). Consecutive CLC ids then walk N for a fixed 256-row band of A.

**Arithmetic intensity** - FLOP per byte moved across a given interface; for this mainloop 128 FLOP per L2 byte and 85.3 FLOP per byte delivered to shared memory, per cluster per k-tile (D8), the reason the kernel is compute-bound.

**Async proxy / generic proxy** - Two views of memory in the PTX memory model: ordinary loads and stores (generic proxy) and the asynchronous engines - TMA (`cp.async.bulk.*`), `tcgen05.*`, CLC responses (async proxy). Ordering between them needs `fence.proxy.async` (W15); the kernel issues it before every TMA store and after every CLC decode (PTX ISA 9.4 "Async Proxy"; CUDA Programming Guide 4.12.2.1).

**Atom (layout atom)** - The smallest repeating tile of a swizzled smem layout: SW128 K-major `Swizzle<3,4,3> o (8,64):(64,1)` for A/B (8 rows x 128 B = 1024 B, hence 1024-byte stage alignment), `Swizzle<2,5,2> o (32,4):(1,32)` for D (32 fp32 x 4 columns = 512 B, hence 512-byte alignment).

**Bank conflict** - Two or more lanes of a warp accessing different 32-bit words that map to the same shared-memory bank in one instruction, serialising the access; swizzles exist to avoid this for the row/column access patterns of TMA, UMMA and the epilogue stores.

**Barrier (named) / `bar.sync`, `bar.arrive`** - Hardware CTA barriers selected by id with a thread count: id 1 x 128 synchronises the 4 epilogue warps twice per subtile; id 6 x 160 lets warp 0 (`bar.arrive`) hand the TMEM base to warps 4-7 (`bar.sync`) without warp 0 waiting (W18/W19; ids from `cutlass/arch/barrier.h:169-178`).

**`barrier.cluster.arrive.relaxed` / `.wait`** - The cluster-wide rendezvous (W16/W17): every thread of every CTA arrives, then waits; it makes the fenced `mbarrier.init`s visible before any remote barrier operation. The kernel computes the initial tile between the two halves.

**Box (TMA)** - The per-instruction tile a tensor map transfers: (64, 64, 1) fp16 = 8192 B for A/B, (32, 16, 1) fp32 = 2048 B for D. SWIZZLE_128B requires the inner box extent to be at most 128 B (CUDA Programming Guide 4.12.2.2.5, Table 25).

**Bulk group (`cp.async.bulk.commit_group` / `wait_group.read N`)** - The completion mechanism for TMA stores: the issuing thread batches stores into a group, commits it, and `wait_group.read N` blocks until at most N groups still read shared memory (W24/W25). Only the issuing thread can wait, which is why only warp 4 issues stores.

**Cache hint (`L2::cache_hint`, EVICT_NORMAL)** - The 64-bit operand `0x1000000000000000` on every TMA load (`kCacheHintEvictNormal`, `explicit.cu:188`), CUTLASS's default `Sm100MemDescDefault`.

**Carveout** - The shared-memory budget the collective builder divides among pipelines: opt-in 232448 B minus 192 B of small barriers minus 33792 B of epilogue storage gives floor(198464 / 24592) = 8 mainloop stages (note 6.1); the resulting 230400 B forces one CTA per SM.

**CLC (Cluster Launch Control)** - Blackwell's hardware work-stealing primitive: `clusterlaunchcontrol.try_cancel` atomically cancels a not-yet-launched cluster of the same grid and returns a 16-byte response (multicast to every CTA of the requesting cluster, completing an mbarrier with 16 tx bytes); `query_cancel.is_canceled` / `get_first_ctaid` decode it (W33/W34). A failed response means no unlaunched clusters remain; issuing another request after observing a failure is undefined (CUDA Programming Guide 4.13.1.2).

**CTA tile / cluster tile / MMA tile** - CTA tile: the 128 x 128 output block one CTA owns (its TMEM accumulator and its D stores). Cluster tile: the 256 x 256 block the 2 x 2 cluster owns, the unit the CLC hands out (1024 of them). MMA tile: the 256 (M) x 128 (N) x 16 (K) block one `tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2` computes for a pair.

**Descriptor (smem, UMMA)** - The 64-bit operand describing an A or B operand tile in shared memory: 14-bit start address in 16-byte units, LBO, SBO = 1024 B, version 1, layout type SWIZZLE_128B (`0x40004040_000lo`, R7). The kernel forms it with a 32-bit add on the low word per stage and k-block.

**Descriptor (instruction, `idesc`)** - The 32-bit operand encoding data formats, majorness and M/N of a `tcgen05.mma`: 0x10200010 here (F32 accumulate, F16 inputs, K-major, N = 128, M = 256).

**DSMEM (distributed shared memory)** - The ability of CTAs in a cluster to address each other's shared memory through `shared::cluster` addresses; used here only for barriers (remote `mbarrier.arrive`, TMA/commit multicast, the peer-bit trick) and the multicast TMA destinations, never for generic loads/stores.

**`elect.sync`** - Returns a predicate true in exactly one lane of a converged warp (W2); for a given `membermask` the election is deterministic (PTX ISA 9.4: the same lane is elected every time; Chapter 6, Section 6.2.2 and Chapter 11, Section 11.3.2 quote the rule), and `.sync` makes each election a warp convergence point. Used to issue single-thread operations (TMA, MMA, commit, `try_cancel`, barrier init) from a warp. In SASS the uniform-datapath instruction executes once per warp anyway, so the election is folded away [M, D.2].

**Epilogue** - The phase that turns the TMEM accumulator into D: per subtile `tcgen05.ld` -> FMUL/FFMA -> swizzled `st.shared` -> `fence.proxy.async` -> `bar.sync` -> 4 TMA stores -> `commit_group` -> `wait_group.read 1` -> `bar.sync` (`explicit.cu:1034-1071`).

**`expect_tx` vs `arrive.expect_tx`** - `mbarrier.expect_tx` only adds bytes to the current phase's tx-count (no arrival is counted); `mbarrier.arrive.expect_tx` adds the bytes and performs one arrival in the same operation. The explicit kernel uses only the fused form: the mainloop `full[s]` (49152 B, the leader lane, `explicit.cu:736`) and the CLC `full[]` (16 B, remote from rank 0's lanes 0..3, `:842`); the omitted C path uses the bare `expect_tx` (one thread, 8192 B) plus 32 plain arrives (G2). Because a phase completes only when both the pending-arrival count and the tx-count are zero and the tx-count may go negative (PTX ISA 9.4, 9.7.15.16.8 and Table 43 in 9.7.15.16.3), bytes may complete before the expectation is registered (R2).

**`fence.mbarrier_init`** - `fence.mbarrier_init.release.cluster` (`cutlass/arch/barrier.h:712-720`, `fence_barrier_init`): a release fence issued after each group of `mbarrier.init` so that the initialised barrier words are visible cluster-wide before the `barrier.cluster` rendezvous lets any remote arrive, TMA `complete_tx` or `tcgen05.commit` touch them. The explicit kernel issues it 4 times (PTX inventory `fence.mbarrier_init.release.cluster` 4 [M, G.3]). It has no SASS mnemonic of its own: the note records "no instruction" for it and attributes, by inference, the bare `FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S` that precedes each init group to its lowering (D.2; four such groups in the explicit kernel's prologue, G.3).

**`FusionStorage`** - The epilogue fusion callbacks' shared-memory struct; for `Sm90LinearCombination` it is an empty tuple of `sizeof` 1. It sits after the four C/D stages at offset 33280 and, because the epilogue `SharedStorage` is `alignas(512)`, pads it from 33281 to 33792, which is why `OFF_SMEM_A = 33792` rather than 33280 (`explicit.cu:158` `static_assert`; note Section 6.2 rows 33280 "FusionStorage, empty tuple, pads to 512" and 33792).

**GDC / PDL (`griddepcontrol`, Programmatic Dependent Launch)** - `griddepcontrol.wait` blocks until all prerequisite grids have completed and flushed (W35; issued by rank 0's warp 1 at the top of `scheduler_role`, `explicit.cu:821`, and by every CTA's warp 2 at the top of `producer_role`, `:764`, before either touches global data; warp 1 of ranks 1-3 never reaches it, and the baseline's third site, warp 3's C path, is not compiled into the explicit kernel: `griddepcontrol.wait` 2 sites [M, G.3]); `griddepcontrol.launch_dependents` signals that a dependent grid may begin launching (warp 0 after its last tile, W36). They only have an effect when the dependent launch carries the PDL attribute (`cudaLaunchAttributeProgrammaticStreamSerialization`, CUDA Programming Guide 4.5.2); the harness does not use it, and the kernel emits them because the fixed build defines `CUTLASS_ENABLE_GDC_FOR_SM100=1` [S, note Section 0].

**`__grid_constant__`** - Qualifier on the by-value kernel parameter block that lets the kernel take its address (needed for `prefetch.tensormap` and the TMA descriptor operands) and keeps it in parameter/constant space (`c[0x0][0x380]` onwards [M, G.3]).

**HBM** - The GPU's main (high-bandwidth) memory; the kernel needs only 512 MiB of HBM traffic for the whole run and is far from HBM-bound (D8).

**K-major / MN-major** - Which dimension is contiguous in memory for an MMA operand: K-major means consecutive k values are adjacent (A row-major M x K and B "column-major" N x K here are both K-major); encoded as `a_major = b_major = 0` in the instruction descriptor and selecting the K-major SW128 atom.

**k-tile (`q`) / k-block (`kb`)** - A k-tile is the 64-wide K slab one smem stage holds (128 per tile); a k-block is the 16-wide K slice one `tcgen05.mma` consumes (4 per k-tile), addressed by `+ 32 B` (2 in 16-byte units) on the descriptor.

**L2 promotion (128 B)** - A tensor-map encode option requesting that TMA fetches be promoted to 128-byte L2 requests; set on all six maps [M, D.1 D3].

**`__launch_bounds__(256, 1)`** - Tells ptxas the kernel runs 256 threads with at least 1 CTA per SM, allowing up to 255 registers per thread; the explicit kernel uses 26 [M, G.3].

**Launch-linear cluster id** - The id `CY x 32 + CX` of the cluster at launch-grid cluster coordinate `(CX, CY) = (blockIdx.x / 2, blockIdx.y / 2)` (grid (64, 64) = 32 x 32 clusters), i.e. `(y0 / 2) x 32 + x0 / 2` for a CLC response's first-CTA id `(x0, y0)`. The 33 natively launched clusters were ids 0..32 and the CLC handed out the cancelled ids 33..1023 each exactly once, in approximately increasing order (D9, D10) [M, D.3]. With AlongN and no swizzle, id L is the cluster tile `(m, n) = (L / 32, L % 32)`, so a cluster's successive tiles are about 33 ids apart.

**`mapa`** - PTX instruction mapping a `shared::cta` address to the corresponding `shared::cluster` address in another CTA of the cluster (W10/W13); lowered by ptxas to a byte-3 insert of the rank (`PRMT ..., 0x654`) [M, D.2].

**mbarrier** - An 8-byte shared-memory synchronisation object with a phase, a pending arrival count and a transaction count; a phase completes when the arrival count reaches zero and the tx-count is balanced. Operations used: `init`, `arrive`, `arrive.expect_tx`, `try_wait.parity` (blocking, with suspend hint), `try_wait.parity` (single peek), `test_wait.parity` (W5-W13).

**Multicast (TMA / commit)** - `.multicast::cluster` with a 16-bit CTA mask: a TMA load writes the same box to the same CTA-relative offset in every masked CTA and signals each destination's barrier; a `tcgen05.commit` arrives on the barrier at the same offset in every masked CTA. Masks: A 0x5 << x, release 0xF, accumulator 0x3 << 2y (R4).

**Occupancy / residency** - How many CTAs (clusters) are simultaneously resident: one CTA per SM here (smem 230400 B), 33 clusters of 4 = 132 SMs [M, D.3], not 148 / 4 = 37, because 2 x 2 clusters need two whole TPCs in one GPC [A].

**Pair leader / peer** - The even rank of an MMA pair {2y, 2y+1} issues the TMEM allocation atomic, all `tcgen05.mma`, both commits, and owns the `full[]`, `acc_empty[]` barriers that the pair uses; the odd rank (peer, `r ^ 1`) loads its halves, runs its epilogue, and arrives on the leader's barriers.

**Parameter space / constant bank 0** - Where `__grid_constant__` kernel parameters live; the device reads `k`, `alpha`, `beta` and the four tensor maps from there (`ld.param`, SASS `LDC`/`LDCU`).

**Peer-bit mask (`0xFEFFFFFF`)** - Clears bit 24 of a `shared::cta` address, turning an odd CTA's barrier address into its pair leader's (R5).

**Persistent kernel** - A kernel whose CTAs loop over many output tiles instead of exiting after one; here every CTA computes about 31-32 tiles, the loop being driven by CLC responses.

**Phase / parity** - An mbarrier's phase is a counter of completions; `try_wait.parity P` succeeds once the phase of parity P is complete (the barrier's current phase has the other parity). Pipelines track a 1-bit phase per stage that flips each time the ring wraps (R6).

**Pipeline (producer / consumer)** - A ring of `Stages` buffers with a full and an empty barrier per stage; producers wait empty, fill, and signal full (or let TMA bytes complete it); consumers wait full, read, and signal empty. Four pipelines here: mainloop (8), accumulator (4), CLC (2), throttle (2).

**`producer_tail`** - The `Stages` extra waits a producer performs after its last fill so that the CTA does not exit while consumers may still arrive on its empty barriers (R10, D7).

**Raster order** - see AlongN.

**`scale_c` / `ScaleOut::Zero` vs `One`** - The `tcgen05.mma` predicate operand that selects `D = A x B` (0, `ScaleOut::Zero`) or `D = D + A x B` (1, `ScaleOut::One`). The first MMA of every tile (q = 0, kb = 0) is issued with `scale_c = 0` and overwrites the TMEM stage, so no TMEM clearing is ever needed; the remaining 511 accumulate (`explicit.cu:917` `uint32_t scale_c = 0;`, `:940` `scale_c = 1u;`; CUTLASS `sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp:676, 706`; note Section 8). In SASS only the k-block-0 `UTCHMMA` carries the live predicate (`UP0`), the other three are predicated on `UPT` [M, G.3].

**Scoreboard** - The SASS-level dependency tracking (per-warp scoreboards encoded in the instruction control words) that ptxas uses to stall a consumer until an asynchronous producer (`LDTM`, `STS` read, `UTMASTG` read) completes; it is why `tcgen05.wait::ld` emits no SASS instruction here (the first `FMUL` after an `LDTM` waits on the scoreboard the `LDTM` sets) and why `wait_group.read 1` is a `DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x1` [M, D.2; the scoreboard decode is inferred]. `fence.mbarrier_init` is a different case (a release fence with no mnemonic of its own; see its entry).

**`shared::cta` / `shared::cluster`** - PTX state spaces for shared memory addressed within the executing CTA (32-bit window address, `__cvta_generic_to_shared`) or within the cluster (a CTA's own `shared::cta` address is also a valid `shared::cluster` address of that CTA, with the rank in bits [24,32) on this compiler/hardware [M, D5]).

**SM / TPC / GPC** - Streaming multiprocessor; a Texture Processing Cluster = 2 SMs sharing some resources (every MMA pair was placed on an SM pair (2j, 2j+1) [M, D.3]; reading that pair as a TPC is the note's inference); a GPU Processing Cluster = a group of TPCs within which a thread-block cluster must be placed.

**Speed of light (SOL)** - The runtime a kernel would have if its single binding resource ran at full rate with zero overhead; Chapter 3 builds the model, G3 applies it.

**Stage (`s`)** - One slot of the mainloop smem ring: 16384 B of A (128 x 64 fp16) at `OFF_SMEM_A + 16384 s` and 8192 B of B (64 x 64 fp16) at `OFF_SMEM_B + 8192 s`, guarded by `full[s]` / `empty[s]`.

**Subtile (`e`)** - One 128 x 16 column slice of the CTA tile the epilogue processes per iteration: one `tcgen05.ld.32x32b.x16` per warp, one 8192-byte C/D smem stage (`e % 4`), four TMA store boxes.

**SW128 / `Swizzle<B,M,S>`** - CuTe's XOR swizzle on byte offsets: keep the low M bits, XOR B bits at position M with B bits S positions higher. `Swizzle<3,4,3>` (bits [4,7) ^= bits [7,10)) is the SWIZZLE_128B pattern the TMA unit applies on write and the UMMA unit on read for A/B; `Swizzle<2,5,2>` (bits [5,7) ^= bits [7,9)) is SWIZZLE_128B_ATOM_32B for D, which the epilogue computes in `st_off` (`cute/swizzle.hpp:42-99`: doc comment from 42, `struct Swizzle` at 55, `apply` at 76, `operator()` at 84).

**`tcgen05`** - The PTX instruction family of the 5th-generation tensor core: `alloc/dealloc/relinquish_alloc_permit` (TMEM management), `mma` (UMMA), `commit` (completion to an mbarrier), `ld`/`wait::ld` (TMEM to registers). Requires `sm_100a` (architecture-specific target).

**Tensor map (`CUtensorMap`)** - The 128-byte opaque descriptor produced by `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled` that tells the TMA unit a tensor's base, shape, strides, box, element type and swizzle; passed in the parameter block, prefetched with `prefetch.tensormap` (W20).

**Throttle** - The 2-stage CTA-local pipeline on rank 0 (counts 32/32) that lets the scheduler issue query t only after warp 2 has begun loading tile t, so at most one CLC query is outstanding per cluster beyond the tile being loaded (note 7.4; [M] never more than one outstanding).

**TMA (Tensor Memory Accelerator)** - The asynchronous copy engine for multi-dimensional tiles between global and shared memory (`cp.async.bulk.tensor`), completing loads through mbarrier tx bytes and stores through bulk groups; it applies swizzles and multicast in hardware.

**TMEM (Tensor Memory)** - Blackwell's 256 KB per-SM on-chip accumulator memory: 128 lanes x 512 columns of 32-bit cells, addressed as `(lane << 16) | column`; allocated in columns (power of two, at least 32) by one warp; a warp may read lanes `[32 (warp % 4), +32)` only (Colfax TMEM tutorial; note B.6). The kernel allocates all 512 columns per pair and holds 4 accumulator stages.

**Token (`WaitDone` / `WaitAgain`)** - The result of a single `try_wait.parity` peek (W7) carried into the next iteration so that the blocking wait (W6) is entered only when the peek failed; the kernel peeks the next stage right after advancing.

**tx-count (transaction count)** - The byte counter of a transaction mbarrier: `arrive.expect_tx` adds the expected bytes, each async copy's `complete_tx` subtracts what it delivered; the phase completes when arrivals and bytes both balance (49152 per mainloop stage, 16 per CLC response).

**UMMA** - CUTLASS's name for the `tcgen05.mma` family and its descriptors (`cute/arch/mma_sm100_desc.hpp`, `mma_sm100_umma.hpp`).

**Uniform datapath / UR** - The per-warp scalar execution path of the SM with uniform registers `URn` and predicates `UPn`; TMA, MMA, commit and CLC issues are uniform instructions (`UTMALDG`, `UTCHMMA`, `UTCBAR`, `UGETNEXTWORKID`) that execute once per warp regardless of how many lanes reach them [M, D.2].

**Warpgroup** - Four consecutive warps (128 threads) with warp ids 4k..4k+3, the unit that Hopper's `wgmma` addresses and that the Blackwell epilogue inherits for its 128-thread named barrier. Here warps 0-3 (MMA, scheduler, producer, idle C loader) form warpgroup 0 and warps 4-7 (epilogue) warpgroup 1; the `tcgen05.ld` lane rule `[32 (warp % 4), +32)` is what maps epilogue warp `w = warp_idx - 4` to TMEM lanes `32 w` (R3).

**Warp specialisation** - Assigning different roles to different warps of one CTA (producer, scheduler, MMA, epilogue) so that each runs a simple loop and communicates through barriers; the structure of `explicit.cu` sections 6-9.

**Wave quantisation** - The efficiency loss when the number of work units is not a multiple of the number of workers: 1024 tiles / 33 clusters = 31.03 (loss about 3%), 256 / 33 = 7.76 (G3).

**SASS mnemonics used in the lecture** - `UTCHMMA.2CTA` (`tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2`), `UTCBAR.2CTA.MULTICAST` (`tcgen05.commit` multicast), `UTCATOMSWS` (TMEM alloc/dealloc atomics), `LDTM.x16` (`tcgen05.ld`), `UTMALDG.3D[.MULTICAST].2CTA` (TMA load), `UTMASTG.3D` (TMA store), `UTMACMDFLUSH` (`commit_group`), `DEPBAR.LE SB0, N` (`wait_group.read N`), `UTMACCTL.PF` (`prefetch.tensormap`), `SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64[.TRYWAIT]` (`mbarrier.test_wait/try_wait`), `SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64[.RED]` (`mbarrier.arrive`, remote with `.RED`), `SYNCS.EXCH.64` (`mbarrier.init`), `UGETNEXTWORKID.BROADCAST` (`try_cancel`), `ACQBULK` (`griddepcontrol.wait`), `PREEXIT` (`launch_dependents`), `UCGABAR_ARV/WAIT` (`barrier.cluster`), `FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S` + `MEMBAR.ALL.CTA` (`fence.proxy.async`) [M, note D.2 dictionary].

### 14.4.2 CUDA Programming Guide (NVIDIA, v13.4.2, opened 2026-10-03)

- Index: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/
- 4.5 Programmatic Dependent Launch and Synchronization: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/04-special-topics/programmatic-dependent-launch.html - `cudaGridDependencySynchronize` ("block until all primary kernels the secondary kernel is dependent on have completed and flushed results to global memory"), the implicit trigger at primary exit, the `cudaLaunchAttributeProgrammaticStreamSerialization` attribute.
- 4.10 Asynchronous Barriers: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/04-special-topics/async-barriers.html - phases, parity ("an even phase has integer parity 0 and an odd phase has integer parity 1"), transaction counts (4.10.6: the wait "blocks threads at the wait operation until all the producer threads have performed an arrive and the sum of all the transaction counts reaches an expected value").
- 4.12 Asynchronous Data Copies: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/04-special-topics/async-copies.html - TMA tensor maps and boxes (4.12.2.2), swizzle modes and the 128-byte inner-dimension limit (4.12.2.2.5, Table 25), mbarrier byte-count completion for loads and bulk async-group completion for stores (only the initiating thread can wait), the `fence_proxy_async` requirement before a bulk copy reads thread-written shared memory (4.12.2.1), cluster multicast.
- 4.13 Work Stealing with Cluster Launch Control: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-programming-guide/04-special-topics/cluster-launch-control.html - the `try_cancel` / `query_cancel` flow with a 16-byte result and `mbarrier_arrive_expect_tx`, failure when no indices remain, and "Submitting another cancellation request after observing a previously failed request is undefined behavior" (4.13.1.2).
- Legacy single-page guide (thread block clusters, distributed shared memory, `cluster.map_shared_rank`): https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/index.html (table of contents opened; the cluster/DSMEM text was located through search results from this page's archive versions and not quoted).
- Verbatim quotes the lecture relies on (re-read on 2026-10-03): 4.12.2 "When the bulk-asynchronous operation writes data from shared memory to global or distributed shared memory, only the initiating thread can wait for the operation to have completed." (why only warp 4 issues and waits the D stores); 4.12.2.1 "To make the writes visible to subsequent bulk-asynchronous copies, the `cuda::ptx::fence_proxy_async` function is used." (M3); 4.12.2.2.5, Table 25 "Requirements and properties of the different swizzle patterns for Compute Capability 9", row `CU_TENSOR_MAP_SWIZZLE_128B`, "Shared box's inner dimension": "<=128 bytes" (R8, Box); 4.13 "The cancellation will fail if there are no more thread block indices available or for other reasons"; 4.13.1.2 "Submitting another cancellation request after observing a previously failed request is undefined behavior." (CLC).
- CUDA Driver API, `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled` (https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__TENSOR__MEMORY.html, opened 2026-10-03), quoted for M4 / G1: "boxDim array, which specifies number of elements to be traversed along each of the tensorRank dimensions, must be non-zero and less than or equal to 256."; "CU_TENSOR_MAP_SWIZZLE_128B* require the bounding box inner dimension to be <= 128."; "When interleave is CU_TENSOR_MAP_INTERLEAVE_NONE, { boxDim[0] * elementSizeInBytes( tensorDataType ) } must be a multiple of 16 bytes."; "globalStrides array, which specifies tensor stride of each of the lower tensorRank - 1 dimensions in bytes, must be a multiple of 16 and less than 2^40."; the enumerator comment "CU_TENSOR_MAP_SWIZZLE_128B_ATOM_32B, // Swizzle 32B chunks within 128B span".

Do not expect both slots to be in flight: the scheduler must `consumer_wait` the throttle before every query and rank 0's warp 2 arrives on the throttle only when it starts loading tile t, so query t is issued only once tile t is being loaded and query t+1 only once tile t+1 is; the two slots alternate and never overlap (never more than one query outstanding per cluster, 0 violations in 1024 queries [M, D.3]; the WHY is note Section 7.4).

### 14.4.5 Articles opened and found accurate

- Colfax Research, "CUTLASS Tutorial: Writing GEMM Kernels Using Tensor Memory For NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs", https://research.colfax-intl.com/cutlass-tutorial-writing-gemm-kernels-using-tensor-memory-for-nvidia-blackwell-gpus/ - TMEM organisation ("512 columns and 128 rows, or lanes, of 32-bit cells"; "bits 31-16 denote the lane ID while 15-0 denote the column"), per-warp lane restriction, single-warp alloc/dealloc, `tcgen05.ld` shapes.
- Colfax Research, "CUTLASS Tutorial: GEMM with Thread Block Clusters on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs", https://research.colfax-intl.com/cutlass-tutorial-gemm-with-thread-block-clusters-on-nvidia-blackwell-gpus/ - pair-UMMA with the even CTA as leader, half-operand loading per CTA, parity-restricted TMA multicast, the peer-address rule ("setting the 24th bit to 0", `0xFEFFFFFF`), transaction-count accounting on the leader's barrier.
- Colfax Research, "Dynamic persistent tile scheduling with Cluster Launch Control (CLC) on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs", https://research.colfax-intl.com/dynamic-persistent-tile-scheduling-with-cluster-launch-control-clc-on-nvidia-blackwell-gpus/ - static vs dynamic persistent scheduling, `try_cancel` as an atomic request with a 16-byte response delivered through mbarrier bytes and multicast to all CTAs of the cluster, the scheduler executed by the first CTA, offsetting the cancelled cluster's first-CTA id by the CTA's cluster coordinates.
- NVIDIA Technical Blog, "NVIDIA Blackwell and NVIDIA CUDA 12.9 Introduce Family-Specific Architecture Features", https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/nvidia-blackwell-and-nvidia-cuda-12-9-introduce-family-specific-architecture-features/ - the `a` (architecture-specific, not forward-compatible) vs `f` (family) target suffixes; the reason the build uses `sm_100a`.

## Checkpoint

**1. Which two numbers in the numbers card are measured at run time by the kernel itself and must never be hard-coded, even though their values are known?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

`smem_base` (`0x400 + (r << 24)`, computed by `smem_u32(smem)` at `explicit.cu:1098`) and the TMEM base `T` (read from `smem + OFF_TMEM_BASE_PTR` after `tcgen05.alloc`, `explicit.cu:888`). Both were measured (0x400 and 0) [M, D.1 D5/D6], and every address formula depends on them, but the kernel derives them at run time: the descriptor low words are built from the computed base (`explicit.cu:896-897`) and `tmem_c = T + 128 st`. Hard-coding either would silently break on a different driver/toolchain placement.
</details>

**2. One count in the barrier table depends on beta. Which, and what are its two values?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

The CLC empty count: 800 = 32 + 4 x (32 + 32 + 128) for beta = 0 (warps 0, 2, 4-7 of each CTA plus rank 0's warp 1), and 928 = 32 + 4 x (32 + 32 + 32 + 128) when warp 3 (the C loader) also consumes responses. The explicit kernel hard-codes 800 (`explicit.cu:183`); the CUTLASS kernel selects 928 or 800 at run time on `is_producer_load_needed` [M, D.2].
</details>

**3. Why does the mainloop tail always wait with parity 1, whereas the accumulator and CLC tails need a per-barrier parity?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

The tail continues the producer state after N steps; step i waits parity `1 ^ (((N + i) / Stages) & 1)`. For the mainloop N = 128 T and Stages = 8, so `(N + i) / 8 = 16 T` for all i = 0..7, which is even for every T: parity 1 for all eight barriers (and the index runs 0..7 from 0). For the accumulator (N = T, Stages 4) and CLC (N = T, Stages 2) the quotient `(T + i) / Stages` changes within the tail unless `T % Stages == 0`, so the indices wrap and the parity flips mid-tail (D7: T = 29 gives accumulator indices 1, 2, 3, 0 with parities 0, 0, 0, 1).
</details>

**4. State the arithmetic intensity of the mainloop at the L2 interface and explain in one sentence why the A multicast does not change it but does change what lands in shared memory.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

128 FLOP per L2 byte: 8.39 MFLOP per cluster per k-tile against 8 boxes x 8192 B = 65536 B requested from L2. Multicast delivers each A box to two SMs from one L2 read, so the L2 request count is unchanged while shared memory receives 98304 B (each CTA gets the full 16384-byte A stage although it only requested 8192 B of it), which is why the intensity per smem byte is lower: 8388608 / 98304 = 85.3.
</details>

**5. If you had to delete exactly one of the four exit tails to "save instructions", which CTA would be the first to misbehave in each case?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

Mainloop tail (warp 2): any CTA, since both leaders' `tcgen05.commit` with mask 0xF target every CTA's `empty[]`; CLC tail (rank 0's warp 1): CTA 0, whose `clc_empty[]` receives the 800 remote arrivals for the last two responses; accumulator tail (leader's warp 0): the leader CTAs (ranks 0 and 2), whose `acc_empty[]` receive 256 arrivals per stage from both epilogues; dealloc handshake: the pair, because one CTA could `tcgen05.dealloc` the shared allocation while the other's epilogue is still reading TMEM. None of these can be removed; the throttle pipeline needs no tail because it is CTA-local.
</details>

**6. In D3 the four CTAs issue eight TMA loads for one k-tile. How many of the eight `cp.async.bulk.tensor` instructions carry a multicast mask, and how many distinct mbarrier addresses do the eight instructions name?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

Four carry a mask (the four A loads: masks 0x5, 0xA, 0x5, 0xA); the four B loads do not. The eight instructions name only two distinct barrier addresses: rank 0's `full[s]` (`0x00000420` for s = 4) from ranks 0 and 1, and rank 2's `full[s]` (`0x02000420`) from ranks 2 and 3, because the peer-bit mask redirects the odd ranks to their leader. Each of the two barriers therefore receives 6 x 8192 = 49152 bytes, matching the single `expect_tx` of its leader lane.
</details>
